arxiv:2611.34209v1.text: Graph-Informed Deep Factor Model for Statistical Arbitrage. Statistical arbitrage exploits temporary mispricings between similar assets in the cross-section of daily equity returns. We propose a nonlinear single-factor model, called a Graph-Informed Deep Factor (GIDF) model, whose per-stock loadings have cross-sectional dependence conditional on a latent network. The network captures cross-sectional return dependencies that remain after removing the dominant eigenmodes of the return correlation matrix, thereby providing a complementary representation of inter-asset relationships beyond the leading sources of systematic variation. It is reconstructed from data using a novel method that we call the Factor-Adjusted Dynamic EWMA (FADE). A signed-edge graph attention mechanism then combines the reconstructed network with exogenous firm characteristics and macroeconomic variables. This graph-informed specification is designed to produce residuals that more effectively separate idiosyncratic mean-reverting dynamics from cross-sectional co-movements, yielding economically useful signals for daily statistical arbitrage. In a comprehensive empirical study on daily U.S. equities from 2015 to 2024, GIDF outperforms classical factor models and state-of-the-art deep learning methods, achieving an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 1.78 under the canonical Avellaneda--Lee rule.
arxiv:2611.34209v1.author: Evelyn Zhu et al.

arxiv:2611.30843v3.text: Cleaning correlation matrices with external information: the Maximum Variance estimator. Rotationally invariant estimators clean the eigenvalues of an empirical correlation matrix but keep its noisy eigenvectors. We study an estimator that corrects the eigenvectors by using external information, namely a partition of the assets into groups such as asset classes or regions. The Maximum Variance (MaxVar) estimator restricts the leading eigenvectors to linear combinations of the maximum-variance portfolios of the groups and replaces the rest of the spectrum by a single eigenvalue. It is a factor model with about n parameters instead of n2/2, and it is positive de nite even when the number of observations is smaller than the number of assets n. We apply it to the correlation matrix of 47 futures on stock indices, bonds and currencies, with the three asset classes as groups. In an illustrative Monte Carlo test, in which the reference matrix has the structure assumed by the estimator, the distance to the reference is reduced by one third with respect to the empirical matrix, against less than 10% for the rotationally invariant estimator. The decisive test is the performance of a portfolio on real data: over 1993-2018, the Sharpe ratio of the risk parity portfolio, which involves the inverse of the matrix, is 1.28 with the MaxVar estimator, 1.24 with the rotationally invariant estimator and 1.17 with the empirical matrix, and the advantage increases when the estimation window is shortened.
arxiv:2611.30843v3.author: Sébastien Valeyre

arxiv:2611.30584v1.text: Do Candlestick Charts Suffice? The Incremental Economic Value of Technical Indicators in Stock Return Prediction. Although technical analysis remains widely used in practice, the need for manually constructed indicators is increasingly questioned as deep learning models can extract features directly from OHLC price data. This paper examines the standalone economic value of trading volume and manually constructed technical-indicator groups and whether adding these groups to OHLC candlestick charts provides incremental economic value. Using daily data for 1,707 Chinese A-share stocks from 2013 to 2025, we construct approximately 3.36 million stock-window samples and encode them as multi-channel images containing candlestick charts, trading volume, and seven widely used manually constructed technical indicators. The primary analysis uses a 2D CNN on these images; complementary tests apply a logistic regression, a 1D CNN, and an LSTM to numerical representations of the same samples. Out-of-sample performance from 2021 to 2025 is evaluated using decile portfolios, Sharpe ratios, Fama--French alphas, and formal pairwise tests. Our empirical results yield two central findings. First, specifications based separately on OHLC, trading volume, and each technical-indicator group produce significantly positive high-minus-low returns and factor-adjusted alphas, together with economically meaningful Sharpe ratios; the OHLC-only specifications generally perform best under the nonlinear models. Second, adding these technical-indicator groups to OHLC does not systematically improve any of these performance measures in our setting. Together, these results provide the first large-scale evidence from the Chinese A-share market on the standalone and incremental economic value of these technical-indicator groups across multiple representations and model architectures.
arxiv:2611.30584v1.author: Peng Liu et al.

arxiv:2611.28524v1.text: Modeling Joint Tail Risk and Dependence for Cryptocurrencies via a Copula-Based Semiparametric Framework. This study proposes a Bayesian copula-based bivariate semiparametric framework for jointly forecasting Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) while modeling cross-asset tail dependence. The marginal dynamics are specified using four ES-CAViaR-type models, including extensions incorporating Rogers-Satchell and Garman-Klass volatility measures. To construct the copula inputs, we use the empirical ranks of standardized residuals, which depend on the marginal parameters, thereby linking marginal tail dynamics and dependence modeling without requiring fully specified marginal distributions. Clayton and BB1 copulas are considered, and adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo methods are used for estimation and joint tail-risk forecasting. A simulation study under a DCC-GARCH-$t$ data-generating process evaluates the finite-sample forecasting performance of the proposed framework. Using Bitcoin and Ethereum data, we evaluate one-step-ahead forecasts from 2020 to 2025 through a rolling-window forecasting scheme and compare the proposed models with Bayesian DCC-GARCH-N and DCC-GARCH-$t$ benchmarks. Rolling copula estimates also reveal time-varying asymmetry in Bitcoin-Ethereum tail dependence, with lower-tail dependence remaining higher than upper-tail dependence for most of the period. The proposed framework delivers competitive forecasting performance for both marginal and joint tail risk.
arxiv:2611.28524v1.author: Cathy W. S. Chen et al.

11月26日，币安发布公告称，提现恢复工作已经完成，因10月安全事件实施的提现暂停已全部解除；提现在几乎全部网络上重新开放。公告同时写明：另有少数网络因维护或计划中的升级暂时暂停提现，这与此次恢复工作不是一回事，影响的是日常提现里很小的一部分，具体是哪些网络，公告里没有逐一列出，需要以币安官方的网络状态页面为准。币安还表示，用户资产仍然足额储备，并可在其准备金证明（Proof of Reserves）上查看。CoinDesk、Decrypt等媒体转述了上述公告。需要分清：这是“与那次事件相关的提现限制已经解除”，不是说被盗资金已经全部追回，也不是说所有网络此刻都能提现。背景是：10月29日，币安称热钱包遭到未授权访问，受影响资产约63.4亿美元；平台随后暂停部分网络提现，并从11月1日起分阶段恢复。币安当时表示将覆盖用户损失。同一份更新还提醒：此类事件之后往往会出现钓鱼；官方不会主动联系用户要求“加速提现”“优先处理”或把资产转到所谓“币安金库”，也永远不会索要密码、双重验证码或助记词。

3. 约68亿美元名义本金的比特币期权已于周五到期结算，结算价约61,600美元；这不等于有这么多钱当天易手
据Decrypt援引CryptoQuant，周五（11月27日）在衍生品交易所Deribit到期的比特币期权，名义本金约68亿美元，大约相当于当时该所未到期比特币期权的四分之一。名义本金是按合约对应的比特币数量乘以价格算出来的规模，不是当天真的有这么多现金或比特币交割。Decrypt报道称，这是本月该所最大的一笔到期，但小于今年10月约108亿美元的那一笔。到期结算时间在世界标准时间8:00（上海时间27日16:00）。另有报道称，当天合约结算价约为61,600美元。Decrypt还写道，结算前比特币大约在61,000美元附近，随后在周五晚些时候落到59,000美元下方；这与CoinGecko记录的近24小时低点约58,910美元相符，但不能据此断言“就是期权到期导致了后面的下跌”。Decrypt提到，下一次较大的到期日在12月25日，合约规模按结算价粗算约100亿美元；这只是日历上的事实，不是对那一天涨跌的判断。

4. 以太坊开发者决定按现有方案推进Glamsterdam升级，并定于12月15日在测试网做最后一次公开演习；主网上线仍要等到明年
据CoinDesk报道，以太坊核心开发者在周四（11月26日）的会议上大致达成一致：Glamsterdam这次升级将按现有技术说明继续推进，包括一项有争议的存储费用规则（编号EIP-8037）。这项规则会明显提高在链上“新写下、并长期保存数据”的费用，目的是避免区块能装下更多交易之后，链上存储膨胀过快。代价是：一些按旧费用写成的智能合约，可能在一笔操作做到一半时费用不够用而失败。CoinDesk转述称，开发者估计，全网约9,000万个合约里，最多约1.5万个可能受到影响；安全公司ChainSecurity等已标出约200处具体问题，其中24个需要升级程序，或把用户和资金迁到新合约。最后一次公开测试定于12月15日，在名为Hoodi的测试网上进行。这次公开测试比原计划晚了约七周（10月26日的一次测试此前已取消）。开发者在上周的会议上表示，该升级登陆以太坊主网不会早于明年1月中旬，更可能在1月下旬或2月上旬。在此之前，相关团队还需在12月15日前处理最严重的问题，其余问题的期限是1月10日。上述时间表仍可能调整，以后续官方开发者会议和公告为准。

5. 马来西亚首只符合伊斯兰金融规则的现货比特币ETF，定于12月2日在马来西亚交易所上市；目前尚未开始交易
基金管理公司Halogen Capital在其官方页面公布，Halogen Shariah Bitcoin ETF将于2026年12月2日在马来西亚交易所（Bursa Malaysia）主板上市交易。官方称，这是全球首只符合伊斯兰金融规则（Shariah）的比特币ETF，也是马来西亚交易所的首只数字货币ETF。基金目标是尽量贴近FTSE比特币指数的价格表现，并以现货比特币为主要投资对象；比特币由托管机构BitGo隔离保管，信托人为Universal Trustee (Malaysia) Berhad，伊斯兰教法顾问为Amanie Advisors。交易货币为马来西亚林吉特和美元，股票简称分别为BTCETF-MYR、BTCETF-USD，股票代码分别为0840EA、0840EB。官方写明年管理费最高为基金净值的0.60%，受托人费用最高为0.05%（不含境外托管等费用）。该产品需通过马来西亚交易所的参与券商、用证券账户买卖。官网还挂出了11月27日的电子招募说明书通知。需要分清：上市日期是12月2日，今天还不能交易；它跟踪的是比特币价格，不是保本产品。

数字与进展可能迅速变化，请以官方公告为准。不构成投资建议。

What happens when major whales start reducing their altcoin exposure while liquidity continues to leave the crypto market?

With Bitcoin struggling to hold key support levels and altcoins facing even heavier pressure, I wanted to understand what large investors are actually doing and what their behavior could mean for the next 90 days.

I turned to @SurfAIHQ  to analyze whale activity, stablecoin supply, ETF flows, exchange reserves, derivatives positioning, and historical market patterns.

The findings point to a defensive market environment.

Here are the key takeaways:

• Stablecoin liquidity is shrinking: Total stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2B over 30 days, marking its fastest decline since June 2022. This suggests capital is leaving the crypto ecosystem rather than simply moving into stablecoins.

• Institutional pressure remains strong: Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded $6.05B in net outflows over 30 days, while Ethereum ETFs saw another $1.56B leave during the same period.

• Whales are reducing risk: Smart-money wallets recorded $34M in sales against $27M in purchases over 30 days. Selling activity has recently slowed, but there is still no clear sign of renewed accumulation.

• Leverage has already declined significantly: Bitcoin futures open interest dropped 34% from its peak, while around $2.5B in liquidations occurred during the November 21 selloff.

Surf AI's three scenarios for the next 90 days:

- Bearish: 40% — BTC could revisit the $45K–$55K range.
- Sideways: 42% — BTC could consolidate between $55K and $72K.
- Bullish: 18% — A recovery toward $72K–$85K becomes possible if liquidity returns.

One detail that stood out to me is that coins moving into self-custody does not automatically mean whales are preparing to buy more. Wallet activity alone cannot confirm their intentions.

The most important signal to watch is the 30-day change in stablecoin supply. Until it turns positive and ETF flows begin recovering, the market may remain defensive.

The next major move could depend less on leverage and more on whether fresh capital actually returns to crypto.

11.28梭哈晨报
周五 BTC 刚摸到 6.2 万，70 亿期权到期一巴掌又给拍回 6 万下面了。ETF 还在创纪录地跑路，但链上新钱包创了三个月新高——有人在跑，也有人在偷偷接。

1. $BTC 现在约59,800美元，一天跌了1.1%，在58,792到62,249美元之间晃。周五白天一度冲到62,125美元，结果期权到期，半小时就砸到58,719美元，6万刚站上去又掉了。11月到现在跌了23%，上边先看63,000-64,000美元，下边撑在57,500-58,000美元。
2. $ETH 现在约1,659美元，一天跌1.6%，在1,634到1,755美元之间。11月跌了30%，三巨头里跌得最惨。撑住先看1,634-1,650美元，压力在1,755美元那块。
3. $SOL 现在约71.5美元，一天涨0.7%，在70.12到73.93美元之间，三巨头里就它收红。11月也跌了30%，先看73.9美元能不能冲过去，冲不过去就继续在70美元上下磨。

4. 70亿期权到期砸盘：周五 Deribit 上70亿美元 BTC 期权到期，11.2万张合约，BTC 半小时从62,125美元砸到58,719美元。全市场24小时爆仓4.78亿美元，多头占了2.77亿，BTC 爆仓连续三天超1亿美元。——感恩节涨的那点，全让期权到期吐回去了。
5. 美国现货比特币 ETF 创下史上最惨一个月：11月累计净流出53.9亿美元，破了 ETF 上市以来的月度纪录；18个交易日里16天都在流出，11月23-25日三天就流了12.54亿，贝莱德 IBIT 一家占了45亿。——价格在涨，机构在跑，这反弹看着就不太踏实。
6. 以太坊 ETF 也没好到哪去：11月23-25日三天流出2.175亿美元，是前一周同期2.8倍，三天全是净流出。——两边一起失血，整个市场都在等一个喘口气的理由。
7. 恐惧贪婪指数只有11-12，极度恐惧区躺平；加密总市值约2.10万亿美元，BTC 市占率约58%。——指数都快跌到个位数了，该割的也割得差不多了，剩下的要么是死拿的，要么是真不怕的。
8. 美股感恩节休市，周五只开半天：纳指期货涨近3%、标普涨2%、道指涨1.3%，抄底 AI 股的资金先回来了。纳指周三收23,585.80点，11月跌约7.3%，有望创2008年以来最差11月；纳指100周三盘中一度较10月高点跌20%，短暂进了熊市。——美股这波反弹也是在量很薄的假期里走出来的，别急着当真。
9. 美联储12月加息几乎板上钉钉：CME FedWatch 显示12月9日加息25个基点概率97%-99%，10年期美债收益率约4.87%。——降息别想了，年底这场会就是来加息的。
10. 美国经济数据火上浇油：三季度 GDP 上修至4.3%，远超预期的3.5%；10月核心 PCE 同比3.3%，也高于预期的3.2%。——经济越热，加息越跑不掉，风险资产的日子就越难。
11. 英伟达治理风波还没完：联合创始人周一重回 CEO，标普当天涨4.7%；但周三英伟达盘中一度跌9.1%，收跌3.91%，董事会还在审国家安全问题，周五盘前才反弹约4%。——AI 龙头的椅子还没坐稳，整个 AI 板块都跟着晃。
12. 特朗普政府拟对14个贸易伙伴启动301关税调查，包括台湾。——芯片供应链又添一层不确定性，半导体股刚喘口气又得提心吊胆。
13. 油价冲击卷土重来：布伦特逼近98美元，涨2.07%至96.57美元，WTI 涨1.47%至84.91美元。——油一涨通胀预期就抬头，美联储加息的理由又多一条。
14. 黄金反弹回3,600美元上方，此前一度跌到3,567美元。——避险资金也在找地方躲，黄金和比特币这对老冤家最近走势倒是挺同步。
15. KuCoin 11月30日下架门罗币 XMR：充值已停，提现12月31日截止；XMR 一天跌约11%至450美元。这是本月第二家下架 XMR 的大所，MEXC 本月早些时候已动手；欧盟反洗钱新规2027年7月10日起限制隐私币，灰度则力挺 Zcash。——隐私币的路越走越窄，合规这把刀是真落下来了。
16. 链上出现分化信号：比特币新增非零地址创三个月新高，日均30.69万个，峰值33.32万；持币1,000-10,000枚的大户整个四季度都在悄悄接盘，跟 ETF 赎回对着干。——散户新钱包在进，大户在接，只有 ETF 在跑，这出戏唱得挺分裂。
17. BTC 期货未平仓合约降至2024年10月以来最低，周均283.6亿美元。——杠杆先撤了，场子冷清了，波动反而可能更大。下周看点：11月非农12月4日、美联储会议12月8-9日。

---
收尾总评：说白了，周五就是冲高回落，6万得而复失，期权到期加 ETF 创纪录流血，两头夹击，恐惧指数11还是极度恐惧。不过链上没那么糟——新钱包创三个月新高，大户在接，期货杠杆也撤干净了。反弹是真的，但也是在美股休市、量很薄的时候走出来的，别急着喊反转。下周非农和美联储决议才是硬仗，守住5.75-5.8万是底线，站上6.3-6.4万再说转势。管住手，别追高。

🌒 MARKET STRUCTURE CENSUS — NOV. 27, 2026

The stock market recovered the week by Friday’s 1 PM close. Two of its biggest trades didn’t.

After Monday’s squeeze, Tuesday’s reality check, and Wednesday’s multi-asset low, Black Friday’s shortened session opened +2.9% higher... and this time, buyers stayed.

The Nasdaq-100 held ~94% of its opening gap, led by chips... where all 30 index members closed green.

The Nasdaq ended above Monday’s close. The broader stock market recovered the week.

That was the comeback.

The incomplete part was just as important.

$NVDA remained 8.8% below Monday’s close. $BTC stayed below $60K, even after recovering from its weekly low.

Closing numbers:

- S&P 500 → 7,297.49 (+1.60%, week +5.6%)
- Dow → 50,774.94 (+1.18%)
- Nasdaq → 24,129.50 (+2.31%, week +6.68%)
- $NVDA → $150.49 (+0.80%)
- $ANT → $91.88 (+10.98%)
- 10-year → ~4.9%
- Gold → ~$3,675 (futures, +2.9%)
- $BTC → ~$59.8K
- Brent → $95.44

What the day confirmed:

→ Did the Nasdaq keep more than half its opening jump? Yes... ~94%. Buyers stayed beyond the opening.

→ Did $NVDA hold $150? Yes. It closed at $150.49. Compliance headlines didn’t push it lower.

→ Did $BTC hold $60K with ETFs open? No. It reached $58.7K and recovered to ~$59.8K, but couldn’t reclaim $60K.

→ Did gold hold $3,600? Yes, at the last reading. Forced selling appeared to have paused.

Other developments:

→ November spot-ETF outflows hit a record $5.39B. Bitcoin was the only major asset that didn’t participate in the rally.

→ Jensen Huang’s interviews and Senate hearing appearances are scheduled for Dec. 1–3.

→ Brent gained ~3% on the week ahead of Sunday’s OPEC+ meeting.

The broader market found its footing. $NVDA still has ground to recover, and $BTC still has $60K waiting.

Full weekly breakdown drops in tomorrow’s newsletter🙏🤞.

🚨 BitMart has a $319.5M hole and $1.9M in liquid assets to fill it.

Nikkei Asia reports BitMart told its restructuring adviser, Alvarez & Marsal, that only $1.9M is available to repay users.

The $319.5M shortfall is what BitMart blames mostly on a December 2021 hack, valued at Dec 4, 2021 prices:

- Ethereum: $164.1M
- BNB: $96.5M
- Bitcoin: $51.5M
- Other: $7.4M

Trading stopped Aug 26. Full closure is planned for Jan 31, 2027.

At least 74 users holding about $34M have hired a lawyer. They're fighting BitMart's plan to turn crypto balances into dollar claims, because the user agreement says the customers own the crypto.

Some were drawn in by a 14-day product advertising up to 18.8% annualised yield. Per Nikkei, BitMart kept marketing these products in the weeks before announcing the closure.

BitMart's own plan offers a share of liquid assets, or tokens tied to hack recoveries and future profits.

What happened in markets today:

1. A half day that felt like a full statement. The session closed at 1 p.m. ET after the Thanksgiving break, and buyers did not waste a minute of it. $SPY closed up 1.62%, with the S&P 500 at 7,297.49, up 114.71 points or 1.60%. Thin trade, real conviction, and not a lot of sellers around to argue.

2. The other indexes ran even hotter. $QQQ closed up 2.69%, with the Nasdaq Composite at 24,129.50, up 543.70 points or 2.31%. $DIA closed up 1.26%, with the Dow at 50,774.94, up 591.99 points or 1.18%, a third straight close above 50,000. About four in five S&P 500 stocks rose, so the move was broad, not just a few big names doing the lifting.

3. For the week, the numbers are hard to shrug off. The S&P 500 gained 5.6%, the Dow gained 5.5% and the Nasdaq gained 6.7%. That is the best week in over a year for the market, and the best week since 2022 for the Dow. November still looks rough on the month, and the Nasdaq is still well below its peak, so room to be wrong stays very real here.

4. Chips led the whole tape, and memory led the chips. $SNDK jumped 15.96%, $MU rose 7.60% to $646.95 and $MRVL added 7.34%, with the semiconductor fund up 4.8% on the day. $DELL rose 6.70% as well. After weeks of getting hit first and hardest, the sold off AI hardware names were the ones buyers wanted most. Worth watching whether that bid holds on a full volume Monday.

5. The odd one out was $NVDA, and that tells its own story. Shares slipped close to 3% early, then clawed back to close up just 0.80%. The rest of the AI complex ripped while the biggest name in the trade mostly treaded water. Rotation inside the trade, not out of it, is the read that fits the tape best.

6. Retail had a solid day too, helped by the shopping numbers. $AMZN rose close to 4% as early Black Friday demand came in strong. Thanksgiving online sales hit $8.8 billion in the U.S., up 5.1% from last year, with $37.2 billion worldwide. $WMT added 0.90% as well. A consumer that keeps showing up like that is hard to ignore, even in a nervous market.

7. The bid started overseas. Asia ripped overnight, with mainland shares posting their best day in two years, the CSI 300 up 3.8% and Hong Kong tech up about 6%. That risk on tone rolled straight into the U.S. open and never really faded. Europe held gains as well, and the global mood into the weekend close was calmer than at any point in the last two weeks.

8. Cross assets told a mixed, interesting story. The 10 year Treasury yield rose 9 basis points to 4.94%, and the VIX fell 15.84% to 23.81 as fear drained out fast. Gold rose about 2.2% to near $3,644 an ounce and silver jumped 6.2%, while oil held near its high for the month ahead of the Sunday OPEC+ meeting. $BTC traded near $61,748, up about 1.6%, though U.S. spot bitcoin funds still saw record November outflows of $5.39 billion, so that bid stays fragile.

9. On the data front, the advance goods trade deficit widened to $149.5 billion in October from $135.1 billion in September, well above the $133 billion expected and the widest since March 2025. On deck next: a stacked Tuesday after the close with Marvell and CrowdStrike reporting, then Salesforce and Snowflake on Wednesday, with the Fed in its quiet period ahead of the December 9 meeting. A loud finish to a short week, and a proper test waiting on Monday.

𝟱 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗗 𝗻𝘂𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲, 𝗖𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲𝘅, 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗻𝗼 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗻𝗼 𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗸𝗲𝘆.

Most "AI + DeFi" setups ask you to hand an agent a wallet on day one.

You don't need to.

USDD publishes a skills package with a small, separate analytics server that can only read public data.

It can't sign, can't hold keys, and can't send anything.

It's the right first step, so here's how to set up just that part.

What you're installing: @usdd/usdd-skills (version 1.0.0, MIT licence).

It contains four agent skills plus a local "usdd-analytics" MCP server with 14 read-only tools, all reading the public USDD API.

The write-capable server is a different package (@usdd/mcp-server-usdd), and this tutorial deliberately leaves it out.

1. 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸 𝗡𝗼𝗱𝗲:

Run node -v.

You need version 20 or newer; the package refuses older versions.

2. 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗮𝗴𝗲:

Run npm install -g @usdd/usdd-skills.

That gives you a usdd-skills command.

Heads-up: the docs' one-line "setup" command also installs the write-capable server globally and registers both.

That's fine if you want both later.

For read-only use, register just the analytics server as in step 4.

3. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀:

Run usdd-skills list-tools.

You should see 14 tools, things like get_earn_apy, get_usdd_supply, get_susdd_supply, get_latest_collateral and get_smart_allocator_detail.

If you see fewer, the docs' troubleshooting table covers it.

4. 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲𝗿:

In Claude Code, the docs' command is: claude mcp add -s project usdd-analytics -- usdd-skills mcp-server

In Claude Desktop or Cursor, add a server named usdd-analytics with command usdd-skills and argument mcp-server to your MCP config.

Then fully restart the client.

Tools don't appear until you do.

5. 𝗔𝘀𝗸 𝗮 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

Try the docs' own example: "Which chain has the highest USDD Earn APY today?"

The agent should call get_earn_apy and answer with the per-chain rates (4% on TRON, Ethereum and BNB Chain at the time of writing).

Other good first questions: "How is sUSDD supply split by chain?", "Show TRON collateral for the last month", "What's the Smart Allocator's current APY?"

Prefer a terminal?

The same data is available without any AI client.

From the package folder, node scripts/usdd_api.mjs earn-apy prints JSON.

Run it with no command to see the full list.

𝗧𝘄𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗵 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴:

The answers carry a timestamp field, _meta.dataTime.

The docs are careful to say this is when the package fetched the data, not necessarily when the upstream number was recorded.

If freshness matters, check the source.

The docs also say not to use this output as an oracle or settlement source, and not to build unattended trading or liquidation bots on it.

It's informational data for humans and agents to reason with.

What I like about this design: the read and write paths are separate packages with separate servers, so 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗰𝗮𝗻'𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗴𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮 𝘄𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁. When you're ready to let an agent act, that's a deliberate second install, with its own confirmation rules.

Small request for the team: a published changelog for the skills package (the docs note there isn't one yet) would make upgrades easier to trust.

Read-only tools carry no transaction risk, but anything you later connect to a wallet does; keep that step separate and deliberate.

The full USDD Skills reference: https://t.co/YTkOYQFPgj

🚨 XRP GIẢM 74% TỪ ĐỈNH: CƠ HỘI TÍCH LŨY HAY MỘT CÁI BẪY GIÁ RẺ?

Ripple liên tục mở rộng hợp tác với các ngân hàng, phát triển stablecoin RLUSD, thúc đẩy token hóa tài sản thực và chuẩn bị triển khai dịch vụ cho vay trên XRP Ledger.

Thế nhưng XRP vẫn giao dịch dưới 1 USD.

Điều gì đang xảy ra với một trong những đồng coin lâu đời nhất thị trường?

1. Bức tranh thị trường XRP ngày 28/11/2026

▪️ Giá tham chiếu: 0,95 USD.
▪️ Vốn hóa: khoảng 60,3 tỷ USD.
▪️ FDV: khoảng 95 tỷ USD.
▪️ Xếp hạng vốn hóa: Top 6.
▪️ ATH: 3,65 USD theo CoinGecko.
▪️ Giảm từ ATH: khoảng 74%.
▪️ Tháng 11: giảm 24,57% tính đến hết ngày 26/11.
▪️ Từ đầu năm 2026: giảm 48,75%.
Đến hết ngày 26/11, XRP đã có 13 phiên đóng cửa liên tiếp dưới 1 USD và 7 tuần giảm giá liên tiếp.
Đáng chú ý, XRP cần tăng khoảng 284% từ vùng giá hiện tại mới có thể quay lại ATH.
Giảm sâu không có nghĩa là định giá đã rẻ.

2. XRP thực sự được sử dụng để làm gì?

XRP là tài sản gốc của XRP Ledger (XRPL), blockchain hoạt động từ năm 2012, được xây dựng hướng đến thanh toán, chuyển tiền và trao đổi tài sản.
Các công dụng chính:
• Thanh toán phí giao dịch.
• Làm tài sản trung gian chuyển đổi giữa các loại tiền tệ.
• Cung cấp thanh khoản trên mạng lưới.
• Giao dịch tài sản thông qua DEX và AMM.
• Tham gia các ứng dụng tài chính trên XRPL.

Lợi thế của XRP là tốc độ xử lý nhanh, chi phí thấp, lịch sử hoạt động lâu năm và khả năng tiếp cận các tổ chức tài chính truyền thống.

Tuy nhiên, cần phân biệt rõ Ripple là doanh nghiệp, XRP Ledger là blockchain và XRP là tài sản kỹ thuật số.

Ngân hàng sử dụng sản phẩm của Ripple không nhất thiết phải mua hoặc nắm giữ XRP.

Người sở hữu XRP cũng không có quyền hưởng lợi nhuận hay cổ tức từ Ripple.

Đây là điểm rất nhiều nhà đầu tư đang bỏ qua.

3. Tokenomics: Áp lực nguồn cung vẫn rất lớn

▪️ Nguồn cung tối đa: 100 tỷ XRP.
▪️ Nguồn cung lưu hành theo dữ liệu thị trường: 63,52 tỷ XRP.
▪️ Tỷ lệ lưu hành: 63,52%.
▪️ XRP trong escrow của Ripple: 31,1 tỷ.
▪️ XRP đã bị đốt: khoảng 14,5 triệu.
▪️ Không có hoạt động khai thác tạo thêm XRP mới.
Nguồn cung tối đa đã được tạo ra từ ban đầu. Mỗi giao dịch sẽ đốt một lượng XRP nhỏ, khiến tổng nguồn cung giảm dần.
Tuy nhiên, lượng XRP bị đốt mới chỉ tương đương khoảng 0,0145% nguồn cung ban đầu.
Trong khi đó, hàng trăm triệu XRP có thể rời khỏi escrow mỗi tháng.
Vì vậy, câu chuyện giảm phát của XRP hiện chưa đủ mạnh để cân bằng với lượng token được đưa ra khỏi escrow.

4. Ngày 01/12: 1 tỷ XRP tiếp tục được mở khóa

⏰ Thời gian: 07h00 ngày 01/12/2026 (giờ Việt Nam).

▪️ Khối lượng đủ điều kiện mở khóa: 1 tỷ XRP.
▪️ Giá trị tham chiếu: 950 triệu USD.
▪️ Tương đương 1,57% nguồn cung lưu hành hiện tại.

Trong 12 tháng gần nhất:

• Tổng lượng mở khóa: 12 tỷ XRP.
• Lượng được khóa trở lại: 8,4 tỷ XRP.
• Lượng rời escrow ròng: 3,6 tỷ XRP.

Nếu Ripple tiếp tục duy trì tỷ lệ khóa lại 70%, khoảng 300 triệu XRP sẽ rời escrow trong tháng 12, tương đương 285 triệu USD theo giá hiện tại.

Đợt mở khóa kế tiếp dự kiến vào ngày 01/01/2027, cũng với 1 tỷ XRP.
Cần lưu ý: Mở khóa không phải là bán ra thị trường. XRP rời escrow có thể được sử dụng cho thanh khoản, hoạt động kinh doanh hoặc tiếp tục được nắm giữ.
Dù vậy, nguồn cung tiềm năng vẫn là yếu tố cần theo dõi trong nhiều năm tới.

6. Chất xúc tác lớn nhất: XRP Ledger chuẩn bị triển khai cho vay

Đây có lẽ là thông tin đáng chú ý nhất của XRP trong những ngày gần đây.

Theo dữ liệu được công bố ngày 27/11:

▪️ SingleAssetVault: 29/35 validator ủng hộ.
▪️ LendingProtocol: 28/35 validator ủng hộ.
▪️ Ngưỡng cần thiết: 29/35 validator, duy trì trong 2 tuần.
▪️ SingleAssetVault có thể kích hoạt ngày 09/12 nếu duy trì đủ số phiếu.
Tính năng cho vay sẽ mở rộng XRPL từ mạng lưới thanh toán sang các hoạt động tín dụng trực tiếp trên blockchain.
Người dùng có thể gửi XRP hoặc stablecoin vào các kho tài sản để tài trợ cho hoạt động cho vay và nhận lãi.

Các khoản vay có thể được triển khai mà không cần tài sản thế chấp trực tiếp trên blockchain, dựa trên việc thẩm định người vay của các bên môi giới tín dụng.

Tiềm năng rất lớn, nhưng rủi ro tín dụng cũng không nhỏ.

Nếu người vay mất khả năng thanh toán, người gửi tiền có thể chịu tổn thất.

Ngoài ra, ngày 09/12 mới là mốc dự kiến kích hoạt Vault, chưa phải ngày chắc chắn dịch vụ cho vay đi vào hoạt động.

Nếu LendingProtocol thành công, một phần nguồn vốn stablecoin có thể được đưa vào các hoạt động tạo lợi suất.

8. Ripple đang phát triển mạnh đến đâu?

Ngày 25/11, Ripple công bố ngân hàng Yapı Kredi tại Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ sử dụng giải pháp Ripple Custody, bao gồm phục vụ nền tảng giao dịch tài sản kỹ thuật số.

Ripple đang mở rộng hệ sinh thái theo nhiều hướng:

• Thanh toán xuyên biên giới.
• Lưu ký tài sản số.
• Stablecoin RLUSD.
• Token hóa tài sản thực.
• Dịch vụ tài chính dành cho tổ chức.
• Hạ tầng thanh khoản.

Đây là những bước đi tích cực đối với doanh nghiệp Ripple.
Nhưng để đánh giá tác động đến XRP, tôi muốn nhìn thấy các số liệu cụ thể:
Bao nhiêu XRP thực sự được các ngân hàng sử dụng? Bao nhiêu XRP được giữ làm thanh khoản? Nhu cầu mua XRP có tăng tương ứng với doanh thu của Ripple hay không?
Đó mới là những dữ liệu có thể hỗ trợ định giá token.

15. Góc nhìn của Lý Tiểu Lãi

Tôi đánh giá XRP là một tài sản có câu chuyện phát triển dài hạn đáng theo dõi, đặc biệt ở lĩnh vực thanh toán, token hóa tài sản và tài chính tổ chức.

Nhưng ở mức vốn hóa hơn 60 tỷ USD, XRP không còn là một dự án nhỏ đang chờ được thị trường khám phá.

XRP cần chứng minh rằng sự phát triển của Ripple và XRP Ledger có thể chuyển hóa thành nhu cầu mua, sử dụng và nắm giữ XRP thực tế.

Ba mốc tôi sẽ đặc biệt theo dõi:

📌 Ngày 01/12: Mở khóa 1 tỷ XRP.

📌 Ngày 09/12: Khả năng kích hoạt SingleAssetVault.

📌 Mốc giá 1 USD: Tín hiệu kỹ thuật quan trọng để đánh giá sức mạnh phục hồi.

Tôi quan tâm đến việc XRP tạo ra nhu cầu thực tế như thế nào hơn là những dự đoán giá 10 USD hay 100 USD.

Công nghệ tốt, doanh nghiệp phát triển và token tăng giá là ba câu chuyện có liên quan, nhưng không phải lúc nào cũng diễn ra cùng nhau.

Theo anh em, XRP dưới 1 USD là cơ hội tích lũy cho chu kỳ tiếp theo hay vẫn đang được định giá quá cao so với giá trị mà token thực sự tạo ra?

𝗔 𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗲𝘅𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗘𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘂𝗺 𝗟𝟭 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗱𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝗪𝗕𝗧𝗖 𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴. The feature to care about is the exit door.

On Oct 8, 2026, Derive launched V3, per TokenPost:
▶ Settlement on Ethereum L1
▶ WBTC borrowing
▶ Cross-margin across ETH and BTC positions
▶ Force withdrawals through L1
▶ Not available to US persons

What cross-margin means for a WBTC holder: one account where your WBTC and ETH collateral back all your positions together. Gains on one side can support the other. Losses on one side can also drag the whole account toward liquidation.

What a force withdrawal means: if the exchange's normal path stops working, you can submit your exit on Ethereum L1 yourself. That is a real safety feature, but only if you know how to use it before you need it.

Checklist before you post WBTC as margin anywhere:
➡ Read the margin rules: what haircut applies to WBTC collateral?
➡ Find the liquidation threshold for the whole account, not just one position
➡ Learn the force withdrawal steps and the gas cost on L1
➡ Check if borrowing WBTC has a variable rate and how fast it moves
➡ Confirm you are eligible in your country before depositing

What to watch next: how much WBTC actually gets borrowed on V3, and whether force withdrawals get tested in public.

Takeaway: on any venue, judge it by how you get out, not by how you get in.

ตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐฯ ปิดตลาดวันศุกร์ที่ 27 พฤศจิกายน 2026 ด้วยการปรับตัวขึ้นอย่างแข็งแกร่ง หลังนักลงทุนกลับเข้าซื้อหุ้นเทคโนโลยี หุ้น AI และกลุ่มเซมิคอนดักเตอร์ที่ปรับตัวลงหนักในช่วงหลายสัปดาห์ที่ผ่านมา ส่งผลให้ตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐฯ มีผลงานรายสัปดาห์ดีที่สุดครั้งหนึ่งในรอบหลายเดือน แม้ยังมีความกังวลเรื่องต้นทุนการลงทุน AI หนี้สิน และทิศทางดอกเบี้ยของธนาคารกลางสหรัฐฯ (Fed)

ดัชนี S&P 500 ปรับขึ้น 1.60% ขณะที่ Nasdaq 100 พุ่ง 2.61% และ Dow Jones เพิ่มขึ้น 1.18% ส่วน VIX ซึ่งเป็นดัชนีวัดความผันผวนของตลาด ลดลง 11.16% มาอยู่ที่ 23.81 สะท้อนว่าความกังวลของนักลงทุนเริ่มผ่อนคลายลง

การฟื้นตัวครั้งนี้เกิดขึ้นหลังจากหุ้น AI ถูกเทขายอย่างหนัก โดยมีแรงหนุนจากการกลับมารับตำแหน่ง CEO ของ Jensen Huang ใน Nvidia รวมถึงนักลงทุนที่เข้าซื้อหุ้นซึ่งราคาปรับตัวลงมามาก

ตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐฯ มีเวลาซื้อขายสั้นกว่าปกติในวันศุกร์ เนื่องจากเป็นช่วงวันหยุด Thanksgiving ทำให้สภาพคล่องในตลาดลดลง

หุ้น AI และเทคโนโลยีกลับมาฟื้นตัว

แรงซื้อกระจายไปยังหุ้นเทคโนโลยีหลายกลุ่ม โดยเฉพาะบริษัทที่เกี่ยวข้องกับโครงสร้างพื้นฐาน AI และเซมิคอนดักเตอร์

Nvidia (NVDA) ฟื้นตัวต่อเนื่องตลอดสัปดาห์ หลัง Jensen Huang กลับมาดำรงตำแหน่ง CEO อีกครั้ง อย่างไรก็ตาม หุ้นยังต้องเผชิญความเสี่ยงด้านกฎระเบียบ และการขึ้นให้ข้อมูลต่อคณะกรรมาธิการวุฒิสภาสหรัฐฯ ในวันที่ 3 ธันวาคม

Sandisk (SNDK), Lumentum (LITE) และ Dell (DELL) ปรับตัวขึ้นจากแรงซื้อหุ้นฮาร์ดแวร์และโครงสร้างพื้นฐาน AI ที่ราคาลดลงมามาก

Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Meta (META) และ Oracle (ORCL) ช่วยหนุนการฟื้นตัวของหุ้นเทคโนโลยีโดยรวม

ด้าน Nvidia หุ้นปรับตัวขึ้นประมาณ 20% ตลอดสัปดาห์ แม้ระหว่างทางจะมีความผันผวนสูง

ตัวเลขเศรษฐกิจและปัจจัยที่ต้องจับตา

อีกหนึ่งประเด็นสำคัญคือการขาดดุลการค้าสินค้าของสหรัฐฯ ในเดือนตุลาคม ซึ่งเพิ่มขึ้น 10.7% มาอยู่ที่ 149,500 ล้านดอลลาร์ สูงที่สุดนับตั้งแต่เดือนมีนาคม 2025

อีกเหตุการณ์สำคัญคือ Jensen Huang มีกำหนดขึ้นให้ข้อมูลต่อวุฒิสภาสหรัฐฯ ในวันที่ 3 ธันวาคม ซึ่งอาจสร้างความผันผวนให้กับหุ้น Nvidia และกลุ่ม AI

ตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐฯ จบสัปดาห์ด้วยการฟื้นตัวอย่างแข็งแกร่ง โดย S&P 500 มีโอกาสปิดบวกประมาณ 5% ในรอบสัปดาห์ ขณะที่ Nasdaq 100 เพิ่มขึ้นประมาณ 6% ถือเป็นผลงานรายสัปดาห์ที่ดีที่สุดของ S&P 500 นับตั้งแต่เดือนเมษายน และดีที่สุดของ Nasdaq นับตั้งแต่เดือนสิงหาคม

อย่างไรก็ตาม การดีดตัวครั้งนี้ยังต้องพิสูจน์ว่าจะไปต่อได้หรือไม่ เมื่อกลับเข้าสู่การซื้อขายเต็มรูปแบบและมีสภาพคล่องตามปกติ

สิ่งที่ต้องจับตาคือแรงซื้อหุ้น AI จะต่อเนื่องหรือเป็นเพียงการซื้อคืนหลังราคาปรับตัวลงแรง เพราะความกังวลเรื่องหนี้สินและเงินทุนที่ใช้สร้าง Data Center ยังไม่ได้หมดไป ขณะที่อัตราผลตอบแทนพันธบัตรที่เพิ่มขึ้นและความเสี่ยงเรื่องดอกเบี้ยยังเป็นแรงกดดันต่อหุ้นเติบโต

การฟื้นตัวของตลาดครั้งนี้ช่วยลดแรงกดดันจากการเทขายในช่วงก่อนหน้า แต่ยังเร็วเกินไปที่จะยืนยันว่าตลาดกลับเข้าสู่แนวโน้มขาขึ้น

Even if a rogue actor secretly built a working quantum computer or found an AI shortcut tomorrow, an "overnight" market wipeout still wouldn't be their first move:

• Stealing Quietly Is More Profitable: Draining every wallet at once crashes the token price to $0.00 before the attacker can cash out. A smart attacker would quietly siphon funds from old, dormant wallets a little at a time without alerting the market.

• Nation-State Priorities: Any government or lab that achieves this breakthrough first would target state secrets, military communications, and global financial networks long before exposing their secret weapon on a public cryptocurrency ledger.

But I do find fascinating is the Op_Messages would be left untouched.

If a sudden quantum computing attack hit current blockchains overnight, Ethereum, Bitcoin, stablecoins, and virtually every major cryptocurrency would collapse together because they all rely on the same vulnerable Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) to secure user wallets. 

Using Shor’s algorithm, a quantum attacker could derive private keys from exposed public keys to forge digital signatures, draining active wallets and compromising stablecoin admin keys until ownership became meaningless, economic value dropped to zero, and the networks functionally disintegrated—forcing developers to execute an emergency hard fork rollback and migrate users to quantum-resistant cryptography. 

However, even in a total network collapse, old OP_RETURN messages and historical blockchain records could not be scrubbed by either a conventional hack or a quantum computer because they rely on completely different math. 

While stealing coins only requires forging a new signature today, erasing past OP_RETURN data would require breaking SHA-256 cryptographic hashes—which have no mathematical shortcut for quantum computers—and re-mining every subsequent block faster than the global network while overriding tens of thousands of independent nodes storing local copies of the ledger, which is like trying to secretly edit a scene out of every physical VHS tape and streaming server on Earth and claiming the Mandela Effect.

For example you can look up the Op_Message from one of my eps, actually episode 11 and its verified on the blockchain.

今年币安被盗63亿美金，Bitget被盗3亿多美金。所以我的交易资金是拆开放的：币安55%、Bitget 30%、Backpack 10%、Kraken 5%，哪怕币安直接倒闭了，我起码还有一半资金不受影响。

兄弟们好，我是币哥。

其实很多时候我们相信的这些大交易所也会倒闭。远古的门头沟，前两轮牛市里排名全球前三的FTX，都没扛住，FTX是因为挪用用户资产，几天时间就被挤兑倒闭了。我在加密货币这个圈子待的时间很长了，这期间见了很多交易所出事倒闭，或者因为各种原因跑路，我自己也是靠着仓位控制，在这个圈子一直活到现在。

交易所怎么选、钱怎么分，存下来照做：

1. 本金小于3万美金：现阶段只用币安或者Bitget，比较安全，也足够
2. 本金大约3万美金以上：开始有仓位意识，慢慢多用几个交易所，把资金分散
3. 先把钱分成两块：交易资金、理财存钱的资金
4. 交易资金：币安55%、Bitget 30%、Backpack 10%、Kraken 5%
5. 理财存钱：币安30%、Kraken 30%、冷钱包20%、Bitget 10%、欧易10%
6. 合规交易所挑一两家能用的，从现在开始慢慢养号，我用的是Kraken
7. Kraken用大陆身份证KYC；要地址证明，就交跟身份证地址相同的水电费账单或信用卡账单
8. Kraken本金10万美金以下，不用特别担心流动性
9. Backpack只放很小仓位，5万美金以下只交易 $BTC、$ETH、Solana、Hyperliquid，其他代币不交易
10. 冷钱包只用OneKey和Trezor，放最长期保存的钱

先问一句：你现在的钱放在几家交易所？回个数字。

▌币圈没有存款保险

银行存款不管是国内还是海外，都有存款保险，银行倒闭了多少还能赔点；美国的合规券商也有券商保险。但是目前加密货币交易所没有这一层。

交易所目前最靠谱的，就是有自己的风险准备金，出现被盗、被黑客攻击产生的损失，准备金能赔。这个机制和规则其实很好，但它也有小漏洞，就是赔不赔、赔多少，官方说了算。所以在我自己的安全认知范围内，我的安全靠我自己用仓位去分散单点暴雷的风险，不靠一家交易所来保证。反正我自己是这么做的，之前也一直这样跟兄弟们分享。

肯定有兄弟会问：币安、欧易、Bitget都很赚钱，家大业大，为什么一家保证不了你的安全？原因就两个，倒闭和被盗。

倒闭呢，不管是因为挤兑倒闭、挪用用户资金倒闭，还是被监管清退，只要它倒闭了、里边的钱提不出来，在我眼中你的钱基本上就没了。FTX挪用用户资金，用户挤兑提款，最后倒闭，那些没提走资金的受害用户在破产程序里等了两三年，到现在很多国家的用户都还没拿到自己的钱。这还是大交易所，小交易所根本扛不住一次事故，被挤兑一次就直接破产。

然后我们现在主力使用的，其实都是所谓的离岸交易所，它还有一些政策风险。某个国家、某个地区的市场被清退了，这部分用户就要赶紧把钱提走，变相就是一次挤兑，交易所整体大盘子的资金流动性就会慢慢下降。

被盗这一块，AI的能力越来越强，变相的黑客能力也越来越强。近两年我们陆续看到，Bybit去年被盗15亿美金，Coinbase涉及用户隐私泄露的丑闻，币安今年被盗63亿，Bitget今年被盗3亿多。钓鱼网站、假APP、换脸的视频会议、克隆声音，这些都让攻防不对等：不管是我们自己防诈骗，还是交易所防网络攻击，都要每次都防住；攻击者的成本越来越便宜，成功一次就能赚很多钱。

▌只剩两类交易所

拉长时间去看，可能是三五年，也可能是五到十年，我自己主观上觉得这个市场基本上只会剩下两大类几家交易所：一类是在各国持牌的合规交易所，一类是头部的离岸交易所，其他交易所会慢慢关闭。

合规交易所里能说得上名的，有Coinbase、Robinhood，包括Kraken。全球监管规则越来越清晰，欧洲的MiCA法案全面生效，美国的稳定币法案也通过了，这些规则都天生利好合规交易所。对我们用户来说，合规交易所相对比较安全，出事起码有法律管着，钱要托管在合规银行，美元欧元这些法币出金通道也比较顺畅。而且这三家都是纯血美国交易所，网络黑客攻击的更多是离岸交易所，因为离岸交易所很有钱，手里又没有主权军队。

合规也有代价，手续费贵，流动性不是特别好，种类比较少，KYC、KYT体系特别成熟，起码要实名反洗钱，不少地方它还不提供服务。

头部离岸交易所，在我认知当中基本上就是币安、欧易、Bitget，包括Bybit。监管从之前的打，你不合规我就关闭你、查封你，变成了现在的发牌照模式。币安跟美国达成和解，罚了43亿美金，欧易也达成和解认罚，SEC在25年撤销了对Kraken、币安、Coinbase的各种诉讼。头部离岸交易所的优点很明显，手续费便宜，盘口流动性好，交易对多，产品花样多，对我们大陆用户来说还有人民币的法币C2C出入金。

但拉长时间看，我觉得离岸交易所到头来可能只剩一两家或两三家。做合规拿牌照的成本非常非常高；新用户增长差不多到头了，获取用户的成本也非常高；AI让网络进攻的手段更多样，防守难度变高，运营成本也变高，哪怕被盗一次，也基本上是一两年白干。赚钱赚得越来越少，花钱的地方越来越多，这生意赚不了那么多钱了，不赚钱了就关了它。

▌我用的这5家

我的策略很简单。合规交易所里挑一两家我能用的，从现在开始长期养号，用人话来说就是让人家挣点钱，不管是交易手续费，还是理财的利息抽成。离岸交易所里，挑我自己认为最可能活下来的那几家都去用，不all in只用一个。另外还有冷钱包，我只用OneKey和Trezor，因为这两个都是百分之百开源的，其他冷钱包我只会去玩，不会放钱😂

币安在离岸加密货币交易所里是绝对的头部，体量最大，最安全，出事人家也赔得起，流动性是币圈独一档的存在，其他交易所都只能排在第二档。手续费不是最便宜，但是适中，在我自己的体感下就是不贵了。缺点是理财收益一般。如果你是新手，现阶段只选币安没问题。

Bitget的盘口流动性在第二档里属于比较好的，手续费在我用过的头部交易所里算低的，股票代币RWA Token的可玩性真的很高。所以目前我主要的交易场所，就是币安加Bitget的组合。

欧易是老牌交易所，我自己也在用，但目前不在上面做交易，只用它做理财、分散风险，包括用它的人民币出入金。

Kraken是美国的合规交易所集团，有全套的清结算，包括银行的支付牌照。最重要的是，它能让我们中国大陆用户直接使用，用大陆身份证就能KYC，不用提交海外的地址证明，因为用了海外地址证明，税务上可能会有大坑。Kraken在合规交易所里手续费是不高的。缺点是流动性真的一般，没办法跟币安、欧易、Bitget比，但本金10万美金以下不用特别担心；另外产品交互一般，毕竟是老外开发的，下单和平仓逻辑需要一些学习门槛。

Backpack是合规持牌的新势力，最近拿到了美国清结算的三块牌照，还收购了FTX的欧洲业务。它的全局统一保证金模式我非常喜欢，美股数据看板我平常也喜欢用来看美股数据，哪怕我不用它交易美股。但缺点很明显，它现阶段还很小，流动性也一般，5万美金以下交易比特币、以太坊、Solana、Hyperliquid基本上不用担心特别大的滑点，其他代币就不用交易了。所以我真的只敢放很小很小的仓位。

▌不用Coinbase和Bybit的原因

Coinbase不支持中国大陆地区使用，想用的话，必须用大陆护照加香港的地址证明才能注册，使用的时候还一定要用对应香港的IP，用其他地方的IP还有可能被封号。这个操作路径非常麻烦，而且大陆护照加香港地址证明这套组合，未来税务上一定有大坑。

Bybit之前我也用，但现在不用了。自从Bybit被盗之后，我自己的真实使用体感，包括他们的运营策略给我的感觉，就是非常不舒服：乱封号，乱冻结资金，顾头不顾尾，被盗之后动作明显变形了，所以对我来说尽可能远离。其他小交易所，目前我也是一个都不用。

▌3万美金这条线

很多兄弟会问：我刚入门，资金还不多，需不需要用这么多交易所？先强调一下，这个很主观。我认为本金大约3万美金以上，就要有仓位意识，慢慢多用几个交易所体验尝试，把资金分散一下，毕竟3万美金对大多数人来说不是一笔小钱，别因为这种事一下归零，对吧。如果本金小于3万美金，在现阶段，或者说最少一两年，我觉得只用币安或者Bitget还是比较安全，而且是足够的。

你现在的钱分在几家交易所？评论区回个数字，1家也直接回1。

以上只是我个人的选择和仓位，各平台规则以官方当前页面为准。

🚨 HYPE ĐƯỢC FRANKLIN TEMPLETON ĐƯA VÀO ETF, NHƯNG HƠN 600 TRIỆU USD TOKEN SẮP MỞ KHÓA: CƠ HỘI HAY BẪY TĂNG GIÁ?

HYPE đang trở thành một trong những altcoin đáng chú ý nhất cuối tháng 11.

Trong khi nhiều đồng coin vẫn vật lộn tìm đáy, Hyperliquid có ba thông tin khiến tôi đặc biệt quan tâm:

🟢 Franklin Templeton dự kiến bổ sung HYPE vào ETF chỉ số từ ngày 01/12.

🟢 Hyperliquid tạo khoảng 80,3 triệu USD doanh thu trong 30 ngày, gắn với cơ chế mua lại HYPE.

🔴 Tokenomist dự phóng 9,92 triệu HYPE có thể được mở khóa ngày 06/12, trị giá khoảng 632 triệu USD theo giá tham chiếu.

Câu hỏi lớn nhất: lực mua từ ETF và doanh thu giao thức có đủ hấp thụ nguồn cung mới?

Cùng Lý Tiểu Lãi phân tích. 👇

1. FRANKLIN TEMPLETON ETF: TIN TỐT NHƯNG ĐỪNG HIỂU NHẦM

Theo hồ sơ bổ sung gửi SEC ngày 25/11, Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) dự kiến bổ sung HYPE vào danh mục khoảng ngày 01/12.

HYPE sẽ nằm cùng BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL và một số tài sản khác.

Đây không phải ETF HYPE độc lập, cũng không có nghĩa hàng tỷ USD lập tức chảy vào token.

Dòng tiền mua thực tế phụ thuộc quy mô ETF và tỷ trọng HYPE trong chỉ số.

Dù vậy, đây vẫn là một bước tiến về khả năng tiếp cận thị trường tổ chức.

2. HYPERLIQUID ĐANG TẠO RA BAO NHIÊU TIỀN?

Dữ liệu gần nhất:

Doanh thu 30 ngày: 80,3 triệu USD.
Doanh thu 12 tháng: 681,6 triệu USD.
Phí giao dịch 30 ngày: 105 triệu USD.
Giá trị mua lại HYPE 30 ngày: khoảng 80,3 triệu USD.
Khối lượng giao dịch 24 giờ trên Hyperliquid: khoảng 9,18 tỷ USD.

Điều khác biệt của Hyperliquid là nguồn thu gắn trực tiếp với hoạt động giao dịch trên nền tảng.

Phần lớn phí đủ điều kiện được chuyển vào Assistance Fund để mua HYPE.

Khi khối lượng giao dịch tăng, hoạt động mua lại có thể tăng theo.

Nhưng nếu người dùng giao dịch ít đi, nguồn doanh thu cũng suy yếu.

Đây không phải mô hình bảo đảm giá token luôn tăng.

3. TOKENOMICS: NGUỒN CUNG GIẢM NHƯNG ÁP LỰC UNLOCK VẪN CÒN

HYPE được thiết kế với nguồn cung ban đầu 1 tỷ token.

Phân bổ gồm:

38,89% dành cho phát hành và phần thưởng cộng đồng tương lai.
31% phân phối ban đầu.
23,8% cho đội ngũ đóng góp.
6% cho Hyper Foundation.
Phần còn lại dành cho các mục đích khác.

Sau quá trình mua lại và ghi nhận đốt token, nguồn cung tối đa điều chỉnh đã giảm xuống khoảng 949 triệu HYPE theo CoinGlass.

Tuy nhiên, điều đó không loại bỏ áp lực từ các token chưa phân phối.

4. UNLOCK NGÀY 06/12: ĐÂY MỚI LÀ THỬ THÁCH LỚN

Tokenomist dự phóng 9,92 triệu HYPE sẽ được mở khóa cho Core Contributors.

Theo giá khoảng 63,69 USD, quy mô tương đương 632 triệu USD.

Blockworks có mô hình thấp hơn, khoảng 8,60 triệu HYPE.

Đáng lưu ý: đây là ước tính theo lịch phân phối, không phải số lượng chắc chắn sẽ được chuyển ra thị trường.

Việc mở khóa cũng không có nghĩa toàn bộ token sẽ lập tức bị bán.

Nhưng tôi cho rằng đây là yếu tố cần theo dõi sát hơn cả tin ETF.

Chỉ cần một phần token phân phối được bán ra cũng có thể tạo áp lực khi thanh khoản suy yếu.

5. PHÁI SINH: DÒNG TIỀN ĐẦU CƠ ĐANG QUAY LẠI

Số liệu HYPE gần nhất:

Giá: 63,69 USD.
OI: khoảng 2,64 tỷ USD.
OI tăng 3,4% trong 24 giờ.
Futures volume: khoảng 2,29 tỷ USD.
Spot volume: khoảng 215 triệu USD.
Funding có trọng số OI: +0,0024%.

Khối lượng phái sinh lớn gấp hơn 10 lần giao ngay.

Điều này phản ánh thị trường HYPE đang có sự tham gia mạnh của các vị thế sử dụng đòn bẩy.

Tuy nhiên, funding vẫn dương nhẹ, chưa cho thấy tình trạng quá hưng phấn rõ rệt.

Tôi sẽ theo dõi xem giá tăng tiếp nhờ lực mua spot hay chủ yếu do các vị thế Short bị đóng.

6. NHỮNG VÙNG GIÁ HYPE CẦN THEO DÕI

🟢 60–62 USD: Hỗ trợ gần.

🟡 66–67 USD: Kháng cự sát giá hiện tại.

🔴 68–70 USD: Vùng kiểm tra phục hồi.

🔴 75–80 USD: Kháng cự mở rộng nếu dòng tiền tích cực.

⚠️ 56–58 USD: Hỗ trợ sâu hơn nếu mất mốc 60 USD.

Đây là những vùng phân tích kịch bản, không phải mức giá chắc chắn sẽ chạm tới.

7. BA KỊCH BẢN CHO HYPE

📈 TÍCH CỰC

HYPE giữ 60–62 USD, vượt 67 USD với lực mua spot cải thiện và tiến tới thử thách 70–75 USD.

➡️ TRUNG LẬP

Giá dao động 60–67 USD trong lúc thị trường chờ việc ETF tái cơ cấu và xác nhận lượng unlock.

📉 TIÊU CỰC

8. HYPE CÓ ĐẮT KHÔNG?

Yutori can open a new speculative vertical by turning Hyperliquid’s deep, 24/7 perps (crypto + HIP-3 stocks, indices, gold, oil) into retail-friendly, defined-risk directional bets that behave like options without requiring a full options order book or the constant wick/liquidation risk of raw leverage.

Traders set a max loss (budget) that doubles as premium and hard floor; the engine dynamically holds the perp at the option’s live delta so the position grows when right and shrinks when wrong, auto-closing at the floor. This gives convexity and “room for conviction” on the same account that already has the best on-chain perp liquidity, while keeping funds non-custodial.

The speculative kicker is the $YTR layer: it is burned as engine fuel, staked for Hard Floor gap coverage and tighter pricing/higher size, and supported by continuous buybacks from builder fees plus HYPE rewards to stakers. Volume on the product therefore creates structural token demand and burn, while the product itself feeds Hyperliquid volume. If the engine holds up in live conditions and traders adopt the defined-risk format, it becomes both a new trading primitive and a self-reinforcing token narrative on top of the fastest-growing derivatives venue in crypto.

BITCOIN WHALES ARE HEAVILY SHORT BUT A SHORT SQUEEZE COULD BE BREWING.

The battle around $BTC is getting increasingly intense.

Bitcoin reversed from approximately $62,000 today, triggering a sharp sell-off within minutes. Meanwhile, derivatives positioning is revealing an interesting imbalance: whales are leaning heavily toward the short side.

Here's what you need to understand. 👇

1️⃣ Whales Are Crowding Into Shorts

Data from Hyperliquid trackers indicates that approximately 54%–58% of whale positioning is currently net short.

This suggests that large traders are increasingly betting on further downside.

However, heavily crowded short positions can create an interesting situation: if Bitcoin moves unexpectedly higher, short sellers may be forced to close their positions by buying back BTC, potentially accelerating an upward move.

That's how a short squeeze develops.

But remember, crowded shorts do not automatically mean a reversal is coming.

2️⃣ A $150M Leveraged Long Faces Pressure

One massive Bitcoin long position, reportedly carrying approximately $150 million in exposure at 40x leverage, saw its position reduced by 1,440 BTC as the market declined.

Its reported liquidation level was around $59,700.

This highlights just how dangerous excessive leverage can become.

At 40x leverage, a relatively small adverse price movement can put a trader dangerously close to liquidation. Even a move of approximately 2.5% against the position can consume the initial margin before accounting for fees and maintenance margin.

The lesson? Position sizing and risk management matter more than chasing massive leverage.

3️⃣ The Liquidation Imbalance Is Worth Watching

CryptoQuant data reportedly indicates approximately $16 billion in potential short liquidations between $60,000 and $100,000, compared with less than $5 billion in potential long liquidations.

If accurate, this suggests that a significant amount of short-side exposure could be vulnerable to an upward price movement.

However, liquidation heatmaps and estimated liquidation levels are not guaranteed future market orders. They represent potential liquidity zones, not certainty.

4️⃣ The $62K Battle: What Comes Next?

Bitcoin's ability to reclaim the $62,000 region could become an important signal for market participants.

- Bullish scenario: BTC reclaims $62K and establishes support above it. This could weaken bearish momentum and potentially trigger short covering.
- Bearish scenario: BTC continues struggling below $62K and loses its recent lows. That could strengthen the case for further downside.

The market needs confirmation, not assumptions.

MY TAKE:

Bitcoin is entering an interesting derivatives environment.

When whales are heavily short, leveraged longs are under pressure, and potential liquidation clusters are building, volatility can increase dramatically in either direction.

The biggest mistake traders can make right now is assuming that the majority must be correct.

Markets have a way of punishing excessive confidence on both sides.

Watch the key levels. Respect leverage. Manage risk.

The next major move in $BTC could catch an awful lot of traders off guard.

Prepared around 3:45 PM EST on Friday 27 November, after the US Black Friday half session. This is the full crypto wrap of the day, picking up from this morning's First Hour, prepared at 10:40 AM EST, and only adding what happened since. US stocks closed at 1:00 PM EST and those are final closes. Bonds closed at 2:00 PM EST. Crude and gold are settlement prices, and the dollar index is a live print as of about 3:46 PM EST. Crypto prices are live prints as of about 3:45 PM EST, not closes. I checked the spot ETF flow tables at about 3:45 PM EST and there is no 27 November print yet for any Bitcoin, Ether or Solana fund, so tonight's number is still to come.

1⃣ An AI-era elliptic-curve paper and a "Will Bitcoin inevitably go to zero?" essay put the cryptography question back on the tape

At 12:11 PM EST, Ledger's Charles Guillemet flagged a new paper claiming a fully deterministic subexponential algorithm for discrete logarithms, on elliptic curves and in finite fields. He called it "a very small crack", said it relies on an OpenAI construction that is still under review, and concluded: "Impact on real-world ECC: exactly zero." Blockstream's Adam Back said the method only beats Pollard's rho, today's best general attack, at elliptic-curve key sizes of about 66,000 bits, is about a million times slower than that attack at Bitcoin's 256-bit size, and would need memory equal to about 3,000 times the mass of the solar system. At 2:36 PM EST, investor Chamath Palihapitiya published an essay titled "Will Bitcoin inevitably go to zero?", repeating his view that crypto and Bitcoin are "capped" because AI agents are now settling long-standing maths problems far faster than security designers assumed. Michael Saylor answered at 3:16 PM EST that Bitcoin is "an economic protocol", that if AI breaks encryption "all digital commerce is at risk", and that "the solution is an upgrade to next generation encryption." Back replied to Palihapitiya at 3:37 PM EST: "AI is not magic." A crypto research and brokerage firm said in a note this morning that recent breakthroughs have not shown any compromise of Bitcoin's cryptography, but that AI's progress in mathematics deserves closer attention.

🖊️ Market significance: There is no exploit and no affected wallet, but a high-profile investor telling holders the asset may go to zero is now part of the market narrative, on top of the quantum worries the Bank of England raised on Thursday.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The maths, as the cryptographers read it, is a theoretical result that is useless at real key sizes. The narrative is the part I'd take seriously. Each "small crack" story raises the pressure on Bitcoin to agree a signature migration path, and Bitcoin's governance is slow by design. I'm watching whether developers turn this week's debate into a concrete proposal, because a credible plan matters more to long-term holders than any single paper.

2⃣ OKX Europe went down during the morning flush and was back up at 12:07 PM EST

Users began reporting that OKX's app and website were unavailable at about 9:55 AM EST, in the middle of the 9:40 to 10:05 AM EST leg that took Bitcoin to $58,700. OKX Europe chief executive Erald Ghoos said at 10:33 AM EST that some customers were having trouble accessing OKX Europe and that the team was investigating. At 11:19 AM EST the support desk told one user it was aware that some customers could not close positions. Ghoos said at 11:35 AM EST that "customer funds are safe" and services were coming back, and at 12:07 PM EST that OKX Europe services were "back up and running". No breach or loss has been reported, and rumours of a hack that spread on social media were not confirmed by the exchange.

🖊️ Market significance: A MiCA-licensed venue was unreachable for about two hours while the market was falling, so some European traders could not manage stops, margin or open positions.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Outages during fast markets are the oldest complaint in crypto, and this one hit the regulated European arm, not an offshore venue. I'd watch for compensation claims and for how the exchange handles orders filled during the outage. For price, it means part of this morning's drop came on a thinner book than usual, which is one more reason I'm treating $58,700 as a liquidity low rather than a clean test of support.

3⃣ Russia's VTB opened Bitcoin trading in its brokerage app, and exchange trading is set for 1 December

VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell Bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every crypto buyer must pass. Trading is over the counter for now and limited to qualified investors who pass the test, and VTB holds the coins itself in a separate digital depository account on Russian infrastructure. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. Non-qualified investors will only be able to buy Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, up to 300,000 roubles a year through a single intermediary. Exchange spot trading in Bitcoin, Ether and USDT is set to start on 1 December.

🖊️ Market significance: One of Russia's largest banks is now a live, regulated on-ramp, which moves Russian demand from grey-market desks onto supervised rails.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This morning I treated the test as a gate that would make the venue start slow. The gate is now open on day one, and that speed is the news. The size will be small at first under the caps, but a state-linked bank holding the coins itself is a model other emerging markets will copy.

4⃣ A new stablecoin study set the bar for a lasting recovery, as $250 million of USDC was minted this afternoon

An on-chain analytics firm found that Bitcoin has closed at a record high 39 times since 2022 and none came while USDT supply was shrinking. Over 60-day periods, Bitcoin fell about 9.5% on average when USDT supply contracted and rose about 7.6% when it grew. It also found that about $2.8 billion of the USDT Binance sent back to Tether on Ethereum was reissued on Tron within two hours, so part of the drop was a chain switch rather than money leaving. It is watching three signals: 60-day USDT growth turning positive, the Ethereum decline stopping, and more USDT leaving Tether's treasury than returning. This afternoon, $250 million of USDC was minted at 2:26 PM EST, Tether's treasury sent $200 million of USDT to Binance at 2:18 PM EST, and Aave V4's Core Hub on Ethereum passed $100 million of USDC deposits. Total USDT supply sits near $173.6 billion to $173.9 billion.

🖊️ Market significance: The test for a durable bottom is now explicit: stablecoin supply has to start growing again, and one afternoon of mints is not that.

🗨️ My viewpoint: I like that this study separates the Tron switch from real outflows, because it shows the contraction is somewhat smaller than the headline. Still, the level I care about is the 60-day USDT trend, and that is still negative. A $250 million USDC mint on a holiday is a good sign, and I'd want to see it repeated for a week before calling it a turn.

5⃣ Gemini and the Winklevoss twins face a proposed class action that calls Gemini Predictions an unlicensed sportsbook

A New York user, Rayath Chowdhury, filed a proposed nationwide class action in the Southern District of New York on 25 November against Gemini entities, Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss and Winklevoss Capital Fund. The complaint says Gemini Predictions runs sports event contracts as an unlicensed betting business under state gambling laws, that users could fund bets with crypto held in their Gemini accounts without the deposit limits licensed sportsbooks apply, and that he began losing money in May 2026. It seeks the return of lost wagers, damages, an injunction and a jury trial.

🖊️ Market significance: Private plaintiffs are now joining state regulators in attacking sports event contracts, which puts the legal risk directly on the exchanges and their founders.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A class action is a different threat from a cease-and-desist letter, because it asks for money back. Sports contracts drive most prediction-market volume, so if this theory survives a motion to dismiss, every venue offering them gets the same bill. It also explains why the leaders are pushing into non-sports uses like the small-business contracts I covered this morning.

6⃣ The UAE sold its first dirham digital sovereign bonds, and Injective asked the SEC to let order books trade tokenized stocks

The UAE Ministry of Finance said it has issued its first dirham-denominated digital sovereign treasury bonds: AED 180 million, about $49 million, of two-year paper at a 4.98% yield, the same as its conventional November auction. Issuance and settlement ran on Euroclear's digital market infrastructure, six primary dealers took equal shares and the bonds list on Nasdaq Dubai. Separately, Injective Labs asked the SEC, in a 23 November comment letter that came to light on Friday, to widen the tokenized-stock innovation exemption from automated liquidity pools to permissioned on-chain order books. It offered extra safeguards: surveillance, self-trade prevention, standard price increments, price-band limits and protocol-enforced halts.

🖊️ Market significance: A sovereign issuer pricing a digital bond flat to its conventional curve shows tokenized debt no longer needs a discount, and the SEC's exemption design is deciding which kind of on-chain venue gets to trade US stocks.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The UAE deal is small, but a sovereign issue with no yield penalty is the benchmark tokenized debt has been missing. Injective's letter matters more for crypto structure: if the exemption stays pool-only, it favours AMM designs over order-book chains. I'd treat the SEC's answer as a quiet but real driver of which ecosystems capture tokenized equity volume.

7⃣ Beijing set 1 March 2027 for blockchain digital ID rules, and Argentina's central bank leaned on USDT trading

China published rules on Friday for blockchain-based digital identities, issued by 11 government departments including the People's Bank of China and the Cyberspace Administration of China, taking effect on 1 March 2027. The national blockchain network will provide the infrastructure, providers must collect only the data needed for verification, cross-platform profiling and targeted advertising are banned, and the rules encourage links with the digital yuan, while crypto trading stays restricted on the mainland. In Argentina, industry executives said the central bank made informal recommendations to some wallets and platforms about trades linking the MEP dollar and USDT, though they said trading continued as usual.

🖊️ Market significance: Beijing is building state blockchain rails tied to the digital yuan, and Buenos Aires is testing how far it can steer dollar-stablecoin flows without a formal rule.

🗨️ My viewpoint: China's message is consistent: blockchain yes, open crypto no, and identity tied to the central bank's own money. Argentina is the one I'd watch for market impact, because USDT is a core dollar channel there. Informal pressure usually comes before formal limits, so I'd watch local USDT premiums for the first sign of friction.

8⃣ Monero dipped under $400 before Monday's KuCoin cutoff, while Zcash rose and published its post-quantum roadmap

Monero traded under $400 on Friday and sits near $401, about 9% to 10% lower on the day. KuCoin closes its four XMR spot markets at 3:00 AM EST on Monday, and those markets handled about 58% of tracked Monero volume in the 24 hours to Friday morning. Zcash went the other way, up about 3% near $740, as Shielded Labs published the first technical update on Epoch, its planned post-quantum shielded pool for Zcash, which aims for throughput comparable to Project Tachyon.

🖊️ Market significance: Liquidity in the main privacy coin is being cut venue by venue, while its closest rival is pitching itself on quantum safety on the day cryptography fears are trending.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Losing the venue that carries more than half the volume is a structural hit, not a sentiment wobble, and I'd expect wider spreads and sharper wicks in XMR after Monday. Zcash's timing is good marketing, but a research update is not a shipped pool. I'm watching whether XMR holds $400 into the cutoff.

9⃣ Utexo postponed Saturday's launch of native USDT on Bitcoin

Utexo, a Bitcoin settlement layer built on the RGB protocol, postponed the 28 November mainnet launch of Utexo Mint, its service for issuing and settling USDT natively on Bitcoin. It said it wants its main wallet and exchange partners to finish their integrations so users can reach the stablecoin from day one. No new date was given, and early access on Bitcoin's Signet test network, open since October, stays available.

🖊️ Market significance: Bringing USDT back to Bitcoin itself, rather than on side chains, is still a promise, not a product.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Delaying for integrations is the right call, because a stablecoin no exchange supports would launch dead. Still, I'd wait for a dated launch with named exchange partners before treating this as new demand for Bitcoin block space.

🔟 Bitcoin went 98 minutes without a block on Thursday, and blocks are running slow after Friday's 7.61% difficulty jump

The network went 98 minutes and 19 seconds between block 977,697 at 11:49 AM EST on Thursday and block 977,698 at 1:28 PM EST, the longest gap since July. Since the 7.61% difficulty increase at 12:17 AM EST on Friday, 90 blocks have arrived in about 15 and a half hours, an average of about 10.3 minutes against the 10-minute target. That suggests hashrate is running a little below what the new difficulty assumes, although the period is far too early for a reliable forecast.

🖊️ Market significance: Miners just absorbed a near 8% cost increase at a Bitcoin price near $60,000, and slower blocks are the first sign some machines are being switched off.

🗨️ My viewpoint: One long gap is statistical bad luck. A run of slow blocks right after a big difficulty jump is economics. I'm watching for miners sending coins to exchanges over the weekend, because squeezed operators sell into weakness, and that is supply the market does not need near $58,525.

1⃣1⃣ Leverage did not chase the bounce: funding stayed near flat and open interest barely moved

Bitcoin perpetual funding is close to zero on two major venues, about 1.5% annualised on Hyperliquid and about 0.0013% per eight hours on OKX. Ether funding is slightly negative on OKX. Bitcoin open interest is about 35,370 BTC on Hyperliquid, down about 1.7% since around 10:30 AM EST, and about 32,390 BTC on OKX, up about 0.6%. Ether open interest rose about 2.9% on Hyperliquid and fell about 1.4% on OKX over the same window.

🖊️ Market significance: After this morning's long flush, traders neither rebuilt longs nor piled into shorts, so neither side has fresh fuel for a squeeze into the weekend.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Flat funding after a 4% flush is healthy, because it means the bounce was spot and short covering, not new leverage. It also means there is no crowded short to squeeze through $60,000. For that I need spot buyers, which brings me back to stablecoin supply and tonight's ETF print.

1⃣2⃣ Bitcoin was capped under $60,000 all afternoon, and Galaxy now names $58,525 as the line

Since First Hour, Bitcoin bounced to $60,467 at 11:30 AM EST, with a second venue at $60,500, then faded to $59,434 at 12:45 PM EST, with the second venue at $59,454. It failed just below $60,000 twice, at $59,988 at 12:05 PM EST and $59,979 at 2:40 PM EST, with a second venue at $59,999 and $59,993, and its afternoon low was $59,630 at 3:10 PM EST. It trades near $59,760, about 1.6% lower over 24 hours. The session low is still $58,700 from 10:05 AM EST, so June's $58,525 closing low was never traded through. This week opened at about $61,165, so Bitcoin is on course for an eighth straight weekly loss unless it closes above that level on Sunday at 7:00 PM EST. Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that the bear market ended in June, saying the signal failed and that the bear market is "very likely not over", and it now treats a daily close below $58,525 as the line to watch.

🖊️ Market significance: The morning wick held above June's closing low, but the afternoon could not get back above $60,000, so the session ended in a range between the two.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The level I care about is still $58,525, and it was not tested this afternoon. What I didn't get was the 4-hour close above $60,020 that I said would make this morning a liquidation wick. Two failures just under $60,000 make that the line to beat, and the weekly open at $61,165 is the line for the weekly candle.

1⃣3⃣ Ether stalled at its breakdown shelf, and the ratio stayed under 0.028

Ether bounced to $1,686.36 at 11:30 AM EST, with a second venue at $1,685.50, right into the $1,681 to $1,685 shelf it lost this morning, and turned lower. It hit $1,655 at 12:45 PM EST, traded between $1,662 and $1,674 through the afternoon and is near $1,665, about 2.2% lower over 24 hours and about 3.3% below this week's open near $1,722. The ether to bitcoin ratio is near 0.0279. Solana is near $72, up about 1% on the day, and XRP near $0.950, little changed.

🖊️ Market significance: The old support turned into resistance on the first retest, which confirms this morning's breakdown for now.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The level I care about for Ether is $1,632, today's low, with $1,606 below it. A 4-hour close back above $1,686 would cancel this morning's damage. Until then, I see Ether as the weaker of the two majors, and Solana holding $70 while Ether slipped is the one relative bright spot.

1⃣4⃣ US stocks closed their best week since April 2025, and crypto stocks beat the coins

At the 1:00 PM EST close, the S&P 500 rose 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq Composite 2.31% to 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.18%, or 591.99 points, to 50,774.94. For the week, the S&P 500 gained about 5.6%, its best week since April 2025, led by a rebound in AI and chip stocks. Coinbase closed up 3.20% at $107.04 and Strategy up 2.08% at $81.62, even as Bitcoin fell on the day.

🖊️ Market significance: Equities did everything crypto bulls wanted this week, and Bitcoin still lagged, which points to crypto's own selling rather than macro risk-off.

🗨️ My viewpoint: When stocks have their best week in more than a year and Bitcoin can't hold $60,000, I read it as an asset-specific problem: ETF outflows, shrinking stablecoins and leverage clean-up. Crypto stocks rising on a down day for Bitcoin tells me equity buyers are bargain-hunting the beaten-down names, not the coins.

1⃣5⃣ The 10-year rose to about 4.93%, the dollar index firmed to about 104.05, gold settled up about 3% and WTI slipped

The 10-year Treasury yield ended about 9 basis points higher near 4.93% to 4.94% at the 2:00 PM EST bond close, and the 2-year was near 4.70% to 4.71%, both above Wednesday's closes. The dollar index is near 104.04 to 104.05, up about 0.4%, a live print. Gold for December settled up about $108, or about 3%, at about $3,644. WTI crude for January settled at $83.33, down 35 cents, after reversing from an overnight high.

🖊️ Market significance: Yields and the dollar rose together while stocks rallied, so financial conditions tightened a little even on a risk-on day.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The 10-year at about 4.93% is the warning level I flagged on Thursday, and it got there on the first day back. A firmer dollar near 104 and a 3% gold jump while Bitcoin fell tell me hedging demand is going to gold, not to Bitcoin, right now.

1⃣6⃣ Next up: tonight's ETF print, Bangkok, OPEC+, the weekly close and Monday's Monero cutoff

The spot ETF flow print for Friday's short session lands this evening, after Wednesday's $453 million Bitcoin outflow, the seventh straight day of outflows. Binance Blockchain Week opens in Bangkok on Saturday, OPEC+ meets on Sunday, and Bitcoin's weekly candle closes at 7:00 PM EST on Sunday. KuCoin removes its Monero markets at 3:00 AM EST on Monday, LayerZero's Zero chain launches on 30 November, Russia's exchange crypto trading starts on 1 December and Malaysia's first spot Bitcoin ETF lists on 2 December. US November payrolls follow next Friday, and Monday is the last session of the month.

🖊️ Market significance: The weekend has two scheduled events that can move crypto, Bangkok and OPEC+, and a weekly close that decides whether the losing streak reaches eight weeks.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Tonight's ETF print is the first real read on demand since Wednesday. A day of inflows would be the first good flow news in more than a week. Another outflow on a half session would confirm that the bid this week came from short covering, not new money.

🗨️ My Overall Viewpoint

For the overnight and weekend session, my Bitcoin pivot is $59,700 to $60,000, where price sits now under the afternoon ceiling. Support is $59,630, this afternoon's low, then $59,434 to $59,454, the 12:45 PM EST low and the level I care about most overnight, $59,075, the first low after the morning bottom, $58,700, today's session low, $58,525, June's closing low and Galaxy's line, $57,208, Wednesday's low, and about $55,100, the cycle low. Resistance is $59,980 to $60,000, where price failed twice this afternoon, then $60,467 to $60,500, the 11:30 AM EST bounce high, $61,165 to $61,350, this week's open and the pre-bell shelf, and $62,140, the overnight high. For Ether, the level I care about is $1,632, today's low. Support is $1,661, this afternoon's low, then $1,655, $1,640, $1,632, $1,606 and $1,579. Resistance is $1,674, this afternoon's high, then $1,681 to $1,686, the breakdown shelf and today's bounce high, $1,710, $1,722, this week's open, and $1,753. I'm neutral while Bitcoin holds $59,434 and Ether holds $1,655. A 4-hour close above $60,500 turns me constructive and opens $61,165 for the weekly close. A 4-hour close below $59,434 puts $58,700 and $58,525 back in play. A daily close below $58,525 turns me defensive and opens $57,208. A weekly close below $61,165 on Sunday would mark an eighth straight losing week. For Ether, a 4-hour close above $1,686 opens $1,710 and $1,722, and a close below $1,632 opens $1,606. I'm watching tonight's ETF print, Asia's open, whether USDC and USDT mints continue, any sign of miners sending coins to exchanges, Bangkok on Saturday, OPEC+ on Sunday, the 7:00 PM EST weekly close on Sunday and the Monero cutoff at 3:00 AM EST on Monday. These are my analytical levels, not forecasts, and nothing here is financial advice.

2126347626304192722.text:
Monero fell 13% in 24 hours while 68 of the top 88 coins rose! What really happened?

The trigger was a KuCoin notice. It will delist XMR on Nov 30, and it carried about half of Monero's reported spot trading. Kraken chart below, all times UTC.

> Nov 11 to 17: another exchange, MEXC, announced its exit (futures closed Nov 13, spot Nov 17). XMR was sliding from about $625 on Nov 3.

> Nov 21: a wrapped copy of Monero (XMR1, a stand-in token) was drained of about $13.5M a day earlier. Real Monero held and bounced from $423 to $493 in under 20 hours, which CoinMarketCap read as shorts (bets on a falling price) closing. Closing a short means buying.

> Nov 26: peak $527.94 at 07:00, up 25% from the Nov 21 low. KuCoin published its notice the same day. The first heavy sell candle printed at 11:15, on about 9x recent volume. Deposits closed at once, trading ends Nov 30 at 08:00, withdrawals stay open to Dec 31. By 19:15 it touched $429.50, 17% below the 11:15 open.

> Nov 27: KuCoin's XMR savings product ended at 12:00, and the low came at 14:30: $406.89, 23% under the peak.

Why so hard? Holders on KuCoin must withdraw or sell, and borrowers who pledged XMR as collateral must swap it. A deadline turns waiting into a decision.

Everyone had a motive:
- KuCoin: less exposure to privacy-coin rules. It cited only its own policies. From Jul 10, 2027 the EU's AMLR bars regulated platforms from privacy coins; self-custody stays legal.
- KuCoin holders: keep their coins, so withdraw or sell.
- Dip buyers: stepped in, a +4% candle at 20:00 on Nov 26.
- Grayscale: backs Zcash, whose US ETF held about $406M on Nov 25. Same label, a regulated door.

Three habits this chart supports:
1. Price depends on the doors people use to buy and sell, not only on the code.
2. When one venue carries half the volume, one notice moves the whole market.
3. Deadlines create forced sellers, and they set the price that day.

What do you check first, what a coin does, or where you can sell it?

Experience, not financial advice.

2126462863388901829.text:
3 AI papers that matter, and why:

1️⃣ Plato's Key (Stanford): one rotation lets one AI use another's knowledge, no retraining
2️⃣ GUARD (Google): agents learn on the job without breaking what worked
3️⃣ PyRUA-Dex (PKU, NVIDIA): robot hands learn from AI-written code, not demos

Why it matters 👇

1️⃣ Every AI learns the same facts on its own. Plato's Key shows different AIs store facts in a similar shape, so one rotation lets one borrow another's knowledge. Ask an AI the capital of Germany, slip in another AI's rotated "France", and it answers "Paris": 41% of swaps worked across 20 model pairs, vs ≤2.2% for controls. If it holds beyond facts, models could share knowledge instead of relearning it.
https://t.co/Go0wTqTFa8

2️⃣ AI assistants that "learn on the job" often get worse: a fix for one task breaks another. GUARD keeps a change only if it helps more than it hurts, so it kept improving with zero forgetting: 73.2% on four shifting task streams, +3.3 pts.
https://t.co/TjDPvHbaCz

3️⃣ Robot hands are stuck on data: someone has to demonstrate every skill. PyRUA-Dex lets AI write the hands' program instead, with zero demos: 81.0% vs 40.3% for the best trained model in one simulated test, and a new piano piece from sheet music in as little as 30 min.
https://t.co/ownR0BhSxr

💡 The pattern: none of the three retrains the AI. Progress is coming from reusing what models already know.

🎯 Our take: the next leap may come from reusing models, not retraining them.

Is retraining overrated? Yes or no?

Let's connect 🤝

2126458552000594325.text:
Nvidia got its CEO back. Then it got put on downgrade watch.

Same week, opposite verdicts. The market sent the stock up 31.5% on Monday for Huang's return. S&P spent Wednesday putting Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative, saying a cut to AA- is possible within 90 days.

Read the reason and it's not about chips. S&P says the long tenure of certain board members 'may have compromised their independence,' and that it is 'unaware of any remedial action' by the board. Moody's had already cut the outlook to stable from positive on Nov 18, and left it there after the return.

One notch wouldn't break anything. Nvidia priced $25 billion of bonds in June, weeks after S&P upgraded it to AA. The point isn't default risk — AA- is still very strong. It's the direction. Upgraded in June, on watch in November.

Look at the tenure. Chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have sat on that board since 1993. Thirty-three years. The same board that said on Nov 17 it had no intention of bringing Huang back, then voted unanimously to do exactly that.

The market priced the CEO. The agencies priced the board. And the board is the part nobody has fixed.

Monday's pop has already lost almost a tenth in two sessions — down 5.9% Tuesday, 3.9% Wednesday. The next test isn't an earnings call. It's Dec 1 and Dec 3, when Huang and the board's lawyers face Congress inside S&P's 90-day window.

If the board can't explain itself there, does the market start pricing the governance discount S&P already has?

What Happened in the Biotech World Today?

Biotech Explained · Friday, November 27, 2026

$VERA $VRTX $NEU.AX $ADXN $ABOS $FATE $ERAS $INO $JAZZ $9969.HK $REGN $CRNA

Market temperature

At the U.S. market close

Nasdaq Composite +2.31%
Dow Jones Industrial Average +1.18%
S&P 500 +1.60%
$SOXX +4.76% · Semiconductor ETF
$XBI +1.21% · Biotech ETF

Semiconductors led a broad rally in the shortened post-Thanksgiving session. 
Biotech also rose, although $XBI trailed the S&P 500 by 0.39 percentage points. U.S. equities closed at 1 p.m. ET.

Selected movers

At the market close

$VERA +16.14% · $VRTX −5.24%. In the first U.S. session after Vertex announced a review extension, Vera rallied and Vertex fell. The FDA’s target date for a decision on povetacicept in IgA nephropathy moved from November 30 to no later than February 28, 2027. Vera already sells its competing treatment, atacicept, in the U.S.

$NEU.AX −12.15%. Neuren fell in Sydney after saying the FDA’s preferred Phase 3 design for Pitt-Hopkins syndrome would require more patients than it believes it can recruit.

$ABOS +9.02%. Acumen rose in the first regular session after disclosing two executive departures as part of its restructuring following the discontinuation of sabirnetug development. The reason for the gain remains unclear.

$ADXN +9.56%. Addex rebounded after falling 5.18% on Wednesday, when it reported quarterly results.

$FATE +8.10% · $ERAS +6.57% · $INO −4.42%. No company-specific trigger was confirmed for Friday’s moves.

Five Stories That Mattered

1. $JAZZ · The UK expands Ziihera approval to advanced HER2-positive gastroesophageal cancer
The UK medicines regulator approved zanidatamab for adults with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma. The antibody binds two regions of HER2, a protein that can drive tumor growth. It is used with chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab depending on the tumor’s HER2 expression.

Why it matters

In the 914-patient Phase 3 trial, the three-drug regimen kept the cancer from worsening for a median of 12.4 months versus 8.1 months with trastuzumab and chemotherapy. The trial also showed a survival benefit.

2. $9969.HK · China expands zurletrectinib approval to children aged 2 to 12
The approval covers solid tumors with a genetic alteration called an NTRK fusion. InnoCare reported a 100% response rate by independent review, with an estimated 74.1% of responses still ongoing at two years. The announcement did not specify how many children were evaluated.

Why it matters

Children with cancers in different organs can qualify for the same treatment if their tumors share this genetic alteration. The missing patient count limits how much weight to put on the 100% figure.

3. $REGN · The UK approves Lynozyfic for multiple myeloma after at least three prior treatments
Linvoseltamab is approved on its own for adults whose disease progressed after treatment that included an immunomodulatory drug, a proteasome inhibitor and an anti-CD38 antibody. In the study, 83 of 117 patients responded, including 58 with a complete response.

Why it matters

The antibody brings immune cells called T cells into contact with myeloma cells so they can attack them. It gives patients another option when several established treatments have stopped working.

4. $NEU.AX · Neuren faces a Phase 3 design challenge in Pitt-Hopkins syndrome
According to Neuren’s account of its meeting with the FDA, the agency favors a randomized, double-blind trial against placebo, with a main measure based on changes in everyday abilities. Neuren says the required sample size would be impractical in this ultra-rare neurodevelopmental disorder.

Why it matters

The company needs a trial that can detect changes that matter to families while enrolling enough patients for a reliable result. The Phase 3 design remains under discussion. Neuren plans to submit written input in December to the FDA’s broader initiative on rare disease trials.

 5. $CRNA · Circio reports up to 600-fold higher gene expression in a lab model made from human heart cells
Circio measured gene expression with its circular RNA approach and a reference gene-delivery vector. In the lab model, expression with Circio’s approach reached up to 600 times the level measured with the reference vector.

Why it matters

Higher expression could make it possible to use a lower dose of the delivery vector. The next question is whether a lower dose can produce a therapeutic effect in disease models.

News of the day

It was a close call today between $JAZZ and $REGN. 

Regeneron’s Lynozyfic gives patients with heavily pretreated multiple myeloma another option.

I chose Jazz because its new first-line option for advanced HER2-positive gastroesophageal cancer improved survival in a randomized trial against an active treatment.

$JAZZ · The UK approves a first-line treatment backed by longer survival

In the follow-up presented at ESMO in October, median overall survival was 27.0 months with zanidatamab, tislelizumab and chemotherapy, versus 19.6 months with trastuzumab and chemotherapy. At three years, an estimated 40% versus 23% of patients were still alive
