Taiwan AI supply chain earnings calls | Nov 27

Three suppliers said it yesterday in different words: AI chips keep getting bigger, and substrates and tools are struggling to keep up.

- Nan Ya PCB (8046 TT): ABF and BT lines fully loaded, AI ASIC substrates enter volume production in Q4, ABF seen in short supply through 2027. Bigger, higher layer count designs cut how many units each line can turn out, and tool lead times are longer. 2027 unit growth seen in the single digits, but extra large substrates price at several times the old generation. Pricing set case by case by customer, spec and supply and demand, not an across the board hike.

- Innostar (7828 TT): Q3 revenue NT$443M, +182% y/y, GM 79%, OPM 47%, EPS NT$4.12. Its dual arm machines automate pin insertion for MEMS probe cards. About 53 shipped by October vs a 70 to 80 unit 2026 target, with 2027 shipments seen multiplying. Also won a million unit Cu pillar order for kW class vertical power modules, volume in 3Q27.

- Group Up (6658 TT): Q3 revenue NT$603M, +60.7% y/y. 9M EPS NT$4.36 vs NT$1.38 for all of 2025. Management expects cleaning tools and CoWoS related inspection to pay off in 2027.

Current view:

Substrate growth in 2027 comes from area and ASP, not volume.

Probe card capacity is now limited by how fast pins get placed, so the machine makers sit right on the bottleneck.

Which moves first in 2027: ABF prices or probe card capacity?

Someone just paid $52M for the right to be wrong about $NVDA until March.

THE TRADE

At 11:15 ET someone bought 42,000 NVDA March 19 $165 calls for $52.0M in a single print. At-the-money, 112 days to expiry, long vega by construction — the buyer paid premium and now needs NVDA to move, not merely drift higher. Whether this opens a fresh position or closes a short somewhere else we cannot tell from the tape, but the directional read does not depend on that: this is a bullish, long-volatility bet with a four-month runway.

THE SETUP

The timing is not subtle. Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1 and December 3 on export controls and national security. The March expiry sits well past that event, past January earnings, past the next CES cycle. This is not a headline trade. It is someone writing a $52M check to own convexity through the entire next news cycle at a strike the stock is already sitting on.

NVDA's own book today was mixed — $114M bullish premium against $89M bearish across 64 prints. The rest of the tape is not screaming conviction. This single ticket is.

THE REST OF THE CHIP COMPLEX

INTC was the cleaner story. $44.6M lifted in Feb $40 calls at 10:54 ET, and the whole-name tape ran $44.6M bullish against under $3M bearish — essentially one-sided. Three prints, one direction, big size. Something is moving in Intel positioning that the equity tape has not caught up to.

Anthropic's $100B IPO printed today, and a ticker tagged ANT saw 12,500 March $70 calls bought for $36.5M — positioning horizon, in-the-money, long vega. AMZN, which carries an Anthropic stake, saw 23,250 Feb $280 calls bought in a burst for $23.0M, out-of-the-money and leveraged. Two different ways of expressing the same AI-capex idea: own the names, own the convexity, pay to be in the trade before year-end.

THE FADE

The one print that cut against the grain was META. At 11:01 ET someone sold 11,800 January $635 calls and collected $48.3M. This is premium harvesting — short vega, paid to wait, bearish lean on direction but that lean is a by-product of the vol stance, not the thesis. It may well be a covered call written against stock; we cannot tell. What we can say is that META's whole-name premium today leaned net bearish ($56M vs $44M) across just four prints — a very concentrated book, with the biggest ticket being the one that got paid rather than the one that paid.

THE NOISE

MSTR printed $31M in $30 calls expiring today — 6,124 contracts, deep in the money, direction unsignable. Big dollar number, zero read. TSLA saw $9.2M lifted in same-day $355 calls — an intraday trade, not a view. These are the prints that look important on a leaderboard and mean nothing on a thesis page.

THE TAKEAWAY

One trader paid $52M for four months of upside convexity in NVDA through the Huang testimony. Another collected $48M against META staying under $635 through January. Both are big. Only one is a bet.

Analog Devices beat Wall Street estimates on both top and bottom lines for its fiscal fourth quarter, yet the stock plunged 17.4% on earnings day and stayed stuck at 333.11 dollars by Wednesday's close. Revenue came in at 4.37 billion dollars, topping expectations of 4.36 billion dollars, while adjusted earnings per share reached 4.06 dollars against the 3.92 dollars forecast.

The disaster came entirely from forward guidance: management projected current quarter revenue at a midpoint of 4.4 billion dollars, practically flat from the quarter just reported, with the bottom range pointing to an outright quarter over quarter decline. Investors had piled into ADI because year over year growth had accelerated from 25.9% to 42.2%.

The second that runaway growth curve flattened, institutions dumped it without hesitation, dragging Texas Instruments down 11.2% and NXP Semiconductors down 6.5% along the way. When a stock is priced for nonstop acceleration, a solid beat means nothing if the next quarter stops growing.

The data points to a valuation-driven market downturn colliding with a late-cycle inflation shock, rather than an active broad recession. 

The economy is split down the middle: rate-sensitive sectors, lower-income households, and high-multiple tech are under acute stress, while aggregate employment, corporate credit, and AI capital spending are still holding the floor.

Why the Bear Case Has Real Teeth?

The Fed is trapped by stagflationary pressures. The energy shock from the Middle East conflict and new trade tariffs pushed headline CPI back toward 4% and Core PCE up to 3.3% in October. Unlike a standard downturn where the Fed cuts rates to cushion falling stocks, both Goldman Sachs and U.S. Bank now project two more 25 bps rate hikes (December and March), lifting rates to 4.25%–4.50% with cuts delayed until late 2027. Tightening monetary policy while equities are already correcting is historically how soft landings break into recessions.

Severe concentration risk in AI capex. Business investment is heavily skewed: AI infrastructure (data centers, chips, software) accounts for roughly 40% of capital spending and has masked an ongoing contraction in commercial real estate and traditional manufacturing.

That single pillar is now under pressure. Tighter US semiconductor export controls and doubts over AI profitability crushed chipmakers—wiping over $2.2 trillion off Nvidia from its October peak and compressing the S&P 500 forward P/E down to 16.4 (lowest since 2022) and semiconductors down to 9.4. If equity losses force hyperscalers to scale back 2027 capex, GDP loses its primary growth engine.

Consumer exhaustion beneath the headline numbers. Total US household debt reached $19.11 trillion in Q3 2026. The personal savings rate sits compressed around 4.1%–4.8% (versus a ~7.5% pre-pandemic baseline), credit card balances 90+ days past due remain stuck at 12.9%, and student loan serious delinquency climbed to 10.9%. Spending is being carried by wealthier households riding prior asset gains; a sustained stock market drawdown directly threatens that wealth effect.

Early cracks in labor quality. While headline unemployment held at 4.1%, the October BLS report showed a sharp single-month jump of +339,000 in people forced into part-time work for economic reasons (reaching 4.84 million, with +356,000 citing slack business conditions). Companies are cutting hours before cutting headcount—a classic pre-recession pattern.

What Is Still Preventing a Confirmed Recession?

Credit markets are not pricing systemic defaults. Equities often throw false recession alarms; the corporate bond market rarely does. US High-Yield spreads widened to 3.72%–3.76% (up from 2.59% in early 2025), and investment-grade spreads sit near 1.0%. That reflects tighter financial conditions, not a credit freeze. In true recessions, high-yield spreads typically blow past 6%–8% as refinancing markets shut down.

Layoffs remain historically low. Initial jobless claims printed at 189,000 (4-week average of 196,000) in late November, and continuing claims sit near 1.70 million. Without rising job losses, consumer income does not collapse fast enough to trigger an NBER-defined contraction.

Earnings and GDP momentum haven't rolled over yet. Real GDP growth stayed solid through Q3 2026, with major desks still projecting 2.0%–2.4% real growth for 2027. Even amid the semiconductor sell-off, underlying revenue growth remains strong (for example, AMD posted 45% YoY Q3 revenue growth with data-center revenue up 97%), making the current equity drop primarily a multiple compression rather than an earnings collapse.

Understanding the mechanics of this market.

While it felt really good to see that intraday recovery and the S&P 500 establish a higher low the other day, and while I generally look for the optimistic side of markets, I also try to be a realist and continuously update my thesis and understanding of the market as variables change.

One of the major plaguing issues of this market has been the number of absolute bangers — and I'm talking bad bangers — that just keep coming out of left field.

The most difficult part of navigating markets, in my opinion, isn't analyzing fundamentals or macroeconomics. It's the curveballs. The unforeseen developments that introduce entirely new variables, which the market has a tendency to aggressively overprice to the downside.

What's potentially unique about today's market is the speed, magnitude and persistence of that overreaction. As algorithmic trading, quantitative strategies and systematic funds become increasingly prevalent, similar inputs across different models can generate enormous amounts of selling simultaneously.

Tom Lee recently touched on this, and it's something I've been talking about for months: increasingly, a significant component of market behaviour is being driven by machines responding to other machines.

I really don't like suggesting that systematic funds are all that move markets, but they do need to be understood in their place within the broader market ecosystem.

Here's an interesting article published this morning covering Goldman Sachs' systematic trading desk, which estimates that approximately $70 billion in global equity exposure was mechanically unwound over the past week, with another $100 billion in potential selling over the coming week.

What this helps explain is why market dislocations can persist well beyond what fundamentals and macroeconomic conditions would otherwise seem to justify.

These strategies operate across different time horizons. You can have improving macroeconomic conditions, exceptional corporate earnings and even a fresh bullish catalyst, while billions of dollars in capital are still responding mechanically to the cumulative technical damage of the previous several weeks.

In other words, the original justification for selling can be dissipating while the mechanical consequences of that selling are still working their way through the market.

That being said, the $100 billion is a dynamic projection, not a predetermined liquidation schedule. Discretionary institutional buying, corporate buybacks, retail participation, short covering and faster-moving strategies can overwhelm that selling pressure and ultimately force those slower-moving models to reverse course.

The same machinery that's been exacerbating the downside can eventually become an accelerant to the upside.

There are certainly some constructive developments. Michael Burry unwinding his Nasdaq shorts, Wednesday's intraday reversal and higher low, strong overnight trading in Asian markets and renewed strength in semiconductors, which remain central to the broader US equity market.

The VIX hitting 40 last Friday also had all the characteristics of a potential capitulation event. I'd like to think that marked the bottom.

I'm still hoping the next CPI report provides a meaningful turning point. No promises, but a number of major trading desks and analysts are increasingly constructive. The recurring theme, however, is that everyone is waiting for confirmation. They're waiting for the train to stop, so to speak.

The point of sharing this Goldman article is to help explain why, despite an increasingly constructive setup and the potential for a substantial short squeeze, we could still experience bouts of aggressive selling.

Some of these systematic strategies are effectively trading today's market based on the damage inflicted weeks ago.

📥🔍 27일 12월물 ZQ는 𝟗𝟓.𝟗𝟒𝟓(-𝟎.𝟎𝟎𝟓)로 소폭 내려 내재 금리가 올랐고 11월물 ZQ는 𝟗𝟔.𝟏𝟐𝟎(-𝟎.𝟎𝟎𝟐𝟓). 자체 계산 확률은 𝟐𝟓bp 인상 𝟗𝟖.𝟔%(직전 𝟗𝟕.𝟐%), 동결 𝟏.𝟒%로 인상이 사실상 완전히 반영됨. 🟨 SNF PULSE™      EVENING

WALL STREET JUST DELIVERED ITS BEST WEEK SINCE APRIL 2025. THE COST OF CAPITAL ISN'T COMING DOWN.

Friday, November 27, 2026

Last Friday, investors were liquidating exposure.

This Friday, they were buying across the market.

The S&P 500 completed its strongest week in more than a year and a half. Semiconductor stocks recovered, financials participated, small caps advanced and volatility declined substantially.

But Treasury yields climbed alongside equities.

The market is repairing its technical damage without receiving meaningful relief from monetary policy.

That distinction matters heading into December.

🟨 THE EVENING TAPE | BLACK FRIDAY CLOSE

 🟢 S&P 500: 7,297.49 | +1.60%
 🟢 Nasdaq: 24,129.50 | +2.31%
 🟢 Dow: 50,774.94 | +1.18%
 🟢 Russell 2000: 2,750.30 | +1.71%
 🟢 Semiconductor ETF $SMH: +3.79%
 🟢 VIX: 23.81 | −15.84%

🟨 THE WEEKLY SCORECARD
 
 🟢 Nasdaq: +6.68%
 🟢 Russell 2000: +6.53%
 🟢 S&P 500: +5.60%
 🟢 Dow: +5.46%

The recovery extended across all four major indexes.

The S&P 500 is now approximately 6.7% below its October record, compared with more than 11% below that record last Friday.

Wall Street has recovered a meaningful portion of its recent losses.

The question is whether the buying continues when normal trading conditions return.

🟨 THE BREADTH TEST

Friday delivered one of the more constructive participation readings of the week.

🟢 NYSE advancing stocks outnumbered decliners 3.25 to 1.

🟢 Nasdaq recorded 3,677 advancing stocks against 1,135 declining stocks.

🟢 All eleven major S&P 500 sectors advanced.

🟢 The S&P 500 recorded 12 new 52-week highs and no new lows.

Perhaps most importantly, the number of new lows across the broader exchanges declined substantially.

Wednesday:

 🔴 NYSE: 629 new lows
 🔴 Nasdaq: 479 new lows

Friday:

 🟢 NYSE: 73 new lows
 🟢 Nasdaq: 96 new lows

Friday's shorter trading session limits direct comparisons, but the improvement is nevertheless encouraging.

The market is showing evidence of stabilization beyond its largest companies.

🟨 WHERE THE MONEY WENT

Friday sector performance:

 🟢 Consumer Discretionary +1.99%
 🟢 Technology +1.86%
 🟢 Communication Services +1.65%
 🟢 Materials +1.47%
 🟢 Industrials +1.28%
 🟢 Energy +1.26%
 🟢 Financials +1.09%
 🟢 Real Estate +0.58%
 🟢 Consumer Staples +0.44%
 🟢 Utilities +0.25%
 🟢 Healthcare +0.17%

The leadership also changed.

Technology and consumer discretionary returned to the front of the market, while defensive sectors participated but lagged.

Select individual movers:
 
 🟢 SanDisk: Approximately +16%
 🟢 Micron: +7.60%
 🟢 Tesla: +5.22%
 🟢 Amazon: +3.96%
 🟢 Broadcom: +3.82%
 🟢 JPMorgan: +1.92%

Earlier this week, investors sought alternatives to technology.

Today, they returned to technology without abandoning those alternatives.

That is a more constructive form of participation.

 🟠 THE CROSS-ASSET SIGNAL
 
 🟠 U.S. 2-year Treasury yield: 4.69% | +6 basis points
 🟠 U.S. 10-year Treasury yield: 4.92% | +7.4 basis points
 🟠 Dollar Index: Near 104
 
 🟢 Spot gold: $3,639.61 | +2.1% at 2:01 PM ET
 🟢 Silver: Near $43.44 | +4.7%
 🟢 Brent crude: $95.44 | −1.2%
 🟢 WTI crude: $83.08 | −0.7%
 
🟠 Bitcoin: Traded between approximately $58,700 and $62,200 during Friday's session.

Equities and precious metals recovered together.

Treasuries moved in the opposite direction.

Bitcoin experienced another volatile session following the monthly options expiration, surrendering much of its early advance during U.S. equity trading.

Meanwhile, Brent crude recorded its first weekly gain of November despite today's decline.

The dominant cross asset message is improving equity sentiment without a synchronized improvement in financial conditions.

Investors are accepting more equity risk even as borrowing costs rise.

🟨 THE ECONOMIC REALITY

Today's advance goods trade report added another dimension to the AI investment story.

🟠 October U.S. goods trade deficit: $149.5 billion.
🟠 Deficit increased 10.7% from September.
🟠 Goods imports reached a record $365.3 billion.
🟠 Capital goods imports increased 8.5%.

The infrastructure investment cycle continues generating substantial demand.

However, imported equipment also increases the trade deficit, potentially offsetting part of the domestic growth contribution from that investment.

Strong corporate spending does not translate automatically into equivalent domestic economic growth.

The Federal Reserve must still contend with persistent inflation, resilient demand and elevated financing costs.
Markets continue pricing a December interest rate increase.

🟨 THE POSITIONING QUESTION

The VIX has fallen from 35.89 last Friday to 23.81 today.

That represents a substantial improvement in equity market sentiment.

Following significant reductions in technology exposure earlier this month, investors may now face pressure to rebuild positions as markets recover.

But short covering and renewed institutional accumulation are not necessarily the same thing.

Friday's price action confirms that buyers returned.

Monday must help establish whether those buyers remain committed.

🟨 WHAT SNF IS WATCHING

🟡 SATURDAY AND SUNDAY | BLACK FRIDAY CONSUMER DATA

Watch online spending, retail traffic, promotional intensity and consumer financing.

Revenue growth will be more meaningful if retailers can preserve profitability without excessive discounting.

🟡 SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 29 | OPEC+

Production policy and Middle East supply conditions remain important for inflation expectations.

Watch the oil market's response when futures reopen.

🟡 SUNDAY | 6:00 PM EST | FUTURES REOPEN

The first test of whether Friday's recovery survives the weekend.

Watch equity futures, crude oil, gold, Bitcoin and global risk sentiment.

🟡 MONDAY, NOVEMBER 30 | MONTH END
Normal U.S. equity trading resumes.

Month end portfolio adjustments could introduce additional volatility.

China's official manufacturing PMI, Chicago PMI and the Dallas Fed manufacturing survey will provide fresh economic context.

🟡 TUESDAY, DECEMBER 1 | 10:00 AM EST

ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS job openings.

Watch employment demand, new orders and input prices.

🟡 NEXT WEEK | TECHNOLOGY EARNINGS

Salesforce and Marvell Technology report results.

Enterprise software demand, custom silicon investment and profitability will provide another test of the AI recovery.

🟡 FRIDAY, DECEMBER 4 | 8:30 AM EST

November employment report.

Economists surveyed by LSEG expect approximately 90,000 additional jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate.

The report will help shape expectations ahead of the December 9 Federal Reserve decision.

🟨 THE TWO SCENARIOS

🟢 CONSTRUCTIVE

Friday's broad participation survives normal trading conditions. Technology continues recovering alongside financials and small caps.

Treasury yields stabilize, volatility declines further and Bitcoin establishes more consistent participation.

The recovery begins attracting sustained conviction.

🔴 RISK

Holiday buying proves temporary. Treasury yields continue rising, energy supply concerns intensify and volatility returns.

Technology once again becomes vulnerable to valuation and financing pressure.

The market's strong weekly performance gives way to another defensive repositioning.

🟨 SNF LENS™

🟢 SIGNAL: Broad participation, declining volatility, fewer new lows and the strongest S&P 500 weekly performance since April 2025.

⚪ NOISE: Assuming a powerful recovery during a shortened holiday week means the correction is permanently over.

🟡 CONFIRMATION: Sustained participation under normal trading conditions, stable Treasury yields, improving credit conditions and broader liquidity confirmation.

🔴 RISK: Restrictive monetary policy, elevated borrowing costs, persistent inflation, energy supply uncertainty and unresolved AI financing concerns.

🟨 THE BOTTOM LINE

Wall Street is entering December in considerably better condition than it was one week ago.

Buyers returned.

Market breadth improved.

Volatility retreated.

Technology regained leadership without excluding the rest of the market.

But the economic cost of sustaining that recovery has not disappeared.

THE MARKET REPAIRED ITS PRICE ACTION.

DECEMBER WILL TEST WHETHER THE FUNDAMENTALS CAN SUPPORT IT.

2126458045035356227.text:
Boom! Black Friday gave us a green half day.

The S&P 500 closed up 1.6% at 7,297. The Nasdaq jumped 2.3% to 24,130. The Dow added 592 points, up 1.2%, to 50,775. Not bad for a market that shut at 1 PM.

The big story? Chips came back. The chip index bounced nearly 5%. AI fear took a break after a rough month. $MU ran more than 7%. Memory names loved it.

$AMZN rose about 4%. Black Friday shopping news was the fuel. Adobe sees $275 billion in online holiday spend. Cyber Week alone could be close to $50 billion. People are still buying.

$TSLA also popped about 5% to $400. Big round number. Let's see if it holds.

Now the tone. Fear cooled off. The VIX fell to about 24. That is still high, but it was near 36 just one week ago. Small caps joined in too. The Russell 2000 was up 1.7%.

But don't get too comfy. The S&P is still down for November. It is still almost 7% under its October high.

What am I watching? Monday is the last day of the month. OPEC meets Sunday, and oil has been jumpy. Jobs data is on deck. Jensen Huang goes to Congress, so $NVDA could swing. And the Fed meets in December. Rates are still the big worry.

My take? One green half day on light volume is not a trend. Thin days can fool you. I want to see chips hold these gains on a full day with real volume. If they do, the dip may be done. If not, expect more chop. I'd rather be patient than chase.

Did the dip end, or is this just a holiday bounce? Tell me below.

According to Reuters, the U.S. privately encouraged Venezuela and Iraq earlier this year to consider leaving OPEC, allowing them to ramp up oil production without being restricted by the cartel’s quotas.

In Venezuela, Washington even blocked Caracas from paying its annual OPEC membership dues. The pressure reportedly stopped only after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened and urged the U.S. to back off.

In Iraq, Prime Minister al-Zaidi raised the possibility of leaving OPEC following discussions with U.S. officials. However, Iraq’s oil ministry opposed the move, arguing that Baghdad should push for a larger production quota instead.

The bigger picture: Washington is trying to reshape the global oil market — and OPEC is in its sights.

【11/28朝の相場まとめ】

■米国市場
11/27は短縮取引で大幅反発。ダウ50,774.94（+1.18%）、S&P500 7,297.49（+1.60%）、NASDAQ 24,129.50（+2.31%）。売られていたAI・半導体株に買い戻しが入り、フィラデルフィア半導体指数は+4.69%。週間ではダウ+5.46%と2022年10月以来の大幅上昇。米10年債利回りは4.93%へ上昇、VIXは23.81に低下。

■ドル円
NY終値は159.51円前後と小幅なドル高・円安。159円台前半の小動きが続いた。

■日本市場
11/27は大幅続伸。日経平均58,711.11円（+2.11%）、TOPIX 3,815.20（+1.73%）。半導体関連を中心に買いが優勢で、アドバンテスト+7.06%、東京エレクトロン+4.43%。11/25の急落分を2日でほぼ取り戻した。

■月曜（11/30）の見通し
夜間先物は大証58,810円前後、シカゴCME 58,970円と堅調。米株の大幅反発を受け、月曜は買い先行で反発継続のスタートが見込まれる。ただ米国は短縮取引で薄商いだったうえ、米10年債利回り4.93%・VIX 23.8と高めで、寄り後の上値の重さには注意。注目は11/29のOPEC+閣僚級会合と、12/17〜18の日銀会合に向けた利上げ観測の行方。

■株価材料ニュース
（1）東京都区部コアCPIは+2.9%で16カ月ぶりの高水準。12月日銀利上げ観測が強まる
影響の観点：銀行株には追い風、円高圧力を通じて輸出株には逆風になりやすい。12/18朝の全国CPIが次の試金石。

影響の観点：金・エネルギー関連や商社株には材料。供給不安が長引けばインフレ再燃→金利観測にも波及。11/29のOPEC+会合次第で原油がさらに動く可能性。

（3）ECB次期総裁にデコス氏（BIS総支配人）が決定
影響の観点：欧州の金融政策の方向性を通じて日本株にも間接的に波及しうるが、当面の直接の影響は限定的。

■増配ピックアップ
京成電鉄（9009）が増収増益・通期予想の上方修正と増配を発表。年間配当は22円→30円（うち特別配当5円）。増配の原資にオリエンタルランド株の売却益を含む点には注意。

#ULTIMAHORA | Resumen financiero del viernes 27 de noviembre de 2026 📊

Wall Street cerró con fuertes ganancias una semana de enorme volatilidad, recuperando buena parte de las pérdidas de la semana anterior. Los inversionistas dejaron momentáneamente de lado sus preocupaciones respecto a la rentabilidad de las inversiones en inteligencia artificial (IA).

📈 Así cerraron los principales índices bursátiles:
🔹Nasdaq: +2.3% hoy y +6.7% semanal, su mejor semana desde abril, después de haber perdido 10% la semana anterior.
🔹S&P 500: +1.6% hoy y +5.6% semanal, su mayor avance desde abril de 2025.
🔹Dow Jones: +1.2% hoy (592 puntos) y +5.5% semanal, su mejor semana desde 2022.

Los 11 sectores que componen el S&P 500 registraron ganancias tanto en la jornada del viernes como en el acumulado semanal.

El acontecimiento más importante de la semana fue el regreso de Jensen Huang como director general de Nvidia. Las acciones de la compañía se dispararon 31% el lunes, recuperando casi un billón de dólares en capitalización bursátil en una sola jornada, algo sin precedentes para cualquier empresa.

Sin embargo, las preocupaciones en torno a la IA provocaron nuevas caídas el martes y miércoles, antes del repunte de este viernes.

arxiv:2611.24028v1.text: Algorithmic Market Making Can Lead to Rough Volatility Through the Order Book. Existing work suggests that markets can show volatility with paths rougher than those of Brownian motion. In theory this can happen when the order flow is close to instability with memory that decays as a power law. However, it is not fully clear how such order flow could arise from the predominantly algorithmic market making that characterizes order book dynamics. We show one such consistent mechanism. We treat each market maker as a desk that uses a first-order gradient rule to move the distances of its orders from the mid price toward target distances provided by an unknown oracle. We assume that distinct desks do not act synchronously in time but act whenever new information relevant to their respective oracles arrives, which each desk samples over its own characteristic lookback horizon. Across all desks the rule therefore takes the form of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with information-driven (mini-batch) noise. In the continuum limit this update rule makes the volume of the order book follow a conservative stochastic partial differential equation (the Dean--Kawasaki equation) whose fluctuations drive the order flow. The distinct horizons of the desks further induce a persistent memory in the order flow that decays as a power law. Standard scaling arguments then lead to rough volatility. We confirm the key predictions of the model on simulated agents and on six months of Binance data with about 790 million orders. In liquid markets governed mainly by market makers, such as the perpetual futures of Binance, the order books are consistent with how our desks change the book.
arxiv:2611.24028v1.author: Sai Niranjan Ramachandran

arxiv:2611.23126v1.text: Which Past Matters? Training History and Multi-Forecast Horizon in Equity Transformers. More historical data can improve estimation while introducing relationships that transfer poorly to current market conditions. We therefore examine how training quantity and historical selection interact with forecast horizon in intraday equity prediction. We deploy twelve configurations which combine four sampling and validation policies with 6, 12 and 24 month training quantities under a fixed cross-sectional Transformer and feature set. A monthly walk-forward experiment produces 264 refits and eight cumulative return forecasts from 5 to 120 minutes. Evaluation covers January 2025 through 20 October 2026 and uses cross-sectional Spearman information coefficients against future five-factor residual returns. Six-month recency sampling leads individual models at 5-15 minutes, while multi recency configurations lead at 20-30 minutes and uniform configurations at 60-120 minutes. Increasing training quantity does not uniformly improve accuracy while an equal-weight ensemble of all twelve models exceeds every individual mean at 15, 20 and 25 minutes, but not at the remaining horizons. These findings support evaluating historical selection jointly with forecast horizon without identifying a universal policy or a causal benefit from recency.
arxiv:2611.23126v1.author: Chariton Chalvatzis

arxiv:2611.21897v1.text: Revisiting Equity-Bond Diversification under Tail Risk and Structural Market Change: Evidence from Global ETFs and Model-Implied Option Prices. This study examines thirty equity--bond and multi-asset exchange-traded funds (ETFs) listed in the United States, Canada, and Australia using daily U.S.-dollar returns over 2020--2024. A rolling-window framework compares minimum-variance and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) portfolio optimization under long-only and long--short constraints against an equally weighted benchmark. Performance is assessed using risk-adjusted measures, downside risk, extreme-tail estimation, and conditional volatility models. Optimized portfolios exhibit lower empirical VaR and CVaR than the benchmark, with long--short strategies generally providing greater downside-risk reduction. However, the equally weighted benchmark achieves the highest reported Sharpe, Sortino, and Rachev ratios. GARCH and FIGARCH comparisons favor GARCH based on information criteria. A historically estimated Normal Inverse Gaussian model further generates European option prices and model-implied volatility surfaces under a martingale-corrected pricing specification. The findings highlight trade-offs between risk reduction, risk-adjusted performance, and practical implementation costs.
arxiv:2611.21897v1.author: Farzana Afroz et al.

arxiv:2611.19937v1.text: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data. Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.
arxiv:2611.19937v1.author: Annan Wang et al.

arxiv:2611.19903v1.text: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization for Multi-Asset Portfolios. Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) insulates asset allocation from Markowitz covariance ill-conditioning. However, classical tree clustering relies on static pairwise Pearson correlation, failing to capture time-varying, asymmetric downside risk contagion across multi-asset markets. We propose a unified deep graph machine learning architecture: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization (ST-GAT-NCO) for multi-asset tactical allocation. The framework extracts temporal momentum and downside risk dynamics via causal dilated 1D-convolutions, then deploys a multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) over dynamic market topologies to learn latent spatial node representations. These learned embeddings define an angular metric distance space that guides two-stage downside NCO optimization under institutional constraints and turnover smoothing. Evaluated over a 73-month non-anticipative walk-forward out-of-sample window (January 2020 to January 2026) across 13 global asset classes net of 10 bps transaction costs, ST-GAT-NCO achieves a 5.32% CAGR and 37.06% cumulative net return, delivering an excess Sharpe ratio of 0.30 and a Sortino ratio of 0.48. This substantially outperforms classical Minimum Variance (3.68% CAGR, 0.08 Sharpe), Hierarchical Risk Parity (2.65% CAGR), and Plain Symmetric NCO (4.11% CAGR, 0.15 Sharpe), while restricting maximum drawdown to -13.07% (versus -19.44% for Equal-Weight and -16.36% for Downside NCO) under a controlled one-way turnover of 15.31%/month. Regime analysis confirms active capital preservation across the 2020 COVID-19 crash, 2022 monetary tightening, and 2023-2026 disinflation rallies.
arxiv:2611.19903v1.author: Supriadi

arxiv:2611.17170v1.text: Improving Algorithmic Trading for BESS on Intraday Electricity Markets through Distributional Price Forecasts. Grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) are becoming increasingly important in short-term energy markets, where they help balance fluctuations in variable renewable generation. In many countries, the continuous intraday market is the most important wholesale market for BESS to monetize their flexibility. In this paper, we propose an extension to the myopic rolling intrinsic policy that incorporates intraday price forecasts tailored specifically to the BESS trading problem. While a large literature addresses intraday price forecasting, most existing work focuses on volume-weighted prices during the last hours of trading and consequently fails to capture the features most relevant to BESS trading. Our approach addresses this gap by introducing a novel target variable derived from the limit order book and its dynamics. The resulting forecasts are designed to inform the optimization about future profit opportunities while preserving computational efficiency and avoiding the burden of full stochastic optimization. In a realistic high-frequency simulation setting covering 2023 and 2024, our method improves profits by up to 42% over the naive rolling intrinsic formulation. We further analyze the relationship between forecast accuracy, stability, and financial performance, establishing a clear inverse relationship between accuracy and stability. Finally, we find evidence that BESS size and duration jointly influence both overall profitability and the marginal benefit of incorporating forecasts.
arxiv:2611.17170v1.author: Simon Hirsch et al.

arxiv:2611.16540v2.text: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs. Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. Relaxing the target-adjustment limit changed exposures, turnover, and some returns more than varying scenario count or seed in the examined tests. These findings suggest that assessments of conditional return inputs should consider portfolio constraints and trading requirements.
arxiv:2611.16540v2.author: Abigail A. Mensah et al.

arxiv:2611.15657v1.text: Global Seasonality Factor Investing. We study seasonality as a factor for predicting risk-adjusted returns across global futures markets. We document five seasonality anomalies that, in aggregate, are pervasive across bond, commodity and equity markets. We demonstrate that each seasonality factor produces excess returns that are not reasonably explained by established global time series carry, momentum and skewness factors. We apply recent innovations in statistical learning and fit nonlinear seasonality models at the individual market level, thereby allowing each feature-market pair to express its unique seasonal prediction pattern. We discuss candidate economic rationales for the existence and persistence of each seasonality anomaly. Walk-forward out-of-sample testing demonstrates that fast-moving seasonal patterns, such as day-of-week and day-of-month, produce strong gross performance but with extremely high turnover, resulting in negative performance net of transaction costs. In contrast, slower-moving seasonal patterns, such as day-of-quarter, day-of-half-year and day-of-year, produce positive gross performance and, with the exception of day-of-quarter, positive net performance. An equal-weight ensemble of seasonality models produces an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio that is competitive with, and uncorrelated to, established global time series factor portfolios. Empirical results demonstrate that adding seasonality to a global factor portfolio increases the out-of-sample Sharpe ratio by approximately $30\%$ over the full evaluation period.
arxiv:2611.15657v1.author: Andrew Butler et al.

arxiv:2611.15646v1.text: Idiosyncratic Market Effects in Global Time Series Momentum. Time series momentum is a pervasive explanatory factor in financial markets whereby a market's recent historical average return positively predicts future returns. Recent applications of statistical learning augment the traditional linear model definition with a more descriptive global nonlinear factor model. We extend the work of \citet{MoskowitzNonlinear} and demonstrate that models fit at the individual market level exhibit response curves that are distinct from the global factor model. We highlight the heterogeneity of forward market returns as a function of time series momentum and provide a framework that enables each feature-market pair to express its unique prediction behaviour. Empirical results demonstrate that, despite substantially smaller sample sizes, fitting nonlinear models to individual markets is a robust and often overlooked modelling approach that can result in a marginal improvement in out-of-sample performance.
arxiv:2611.15646v1.author: Andrew Butler et al.

arxiv:2611.14245v1.text: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation. We analyze the solution map of a optimal execution problem in which price dynamics are subject to a general transient impact kernel. Given the structure of the optimal trading strategy derived by Abi Jaber and Neuman in \cite{https://doi.org/10.1111/mafi.12465}, we show that the strategy is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the underlying model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact as well as the fundamental price process. Continuity of this map justifies the application of neural-net based approximations which take model parameters as inputs. We propose a method generating samples of the transient price impact kernel for the purposes of creating training data, and a method of projecting the kernel to a finite dimensional representation appropriate for input to a neural net, and a dimensional reduction based on the relationship between inventory and trade signal. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained neural net and use it to quantify the potential financial costs associated with misspecifying the transient impact kernel.
arxiv:2611.14245v1.author: Ryan Donnelly et al.

arxiv:2611.14117v1.text: Fine-Tuning an Order-Flow Foundation Model for Sub-Second Forecasting. Generative models have become the standard approach in language and vision. These models are typically pretrained first and then fine-tuned. Recent work demonstrates how to pretrain an autoregressive generative model on Level-3 order-flow data. However, to our knowledge, no one has fine-tuned such a model yet for downstream tasks. Here we first pretrain a 300M-parameter generative model on Level-3 order-flow data collected from two crypto exchanges, Bitstamp and Bitfinex. Then we fine-tune the pretrained model to predict the microprice return and its realized volatility. We show that our fine-tuned model outperforms classical baselines, such as gradient boosting on handcrafted features, in predicting microprice returns over sub-second horizons. Furthermore, the predictive ability of the model transfers zero-shot to assets it was never fine-tuned on. Due to the short-term nature of these forecasts, the predicted microprice moves are smaller than the bid-ask spread plus fees, so the natural applications are in execution and market making. These results indicate that a pretrained generative model can be turned into a competitive short-horizon price forecaster via fine-tuning.
arxiv:2611.14117v1.author: Fedor Shabashev

North Korea Moves $247 Million of Binance Hack Funds

North Korean-linked hackers have moved at least $247 million from the $6.4 billion Binance theft into Bitcoin mixing services, according to Elliptic. The mixing uses coinjoins to obscure the trail.

The FBI has attributed the October theft to the TraderTraitor group. Elliptic said almost all the recent mixing was coordinated by one individual who refuses to block such funds. On November 17 the attackers shifted about 488,000 ETH into new addresses before bridging to Bitcoin.

Roughly $2.85 billion of the stolen crypto has been frozen. Another $2.35 billion remains in theft-linked addresses, including 18,270 bitcoin that has not moved since the hack.

Binance has said it will cover customer losses. Little of the funds has been cashed out so far.

Elliptic reported the mixing accelerated in mid-November.

The biggest opportunities in crypto right now are paperwork:

1. build the list of crypto money people are owed and have not claimed

FTX began paying out about $900 million on 31 July. Anyone with an approved claim who has not finished signing up with a payout provider within six months of that date may lose it. That is the end of January. Roughly 34,000 bitcoin at Mt. Gox is still waiting to be handed out, the trustee blames unfinished creditor paperwork, and the deadline just moved to 31 Oct 2027. New York made KuCoin refund $16.7 million to 177,800 customers, and one claims tracker shows that window open until February 2029.

First version: one page. Every open payout, who qualifies, the deadline, the official link. Check it weekly. You never file for anyone, never ask for a login, never take a percentage. The people who do are the scam.

2. build the moving-out service for europeans whose exchange is closing their account

Binance has told users in France, Italy, Spain and Poland that their accounts close on 31 Dec. From 29 Nov it takes 0.025% of whatever is left each month, or 10 USDC if that is more. Deposits are blocked. Withdrawals work. Plenty of these people have never moved a coin off an exchange.

First version: one country, one language, one hour on a call. Download the full trade history first, because that is their tax record. Pick a licensed exchange from the EU's public register. Send a small test, then the rest. They click, you watch. Never take a login, never hold a coin.

3. build the december loss check

In the US you can still sell a coin at a loss, buy it straight back, and keep the tax loss. Stock investors can't. The sale has to happen by 31 Dec to count for 2026. But a bill that cleared a House committee 38-5 in September would end that, and its text reaches back to anything sold after 14 Sept. It has not passed. Almost nobody sitting on a loss knows either half of this.

First version: one person, one hour, one list: which coins sit below what they paid, and by how much. You make the list. Their tax preparer makes the call on the rebuy.

4. build the gift receipt for crypto

When someone is given coins, they take over the giver's purchase price and purchase date. Years later the tax on the sale is worked out from a number only the giver ever knew. December is when crypto gets given.

First version: a card to print and put in the envelope. Date bought, price paid, value on the day it was given, the transaction ID. In the US a gift up to $19,000 a person needs no gift tax return in 2026. US rules. Not tax advice.

5. build the "log in before the state takes it" reminder

Since 1 Jan, California treats crypto left on an exchange like a forgotten bank account. Three years untouched and the exchange has to hand it to the state, after sending a warning. California keeps the coins as coins. Most states that take crypto sell it first and hold the cash.

First version: one page listing every exchange a person ever signed up to, and a yearly reminder to log in and answer any notice. Page two: how to search the state's unclaimed property site for a parent's name. The search is free. Check what your own state counts as activity.

6. build the rate sheet for dollars held as stablecoins

On 21 Oct a US bank regulator confirmed that the company issuing a stablecoin cannot pay you interest for holding it. The app you hold it in still can, and those programs get judged one by one. So PayPal pays a variable 4% on its own coin inside its app, and Robinhood advertises an estimated 7% through a lending program that reviewers found closed to New York and Texas. Nobody keeps the table.

First version: ten US apps. The rate today, who actually pays it, what you must do to get it, which states are left out. Assume none of it is insured like a bank account until you have read otherwise. Say so at the top.

7. build the real-cost test for stablecoin cards

Visa counts more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs. Spending on them reached about $5.2 billion in 2025, up 319%, which is still 0.04% of Visa's volume. The pitch is spend your digital dollars anywhere. The small print is subscription fees, conversion spreads and foreign-transaction fees.

First version: three cards you can get in your country, your own $100 on each, the same five purchases: a coffee, a subscription, something priced in another currency, a cash withdrawal, a refund. Publish what each one really cost. Pay for the cards yourself. No affiliate links.

8. build the rules reader for prediction markets

Nearly 2,000 Polymarket contracts were disputed in the year to May. In April alone 230 markets with more than $1 billion traded went to a vote of token holders. In February a Kalshi Super Bowl market with $47 million traded came down to whether dancing on stage counts as performing. People think they are betting on what happens. They are betting on what the rules say happened.

First version: every Monday, the ten biggest open markets, two sentences each: what exactly counts as yes, and the outcome that would surprise most people holding it. Fine print, not picks.

9. build the "what do you actually own" label for stock tokens

The SEC said in January that many stock tokens sold to ordinary buyers only track a share's price. No vote, no claim on the company. Europe's markets regulator warned that buyers may believe they own shares when they do not. One industry newsletter counted that everything added since September 2025 was issued without the company's consent.

First version: the twenty most-held stock tokens, four answers each, read from the product's own terms: do you get a vote, do you get the dividend, can you swap it for the real share, who owes you if the issuer fails. A label, not a rating.

10. build the crypto worksheet for a divorce

New York rewrote its divorce financial forms this year to ask about crypto, NFTs, wallets and exchange accounts by name. One lawyer told the American Bar Association's journal that under about $100,000 of crypto, the fees to fight over it can come close to the amount. Most couples need a tidy list, not a forensic firm.

First version: one state, one worksheet. Every exchange, every wallet, which statements to download, the value on the date the court uses. You organise what someone already has. You do not hunt hidden coins, and you are not their lawyer.

BITCOIN DEEP MACRO & ON-CHAIN ANALYSIS

Capital & Institutional Flow.  
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded multi-billion-dollar net outflows over both the past seven and thirty trading days, with a string of consecutive negative sessions. At the same time, aggregate stablecoin market capitalization has declined roughly 5.8 percent (approximately $16 billion) over 30 days. Together these figures indicate a contraction in both traditional institutional and on-chain liquidity demand. The market is not receiving fresh capital from the vehicles that previously drove expansion.

Network Valuation & Profit Taking.  
The MVRV ratio near 1.13 means the market is valued only modestly above the aggregate price at which all coins last moved on-chain. This is well below the 1.5 threshold associated with strong expansion and far from historical overheating levels. The Spent Output Profit Ratio near 0.999 shows that coins being spent are realizing returns close to breakeven, consistent with consolidation or mild loss realization rather than widespread profit-taking or full capitulation. Short-term holders (coins moved within the last 155 days) remain below their average cost basis, while the network as a whole has not yet fallen beneath its realized price.

Derivatives & Leverage Squeeze Risks.  
Perpetual funding rates are only modestly positive, annualizing near 6 percent. Open interest is well below its 90-day high. This combination indicates that speculative long positioning is not crowded. The risk of a sharp, leverage-driven squeeze is therefore limited on the upside; any meaningful recovery would need to be driven by spot demand rather than forced short covering.

OUTLOOK & FALSIFICATION CONSTRAINTS  
No prior forecast revision triggers have fired. The standing view remains that Bitcoin continues in Structural Repair until either institutional flows reverse or a structural cost-basis level is decisively broken.  

Fourteen-day risk boundaries:  
Upside invalidation: Three consecutive daily closes above the short-term holder cost basis (~$72,600). This would exit the repair regime.  
Downside invalidation: Sustained trade and closes below the network realized price (~$53,100). This would shift the market into Stress/Capitulation.  

Until one of these levels is cleared, the base case is continued range-bound repair roughly between $55,000 and $64,000.

I think there's a possibility that we're still underestimating how high GameStop can go in this cycle.

One of the more interesting spreads I've been monitoring alongside Bitcoin Dominance is $GME vs (HYG/LQD).

In TradingView:

NYSE:GME/(AMEX:HYG/AMEX:LQD)

For those unfamiliar, $HYG tracks high-yield corporate debt, while $LQD tracks investment-grade corporate debt. When $HYG / $LQD is climbing, it generally signals an increasing willingness within the credit markets to take on more risk by financing less creditworthy borrowers. This can also be indicative of a broader expansion in credit availability and higher risk appetite throughout the financial system, including your neighborhood bank.

What makes this spread combination so powerful for GameStop is that it's already breaking out of a multiyear descending resistance structure against this measure of risk appetite.

Now imagine what happens when the broader credit market begins aggressively repricing risk following a potential peace agreement between the US and Iran.

$HYG / $LQD could accelerate higher while GameStop disproportionately outperforms it.

We're potentially looking at an expansion in Excess Risk Liquidity coinciding with the Float Scarcity Effect.

I don't think people fully appreciate the magnitude of price appreciation this could produce over the next several months.

Where/what is your evidence of a mass exodus of Monero users to Zcash?

I disagree on pointing the problem to Monero's "culture". Every project has a faction within its community to be hardcore maximalist in which you inscribed them as having a cult-like attitude. Yet, this faction is very small and some hardcore maximalists I've seen are also just speculators (longing Monero, trading it for profit) rather than actually using it as a cryptocurrency. None of these maxis decide the future of Monero, nor officially represent Monero in a broader sense.

Also, when exchanges delist Monero, the "cult-like" culture was never a factor taken into consideration in their decision making process. The decision was primarily made due to pressure by governments and regulatory bodies because of their inability to trace Monero, and no leader/founder/board/foundation to pressure, made accountable, directly threaten, corrupt or even arrest like what Satoshi faced during the early days of Bitcoin. 

USDT and TRX are significantly used more and prefered by criminals than Monero but they are still listed in exchanges. Zcash has been used in terrorism financing and money laundering, has its own faction of maxis, yet it is still listed in many exchanges. The only uncommon denominator here is that, Monero has no public facing founder, nor highly influential developers or community members directly tied to the development of Monero to question, arrest or make an example of.

Delisting from CEXs could mean several things moving forward - lesser manipulation, lesser speculation trading and that people who still obtain Monero from other means and channels is because of genuine need and demand. Like the delisting of XMR from Binance a few years ago, dropping XMR to a low in the short term, the price recovered a year later.

Monero doesnt need a Barry Silbert, Michael Saylor, booths in crypto events or a poser speaking about it on stage, or pressure tradfi to wrap it into a financial product like an ETF. Monero simply works as intended and because its already a Product Market Fit, it will continue to be in demand over time.

Long term gain over short term pain.

Coldcard: press reports describe a $112M-scale exploit against a device said to have passed 15 security reviews. If there is a reproducible firmware or supply-chain defect, the damage lands on the self-custody narrative, not on any one token.
Wrong if Coinkite clarifies the figure is an aggregate of historical thefts or traces to seed-phrase compromise rather than firmware, or if no CVE and no emergency firmware release follows.

Ethereum ETFs: a record month of net outflows at roughly 643,000 ETH, including a reported $523M single day, with $ETH trading below $1,650. This is direct, mechanical sell pressure, and it is running decoupled from onchain fundamentals — Glamsterdam work is still progressing.
Wrong if Farside and SoSoValue show sustained net inflows through the first two weeks of December and the 643k cumulative figure cannot be reproduced independently.

Solana: Anza asked mainnet validators to upgrade Agave immediately, posted 23:49Z on November 27. Urgent upgrade requests usually map to a consensus or DoS-class defect, and the speed of validator adoption determines whether block production degrades.
Wrong if Anza confirms it was a routine performance patch, or if stake-weighted adoption stays under 50% for 72 hours with no observable block-time or confirmation anomalies.

Franklin Templeton: its crypto index ETF is set to add HYPE around December 1. Index inclusion brings passive bid plus the signal that an asset can sit inside a traditional wrapper — but the size of the actual bid is bounded by the fund's assets.
Wrong if post-December 1 disclosures show no HYPE, or if inclusion happens while the fund's total AUM is under $100M, in which case the event is real but the mechanism is not.

2126473650757066873.text:
Everyone is asking if the AI labs secretly broke encryption. I went through everything I could find on it. Here's where it stands.

The source is Scott Aaronson, a UT Austin computer scientist who used to work at OpenAI. On Nov 25 he wrote that he's "virtually certain" the labs are sitting on one or more big cryptography results. In the same breath he said he doesn't know what they are, and he's worried the details got mangled passing from person to person.

On Nov 27 he got more specific, and this is the part most people skipped. He says he knows of a big theoretical code-breaking result the labs are about to publish, and that it doesn't put anything in use today in immediate danger. The scary versions (RSA cracked, Bitcoin keys cracked) he takes seriously, but says he has nothing concrete on them.

So what is it? Nobody outside the labs knows. My guess, and it's only a guess:

A new way to factor huge numbers that wins on paper but is too slow to crack a real key. He said the part he's sure about falls well short of fast factoring. Google just put out six AI-written papers and the headline one was that same flavor, factoring math that moved without breaking a single key. And theoretical is the word you use when the math moves and the locks don't.

Second guess is a hit on lattice math, which is what the new quantum-proof encryption is built on. Anthropic did a version of this in July, when Claude badly weakened a signature scheme called HAWK before it was ever deployed.

Does it touch crypto?

If it's factoring, not directly. Bitcoin and Ethereum don't use RSA. They sign with elliptic curves, and the known factoring tricks have never worked on the curves Bitcoin uses.

The one that would hurt is a real attack on elliptic curves. There's no public evidence of that. If it ever happened, the first coins at risk are the ones whose public keys are already visible on chain. Estimates I've seen run from 7 to 8 million BTC.

What's already real is the reaction. The Ethereum Foundation now calls AI a more urgent risk than quantum computers and wants to be on hash-based signatures by 2029. Ledger's CTO says he's heard the rumors and isn't panicking.

My read: something is coming, it'll be a big deal for math, and if Aaronson is right your wallet works the same the day after. The thing to watch is whether the next one is still only theory.

Backpack Exchange（背包交易所 / 背包所） 是一家注重合规的全球加密货币交易所，起源于 Solana 生态，后来扩展到现货、永续合约、借贷、美股证券等产品，并强调统一账户与资金效率。 背景与起源 •创始人兼 CEO 是 Armani Ferrante（前苹果工程师，Solana Anchor 框架创建者）。团队有前 FTX 相关背景（如法律顾问 Can Sun 等）。 •2022 年先推出 Backpack Wallet（自托管钱包，支持 xNFT），并推出 Solana 上热门 NFT 系列 Mad Lads。•2022 年 FTX 崩盘时，团队约 88% 的公司资金被困。 •交易所于 2023 年成立，同年11 月 Beta 上线，早期与 Solana 生态紧密相关，后逐步拓展多链与合规业务。 核心产品与特色 Backpack 主打“一个账户搞定一切”的设计： •现货 + 永续合约（Perps）：支持主流币及部分山寨币。永续资金费多为每小时结算（而非常见的 8 小时）。 •全仓 Cross-Margin 架构：存入资产统一在一个账户，可同时作为交易抵押品和生息资产，无需在不同子账户间转账。 •Auto Lend（自动借贷）：资产自动进入借贷池赚取利息，同时仍可作保证金使用；部分资产（如 SOL）还能叠加质押收益。 •Backpack Securities：在符合条件的地区，可用同一账户交易真实美股/ETF（证券权益，用 USDC 结算），并支持代币化股票在 Solana 上的 1:1 转换与DeFi 交互。 •其他：网格交易机器人、兑换（RFQ 报价）、预测市场相关功能、与钱包深度集成等。 •有 iOS/Android App，需完成 KYC。 监管与合规进展 •持有迪拜VARA 牌照。 •收购原 FTX EU 资产，获得欧盟 MiFID II 相关牌照（受 CySEC 监管），并向原 FTX EU 用户归还资金。 •2026 年 11 月：获得美国 CFTC 批准，注册为指定合约市场（DCM）和衍生品清算组织（DCO），并完成 FCM 等相关注册，为在美国提供合规衍生品（永续等）铺路。这是其近年最重要的监管里程碑之一。 覆盖 150+ 国家，累计交易量官方数据已达数百亿美元级别（不同来源有 100B、400B+ 等表述）。 平台币 BP BP 是 Solana 上的原生代币（总量 10 亿，合约地址：BPxxfRCXkUVhig4HS1Lh7kZqV6SPJhzfEk4x6fVBjPCy）。 •2026 年 3 月 TGE，25% 直接空投给积分用户和 Mad Lads 持有者，无团队/投资者预售分配。 •用途：质押可降低交易手续费、解锁 VIP 权益等。 •特色机制：长期质押（通常需 1 年以上）可在公司 IPO 或收购等退出事件时，选择将 BP 兑换为公司股权（有上限，强调与用户利益对齐）。剩余供应随监管/产品里程碑逐步解锁给用户。 费用（基础档，会随交易量/质押 BP 等下降） •现货：约 0.08% Maker / 0.10% Taker。 •永续：约 0.02% Maker / 0.05% Taker。 •高等级 VIP 可做到 Maker 0%、Taker 更低。USDT/USDC 等稳定币对常有优惠。 简要评价 Backpack 定位是“合规 + 资金效率高”的交易所，尤其适合看重统一账户、自动生息、美股/代币化证券以及 Solana 生态的用户。它从钱包起家，经历 FTX 冲击后转向强监管路线，近期美国衍生品牌照是重要进展。 注意：交易所产品、地区可用性、费用和功能会随监管与业务调整而变化。交易有风险（尤其永续杠杆），使用前建议自行查阅官网（https://t.co/9BS6RZpLje）https://t.co/GqahCyL6bk

【世界最大級の資産運用会社が、HYPEに注目。暗号資産の世界が変わり始めています】

「HYPEって何？」
そう思った方も多いかもしれません。
実は今、暗号資産の世界で見逃せない動きが起きています。

世界的な資産運用会社、フランクリン・テンプルトンが、DeFiの注目銘柄「HYPE」をETFに加える準備を進めているというニュースです。

これ、単にひとつのトークンが注目されたという話ではありません。

60代から暗号資産を学んでいる私にとっては、金融の大きな流れが変わり始めているように感じる出来事です。

今日は初心者の方にもわかるように、順番に整理してみます🍵

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ そもそもフランクリン・テンプルトンって何者？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

まず、会社の規模に注目です。
フランクリン・テンプルトンは、アメリカに本社を置く世界有数の資産運用会社です。
世界中の投資家や機関から預かった資金を運用しており、その規模は約1.5兆ドルともいわれます。

日本円にすると、200兆円を超えるような巨大な規模です。

そんな会社が暗号資産の世界に積極的に関わっている。

数年前まで、暗号資産に対して慎重な姿勢を見せていた大手機関が、今では投資商品の開発を進めているわけです。

ここが今回のニュースの重要なポイントです。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ETFって何がすごいの？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

「ETF」という言葉、聞いたことはありますか？

正式には、上場投資信託といいます。

簡単にいうと、証券取引所で株のように売買できる投資商品です。
例えば、複数の企業の株をひとまとめにしたETFがあります。
暗号資産のETFも同じように、特定の暗号資産の値動きに連動する商品などがあります。

ETFが注目される理由は、投資家にとって参加しやすくなること。

暗号資産を直接購入する場合は、取引所の口座やウォレットの管理などが必要になることがあります。

一方、ETFなら証券口座を通じて投資できる仕組みがあります。

つまり、これまで暗号資産に馴染みがなかった人たちにも、投資の入り口が広がる可能性があるのです。

ただし、ETFの仕組みや対象資産によって違いがあり、HYPEを含む商品が実際にどのような形になるかは確認が必要です。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ そもそもHYPEって何？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ここが今回の主役です。

HYPEは「Hyperliquid（ハイパーリキッド）」というDeFiプラットフォームのネイティブトークンです。

DeFiとは、銀行などの中央機関を介さず、ブロックチェーンを使って金融サービスを提供する仕組みのこと。

Hyperliquidは、分散型取引所（DEX）として知られています。

簡単にいえば、ブロックチェーン上で暗号資産の取引ができるサービスです。
では、なぜHYPEが注目されているのでしょうか？
大きな理由のひとつが、2024年末の大規模なエアドロップです。

エアドロップとは、プロジェクトが利用者などにトークンを配布する仕組みのこと。

Hyperliquidは、これまでプラットフォームを利用していたユーザーなどにHYPEを配布しました。

その規模の大きさは、暗号資産業界でも大きな話題になりました。

さらに特徴的なのが、外部のベンチャーキャピタルから資金調達をせずに成長してきたという点です。

大手投資会社の資金に頼るのではなく、ユーザーやコミュニティを中心に発展してきたプロジェクト。

こうした独自の成長ストーリーも、HYPEが注目される理由のひとつです。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ なぜ今、大手金融機関が暗号資産に注目するのか？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

少し過去を振り返ってみましょう。

2024年1月
アメリカでビットコイン現物ETFが承認。

2024年5月
イーサリアム現物ETFの承認が発表。

この流れによって、暗号資産は一部の熱心な投資家だけのものではなく、伝統的な金融市場でも扱われる資産へと変化し始めました。

そして今、注目される対象はビットコインやイーサリアムだけではなくなっています。

DeFiやブロックチェーン上の金融サービスなど、新しい分野にも機関投資家の関心が広がっています。

今回のHYPEをめぐる動きも、その流れの中で見ると理解しやすいと思います。
つまり、暗号資産の世界では、
「次にどんな技術やプロジェクトが金融市場に受け入れられるのか？」

という新しい競争が始まっているのです。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ 大手が注目すれば、HYPEは安全なの？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ここは誤解してはいけないところです。

大手資産運用会社が注目したからといって、HYPEの価格が必ず上昇するわけではありません。
また、ETFへの採用準備や申請が進んだからといって、承認や実際の販売が確定したわけでもありません。

大手機関が調査・検討することには意味があります。

しかし、それは価格上昇の保証でも、安全性のお墨付きでもありません。

暗号資産には、

・価格が大きく変動するリスク
・規制が変更されるリスク
・技術的な問題やハッキングのリスク
・プロジェクト自体が成長しないリスク

こうした危険があります。

だからこそ、ニュースの見出しだけで飛びつかず、何が決まり、何がまだ準備段階なのかを確認することが大切です。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ 60代の私が今回のニュースから感じたこと
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

正直、私も暗号資産を始めた頃は、
「こんなもの、本当に大丈夫なの？」
「怪しい話ではないの？」
と思っていました。

でも、学び続けていると、少しずつ見方が変わってきます。

今、起きているのは単なる価格の上げ下げだけではありません。

世界的な金融機関がブロックチェーン技術に関心を持ち、新しい投資の仕組みを作ろうとしている。

これは、数年後の金融の姿にも関係してくるかもしれません。

もちろん、今すぐHYPEを買う必要はありません。

私が大切だと思うのは、まず知ること。

そして、なぜ大手企業が動いているのか、その背景を理解することです。
60代からでも、学ぶことはできます。
知らないから怖い。
でも、知れば冷静に判断できるようになる。
私はそう思っています🌱

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ 今日のまとめ
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

今回のポイントは5つ。

① フランクリン・テンプルトンは世界有数の資産運用会社。
② ETFは証券口座から投資できる上場投資信託。
③ HYPEはDeFiプラットフォーム「Hyperliquid」のトークン。

④ 暗号資産への機関投資家の関心は、ビットコインやイーサリアム以外にも広がりつつある。

⑤ 大手が注目しても価格上昇や安全性が保証されるわけではない。
暗号資産の世界は、私たちが思っている以上に速いスピードで変化しています。

でも、すべてを理解する必要はありません。

ひとつずつ知識を増やしていけばいい。

情報を持っておくことは、将来の自分を守ることにもつながると思います。

猫笔刀加密日报 · 2026.11.28 周六

1、今日一句话总结

67 个主流 USDT 交易对里有 45 个在涨，BTC 却跌 1.05%，最新 59932 美元，恐惧贪婪指数 10。

2、市场温度计

温度在冰点恒温，今日 10，从今天往回数七天是 10、12、11、13、11、11、11，最高摸到 13，一次都没爬出去。

可仓位一点都不冰，全体账户多空比 2.97，多头账户占 74.8%，大户那边持仓多空比 2.06 也还是多。

这两个比值不是一个尺子，一个按账户数、一个按持仓量，方向一致就够看了：怕归怕，手上都还是多。

3、今日核心行情

BTC 59932 美元，24 小时跌 1.05%，全天在 58792 到 62248 之间晃，振幅 5.88%。

6 万这个整数关又丢了。

ETH 1662.88 美元跌 1.56%，ETH/BTC 0.02775 再跌 0.54%，以太这一根还是被压着的那一头。

广度反倒挺好看，67 个样本 45 涨 22 跌，上涨占比 67.2%，涨幅榜首 PORTAL 涨 228.77%，成交 6330 万美元。

小票在开派对，大饼在守灵。

板块各过各的，量子抗性涨 6.68%，ZK 涨 6.33%，期权那头跌 7.11%，预测市场跌 7.09%。

全网市值 2081.7 十亿美元，24 小时缩水 3.49%，BTC 占比反倒升到 57.78%，不是有人往大饼里搬钱，是山寨跌得比它狠。

4、今日最重要的消息

1、KuCoin 公告 11 月 30 日下午 4 点起停掉全部 XMR 现货，MEXC 这个月早些时候已经停了现货、把永续也一起下架。

XMR 周四那一刀收盘跌 10.5% 到 11%，从 525 的高点砸到 447 只用了五个小时，报道说这是 6 月 4 日以来最狠的一根。

今天这根也不省心，最新 407.53 美元，24 小时又没了 10.95%。

2、另一头 Grayscale 还在往 Zcash 上加码，ZEC 今天涨 7.82%，报 734.85 美元，一边把门关上，一边把椅子搬过来。

3、摩根大通 11 月 26 日的研报说，Strategy 的 mNAV 在 11 月 25 日跌到 0.88 倍，破了 6 月底的旧低。

市场给它的估值只有它手上 BTC 的 88%，折价 12%，这家投行把这叫比特币投降。

隐私币这碗饭不是被市场砸的，是公告掐的。交易所省下合规的麻烦，做市商在五个小时里赚了波动的价差，剩下流动性那口缺口，摊到还抱着仓位的人头上。

投降这词我不太买账，0.88 倍（八八折）说的是没人再愿意为「拿币的公司」付溢价，愿意溢价买的人早跑光了，这跟币价见底是两码事，没啥好多说的。

5、今日值得关注的信号

先说钱在往外走，脚步没那么急了。美国现货 BTC ETF 从 11 月 20 日到 27 日这五个交易日净流出 19.6 亿美元，五天全是负的。

我算了一下，头一天 6.69 亿最狠，25 号还反弹到 4.53 亿（比前一天翻了一倍），最后一天只剩 4100 万，前三天加起来是后两天的三倍。

卖压在往下走，但不是一路直下。

链上也没人抢跑道，https://t.co/5Zu7f9GKIW 那个节点上待确认的还有 66100 笔，手续费 1 sat/vB，全网一天只走 55 万笔转账。

第二个信号是合约端压根没慌，BTC 资金费率还挂在 +0.0083%，年化 9.11%，账户里 74.8% 是多头，每 8 小时给空头结一次利息。

我跟你们说，现货在割肉，合约在加价抱着，这两拨钱不是一拨人，真挤干净的时候费率该翻负、多空比该掉到 1 附近，现在离那儿还远。

多头这个姿势是要付钱的。年化 9.11% 摊到 100 万刀的仓上，一年光利息就是 9 万多，币价再跌 1% 又亏 1 万，账越抱越沉。

总持仓名义 58.9 亿美元，一小时还多了 0.26%，这个数含着价格波动，不能当成谁在偷偷加仓。

跌幅榜首 INIT 一天没了 37.48%，涨幅榜首那个翻了两倍多，同一天里有人在涨幅榜那头接刀，有人在跌幅榜这头认赔。

可场外那 19.6 亿的窟窿还在，热闹的都是场内的存量。

7、猫笔刀今日观点

美股那边纳指 100 涨 2.61%，英伟达转涨 0.80%，VIX 掉 11.16%，同一晚上黄金还涨 3.23%，股和金属手拉手，币圈站在门外。美元指数还挂在 104.01，美债十年 4.94%，便宜钱没回来，涨的是对降息的期待。

这种错位我以前也见过几回，AI 那边的钱后头是订单和资本开支，币圈这头是 58.9 亿美元的合约名义，一边是营收，一边是借来的。

……

我觉得这一轮不是底，是换手换到一半。现货那头的卖压在衰减，合约这头的多头还没认输，价格卡在中间，就是让多头继续交学费。

我这人有个毛病，看见费率还是正的就想再等等，等着等着就等到针上了。

如果后头几天 ETF 那条线翻正、费率也翻负，那我估计就差不多该换个说法了，现在喊底，是在替别人的仓位壮胆。

反过来也一样，BTC 要是硬砸破今天的 58792 低点，而多头占比还挂在 70% 以上，那就不是换手，是排队割肉。

恐惧贪婪 10，多头占比 74.8%，怕的人和扛的人不是同一批，我怀疑先撑不住的是扛的那批。

今早就这些吧。

TSMC's CoWoS math for 2027 points to an unavoidable structural spillover—opening Intel's ($INTC) cleanest side door into hyperscaler AI silicon.

DIGITIMES projects 26M high-end cloud AI accelerators in 2027, with TSMC holding an 85.8% packaging share (54.6% CoWoS-L) on 2.165M wafers of customer demand (~180k/month). Even with Nomura modeling an 80% jump in TSMC CoWoS output to 1.81M wafers, that still leaves a ~355k-wafer annual shortfall.

Where that overflow lands—and what it actually means for $INTC ($57.40, ~$305B cap, -59.7% off its $142.35 peak):

1/ OSATs capture the near-term wave; Intel plays the large-package wedge
In 2027, ASE ($ASX) and Amkor ($AMKR) absorb the bulk of immediate CoWoS-like overflow—466k combined wafers (5.5x YoY)—across server CPUs like AMD Venice and Nvidia Vera. Intel's EMIB wins target hyperscaler ASIC cost and reticle limits instead: partial AWS Trainium 3 adoption on EMIB-M (MIM capacitors) in 1H27, followed by Google TPU v9 on EMIB-T (TSV vertical power delivery) in 1H28.

2/ Attractive unit economics, distant P&L scale
CFO David Zinsner targets ~40% gross margins and ~30% operating margins on advanced packaging with far lower capital intensity than front-end fabs—a multi-billion-dollar annual opportunity per anchor customer. Yet Intel's own roadmap puts full-scale packaging revenue in 2029, not 2027.

3/ Packaging alone cannot offset front-end cash burn yet
In Q3 2026, Intel Foundry posted a -$1.9B operating loss on just $411M of external revenue, while management already guided negative free cash flow for 2027 as 18A/14A CapEx climbs above $20B. Meanwhile, TSMC is developing its own EMIB-like organic bridge (with Kinsus), and Nomura explicitly flagged EMIB-T maturity as a key 2028 execution risk.

EMIB gives $INTC a credible, capital-light wedge back into Amazon and Google's AI supply chain—something leading-edge wafer foundry hasn't unlocked yet. Near-term packaging earnings leverage still belongs to $ASX and $AMKR, while Intel's EMIB thesis remains a 2028–29 execution call.

2126476379659309198.text:
$NVDA has a more interesting problem than whether the AI rebound survives Monday.

Its latest earnings release puts quarterly revenue at 115.8B and GAAP gross margin at 74.8%. Management expects 130B of revenue next quarter, but gross margin guidance falls to 71-72%.

At the midpoint, gross profit rises from 86.62B to 92.95B. That is approximately 7.3% growth against 12.3% revenue growth. The extra week in the upcoming fiscal quarter makes the comparison even less straightforward. On a simple 13 versus 14 week basis, revenue per week rises only about 4.2%.

This is why a product transition can look spectacular in revenue headlines while the underlying economics deserve a much closer look. The incremental gross profit is around 6.33B, and guided operating expenses are 11B versus 9.2B. That leaves roughly 4.53B of incremental operating profit on this simplified bridge, before taxes and other items.

The market is also pricing a business with enormous exposure to a single spending cycle. Data center sales account for about 93% of reported quarterly revenue. The relevant question is not merely whether customers want more GPUs. It is whether those customers can finance deployments, energize facilities and earn enough from the resulting capacity to keep placing orders.

At a reported 3.6T market capitalization, annualizing the latest quarterly GAAP net income of 65.3B gives an illustrative multiple of 13.8x. That is not a forward consensus P/E, and it assumes an unusually strong quarter repeats. A 25% haircut to that annualized earnings base raises the multiple to 18.4x. Neither figure establishes fair value.

Watch the next filing for receivables, customer concentration, inventory, purchase commitments and cash conversion. A shipment is not the same thing as a customer earning a return on its investment. Nor does a buyback authorization guarantee that the share count will fall by the full authorized amount.

Friday's reported rebound in the stock was modest relative to the broader technology rally. I would not treat that as a technical entry signal without a verified closing-price series. The next test is whether the new product ramp produces cash and margins consistent with the revenue guidance. If margin falls below guidance or receivables materially outpace sales, the apparent valuation discount deserves another look.

暴落で藁にもすがりたいホルダーたちの心理に刺さるのだろうけど、冷静に読むとどうにも論理が破綻しているような。

「SpaceXとAnthropicの史上最大IPO、Meta・Alphabetの巨額増資で現金が吸い上げられたから暴落した。だがAnthropic上場で換金売りは終了、現金が戻って急反発する」というのが彼の主張。

でも、彼自身がいう「巨額の資金調達＝市場からの現金吸い上げ」という前提をそのまま使うだけで、この結論は自壊する。

① OpenAIという同規模の巨象Anthropicに匹敵する評価額1.25兆ドル規模のOpenAIが控えており、SECへのS-1非公開提出もすでに報じられている。
本当に彼の理屈が正しいなら、次の巨大バスが並んでいると誰もが知っているのに、なぜ今ここで買い上がれるのか。

② Metaの追加増資（投稿自身の矛盾）
彼自身が「2027年初頭からさらに最大600億ドル」と書いておきながら、結論で「強制売りは終わった」と結ぶのは完全に自己矛盾。

③ ほかにも控える需給と金利の重石12月のSpaceXロックアップ解除、来年も続くAI関連の起債ラッシュ、12月FOMCの利上げ観測と、下押し材料は目白押し。

④ 資金の誤認と因果のすり替えそもそもIPOで吸い上げた現金は市場に戻らず企業の設備投資に消える。「資金回帰の証拠」とした月曜のNasdaqも、NvidiaのCEO復帰報道という個別材料が引き金だっただけ。

結局、今そこにあるのは「大底を打った強気相場の始まり」でもなんでもなく、
次の巨額供給までの空白期間を狙った、短期筋のボラの激しい遊び場にすぎないのでは？

9割の事実を並べて、1割の因果を都合よくすり替える。

【Market Atlas Weekly｜11月24〜27日】

日経平均2,274円高。底打ちは本物か？

先週の日経平均は7.70％下落。今週は4.03％上昇の58,711.11円です。反発を「価格×商い×広がり」と信用市場から振り返ります。

■ 価格｜反発の中にも大きな揺れ

24日に2,207.98円高、25日に1,633.01円安、26日に487.54円高、27日に1,211.95円高。金曜は水曜の下落分を取り戻し、高値に近い水準で引けました。TOPIXも週間＋3.84％。ただし日経平均は25日線60,579.42円を3.08％、TOPIXも25日線を1.70％下回っています。短期反発と中期反転は別です。

■ 商い｜営業日数と資金集中

日本市場は祝日を挟み4営業日。東証プライムの週間売買代金は約30.18兆円、出来高は約101.52億株です。一日平均で比較すると前週比それぞれ−6.27％、−1.45％。金曜は商いが増えましたが、売買代金の約23％をキオクシア1社が占め、全体の増加分の約85％が同社分でした。

金曜日の同社終値は8,450円（＋688円、＋8.86％）。NVIDIAとの技術実証や指数連動型の需給が注目されます。商用受注や買い入れ実額が確認されたわけではなく、売買代金も純流入額ではありません。

■ 広がり｜売り一色から改善

週間の値上がり銘柄比率は銘柄×日の延べで58.4％。25日に日経平均が急落した一方、993銘柄が上昇しました。指数と市場全体には差があります。週間の業種騰落率は日次の複利近似で30業種が上昇。非鉄＋7.34％、電気機器＋6.26％が上位。ただし25日騰落レシオは87.90％とまだ100未満です。

■ 米国｜急反発、ただし短縮取引

11/27のダウは50,774.94（週＋5.46％）、S&P500は7,297.49（＋5.60％）、NASDAQは24,129.50（＋6.68％）。Russell 2000も＋6.53％です。SOXも週＋9.25％。感謝祭翌日は短縮取引で、通常日と出来高を単純比較できません。

■ 信用・資金市場｜株価の反発だけでは見えないもの

11/25時点の米SOFRは3.95％、上位1％の境界は4.03％。差は8bpで前日と変わりません。広範な資金調達停止は確認できませんが、低格付けCCC社債の信用スプレッドは前週末から15bp拡大。高格付け企業との違いに注目です。金曜反発前のデータですので信用不安の解消は未確認です。

米現物ビットコインETFは11/25まで7営業日連続流出、計30.52億ドル。世界の金ETFも11/20週は暫定で約21.49億ドル流出。一方、米MMFは11/18〜24に政府系が約50.1億ドル増加しました。期間と範囲が異なるため、直接の資金移動とは言えません。

日本も前週の海外投資家は現物売り・先物買い。今週の実際の投資主体別動向は次回公表を待ちます。

■ 来週の観察

①今週高値59,262円台を突破し、6万円・25日線を回復できるか。

②値上がり銘柄の広がりと一日平均の商いが継続するか。

③57,447円、さらに56,503円・前週末56,437円を下回らないか。

④信用スプレッド、短期資金調達、ETFフローに改善が伴うか。

今週は「反発の兆し」から「短期反発の確認」へ。ただし、次は継続確認です。中期反転を急いで決めつけず、相場の流れを観察し続けます。

From $265 to $317 — Dell rode two roller coasters in one week. On Saturday, November 28 (Singapore time), I lined up Dell's closes for the week and closed the books on it.

Friday, November 27 half-day close (1:00 p.m. ET): Dell closed at $316.96 (+6.70%, +$19.90), open $307.03, intraday high $317.50, intraday low $297.10. Source: Finnhub daily candles and the stockanalysis daily table, multiple sources agreeing, Friday, November 27 1:00 p.m. ET half-day close; one other source reported $312.24, and I went with $316.96, where Finnhub and stockanalysis agree.

I lined up the week: Monday, November 23 closed at $334.91 (+20.46%); Tuesday, November 24 closed at $295.28 (-11.83%); Wednesday, November 25 opened at $267.57, hit an intraday low of $265.00, and closed at $297.06 (+0.60%); Friday, November 27 closed at $316.96. Friday's close sits 5.4% below Monday's close (my calculation) and 19.6% above Wednesday's intraday low of $265.00 (my calculation), with a 5-session gain of +1.23%. One earnings report, three prices in one week — I look at the close first, then the intraday low.

I split Dell's week into three books. The first is "orders": an AI backlog of $132.3 billion. The second is "revenue": third-quarter revenue of $54.94 billion, up 103% year over year, adjusted EPS of $9.45 against an expected $6.59, and AI server revenue of $22.03 billion, up 291%. The third is "profit": a non-GAAP gross margin of 21.2%, only 0.1 percentage points above last year. Tuesday, November 24 fell 11.83% because the market did the "profit" book first; Wednesday, November 25 climbed from $265 to $297 because the market re-did "orders plus revenue"; Friday, November 27 gained another 6.70% because the Black Friday rebound remembered AI servers. The same week brought one more item: the Financial Times reported on Thursday, November 26 that Nvidia asked Dell and Supermicro to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia — Dell, the company asked to pause shipments, rose 6.70% the same day. A shipment pause and a rally can both be true. I sorted out "pause shipments" from "ban chip sales" first, then talked about how much revenue is at stake.

I left myself two levels to watch: whether $317 (near Friday's close) holds on Monday, November 30, and whether rising memory costs squeeze the "profit" book further — "orders" and "revenue" already answered, "profit" only half-answered.

How many points did the "profit" book score in your AI holdings? I did the three-book check first, then talked about rebound versus reversal.

2126483755091038674.text:
Funny how the “AI infrastructure boom” that was sold as inevitable progress turned into a credit mess the moment the maturity walls came into view.

CoreWeave’s unsecured notes are trading in the mid-70s cents on the dollar with yields pushing toward 18%. The Nasdaq-100 is still roughly 10% off its late-October highs after a month of violent swings concentrated in semiconductors, memory, and neoclouds. Meanwhile the Fed’s own stability report flagged AI-related debt as about 31% of nonfinancial investment-grade issuance this year, with public outstanding advanced-computing debt over $1.1 trillion and far larger off-balance-sheet leases and take-or-pay commitments sitting on top.

Not saying anyone engineered the overbuild. But when the same handful of hyperscalers, chip vendors, and private-credit funds keep underwriting each other’s circular deals, and the Fed is still the backstop that can lower the cost of money whenever the stress gets too visible, it starts to look less like organic growth and more like a controlled shakeout. Weaker, heavily leveraged players get squeezed. Capacity consolidates onto fewer, better-connected balance sheets. The survivors become even more dependent on the same capital sources that just got cheaper.

The technology can still work. The financing just happens to fail in a way that transfers the assets and the control. Happened with railroads, telecom, and the last couple of tech cycles. Coincidence that the people who flagged the private-credit concentration in data centers a month ago are now watching the exact scenario play out while the usual names stay quiet on who ultimately holds the residual risk?

Just an observation.

就算你看多半导体，我也不建议用三倍杠杆去赌

上周四收盘到今天
$SOXX 跌了2.8%
$SOXL 跌了19.3%

按"三倍"的直觉应该跌8%左右，多出来的11个点，全耗在来回震荡里

每天是这样的
11/20 SOXX -10.5%，SOXL -31.8%
11/23 SOXX +13.6%，SOXL +39.9%
11/24 SOXX -8.3%，SOXL -24.6%
11/25 SOXX -0.5%，SOXL -1.8%
11/27 SOXX +4.8%，SOXL +14.2%

最直观的是前两天
SOXX先跌10.5%再涨13.6%，两天净涨1.6%
SOXL先跌31.8%再涨39.9%，两天净亏4.6%

原因很简单
三倍杠杆是每天重新算三倍，不是一段时间的三倍
跌了31.8%之后，要涨46.6%才回本
第二天SOXX涨13.6%，SOXL涨39.9%，补不回来

换个整数的例子
指数先跌20%再涨25%，回到原点，不赚不亏
三倍杠杆是先跌60%再涨75%，最后亏30%

方向看对了，路径不对，照样会亏
单边上涨的时候三倍杠杆能跑出超过三倍的收益，震荡的时候就反过来一路磨损

麻烦在于，很多人恰恰是在最震荡的时候冲进去的
10月有一周SOXL单周流入61亿美元，创了纪录
有两周合计流入超过90亿美元，也是纪录
韩国散户10月净买了29.7亿美元SOXL，占他们当月美股净买入的一半以上
到了11月初那一周，SOXL又成了全市场赎回最多的ETF，流出9.31亿

10月28日到今天，SOXX跌了23%，SOXL跌了66%

Direxion自己的产品说明里也写得很清楚：SOXL只追求单日三倍，是给短线交易用的工具，持有超过一天，收益可能和三倍差很远

2126481203251593219.text:
OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960 by five countries, including Iraq and Venezuela.

Per a Reuters exclusive citing ten sources, Washington spent this year nudging both of them to consider leaving, and blocked Venezuela from paying its OPEC dues.

Why those two? The US has unusual financial leverage over both:
- Venezuela: after Maduro's capture in January, the US controls access to state funds held in a US-controlled account
- Iraq: its oil revenue runs through a New York Fed account dating back to the 2003 war

The motive, per Reuters, is that Washington wants US majors pumping more oil in both countries without OPEC limits getting in the way. Exxon and Chevron are planning big investments in Iraq.

What happened next:
- Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly persuaded the administration this summer to stop pressing on Venezuela
- Iraq's PM raised quitting at a government meeting, but the oil ministry talked him into staying and possibly asking for a higher quota
- The State Department says OPEC wasn't raised with Venezuela by high-level officials, and that Iraq talks focused on energy infrastructure, not OPEC

The context: OPEC is down to 11 members after losing Qatar, Ecuador, Angola and, this year, the UAE. "The risk of OPEC fracture is rising," says Alpine Macro's Dan Alamariu.

Neither country has left. But if Washington keeps pushing members toward the exit, how long does OPEC's control over supply last?
