Bitcoin’s 90-day correlation with gold just hit a record high, yet @galaxyhq says the bear market is still ongoing.

Galaxy Research showed the 90-day correlation peaked at 0.56 on October 22, breaking the previous high of 0.50 from November 2020. By November 23 it stood at 0.54, with the 30-day reading at 0.59. For most of the first half of 2026 the correlation sat near 0.1. The average from 2020 through 2025 was only 0.11.

At the same time, Galaxy withdrew its earlier view that the bear market ended in June (not good for HODLers 🙄). Bitcoin closed the week of November 22 near $61,104 after seven straight weekly losses. The firm is watching the June 30 closing low of $58,525; a break below it would open the door to materially lower levels. The current drawdown is already 412 days old and Bitcoin is down roughly 53% from its October 2025 high, which is still milder than the 77–93% declines of prior cycles, and painful non-the-less.

Higher correlation with gold does not, by itself, change the price action. It does change the conversation around what Bitcoin is trading with and what it means for Bitcoin as a store of value.

Thanksgiving is over. Wall Street is back — but only for half a day.

US markets were closed on Thursday 26/11 for Thanksgiving. Yesterday, Friday, they opened at 9:30 ET and shut early at 13:00 ET — a shortened session where thin volume can turn a small move into a big one.

Thursday night futures were pointing up: Dow +303 points (+0.6%), S&P 500 +0.8%, Nasdaq 100 +0.7%, as global markets followed Wednesday's wild reversal.

And what a Wednesday it was. The Dow fell more than 1,100 points intraday — then closed UP 0.33% at 50,183, holding the 50,000 level. The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2%, even breaking below 7,000, before closing down just 0.25% at 7,183. The Nasdaq dropped as much as 4.64% and closed down 0.62% at 23,586. The Nasdaq 100 even touched bear-market territory inside the session. The VIX closed at 28.29 after spiking to 34.95.

And the half-day delivered. The Dow jumped 597.69 points (+1.19%) to close at 50,780.64 — its best week since October 2022, up 5.5% for the week. The S&P 500 gained 115.56 points (+1.61%) to 7,298.34, up 5.6% for the week. The Nasdaq surged 543.70 points (+2.31%) to 24,129.50 — its best week in seven months, up 6.7%. The Russell 2000 added 1.7% on the day, 6.5% for the week. The VIX collapsed 14% to 24.17, down from 28.29 on Wednesday. Gold jumped about 2% to $3,674.60 an ounce, rebounding hard from its one-year low near $3,515. Nvidia finished up 0.8% after falling nearly 3% early in the session.

Bitcoin was the odd one out: it slipped back below $60,000, trading around $59,850, after roughly $7 billion in options expired on Deribit. Stocks celebrated. Crypto did not get the invitation.

Oil rose after Houthi forces in Yemen attacked a Saudi port on the Red Sea. Copper is up about 3% from an 11-month low. The S&P 500 is still down 5.2% for November through Wednesday's close — and S&P has put Nvidia on negative credit watch.

A half-day session, thin volume, a market that just survived its wildest week of the month — and Friday closed green across the board. Was that the real turn, or just a holiday-thin bounce before Monday's real test?

The harsh truth most people won't tell you about the economy right now.

I believe we're heading towards a financial crisis that has the potential to be worse than 2008, and most people are financially unprepared for it.

Take a close look at the chart below.

The Benner Cycle, based on a theory dating back to 1875, identifies specific periods of prosperity, financial panic and economic hardship.

Notice these two years:

> 2007: A year of high prices and a time to sell.
> 2026: The exact same classification.
Following the 2007 market peak, the S&P 500 lost approximately 57% of its value.

I'm not basing my economic outlook on a 150-year-old chart, but the similarities become interesting when you understand what's happening in the financial system today.

Bitcoin, gold and stocks have all experienced significant selling pressure recently.

In 2008, even gold was being liquidated because institutions needed liquidity to cover losses elsewhere.

The biggest problem wasn't the housing market itself. It was how much of the financial system was exposed to it.

Today, look at what's happening with AI.

Hundreds of billions of dollars are being borrowed and invested into infrastructure based on expectations of future revenue.

Banks, private credit funds, institutional investors and technology companies are becoming increasingly interconnected through these investments.

What happens if AI companies fail to generate enough revenue to justify their valuations and service their debt?

Lenders start taking losses, institutions reduce their exposure, leveraged positions get liquidated, and the selling spreads to markets that had absolutely nothing to do with the initial problem.

Meanwhile, hedge fund leverage is at its highest recorded level since 2013, government debt is elevated, and persistent inflation could limit the ability of central banks to rescue the economy.

The last thing you want in this environment is to be financially overexposed.

If you're looking for defensive exposure, start researching these sectors and assets:

> Consumer staples: people still need food and essential products during a recession.

> Healthcare: medical needs don't disappear when the economy collapses.

> Utilities: electricity, water and essential infrastructure remain necessary.

> Short-term government bonds: preserve liquidity while generating interest.

> Gold: long-term monetary diversification, despite short-term volatility.

Focus on companies with low debt, strong free cash flow and consistent demand rather than speculative valuations.

And for those heavily invested in crypto, holding 15 different altcoins doesn't mean you're diversified.

Start monitoring corporate credit spreads, unemployment, corporate defaults and bank lending conditions.

These indicators will tell you far more about the health of the economy than your favorite influencer drawing lines on a Bitcoin chart.

US high-yield credit spreads recently stood around 3.77%, compared to nearly 22% at the peak of the 2008 crisis. A sustained increase would be a serious warning that financial stress is spreading.

In the meantime:

> Build enough cash reserves to cover 6-12 months of living expenses.

> Reduce your exposure to leverage and high-interest debt.

> Develop multiple sources of income.

> Keep capital available to accumulate quality assets at distressed valuations.

The biggest mistake you can make right now is assuming that everything will eventually recover simply because it has in the past.

Not every company survives a recession, and not every cryptocurrency survives a bear market.

Imagine being forced to sell your assets to survive while someone else is accumulating those exact same assets at a fraction of their previous value.

You don't want to be on the wrong side of that transaction.

You better wake up before it's too late.

The Case Against a $1.6 Million Bitcoin
Bitcoin's price targets have grown steadily more audacious, and Matt Hougan's suggestion that $1.6 million by 2036 may even be "conservative" deserves skepticism. 
No analysis a prudent adult would accept can justify a number like that, and the reasoning behind it rests on assumptions that investors should question.
Start with what a price target actually demands. Reaching $1.6 million would require Bitcoin's market capitalization to exceed tens of trillions of dollars, rivaling or surpassing the total value of gold. Such projections typically assume Bitcoin will be adopted as a global store of value, a status it has not yet achieved despite more than fifteen years of existence. Forecasts built on "if adoption continues" are narratives, not analysis.
The concept of prudent investing matters here. 
A prudent investor weighs not just potential returns but the quality of the underlying asset: cash flows, earnings, or tangible utility. 
Bitcoin produces no income. Its value depends entirely on what the next buyer is willing to pay, which makes it vulnerable to shifts in sentiment, regulation, and technology.

That last point is especially relevant today. Artificial intelligence is still in its infancy, and the digital landscape is evolving rapidly. Placing significant trust in any single digital product, particularly one with no intrinsic backing, invites risk that cannot be easily quantified. Technologies that seem dominant can be displaced, and a decade-long forecast ignores that uncertainty.

Consider an analogy. Millions of people buy Powerball tickets, fully aware that the odds are roughly one in hundreds of thousands. They do it for entertainment, accepting the loss as the price of a thrill. 
Bitcoin deserve similar treatment: a recreational allocation, money one can afford to lose, rather than a serious cornerstone of a retirement portfolio.

None of this means Bitcoin will fail or that its supporters are dishonest. It has defied critics before. 
But extraordinary price targets require extraordinary evidence, and a bold prediction is not evidence. Until Bitcoin demonstrates durable utility and stability, investors would be wise to treat $1.6 million as a hope rather than a plan.

Notice something strange about the Bitcoin influencer ecosystem?

Almost none of the big Bitcoin podcasters, YouTubers, or X accounts ever mention Michael Saylor’s 2000 SEC accounting fraud.

A sitting public-company CEO personally signed restated financials, settled federal antifraud charges for $8.63M ($8.28M disgorgement + $350K penalty), and remains under a permanent SEC fraud injunction—yet in thousands of hours of softball Bitcoin interviews, virtually the only prominent host who ever pressed him on his record was an independent journalist, Laura Shin.

That silence tells you everything you need to know about "Bitcoin influencers":

• Access over accountability: Ask one hard question about 2000 SEC fraud, the $40M D.C. tax evasion settlement, or $MSTR’s 10-K filings, and you never get the Saylor interview, keynote slot, or retweet again.

• Engagement over truth: Saylor pumps the "number go up" dopamine loop. Challenging him kills clicks, triggers his fanboys, and shrinks the monetization funnel.

• Corporate capture in real time: People who preach "don’t trust, verify" all day suddenly forget how to verify a billionaire’s SEC history the moment he starts buying Bitcoin with other people’s money.

If an influencer only repeats Saylor’s slogans like "Digital Credit" and "going up forever" while hiding a documented fraud record from their own audience, they aren’t Bitcoin educators.

They’re PR agents.

Stop outsourcing your thinking to podcasters chasing access. Read the filings—and hold your own keys.

$6.8 billion expired. Nothing happened. On Saturday, November 28 (Singapore time), I closed the books on this expiry.

At 4:00 p.m. Singapore time on Friday, November 27 (08:00 UTC), about 110,254.8 BTC in options expired on Deribit — roughly $6.8 billion in notional value, about 25.4% of all Deribit open interest. Source: Decrypt, citing CryptoQuant. Calls totaled 61,803.8 BTC against 48,451.0 BTC in puts. Max pain sat at $70,000; settlement came in at about $61,600, 12.0% below max pain (my calculation). Before settlement the Deribit index stood near $60,691, about 15% below max pain.

I lined up Friday's prices: Bitcoin traded near $61,000 ahead of settlement, then dropped below $59,000 later in the day, with a Friday high near $62,249 and a low near $58,792 — the low sat about 4.6% below settlement (my calculation). At 09:37 Singapore time on Saturday, November 28, Bitcoin traded near $60,195 (Finnhub snapshot), down 0.93% over 24 hours and about 2.3% below settlement (my calculation); down 24.25% over one month and 30.64% year to date (Finnhub). Ether traded near $1,669, against a November 27 close of $1,722.90 — about 3.1% lower (my calculation).

I split this expiry into two books. The first is "options": max pain at $70,000 is the price where option sellers are most comfortable, not a forecast — settlement at $61,600 left most call buyers with nothing. And $6.8 billion is notional value, not money changing hands: Deribit settles in cash, no coins move — an expiry is not someone selling $6.8 billion of Bitcoin. The put/call open-interest ratio of 0.89 ran above October's 0.55, so more traders bought protection than in October. The second book is "spot": Friday's $58,792–$62,249 range, a swing of more than $3,000 — the expiry itself did not crash the market; the drop came from funds rotating after US stocks opened: stocks and gold rose while Bitcoin fell, and Bitcoin slipped below $59,000 during Friday's session.

I left myself three levels to watch: the next big one lands on December 25, about 165,000 BTC, roughly $10 billion — bigger than this one, so expiries are a monthly event, not a one-day event; whether Friday's ETF flow data ends this run of net outflows; and whether $60,000 holds before the Fed meeting on December 8–9. The Fed's quiet period runs November 28 to December 10.

Did you sort out "max pain" from "price forecast" in your own Bitcoin position? I sorted that out first, then checked my cost basis — $55,000, $60,000 or $75,000 — before deciding whether this is a recovery or a chase. US stocks rest over the weekend while crypto keeps trading, so liquidity runs thinner and swings can run bigger.

Decrypt, CryptoQuant, Deribit public data and Finnhub snapshots, 09:37 Singapore time, Saturday, November 28. Market observation only — not investment advice.

Crypto News 24-Hour Important Summary

① Bitcoin is grinding around the $60-62k zone, on track to finally snap a brutal seven-week losing streak after Thanksgiving bounce vibes, but the backdrop is still rough with record ~$5.39B November spot ETF outflows and the 90-day correlation to gold hitting all-time highs near 0.56-0.59. Extreme fear index sits around 12, options expiry just passed, and the market is basically treating BTC more like digital gold than tech beta right now.

② Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal freeze that followed the massive $6.3B October hack. CoinDesk and others confirm all affected assets are reported recovered and customer funds fully backed, with only a few networks still paused for routine maintenance. The timeline is breathing a little easier on this one.

③ Monero got absolutely wrecked, down 11-15% after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR on Nov 30 (second major exchange this month). This is pure regulatory pressure ahead of tighter EU rules on privacy coins, and the CT chatter is heavy on whether this is just another coordinated hit or the start of broader delistings.

④ Spain just handed its AML unit (Sepblac) power to freeze crypto accounts for up to five business days without a judge, extending to banks and payment apps too. Meanwhile, eurozone leaders picked Pablo Hernández de Cos as next ECB chief—he’s publicly skeptical of stablecoins and prefers tokenized bank deposits. Regulatory heat is real and spreading.

⑤ Ethereum devs locked in December 15 for the Glamsterdam upgrade’s big Hoodi testnet run after the previous delay, keeping the disputed fee change intact. No mainnet date yet, but the community is watching closely as AI agents and Solana meme narratives continue dominating the broader X chatter in extreme fear mode.

Summary + take: The last 24 hours were classic crypto cleanup—hack resolution, privacy coins under fire, more government tools for freezes, and BTC stubbornly holding key levels despite record ETF bleed and acting more like gold than risk-on. No sugarcoating: outflows are ugly and the fear is still thick. But these are the quiet accumulation windows. Privacy getting squeezed hurts the original cypherpunk dream, yet fixing the Binance mess and seeing BTC refuse to break $60k hard feels like the foundation quietly strengthening. Watch for any ETF flow flip and whether Glamsterdam stays on track. Stack what you believe in, ignore the noise, and let the fear do the heavy lifting for the next leg.

① 比特币在6万-6.2万美元附近磨盘，感恩节后反弹有望终结长达七周的连跌，但背景依旧惨淡：11月现货ETF净流出创纪录约53.9亿美元，与黄金的90天相关性创历史新高约0.56-0.59。极度恐惧指数约12，期权刚到期，市场正把BTC当成数字黄金而不是科技高贝塔。

③ 门罗币暴跌11-15%，原因是KuCoin宣布11月30日下架XMR（本月第二家主要交易所）。这是欧盟隐私币监管压力的直接体现，CT上热议这是又一次 coordinated 打击还是更大规模下架的开始。

④ 西班牙赋予反洗钱单位（Sepblac）权力，可在无需法官批准的情况下冻结加密账户最多5个工作日，同样适用于银行和支付账户。同时，欧元区选定Pablo Hernández de Cos出任下一任欧洲央行行长，他对稳定币持怀疑态度，更倾向代币化银行存款。监管热度持续扩散。

2126495565303398860.text:
Franklin Templeton's crypto index ETF will start holding @HyperliquidX's $HYPE around Dec 1, per an SEC filing from Nov 25.

The buy itself is tiny. EZPZ manages about $17M, and HYPE should land near a 1% weight, close to DOGE's slice. That's roughly $170K, less than a single day of Assistance Fund buybacks.

The route matters more than the size. CF Benchmarks added HYPE to its Institutional Digital Asset Index, which only takes large assets that meet the standards of major financial jurisdictions, and Franklin follows the index automatically. It didn't need a separate SEC approval either: the fund adds HYPE under the generic listing standards for crypto ETFs.

So HYPE now sits in a regulated basket of eight assets next to BTC, ETH, XRP and SOL, through a path other index funds can use too.

This is a better kind of demand than another single-asset HYPE ETF. Those need investors who want HYPE specifically, and they've seen outflows lately. Index funds buy because the rules say so, at every rebalance, whether anyone is excited about HYPE or not. As these funds grow, that bid grows with them, and HYPE's weight rises on its own if it keeps outgrowing the rest of the basket.

Initially pumped too fast and I took a loss top blasting but decided to buy back in because this $YTR is one of the most unique projects I’ve seen - not just on Elysium but crypto as a whole.

Yutori can open a new speculative vertical by turning Hyperliquid’s deep, 24/7 perps (crypto + HIP-3 stocks, indices, gold, oil) into retail-friendly, defined-risk directional bets that behave like options without requiring a full options order book or the constant wick/liquidation risk of raw leverage.

Traders set a max loss (budget) that doubles as premium and hard floor; the engine dynamically holds the perp at the option’s live delta so the position grows when right and shrinks when wrong, auto-closing at the floor. This gives convexity and “room for conviction” on the same account that already has the best on-chain perp liquidity, while keeping funds non-custodial.

The speculative kicker is the $YTR layer: it is burned as engine fuel, staked for Hard Floor gap coverage and tighter pricing/higher size, and supported by continuous buybacks from builder fees plus HYPE rewards to stakers. Volume on the product therefore creates structural token demand and burn, while the product itself feeds Hyperliquid volume. If the engine holds up in live conditions and traders adopt the defined-risk format, it becomes both a new trading primitive and a self-reinforcing token narrative on top of the fastest-growing derivatives venue in crypto.

新成分进入标的指数，投射出基金布局的微妙变化。

Franklin Crypto Trust 最近更新的招股说明书补充文件披露，Hyperliquid（HYPE）将于2026年12月1日起加入该基金的标的指数。这一调整不仅意味着基金持仓结构将有所改变，也将直接影响相关投资产品的表现和资金流动。Hyperliquid作为新兴资产，其纳入或许是对未来市场预期的一种积极回应。

值得注意的是，这一信息披露的时间点正值多只美国现货比特币ETF出现资金净流出，似乎更显得基金方在激烈的加密市场中寻求分散风险或优化组合配置。根据Farside Investors公布的数据，2026年11月25日的资金流表显示多只基金出现数以亿计的净流出，凸显目前投资者情绪的波动。

此外，美国市场上追踪HYPE的三只现货投资产品总资产达到266.5百万美元，说明该资产的市场容量和关注度已具备一定规模。该规模放在现阶段，足以引起基金管理人的注意，但与传统大型数字资产相比仍显“小打小闹”，这也让Hyperliquid的未来表现充满变数。

这次调整的最大看点，当然是Hyperliquid能否通过作为指数成分发挥出其价值，带动相关基金产品的吸引力。基金经理如何平衡风险与收益、以及投资者如何响应资金流向，将直接影响到这一变动的真正影响力度。再加上市场对新兴数字资产的监管环境不断变化，Hyperliquid的成分地位是否稳固，都是值得关注的变量。

最后，令人暗自偷笑的是，基金调整如此“精准”，时间上竟巧妙安排在11月底资金大量流出的“黑五”节之后，真是“黑名单”上的黑马，令人会心一笑。

2126497746085396754.text:
AMD (EEUDumps), NVIDIA (nvlog), Adobe (CacheStorage), and Razer (rzappengine) all got caught hammering SSDs with tens or hundreds of GBs of idle writes.

The common denominator isn't random bugs. It's unthrottled local telemetry daemons. Every vendor shifted to persistent background workers that continuously serialize state, power metrics, and crash dumps to disk as staging buffers for their analytics pipelines. When a poll or token check fails, there is zero I/O rate limiting to stop the loop.

Open Resource Monitor (resmon) → Disk → sort by Write (B/sec) at idle. You might be shocked at what is silently burning through your NVMe TBW.  

Who's next on the list?

・VIXは先週19.30から35.89へ急騰したが、今週は23.81まで低下（週間-33.7%）。市場の警戒感は後退したものの、急騰前の水準を依然として上回る

📌 $NVDA Nvidia +0.80%：先端AI半導体の中国流入を巡る続報
・半導体株が大幅高となるなか、Nvidiaは小幅高にとどまる
・米国の輸出規制対象であるBlackwell搭載の大型AIシステムが、すでに上海のデータセンターに存在するとBloombergが報道
・この施設には、フアンCEOの不倫問題の相手とされるアリス・ファン氏が関係
・11月13日には旧世代のAI半導体の中国流入も報じられていた
・アリス氏が創業したAIクラウド企業Megaspeedは、不正流出疑惑で米当局の捜査を受け、米国の輸出規制リストに追加
・フアンCEOは以前、大型AIシステムの密輸は困難と説明。今回の流入経路は不明で、Nvidiaは取材に回答していない

📌 米インフレ再加速：12月の利上げ観測が強まる
・25日発表の10月PCE物価指数は前年同月比+3.8%（予想+3.8%、前回+3.7%）
・コアPCEも前年同月比+3.3%（予想+3.2%、前回+3.1%）と2023年11月以来の高い伸び
・7〜9月期の実質GDP成長率も年率+4.3%に上方修正（予想+3.5%、速報値+3.4%）
・市場は12月の0.25ポイントの利上げをほぼ完全に織り込み、来年1月の追加利上げも予想
・米国債利回りは大幅に上昇。2年債は+10.1bp、10年債は+9.7bp

📌 株価反発も、AI投資への警戒は根強い
・AI企業の債務拡大、設備投資の伸び鈍化、中間選挙後のデータセンター開発の減速などが懸念材料
・一方、最近の株安はAI投資への懸念よりも、利上げ観測の強まりによるところが大きいとの見方もある

📌 金・銀が反発：最高値からは依然大幅安
・金先物：+2.9%の3,639.60ドル（週間+3.5%）
・銀先物：+7.8%の43.167ドル（週間+5.1%）
・株式市場の反発に伴う換金売り圧力の後退や、空売りの買い戻しが反発の背景との見方
・1月の史上最高値（終値ベース）からの下落率は、金先物が-31.6%、銀先物が-62.5%
・利上げ観測やドル高など、貴金属価格への逆風は残る

【11月30日（月）の緊急警告】日経平均は1,211円高。米NASDAQも2.3％上昇。それでも、月曜日の朝から半導体株に飛びつくのは少し待ってくだされ。
これは異常です。
48歳で資産2億円まで増やして、
株だけで家族を養ってきました。
悪いことは言わない！！！
キオクシアHD（285A）。
アドバンテスト（6857）。
東京エレクトロン（8035）。
ソフトバンクグループ（9984）。
フジクラ（5803）。
そして、AI・半導体関連株を持っている人。
金曜日の大幅反発と、週末の米国株高を見て、月曜日は朝から買っても大丈夫だと思っている人は、最後まで読んでくだされ。
わしが本当に警戒しているのは、金曜日の上昇そのものではない。
急落した相場が大きく反発し、米国株まで上昇したことで、投資家が一気に強気になり、寄り付きから高値を追いかけてしまうことじゃ。
11月25日、日本株はAI・半導体関連株を中心に大きく売られた。
ところが、11月26日には反発。
そして11月27日（金）、日経平均はさらに1,211.95円高。
終値は58,711.11円。
前日比＋2.11％。
TOPIXも3,815.20ポイントまで上昇し、前日比＋1.73％。
東証プライム市場では、値上がり926銘柄、値下がり582銘柄。
売買代金は約7兆7,872億円。
金曜日は、半導体だけでなく市場全体にも買いが広がった。
さらに、11月27日の米国市場では、
NYダウが592ドル高。
S&P500が1.6％高。
NASDAQ総合指数が2.3％高。
米国株も大きく反発して週を終えた。
数字だけを見れば、月曜日も上昇を期待したくなる展開じゃ。
しかし、ここで一つ考えてほしい。
金曜日に1,200円以上上昇した日本株。
米国でもハイテク株を中心に買い戻し。
それだけで、今回の下落リスクが消えたと言えるのか。
ここを間違えてはいけませんぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【まず、11月27日（金）の日本株で何が起きたのか】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11月27日の日経平均は、
始値：57,669.79円。
高値：58,738.02円。
安値：57,447.16円。
終値：58,711.11円。
前日比：＋1,211.95円。
上昇率：＋2.11％。
終値は高値に近い水準。
一度上昇しただけではなく、後場にかけても買いが続いた相場じゃ。
TOPIXも、
終値：3,815.20ポイント。
前日比：＋64.80ポイント。
上昇率：＋1.73％。
東証プライム市場では、
値上がり銘柄：926。
値下がり銘柄：582。
変わらず：41。
33業種のうち26業種が上昇した。
この数字は重要じゃ。
11月26日は日経平均が上昇しても、値下がり銘柄がわずかに多かった。
しかし、11月27日は値上がり銘柄が大きく上回った。
つまり、金曜日は前日までの一部大型株中心の反発から、より広い銘柄に買いが広がった可能性がある。
ただし、日経平均の上昇寄与度を見ると、別の注意点もある。
① アドバンテスト（6857）：約379円押し上げ。
② 東京エレクトロン（8035）：約176円押し上げ。
③ ソフトバンクG（9984）：約73円押し上げ。
④ イビデン（4062）：約61円押し上げ。
⑤ TDK（6762）：約49円押し上げ。
特にアドバンテストと東京エレクトロンの2銘柄だけで、日経平均を約555円押し上げた計算になる。
日経平均の上昇幅1,211円のうち、約半分近くをこの2銘柄が支えたわけじゃ。
ここが重要ですぞ。
市場全体にも買いは広がった。
しかし、指数を大きく押し上げたのは、依然として半導体関連の値がさ株じゃ。
月曜日に確認したいのは、半導体株だけが続伸するのか。
それとも、光通信、電子部品、素材、金融などにも資金が広がるのか。
指数の数字だけで判断してはいけませんぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【① 金曜日に急反発した半導体株。月曜日も買いが続くのか】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
まず、今回の相場の中心にいる銘柄を確認したい。
11月27日の主な終値と上昇率じゃ。
アドバンテスト（6857）。
終値：26,585円。
前日比：＋7.07％。
東京エレクトロン（8035）。
終値：8,220円。
前日比：＋4.43％。
キオクシアHD（285A）。
終値：8,450円。
前日比：＋8.86％。
レーザーテック（6920）。
終値：33,600円。
前日比：＋9.98％。
イビデン（4062）。
終値：5,120円。
前日比：＋9.68％。
フジクラ（5803）。
終値：2,199.5円。
前日比：＋5.90％。
ソフトバンクグループ（9984）。
終値：2,984.5円。
前日比：＋3.13％。
かなり強い数字じゃ。
ただし、ここで注意したいのは、急落後の買い戻しと、新しい資金による継続的な買いは同じではないということ。
売られすぎた銘柄が一気に戻ることはある。
しかし、その上昇が数日続くかどうかは別問題じゃ。
月曜日は、
① 寄り付き後も高値を更新できるか。
② 9時15分を過ぎても出来高が続くか。
③ VWAPを上回って推移できるか。
④ 一度売られた後に買いが戻るか。
⑤ 半導体関連の複数銘柄が同時に上昇するか。
この5つを確認したい。
特に、アドバンテストだけが強いのか。
東京エレクトロンやレーザーテックにも買いが広がるのか。
キオクシアやイビデンにも資金が残るのか。
ここを見極める必要があるのですぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【② キオクシアHD、8,450円まで戻した後に見るべきこと】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
キオクシアHD（285A）。
11月25日の急落後、11月26日に大きく反発。
そして11月27日は終値8,450円。
前日比＋8.86％。
AI向けストレージ需要への期待に加え、NVIDIAとの技術実証も注目材料になっている。
今回の協業では、NVIDIAのソフトウェアとキオクシアのSSDを組み合わせ、AI向けGPUメモリの実効容量を拡張する技術の検証を進める。
発表された構成では、NVIDIA GB200 NVL72システムにキオクシアのSSDを144台搭載し、約1.1ペタバイトの容量を活用する実証が示された。
これは中長期で注目したい材料じゃ。
AIの処理能力を高めるには、GPUだけでなく、大量のデータを効率よく扱うストレージ技術も重要になる。
ただし、技術実証が始まったことと、すぐに大きな売上や利益が確定することは別問題。
期待だけで株価を追いかけてはいけませんぞ。
月曜日に確認したいのは、
① 8,450円を維持できるか。
② 8,500円台に乗せられるか。
③ 8,000円を割り込まずに推移できるか。
④ 急騰後の利益確定売りを吸収できるか。
⑤ 出来高を伴った買いが続くか。
特に、寄り付きで大きく上昇した後の値動きじゃ。
高く始まったのに、すぐに売られる。
出来高だけが増えて株価が伸びない。
こういう動きが出たら、短期資金の利益確定を疑いたい。
人気銘柄だから買うのではない。
上昇した後も買いが残るかを見るのですぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【③ ソフトバンクG、3,000円を回復できるか】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ソフトバンクグループ（9984）。
11月25日に大きく売られた後、11月26日、27日と反発した。
11月27日終値は2,984.5円。
前日比＋3.13％。
注目したいのは、3,000円という節目じゃ。
ソフトバンクGは、一般的な事業会社とは違う。
OpenAIへの投資。
Armの成長。
AIデータセンターへの投資。
世界のAIインフラへの資金投入。
こうした投資資産の評価が株価に大きく影響する。
AI市場が拡大すれば、保有資産の価値が高まる可能性がある。
一方で、投資先の企業価値や資金調達環境が悪化すれば、その影響も受ける。
月曜日に確認したいのは、
① 3,000円を明確に回復できるか。
② 3,000円前後で売りに押されないか。
③ 出来高を伴って上昇しているか。
④ Arm関連のニュースや米国ハイテク株の動きに反応するか。
⑤ AI投資への期待が実際の収益につながる道筋が見えるか。
AIの未来を信じることと、今の株価で買うことは別問題。
急落したから安い。
3,000円を超えたから買い。
そんな単純な判断はできませんぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【④ NVIDIAのGTCが始まる。AI関連株に再び資金が集まるのか】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
月曜日から注目したい海外イベントがある。
NVIDIAの「GTC Washington, D.C. 2026」じゃ。
11月30日はワークショップが開催され、12月1日から3日にかけて本会議や展示会が行われる予定。
AI工場。
データセンター。
高性能コンピューティング。
フィジカルAI。
こうしたテーマが取り上げられる。
日本株にとっても、AI関連の材料が出てくる可能性があるイベントじゃ。
ただし、イベントが開催されるからといって、関連銘柄がすべて上昇するわけではない。
確認したいのは、
① NVIDIAの新たな製品・技術発表。
② GPUやAIサーバーの需要見通し。
③ データセンター投資の採算性。
④ メモリーやストレージの需要。
⑤ 光通信・電力設備への波及。
AI関連株は、期待だけで買われる局面から、実際に受注や利益を伸ばせる企業が選ばれる局面に移る可能性がある。
だからこそ、GPUだけではなく、その周辺を支える企業にも目を向けたいのですぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【⑤ 日銀・植田総裁の発言。金利と為替が相場を動かす可能性】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
月曜日にもう一つ見逃せない予定がある。
11月30日午前10時05分。
植田日銀総裁が名古屋で開催される経済界代表者との懇談会で挨拶する予定じゃ。
市場が注目するのは、12月の金融政策決定会合に向けた発言内容。
特に、物価上昇と追加利上げに対する考え方じゃ。
11月27日に発表された東京都区部の11月コアCPIは、前年同月比＋2.9％。
10月の＋2.6％から伸びが拡大した。
ただし、市場予想の＋2.9％とは一致しており、予想を大幅に上回ったわけではない。
エネルギー価格の上昇が目立つ一方、生鮮食品とエネルギーを除く指数は＋2.5％で、前月の＋2.6％から伸びが鈍化した。
つまり、物価の数字を一つだけ見て、すぐに利上げを決めつけるのは危険じゃ。
植田総裁の発言で、
追加利上げへの警戒が強まるのか。
それとも市場の不安が和らぐのか。
ここを確認したい。
金利上昇が意識されれば、銀行株には追い風となる場合がある。
一方、借入負担の大きい企業や、高い成長期待で買われているグロース株には逆風となる可能性もある。
為替の動きも重要じゃ。
ドル円が円安方向に進めば、輸出企業の採算期待を支えることがある。
反対に、急速な円高は輸出関連株の重しになりやすい。
半導体だけでなく、銀行、保険、自動車、グロース株まで幅広く影響する材料ですぞ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【⑥ 月曜日の朝に確認したい日本の経済指標】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11月30日午前8時50分には、10月の鉱工業生産指数の速報値などが発表される予定じゃ。
小売関連の統計も確認したい。
ここで注目したいのは、
① 国内製造業の生産が回復しているか。
② 電子部品・半導体関連の生産動向。
③ 在庫と出荷のバランス。
④ 小売・消費関連の強さ。
⑤ 企業の設備投資につながる動きがあるか。
鉱工業生産が市場予想を上回れば、製造業や設備投資関連の安心材料になる可能性がある。
反対に、弱い数字なら景気敏感株の重しになることもある。
ただし、単月の数字だけで景気の方向を決めつけてはいけない。
翌日以降には日本の法人企業統計、米国のISM製造業景況指数、ADP雇用統計、そして12月4日の米雇用統計も控えている。
今週は、日本だけでなく海外の経済指標にも相場が反応しやすい週になりそうじゃ。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【⑦ 月曜日、資金が向かう可能性がある日本株20選】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ここからは、金曜日の急反発、米国株の上昇、NVIDIAのイベント、日銀の金融政策を踏まえて、わしが監視したい20銘柄じゃ。
全部買うためのリストではない。
月曜日にどの分野へ資金が向かうのかを比較するための監視リストですな。
【① AI・半導体・メモリー】
① キオクシアHD（285A）
NVIDIAとの技術実証とAI向けSSD需要が焦点。8,450円を維持できるか、急騰後の利益確定売りを吸収できるかを確認。
② アドバンテスト（6857）
金曜日の日経平均を最も押し上げた銘柄。買い戻しが続くか、出来高とVWAPを重視したい。
③ 東京エレクトロン（8035）
半導体製造装置の主力株。米国半導体株の動きと設備投資の先行きを確認。
④ レーザーテック（6920）
先端半導体の検査装置関連。金曜日の急反発後も買いが続くか注目。
⑤ ディスコ（6146）
半導体切断・研削装置。先端半導体の高性能化と設備投資の回復が焦点。
⑥ イビデン（4062）
AIサーバー向け高性能基板。金曜日の大幅高を受け、利益確定売りをこなせるか確認。
⑦ ソフトバンクグループ（9984）
AI投資と保有資産の評価が焦点。3,000円前後の攻防を監視。
【② 光通信・電子部品・データセンター】
⑧ フジクラ（5803）
光ファイバー・データセンター関連。AI通信量の増加が中長期の成長テーマ。
⑨ 古河電工（5801）
光通信・電力ケーブル。データセンターと送配電網の増強需要に注目。
⑩ 住友電工（5802）
電線・光通信・電力設備。AI時代の電力需要を支える企業として監視。
⑪ TDK（6762）
電子部品・電池関連。AI機器やデータセンター向け需要の広がりを確認したい。
⑫ 村田製作所（6981）
電子部品・高周波部品。スマートフォンだけでなくAI関連機器への需要も確認。
⑬ 日立製作所（6501）

nvidia sinks after earnings and coreweave and iren sink harder. the tape is telling you something most holders of this complex do not want to hear: there is only one asset in this entire trade.

strip the costumes. every company in the ai infrastructure complex - chip seller, server assembler, neocloud landlord - is long the same underlying: gpu scarcity rent. nvidia holds it at the manufacturing margin, the assemblers at distribution thinness, the neoclouds as a levered rental stream. different business models, one underlying exposure. that is why they move together, and why the neoclouds move further: their equity is not exposure to the rent, it is a leveraged claim on the rent, with debt service in between. when the underlying reprices, equity at the end of the capital structure reprices with multiples of the move.

this is not sentiment contagion - contagion is irrational transmission. this is leverage mechanics, which is arithmetic. the market is not confused about what these companies are. it is increasingly precise about it.

the forward implication cuts both ways and both are worth holding. if the scarcity rent stabilizes, the same leverage mechanics work in reverse and the neoclouds are the cheapest way to express it. but leverage has no opinion about direction - it amplifies whatever the underlying does. holders of the complex are not diversified across the ai buildout. they are concentrated in one bet, wearing different tickers.

watch the correlation itself as the diagnostic: if coreweave ever decouples from nvidia's daily moves, that is the market saying rental economics have their own observable evidence. until then, one asset.

Why does it matter if articles mislead their readers? Seems unethical.

A lot of people seem to believe the following (all untrue):

1) Renting out servers outside China to Chinese companies was illegal. It wasn't even an export until a new rule on 19 Nov. Oracle leased capacity to Tencent and ByteDance, and Microsoft sells Azure to ByteDance.

2) Remote access to servers is a shady workaround. It's the standard way anyone uses a server or cloud computing, including OpenAI and Anthropic.

3) NVIDIA is required to track where all its chips go. It isn't. Commerce's own guidance says there's no duty to "go behind" a customer absent red flags. Most of its chips go to server makers (Dell, Super Micro, Gigabyte, Foxconn) who sell them on.

4) Restricted chips in China means NVIDIA sold them there. There's been a grey market since at least 2023, and you can buy restricted A100s and H200s on eBay. The rack in this Bloomberg story was built by Gigabyte, and the article itself says "It's unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country".

5) Singapore was 18% of NVIDIA's revenue, so it was selling to China through Singapore. Singapore was an invoicing location. Shipments to Singapore were under 2% of revenue.

6) NVIDIA hid its Singapore sales by changing its reporting. The change was disclosed and prior years were restated. Most of "Singapore" moved to the US, because it was US companies invoicing through Singapore offices.

7) Singapore investigated Alice Huang for espionage. Singapore says she "was not investigated for espionage". Its case was about false declarations when buying servers.

8) The Commerce investigation was "halted" after NVIDIA intervened. It was transferred to the Justice Department, which is running it as a criminal investigation.

9) Commerce approved 3.4m chips for Chinese firms. 3.4m were applied for; about 800k were approved.

10) Super Micro was indicted. Only individuals were charged.

11) NVIDIA and Jensen are under criminal investigation. Reuters reports the Justice Department's probes found no evidence Jensen acted as an agent of China, there was no counterintelligence probe of him, and NVIDIA wasn't a target. The VP said "we were told that he was under no investigation", and the Attorney General calls NVIDIA "a good corporate citizen".

Many people think NVIDIA and/or Jensen are breaking the law because of a flurry of misleading articles that left out key details, and in some cases made claims that were simply wrong.

US Stock News 24-Hour Important Summary

1. Black Friday bounce turned the whole tape green. S&P 500 closed +1.6% at 7,297, Nasdaq ripped +2.3%, Dow added 592 points. Best Thanksgiving week in nearly 20 years after the mid-week AI panic.

2. Chip and AI names led the charge. Micron surged 7.6%, Sandisk nearly +16%, Marvell and others followed. Classic dip-buying after the forced selling. Memory and storage were the easy money.

3. Nvidia lagged the party. Only finished +0.8% after earlier weakness. Reports of Blackwell chips showing up in a Shanghai data center plus Huang’s upcoming congressional testimony kept a lid on the leader even after his CEO return earlier in the week.

4. Amazon popped nearly 4% on solid Black Friday shopping data. Consumer still spending while the AI crowd scrambled back in. Real economy reminder in the middle of the tech drama.

5. SpaceX and Musk headlines mixed in. Pledge of shares to kids through Trump Accounts added to the tech recovery vibe, while broader AI hyperscalers and related names joined the rebound.

Summary: This was pure holiday bargain hunting after weeks of AI fear. The phoenix rose, but the questions about spending returns, China risk, and a Fed still leaning hawkish after the strong GDP revision have not vanished. Stay selective. Quality AI on weakness still makes sense long-term; chasing every bounce is how accounts get smoked. Volatility is the feature, not the bug.

🙏 Thank you for reading!

Crypto News 24-Hour Important Summary

1. Bitcoin pushed back above $61k and is on track to snap a seven-week losing streak. It rode the stock rebound higher, but November is still brutal and the Fear & Greed Index sits in extreme fear territory around 12.

2. Spot Bitcoin ETFs just posted a record monthly outflow. Roughly $5.39 billion left in November with seven straight days of withdrawals. BlackRock’s IBIT led the exits. Institutions are stepping back hard even as price bounced.

3. Binance fully lifted its withdrawal suspension after the October security incident. Four weeks later the freeze is gone across nearly all networks. Confidence in the biggest exchange just got a real test passed.

4. Bitcoin-gold correlation hit an all-time high. Both bounced together after the recent sell-off. Macro hedge narrative is loud right now while crypto still tracks risk assets.

5. Shorts got squeezed on the move higher. Hundreds of millions in liquidations hit, mostly shorts, around the options expiry and the equity open. Classic forced covering in a thin holiday tape.

Summary: This looks like a risk-on bounce tied to stocks, not a clean structural bottom. Record ETF outflows and extreme fear say institutions are still cautious. My take: treat the bounce as a gift for repositioning, not a signal to go full send. Core holdings can stay; new money should wait for clearer inflows or a deeper wash. Crypto winters reward patience over FOMO every single time.

🙏 Thank you for reading!

La rueda en números de W. S. · Viernes 27/11

Lo que pasó
Media rueda después de Acción de Gracias, y el S&P 500 cerró en 7.297 puntos, con una suba de +1,60%. Esta vez fue pareja: subieron 407 de las 500 empresas y la mediana dio +0,92%.
El VIX, el "índice del miedo", bajó a 23,8, desde 28,3 el miércoles.
Ojo con el volumen: media rueda, con RVol entre 0,3× y 0,6× en casi todas. Suba con pocos operando.

Quién tiró del carro: los chips, otra vez
SNDK +16%, COHR +14,1%, STX +7,9%, MU +7,6%, MRVL +7,3%, WDC +7,2%, DELL +6,7%, QCOM +6,3%, INTC +5,4%, PLTR +5,2%, TSLA +5,2%, AMD +4,6%, AMZN +4%, AVGO +3,8% y META +3,1%. NVDA, en cambio, apenas +0,8%.
Afuera del S&P: Anthropic (ANT) +11%, SK Hynix (SKHY) +7,5%, SpaceX (SPCX) +4,8% y TSM +3,2%.
El ETF de semiconductores SMH subió +4,2% (SOXX +4,8%) y el Nasdaq (QQQ) +2,7%. El S&P con el mismo peso para cada empresa (RSP) subió +1,2%: la suba fue más amplia que la de hace una semana, pero otra vez los chips mandaron.

Lo que no acompañó
Las defensivas se quedaron quietas: salud (XLV +0,3%), servicios públicos (XLU +0,3%) y consumo básico (XLP +0,4%). LLY +0%, PG −0,2%.
Los bonos largos cayeron: TLT −1,2%. Bitcoin (IBIT) −0,6%.
Lo que voló: los metales y Brasil. Oro (GLD) +2,1%, plata (SLV) +6,2%, mineras de oro (GDX) +7,2% y Brasil (EWZ) +9,8%.

Bonos del Tesoro: vendieron, pero la semana sigue en compra.
Hoy los bonos se vendieron: el tramo de 2 a 5 años volvió a la zona de 4,70%–4,80%, unos 5 a 10 pb arriba del miércoles, y los bonos largos cayeron (TLT −1,2%).
Pero contra la semana pasada la curva sigue más abajo: contra hace 5 ruedas, el tramo de 1 a 10 años rinde unos 15 a 20 pb menos, y el largo, de 20 a 30 años, unos 10 pb menos. Contra hace 20 ruedas, el medio está unos 10 a 15 pb abajo y el largo apenas 5.

En castellano: con la bolsa arriba, hoy salió algo de plata de los bonos, pero la compra de las últimas dos semanas sigue en pie, sobre todo en el tramo medio.

La Fed: el futuro de tasa pegó un salto
El futuro de Fed Funds (ZQ) cerró hoy en 95,855, con una caída de 0,268 en el día. Traducido a tasa: el mercado descuenta una tasa implícita de 4,145%, unos 27 pb más que ayer. Es el movimiento más brusco desde septiembre.
La tasa hoy está en 3,75%–4,00%. Con 4,145%, el futuro ya no solo da por hecha la suba de 25 pb del 8 y 9 de diciembre: empieza a poner precio a una segunda.
El empujón vino del PCE del miércoles, el dato de inflación que mira la Fed: el núcleo subió a 3,3% interanual (desde 3,1%) y el general a 3,8%.
El posicionamiento lo acompaña (CFTC al 17/11): los fondos apalancados, que estaban comprados apostando a tasas más bajas, achicaron 37.317 contratos y quedaron en +264.298.
Por eso los TIPS subieron: el mercado espera una Fed más dura por más tiempo y la tasa real subió unos 30 pb contra hace 20 ruedas en el tramo corto y medio. 

Lo curioso sigue: los vencimientos entre 2036 y 2040 rinden menos de lo que marca la curva, caros contra sus vecinos, con el T 4.5 02/15/36 como el más desviado.

Opciones: el flip se acerca
Los índices siguen debajo de su gamma flip, pero con la suba de hoy quedaron mucho más cerca. El flip del SPX está en 7.465 puntos, 2,3% arriba del cierre (el miércoles estaba a +3,9%); el SPY quedó a +1,6% (antes +2,9%) y el QQQ a +2,2% (antes +4,6%). La gamma total del SPX bajó a −US$ 45,9 MM, desde −65,5: los dealers todavía aceleran, pero con menos fuerza.
Lo delicado es dónde está parado el precio: la gamma de los puts toca su punto más negativo justo entre 7.300 y 7.400, la zona de hoy. Ahí los dealers aceleran más que en ningún otro lado. Si el S&P pasa los 7.465 cambia el régimen y empiezan a frenar; si vuelve a caer, sale de la zona de máxima aceleración, pero sigue del lado que acelera.

El cambio de hoy: Anthropic (ANT), con el +11%, cruzó arriba de su flip y ahora frena. También quedaron del lado defensivo PLTR, QCOM, TXN y CRWD.
En la zona caliente, abajo del flip y con peso, siguen los chips: NVDA, MU, AMD, AVGO, TSM, LRCX, AMAT, SKHY, DELL e INTC, además de GOOGL, SpaceX (SPCX) y los bancos (JPM, BAC, GS, MS, WFC, C).
Del otro lado, frenando los movimientos, las defensivas: AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META, TSLA, WMT, PG, KO, PEP, JNJ, LLY, V y MA.

El resumen criollo
Viernes de media rueda y de euforia: chips, metales y emergentes para arriba, los bonos devolviendo algo de la semana y el VIX bajando de 28 a 24. Los índices se acercaron al flip, pero no lo cruzaron, y los chips que tiraron del carro siguen en zona de aceleración. Con poco volumen y después de una semana que arrancó con el mismo guión y se dio vuelta en 24 horas, el lunes, con la rueda completa, se ve si alguien le cree a esta suba. 
Seguimos en modo revoleo de moneda con saltos grandes o caídas gigantes... quien se anima a decir como sale el lunes? cara o cruz?

EN

Nov. 27 U.S. regular session: S&P 500 +1.60%, Nasdaq Composite +2.31%, Dow +1.18%. Trading ended early at 1 p.m. ET.

ETF data below was checked at 6:58 p.m. ET on Nov. 27. Crypto continues trading through the weekend.

1、The equity rebound supports sentiment, not a guaranteed crypto rally.
Storage stocks stood out, with Sandisk up 15.96% versus Nvidia’s 0.80%. That could improve risk appetite toward BTC and ETH, but hardware gains do not establish revenue growth for AI tokens. Look for stronger crypto spot volume and broader participation.

2、The rate backdrop remains demanding.
The Treasury’s ten-year par yield rose to 4.94% on Nov. 27. Higher yields leave a meaningful opportunity cost for holding Bitcoin and do not establish cheaper leverage. If a crypto rebound comes mainly with rising futures positioning and funding rates, while spot demand stays weak, its durability needs more evidence.

3、ETF reporting is incomplete.
Farside’s reported Nov. 27 subtotals show BTC ETF outflows of $41 million and ETH ETF outflows of $7.5 million. Several funds, including IBIT, FBTC and ETHA, were still missing. These are not final totals, and the eventual direction can change. Weekend spot trading cannot yet be described as a confirmed return of U.S. ETF buying.

美东11月27日常规时段：标普500涨1.60%，纳指涨2.31%，道指涨1.18%，北京时间今晨02:00提前收市。

下列ETF数据核对截至11月28日07:58。币市周末持续交易。

1、美股反弹改善情绪，币市涨势仍需自己的证据。
存储股表现突出，闪迪涨15.96%，英伟达涨0.80%。这可能改善BTC、ETH的风险偏好，但硬件股上涨不能直接证明AI代币收入增长。验证条件是加密现货成交量改善，以及上涨范围扩大。

2、利率环境仍有压力。
美国财政部11月27日十年期国债平价收益率升至4.94%。持有比特币的机会成本仍高，也不能据此认定杠杆融资变便宜。如果币价反弹主要伴随合约持仓和资金费率上升，而现货需求偏弱，持续性还需要更多证据。

3、ETF资金流还没有报齐。
Farside的11月27日已报小计为：BTC ETF净流出4100万美元，ETH ETF净流出750万美元。IBIT、FBTC、ETHA等基金仍缺数据。这些都不是最终合计，最终方向也可能变化。周末币价上涨，暂时不能解释成美国ETF买盘已经回归。

米国11月27日の通常取引は、S&P500が1.60％高、ナスダック総合が2.31％高、ダウが1.18％高。日本時間28日午前3時に短縮取引を終えました。

以下のETFデータは28日午前8時58分、日本時間の確認時点。暗号資産は週末も取引が続きます。

1、株高は心理面の支援材料。暗号資産の買いは別途確認。
サンディスクは15.96％高、エヌビディアは0.80％高と、ストレージ株が目立ちました。BTCやETHへのリスク選好を支える可能性はありますが、ハードウェア株高がAIトークンの収益増を示すわけではありません。現物出来高と上昇の広がりが確認点です。

2、金利環境には負担が残ります。
米財務省の27日の10年パー利回りは4.94％へ上昇。ビットコイン保有の機会費用は高く、レバレッジ調達が安くなったとも判断できません。先物建玉と資金調達率ばかりが上昇し、現物需要が弱い反発なら、持続性には追加の確認が必要です。

3、ETF資金フローは未集計分があります。
Farsideの27日分の報告済み小計は、BTC ETFが4100万ドル、ETH ETFが750万ドルの純流出。IBIT、FBTC、ETHAなどは未報告でした。最終合計ではなく、流入・流出の方向も変わり得ます。週末の値上がりだけで、米国ETFの買い復活とは判断できません。

아래 ETF 자료는 28일 오전 8시58분 한국시간 확인 기준입니다. 가상자산 거래는 주말에도 이어집니다.

1、주식 반등은 심리적 지원이며, 코인 매수는 별도 확인이 필요합니다.
샌디스크 +15.96%, 엔비디아 +0.80%로 스토리지 강세가 두드러졌습니다. BTC·ETH 위험선호를 지지할 수 있지만 하드웨어 주가 상승이 AI 토큰의 매출 증가를 입증하지는 않습니다. 현물 거래량과 상승 종목의 확산을 확인해야 합니다.

2、금리 부담은 남아 있습니다.
미 재무부의 27일 10년물 파수익률은 4.94%로 올랐습니다. 비트코인 보유의 기회비용이 높고, 레버리지 조달비용이 낮아졌다고 보기도 어렵습니다. 선물 미결제약정과 펀딩비만 오르고 현물 수요가 약하다면, 반등 지속성에 추가 근거가 필요합니다.

3、ETF 자금흐름은 아직 미완성 집계입니다.
Farside의 27일 보고 완료분 소계는 BTC ETF 4100만 달러, ETH ETF 750만 달러 순유출입니다. IBIT·FBTC·ETHA 등은 아직 데이터가 없었습니다. 최종 합계가 아니며 최종 유입·유출 방향도 달라질 수 있습니다. 주말 코인 상승만으로 미국 ETF 매수 복귀를 판단할 수는 없습니다.

Phiên chính Mỹ ngày 27/11: S&P 500 tăng 1,60%, Nasdaq Composite tăng 2,31%, Dow tăng 1,18%. Phiên kết thúc sớm lúc 01:00 ngày 28/11, giờ Việt Nam.

1、Cổ phiếu hồi phục hỗ trợ tâm lý; nhu cầu crypto cần bằng chứng riêng.
Sandisk tăng 15,96%, Nvidia tăng 0,80%, cho thấy nhóm lưu trữ nổi bật. Điều này có thể hỗ trợ khẩu vị rủi ro với BTC và ETH, nhưng cổ phiếu phần cứng tăng chưa chứng minh doanh thu token AI tăng. Cần xác nhận bằng khối lượng giao ngay và độ rộng thị trường.

2、Môi trường lãi suất vẫn tạo áp lực.
Lợi suất par trái phiếu Mỹ 10 năm ngày 27/11 tăng lên 4,94%. Chi phí cơ hội khi giữ Bitcoin vẫn cao; chưa có cơ sở kết luận đòn bẩy đã rẻ hơn. Nếu nhịp hồi chủ yếu đi cùng vị thế hợp đồng và funding rate tăng, còn nhu cầu giao ngay yếu, độ bền cần thêm bằng chứng.

Daily Charts #017: S&P 500 Gains 5.6% in Thanksgiving Week as CTA Positioning Stays Short

The S&P 500 rose 5.6% in Thanksgiving week, the second-best such week since 1950. Most stocks rose even on a down day for the index, yet modeled trend-following positioning remains clearly short. Goldman expects earnings growth to more than halve across major markets next year, and the US 2-year real yield has climbed to about 2.6%. Here are today's five free charts.

1. S&P 500 rises 5.6% in Thanksgiving week, second-best since 1950
According to Carson's data, the S&P 500 rose 5.6% in Thanksgiving week, the second-best such week since 1950 after 12.0% in 2008. Most of the gain came on Monday (4.7%); Tuesday and Wednesday dipped slightly before Black Friday added 1.6%.

2. S&P 500 slips 0.25% while 78% of Russell 1000 stocks rise
According to RenMac, on November 25 the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% after falling as much as 3.2% intraday, yet 78% of Russell 1000 members closed higher and the equal-weight index gained 0.81%. The index decline came mainly from heavily weighted tech stocks while most stocks rose.

3. Modeled CTA and vol-control equity positioning at -2.21 standard deviations
Carson estimates from price trends that global trend-following (CTA) and volatility-control funds' equity positioning stood at -2.21 standard deviations on November 25, in the bottom 2% of the model's daily readings since its data begin in 2023 (April 2025 reached -2.48). It is a model estimate, not actual holdings.

4. Goldman sees 2027 S&P 500 earnings growth slowing to 11%
Goldman Sachs' top-down estimates as of November 12 see S&P 500 earnings growth slowing from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027, Europe's Stoxx 600 from 18% to 7% and Japan's TOPIX (fiscal years) from 24% to 9%. That means earnings growth more than halves across the major markets next year.

5. US 2-year real yield climbs to about 2.6% as Brent retreats
Haver data show the US 2-year real yield (the return after inflation) at about 2.6% on November 27, near its high for the year, while Brent crude fell from a peak of about $117 in late October to about $97. Economist Robin Brooks notes that real rates have surged as the Fed digs in on hikes even while oil prices tumble.

2026 年 11 月 28 日（星期六）。

隔夜全球跨资产市场再次出现了极度撕裂的背离行情：

美股表现强硬：纳斯达克在昨日交易时段显著反弹，收涨约 +2.3%（收于 24,129 点附近），科技与超跌资产出现强劲修复。

加密货币 (BTC) 完全不跟随，反而破位插针：BTC 不仅没有跟随纳指反弹，反而在昨日从 $62,000 一路向下破位，剧烈插针清算至 $58,800 附近（随后微幅收回，目前在 $58,600–$59,000 弱势徘徊）。

原油重回升势：由于沙特石油设施再遭袭击以及霍尔木兹海峡航运威胁升级，叠加市场对周日 OPEC+ 产油国会议的预期，WTI 原油重返 $85.6/桶 上方，布伦特原油攀升至 $97.4/桶 附近，接近三周新高。

针对“纳指大涨 2.3% 而 BTC 却砸穿 6 万插针 58,800”的罕见脱钩现象，咱们从宏观压制、流动性去向与情绪面直接拆解：

一、 为什么美股大涨 +2.3%，BTC 却逆势砸穿 $60,000 插针至 $58,800？
资金“虹吸与轮动”而非全网增量放水：
隔夜美股的反弹（感恩节假期前后的低成交量环境）主要源于超跌科技股的空头回补，以及资金向具备实际现金流和分红防御属性的美股大盘集中。
在宏观高利率环境下，美股吸走了有限的抄底资金，加密市场不仅没有分到流动性，反而遭遇了机构的年末仓位再平衡（Rebalancing）与减仓抛售。

$60,000 心理防线失守触发的“杠杆清算连环阵”：
此前 BTC 在 $62,000 附近横盘已久，$60,000–$61,000 堆积了海量高杠杆多头止损单和链上借贷清算线。在周末前流动性最薄弱的窗口期，少量大额现货卖单直接砸穿 $60,000 关口，引发衍生品自动强平瀑布，瞬间将价格掠夺至 $58,800 附近。

现货 ETF 持续失血：
近期机构资金通过现货 ETF 通道持续呈现净流出状态，使得加密货币丧失了此前与纳指同涨的“高贝塔联动效应”，变成了单向的流动性提款机。

二、 油价反弹、美债收益率与美元指数：紧缩枷锁依然焊死

中东能源设施遇袭 + 霍尔木兹风险 ──► 布伦特原油冲向 $97.4 / WTI 站上 $85.6
                                          │
                                          ▼
        通胀粘性死灰复燃 ──► 美债收益率高位坚挺 + 强美元抽水
                                          │
                                          ▼

Everyone's long $BTC into year-end because the leverage got flushed. The flow data says the marginal seller is a leveraged trader.

Look at the Nov 27 numbers: spot bitcoin funds bled 31,890 BTC in a week, about $1.96B on the 7D. That's allocators trimming on a rebalance schedule. The Glassnode $50k-$58k bid wall is genuine support, and it's thin enough that a third straight week of red ETF prints eats through it faster than most people model.

Meanwhile the crowd reads the China/Japan/Korea/ASEAN regulatory working group as a bullish headline. Read it again. Joint cross-border payment standards is a multi-year plumbing project, and the first thing that kind of coordination produces is more compliance friction on exchanges. The same crowd is pricing a Binance tokenized-IPO program as free upside. Ask why an exchange wants to intermediate primary issuance: it's a fee stream that pulls capital away from the spot bid.

The exposure that cleared was the loud kind. The quiet kind, systematic ETF allocation, is still selling into every bounce. I'm short the idea that $60k holds on the next red ETF week. Cash is only better until it is not.

Cash looks safe because the number does not move. It sits in your account. It looks stable. It looks quiet. But quiet does not mean safe.

Cash in a bank can be frozen. Cash in an account can be drained by one phishing email. Cash in a bank can be hit by a breach. Cash can be inflated away slowly while you think you are winning because the number did not go down.

I have watched people think cash was safe, then lose it all in one click. One fake bank email. One fake text. One fake phone call from somebody pretending to be the bank. One manager who said trust me. One platform that locked them out.

That is the part the numbers do not show. The numbers show price. They do not show custody. They do not show theft. They do not show seizure. They do not show hacking.

This is about power, control, information, and money moving behind closed doors while regular people are told to just trust the system. I have been warning about this for years. You can never just trust people with your money.

So yes, cash was better on a chart this year. But cash in the wrong hands is still the easiest thing to steal.

That is why I keep saying this. Get a secure wallet. Learn how to avoid a hack or a compromised wallet. Stop leaving your future in a place where one breach, one freeze, one bad employee can erase years of work.

If you have built something real, talk to a qualified attorney and tax professional about a WEB3 LLC. A WEB3 LLC TRUST is the only way to keep your assets safe from cyberattacks and it protects assets from theft, seizure or legal claims.

Price goes up. Price goes down. Cash, gold, bitcoin, silver, all of them move. What you protect, nobody can take. That is the real return.

America blacklisted Russia's No. 2 bank.
Ten weeks later, that bank is selling Bitcoin.

VTB, Russia's second-largest lender, switched on Bitcoin trading in its investment app on Nov 27.
Only qualified investors for now, dealing directly with the bank, over the counter, all on Russian infrastructure.

This comes ten weeks after the US Treasury blacklisted VTB for helping Iran evade sanctions — and told every foreign bank to cut ties with it immediately.

Here's the part that matters.
Russia's approved list also includes USDT.
But USDT can be frozen by its issuer — 9,597 addresses, $5.69 billion frozen.
Bitcoin has no issuer.
No one can freeze it with a phone call.

Key point is this.
Sanctions are the hardest stress test for "unstoppable money" — and Bitcoin is passing it in public.
Washington can cut a bank off from dollars, from SWIFT, from every foreign correspondent bank.
And the bank's answer is to sell the one asset Washington can't switch off.

Meanwhile, Russia's central bank already opened BTC, ETH and USDT to ordinary investors on Nov 17.
And the Moscow Exchange is set to start crypto trading on Dec 1.

My take is simple.
The market keeps asking whether Bitcoin is a hedge or a risk asset.
Wrong question.
The right question is why the people with the most reason to fear the dollar system keep reaching for the same asset.
First it was individuals.
Then companies.
Then funds.
Now it's a sanctioned bank in a G20 country, selling Bitcoin from its own app.
That's not speculation.
That's necessity.
And necessity is what turns an asset from a trade into infrastructure.

While US ETF money walks out the door in a record month, the other side of the world is building the on-ramp.
The price will catch up to that reality.
It always does.

🚨 WHY ARE WHALES SELLING BITCOIN?

BILLIONS are flowing out of Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs in November, while some investors are quietly buying the dip.

Is institutional money abandoning crypto, or is this a massive capital rotation before December?

Let’s look at the data. 🧵👇

1/ BITCOIN ETF OUTFLOWS ARE HISTORIC

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $5.39 BILLION in net outflows through Nov. 25.

• 18 trading days
• 16 days of outflows
• Only 2 days of inflows
• Largest daily outflow: $669.2M
• Largest ETF seller: BlackRock’s IBIT, with approximately $4.50B in net outflows

November is already the largest monthly outflow on record for Bitcoin ETFs.

This is not a minor correction in institutional sentiment.

2/ ETHEREUM IS ALSO BLEEDING

Ethereum ETFs have recorded approximately $1.30 BILLION in net outflows during November.

ETH has been hit by continued institutional withdrawals, with the latest reports showing another $68.5M leaving spot Ethereum ETFs on Nov. 25.

Bitcoin and Ethereum are experiencing broad institutional risk reduction.

3/ THE LAST 10 TRADING DAYS ARE EVEN MORE BRUTAL

From Nov. 12 through Nov. 25:

• Bitcoin ETFs: −$3.51B
• Ethereum ETFs: −$591.5M
• Solana ETFs: −$3.4M
• XRP ETFs: −$10.6M

That’s more than $4.1 BILLION in net outflows from BTC and ETH alone over just 10 trading sessions.

The selling pressure is concentrated in the two largest crypto assets.

4/ BLACKROCK IS LEADING THE BITCOIN OUTFLOWS

IBIT has been one of the largest sources of selling pressure.

On Nov. 24 alone, approximately $509.3M exited IBIT.

On Nov. 25, another $329.7M reportedly left the fund.

When the world’s largest asset manager’s Bitcoin ETF experiences sustained redemptions, the market cannot ignore it.

5/ BUT SOLANA IS SHOWING A DIFFERENT SIGNAL

Solana ETFs recently recorded approximately $4.38M in weekly inflows, ending a six-week outflow streak.

SOL had previously experienced weeks of withdrawals, but buyers have started returning.

This doesn’t confirm a bullish reversal yet, but it shows investors are becoming selective rather than abandoning every crypto asset.

6/ XRP IS ALSO SHOWING SELECTIVE BUYING

XRP ETFs experienced outflows during November, including approximately $11.1M during a recent weekly period.

However, XRP ETFs reportedly attracted around $4M in inflows on Nov. 26.

Capital is still moving around the crypto market.

The question is whether these inflows can become a sustained trend.

7/ WHY ARE WHALES SELLING?

There are several possible reasons:

• Risk reduction amid macroeconomic uncertainty
• Profit-taking after previous rallies
• ETF investors withdrawing capital
• Weak price momentum
• Leverage being reduced
• Portfolio rebalancing before year-end
• Concerns about liquidity and interest rates

Not every whale selling is bearish.

Some investors are simply protecting capital and waiting for better opportunities.

8/ WHO IS BUYING?

While ETFs are bleeding, some large holders are still accumulating.

Long-term investors, dip-buyers and selective institutions may be taking advantage of lower prices.

But here’s the problem:

The current buying pressure does not appear strong enough to absorb all the selling.

That’s why prices can continue falling even while whales are accumulating.

9/ WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR DECEMBER?

Three scenarios:

🔴 BEARISH

ETF outflows continue, liquidity remains weak, and BTC struggles to reclaim key levels.

More downside remains possible.

🟡 NEUTRAL

Outflows slow, Bitcoin stabilizes, whales accumulate, and the market enters a consolidation phase.

This could be the beginning of a bottoming process.

🟢 BULLISH

ETF flows turn positive, large holders accumulate aggressively, and BTC recovers key levels.

A reversal could trigger a powerful short squeeze as bearish positioning unwinds.

$ETH keeps printing higher lows inside a box after the November flush, and selling pressure fades on every test. I lean long, but only on a limit fill when price retests the prior low. Not at market. The catch: the bigger trend still points down.

After the sharp November drop, price has been ranging. Each pullback made a slightly higher 12h low on shrinking volume. Last night a 4h selloff broke a short-term low, so the 4h structure turned weak again.

Why the long still holds:
- Three of four technical reads (Wyckoff, Elliott, Divergence) point long. ICT leans short.
- All three mark the same zone: the prior 4h swing low, the 4h Bollinger lower band and the 62-79% retracement of the daily box.
When separate methods land on one zone, it's a level to wait for, not chase.

Divergence view: on the 12h, price made a lower low while RSI and MACD made higher lows. The daily MACD histogram flipped positive, and the 1h shows hidden bullish divergence. But 4h momentum just rolled over, so I'd only take a limit near the lower band.

Where I'm wrong: a 12h close below the latest higher low breaks the base and the divergence together. Losing the November low would flip me short.

Risks: daily, 12h and 4h moving averages are all stacked bearish overhead. The upcoming Fed decision and reports of exploit-linked funds moving into ETH could bring sharp swings.

Two numbers decide whether a perp farm actually pays you. Neither one lives on the points dashboard.  @perptools

The first is funding.

Perps don't settle the way spot does. Every few hours one side of the book pays the other, and if you're holding the side that pays, you're quietly renting your points with real money. Ten thousand dollars long at 0.01% per interval is about a dollar a pop, roughly ninety a month. On a market running hot at 0.08%, the same position bleeds around eight dollars every interval — call it seven hundred a month, gone, to farm a bar that nobody can price yet.

That's the invoice. Most people never open it.

Which is why the first thing I check on a market isn't the chart. It's the funding rate sitting in the market header, right above the order ticket, before I touch size. If the number is against the direction I want, I flip the side, wait for the reset, or pick a market where the crowd is already paying me to hold. Same volume, same points, except one version costs me nothing to carry and the other quietly eats the position.

The second number is fees per round trip. Small per trade, brutal at volume, and it's the reason I stopped making forty tiny entries a week and started making four deliberate ones.

There's a cheaper leg most farmers skip, too. Prediction markets onboard from ten cents, losses are capped at the stake, and it keeps you active during weeks when you don't want directional exposure. Whether a given market qualifies is printed on the dashboard — read it there instead of trusting a thread.

Worth saying what's underneath all this, because a venue that lets you read funding properly is not the same as one that hides it. Three products shipped before a token exists. Around $240M of volume during the private beta alone. Animoca, NEAR and BigBrain on the cap table. Non-custodial on Solana, liquidity shared through Orderly's omnichain book so you never bridge. That's a real venue, not a farming wrapper.

Connect, open one market, read the funding line before you read the chart, and size so the carry can't kill you. Two tabs, five minutes, and you'll never farm blind again — points may count toward future rewards, but the funding bill arrives every eight hours whether you've done the homework or not.

Crypto ETFs Bled While Stocks Ripped: Week Ending November 27, 2026

For the week ending Friday, November 27, the S&P 500 rose 5.6% to 7,297.49, the  Nasdaq Composite gained 6.7% to 24,129.50, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 5.5% to 50,774.94. The Nasdaq posted its strongest week since April 2025, the Dow its best since 2022. The rebound followed the prior week's sharp selloff, when the Nasdaq fell about 10%. AI and chip names led the snap back, with all 11 S&P sectors higher on Friday.

Bitcoin gained 2.32% for the week to $59,861, Ether rose 3.91% to $1,669.62, and Solana rose 5.63% to about $71. Prices bounced. ETF demand did not.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.32 billion across the four trading sessions: $569.7 million on Monday, $231.4 million on Tuesday, $453.0 million on Wednesday, and $61.8 million on Friday. November 26 was Thanksgiving, when U.S. markets were closed. All four days were outflows, extending the streak to eight sessions. Friday's total crypto ETF outflow was $75.8 million: Bitcoin outflow of $61.8 million, Ether outflow of $12.1 million, Solana outflow of $0.9 million, Hyperliquid outflow of $1.0 million. XRP had not yet reported November 27, so the Friday total remains partial.

For November, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have now lost about $5.45 billion, surpassing June's prior monthly record of $4.51 billion. Against $76.25 billion in total spot Bitcoin ETF net assets, that is about 7.1% of assets in one month. This is a comparison of cumulative outflows with net assets, not a direct measure of the percentage decline in fund assets.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $4.50 billion of November withdrawals through November 25. On November 25 alone, IBIT lost $329.7 million of the $453 million withdrawn across all U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. No Bitcoin ETF saw a net inflow that day. On Friday, GBTC, not IBIT, led outflows at $23.0 million.

IBIT held about $44.9 billion in assets on November 25, by far the largest U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF. AUM moves reflect both redemptions and price. One exception: Morgan Stanley's Bitcoin Trust took in $114.1 million in November through November 25.

U.S. spot Ether ETFs lost money for nine straight sessions through November 27, including $68.5 million on November 25, all from BlackRock's ETHA. November outflows reached about $1.30 billion, against $14.37 billion in total spot Ether ETF net assets.

A week earlier, Solana was the exception. Solana ETFs took in $4.38 million in the week ending November 20, their first positive week after six weeks of outflows. XRP also broke its selling run, with a $4.07 million inflow on November 25, all into Franklin's XRPZ, after November withdrawals ended a seven month inflow streak.

Stocks were buying a tech rebound. Crypto faced continued ETF redemptions and leveraged selling. A $6.8 billion Bitcoin options expiry on November 27 drew attention, but notional expiry value is not money withdrawn from the market. Flows show what left, not who sold or why.

What to watch: November U.S. employment on December 4, and the Federal Reserve decision on December 9. If next week's prints break the eight day Bitcoin and nine day Ether outflow streaks, capitulation may be ending. If not, the gap widens.

SoSoValue, US Spot ETF Dashboard
Alpha Finance, Crypto ETF Flows
Investopedia, Nov 27 close, plus Wall Street Journal, Nov 27
BlackRock iShares, IBIT

2126507622190727343.text:
Everyone is quoting the same number from Google's TPU Sync launch: 90% faster KV cache transfer.

I read the blog, the repo, and the Ironwood spec sheet. That number is the least interesting thing in it.

Short version: TPU Sync is a C++ library that moves KV blocks and model weights across TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the datacenter network — the plumbing that makes disaggregated serving possible outside Google's walls.

What it actually ships is the model-state layer TPU never had in public. Google has run prefill/decode disaggregation, tiered KV caching, and RL weight broadcast internally for Gemini for years. External customers got aggregated serving: one whole model, one slice, no escape hatch. TPU Sync plus TorchTPU plus vLLM's KVConnector is that gap closing.

Now, why it had to be built this way.

Per chip: HBM moves 7,380 GB/s. PCIe Gen5 to the host moves about 63 GB/s. That is a 115× cliff. And host DRAM is not a bigger pool either — 960 GiB against 768 GiB of HBM on a 4-chip VM, so 1.25×.

Translation: on TPU, offloading can never win on capacity or bandwidth. It can only win by wasting nothing. Hence the three design choices — layout-preserving zero-copy DMA, transfers that overlap compute without taking PJRT usage locks, and a data path that never enters XLA, so nothing recompiles.

Which means the numbers deserve a second pass.

→ "Seconds to 230 ms" is real, but it's a floor, not a win. At BF16 and ~32K context you are moving ~6 GB; 230 ms is ~26 GB/s, or one saturated 200 GbE NIC. Nothing left to squeeze in software. The next gain has to come from more wire.

→ "TTFT down 60–90%" is measured against not having the library at all. That is closing a capability gap, not taking a lead.

→ "10× cache capacity" only holds once weights have eaten HBM. Compare totals and it is 1.25×.

→ "+30–70% throughput" is the one I believe. It is goodput at sustained load — idle accelerators, not faster tokens.

The bill arrives in two places. In-place buffer aliasing without usage locks moves correctness into block-level leases, where a bug corrupts silently instead of crashing. And the repo pins seven JAX / jaxlib / libtpu combinations, with a warning that a mismatch "crashes far from the cause." Bypass the compiler, pay in version maintenance.

Where it lands: NVIDIA still wins part of the disaggregated serving curve (SemiAnalysis). But the cheapest optimization is not moving data faster — it is not moving it. Prefix-affinity routing and per-rank session pinning now live in llm-d on GKE, and that is the part I would steal regardless of whose silicon I run on.

Status check: 196 stars, 166 open issues, dev-only wheels, the torch path not yet gated on end-to-end performance. Evaluate it. Don't ship on it.

The real story is quieter than 90%: a model-state layer is turning into a software category of its own — NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake, TPU Sync. Whoever standardizes that seam owns the next migration cost.

Wall Street just had its best week since 2022. Bitcoin just had its eighth losing week in a row. That gap is the story going into December.

On Friday's half day session, U.S. stocks closed solidly higher and locked in big weekly gains. Bitcoin went the other way: it briefly topped $62,000, then sold off as New York opened and finished the week below $60,000. When stocks bounce this hard and crypto cannot hold a bid, it is worth asking what crypto is actually trading on right now.

Here is the data, both sides of the argument, and the dates that decide the next leg.

Stocks: a big week inside a bad month
- Friday close (Nov 27): S&P 500 7,297.49, +1.60%. Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50, +2.31%. Dow 50,774.94, +591.99 points or +1.18% (Reuters, CNBC).
- For the week: S&P 500 +5.6%, Nasdaq +6.68%, Dow +5.46% (Reuters). It was the S&P 500's best week since April 2025 and the Dow's biggest weekly gain since October 2022 (Reuters, CNBC).
- Chips led. The broader chip gauge rose 4.7%, Micron +7.6%, Marvell +7.3%. Nvidia ended only +0.8% after being weak most of the session (Reuters).
- Volume was thin: 10.97 billion shares on U.S. exchanges in a session that closed at 1 p.m. ET (Reuters).
- The month is still ugly. Reuters says the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are on track for their worst November since 2008.
- Jamie Cox of Harris Financial Group: "The market is so oversold that a bounce was inevitable." Andrew Slimmon of Morgan Stanley Investment Management said so much fast money has delevered out of tech that the bounce "could have persistence next week as they are forced to chase back in" (Reuters). Both are opinions.

Bitcoin: the rally that did not stick
- Bitcoin climbed as much as 2.3% to top $62,000 on Friday, then fell to a 24 hour low around $58,760 as U.S. stocks opened, and traded near $59,900 afterward (Bloomberg via Mint).
- Yahoo Finance's weekly wrap put Bitcoin at $59,875 at the end of the trading week, down 2% over five trading days. That is eight straight weekly declines, the second longest losing streak on record (Yahoo Finance).
- November damage: down roughly 23% for the month, on track for the worst month in more than four years (Bloomberg via Mint; MarketWatch citing Dow Jones Market Data, which compares it with June 2022's 40.3% drop).
- Same pattern earlier in the week: on Nov 23 Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and Nvidia closed up 31.5% (Nvidia, Reuters). Bitcoin swung from a low near $60,400 to a high near $64,600 that day, then closed it almost flat at about $61,270 (Binance daily data, UTC).
- Live check: Bitcoin $60,161, -0.69% in 24 hours. Ether $1,669, -1.66%. Both as of 09:55 SGT (UTC+8) on Nov 28, CoinGecko.
- Total crypto market cap is about $2.09T, -3.3% in 24 hours, with Bitcoin dominance near 57.8% (CoinGecko, 09:55 SGT).
- The Crypto Fear and Greed Index reads 10 today, after 12 and 11 the previous two days. All Extreme Fear (https://t.co/Xg3rc0bwjU).

The money is still walking out
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw seven straight trading days of net outflows from Nov 17 to Nov 25, totaling about -$3.05B (Farside Investors data; my sum).
- November outflows reached about $5.39B through Nov 25, already a monthly record, with IBIT leading (SoSoValue via The Block). Other trackers count it differently (Observatorio Blockchain cites $4.94B), but every count I found is a record.
- Friday, Nov 27 is not final yet. Farside shows -$61.8M from the funds that reported, with IBIT still missing. Coin365 shows IBIT at -$328.5M and total Bitcoin ETF flows at -$390.3M, plus -$79.9M from Ether ETFs. Treat Friday as incomplete until Farside fills in.
- Whale cushion is thin. CryptoQuant says wallets holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC have an average unrealized profit margin of 5.7% this quarter, the lowest of 2026, down from 33.9% in late September. Unrealized gains for addresses with 1,000+ BTC are $23.8B, down from $124.7B in September and a peak of $294.4B in August 2025 (CryptoQuant via Bloomberg).

Why crypto is not following stocks
Facts first:
- Rates. CME FedWatch showed about 98.9% odds of a 25bp hike at the Dec 8 to 9 FOMC meeting on Nov 27 (CME FedWatch via MacroMicro). For January, the odds of a cumulative 50bp of hikes have ranged from about 60% to 66% in recent snapshots (CME FedWatch via https://t.co/xjGtEC93wk and FXBus). Reuters says traders are almost fully pricing a December hike after strong Q3 GDP and hotter October inflation.
- The dollar. Yahoo Finance notes a rising U.S. dollar is competing with Bitcoin as a store of value.
- Correlation has not disappeared. Bitcoin's 40 day correlation with the Nasdaq 100 had climbed to 0.69 as of Nov 20, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. DWF Labs found that on days the Nasdaq fell 1% or more, Bitcoin fell about three quarters of the time since 2020 (Bloomberg).
- Confidence. Bloomberg points to a run of major crypto hacks and regulatory uncertainty after the U.S. midterms.
My read: equities rallied on positioning, with tech shorts covering and fast money chasing back in. Crypto has no equivalent forced buyer right now. ETF holders are still redeeming, large holders have little profit left to protect, and a hike makes holding cash pay more. Bitcoin is trading like a liquidity asset, not a tech stock.

The oil and OPEC+ layer
- Brent January futures settled at $95.44 on Friday, -1.2%, but +3.1% for the week, snapping a three week losing streak. WTI settled at $83.08, -0.4% on the week (MarketWatch, CNBC).
- Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are at just 31% of prewar levels, per preliminary Kpler data (MarketWatch).
- OPEC+ meets Sunday, Nov 29. Three sources told Reuters the group has agreed in principle to keep Q1 2027 output targets unchanged (via CNBC, FXEmpire). Iraq disputes a preliminary capacity assessment of 4.9M barrels per day, and Kazakhstan wants a higher number too (Iran International citing Reuters).
- Two forecasts pulling opposite ways: Rystad Energy sees a global surplus of about 5M barrels per day in 2027, while ANZ thinks Brent "can still push above $100 a barrel" without another major escalation (Iran International, CNBC).
- Why crypto cares: oil feeds inflation expectations, and inflation expectations feed the Fed hike story. A calm OPEC+ outcome removes one weekend risk; a surprise adds one.

The bull case
- Sentiment is near the floor. A Fear and Greed reading of 10 is the kind of level where it takes less good news to move price.
- Stocks just showed that oversold markets can snap back fast. If equity strength lasts into next week, crypto has room to catch up.
- Outflows may be slowing. Nov 24 was the smallest daily outflow since Nov 13 at -$231.4M (Farside), and Friday's partial count is small outside IBIT.
- Institutional holdings did not collapse: Q3 13F filings showed a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs as of Sept. 30 (Galaxy Research). 13F data is old by the time it is published, and Galaxy notes the funds' total holdings have since fallen by 38,531 BTC through Nov 16.
- A December hike is already priced near 99%. If it arrives as expected, part of the shock is already in.

The bear case
- Eight losing weeks in a row, the worst month in over four years, and Bitcoin could not hold $62,000 even on a day the S&P 500 rose 1.6%.
- Record ETF outflows, led by the largest fund, and Friday's IBIT number points to more of the same.
- Large holders have only a 5.7% average profit cushion, so further downside pushes more of them into loss.
- The market is pricing not just one hike, but odds of a second by January.
- Holiday liquidity is thin. Velo Data's Fredrick Collins expects "thin, volatile trading for the rest of the year" (Bloomberg via Mint). FxPro's Alex Kuptsikevich said a drop to $57,000 "would signal a return to the short-term bearish scenario" (Bloomberg via Mint). That is his view, not a forecast of mine.

Key dates (SGT is UTC+8)
- Nov 29 (Sun): OPEC+ ministers meet on 2027 output policy.
- Nov 30 (Mon): Month end. The November candle closes at 00:00 UTC, which is 08:00 SGT on Dec 1. Final November ETF flows follow.
- Dec 1 (Tue): ISM Manufacturing PMI, 10:00 a.m. ET (23:00 SGT).
- Dec 4 (Fri): November jobs report from BLS, 8:30 a.m. ET (21:30 SGT).
- Dec 8 to 9: FOMC meeting. The decision is due Dec 9 at 2:00 p.m. ET, which is 03:00 SGT on Dec 10. The Fed's pre-meeting blackout runs through Dec 10.
- Dec 15 (Tue): Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled on the Hoodi testnet at 19:12 UTC (The Block, Cointelegraph).

What I am watching
- Whether Bitcoin can rise on days when stocks rise, instead of only falling with them.
- Whether Friday's final ETF total confirms another large IBIT redemption, and whether December starts with any inflow days.
- The November monthly close, and whether the eight week losing streak becomes nine.
- The Sunday OPEC+ statement and Monday's oil open.
- ISM and payrolls next week. Hot data could push January hike odds higher. Soft data could ease them.

Facts above come from the named sources, with times marked. Prices move, so check live quotes. Lines marked "my read" or "watching" are opinion, not forecasts.

Stocks found their forced buyers this week. Crypto is still waiting for its own. Until flows turn, a stock market rally is not enough to lift crypto by itself.

Not financial advice. Investing involves risk. Do your own research.

【重要🚨】AIインフラ投資が再加速するか？米テキサス州、データセンターの環境許可審査を再開！

電力網への接続申請は1,800件超。
申請容量は約474GW。

なんと、テキサス州の電力網における過去最大の電力需要の5倍以上に相当する規模です。

AIバブル崩壊論が広がる一方、実体経済では巨大なAIインフラ投資計画が動いています。

今回のニュースは、半導体、電力、冷却設備、AIクラウド関連株の投資家にとって見逃せない内容です。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ① 何が起きたのか？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

米テキサス州の環境品質委員会（TCEQ）が、データセンター関連の環境許可審査を再開しました。

これまで電力不足、水資源の消費、地域住民への影響などを理由に、許可手続きが一時停止されていました。

今回の再開は、データセンター開発を進める企業にとって前向きな進展です。

ただし、審査再開は建設承認を意味するものではありません。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ② 474GWという驚異的な規模
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

テキサス州政府が8月3日に公表した電力網への接続申請状況。

🔹申請容量：約474GW超
🔹データセンター関連：約90％
🔹過去最大の電力需要の5倍以上

仮に1GW級の発電設備で換算すると、474基分に相当する規模です。

もちろん、すべての計画が実現するわけではありません。

資金調達や顧客の確保ができず、実現しない案件も多いとみられています。

それでも、AIインフラ開発に対する企業の意欲の大きさがうかがえます。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ③ 保存版📌 注目のAIインフラ関連銘柄
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

【AI半導体】
・NVIDIA（$NVDA）
・AMD（$AMD）

【データセンター開発】
・Fermi（$FRMI）

【発電・電力インフラ】
・GE Vernova（$GEV）

【冷却・電源設備】
・Vertiv（$VRT）

建設計画が実際の設備投資に移行すれば、GPUだけでなく、発電設備、変圧器、冷却設備などにも需要が広がる可能性があります。

※今回の審査再開による個別企業の新規受注が確定したわけではありません。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ④ 特に注目したいFermi（$FRMI）
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

テキサス州で大規模AIインフラ開発事業「Project Matador」を進めている企業です。

最新の決算資料によると、主に独自の電力供給網を活用した約11GW規模の開発構想を掲げています。

さらに11月12日には、投資適格のハイパースケーラーとの新たな取り組みを発表。

✅ 約600MWの電力供給計画
✅ 2億ドルの前払い契約
✅ 1,500万ドルの初期建設・敷地開発契約

ただし、長期賃貸契約はまだ正式締結されていません。

また、従来のTensorWaveとの契約は11月10日に終了しています。

今回の審査再開は事業環境にとって前向きですが、Fermi自身の資金調達や顧客獲得が成功するかは別の問題です。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ⑤ AI投資の最大のボトルネックは電力？
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

AIの普及
　　↓
データセンターの建設
　　↓
電力需要の拡大
　　↓
発電所・送電網の不足
　　↓
電力インフラへの投資

高性能なGPUを確保できても、十分な電力がなければ稼働させることはできません。

今後のAI開発競争では、半導体の調達能力だけでなく、安定した電力を迅速に確保できる能力が競争力を左右する可能性があります。

自前の発電設備を持つデータセンターや、発電設備メーカーにも注目したいところです。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ⑥ ただし、2027年の規制リスクに注意
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2027年1月に就任する予定のジーナ・ヒノホサ次期州知事は、データセンター開発に対する規制強化を掲げています。

電力料金の上昇、水資源の確保、地域住民の生活環境など、解決すべき課題も残されています。

そして次の重要イベントは、

📅 12月10日
ERCOTによるデータセンターの影響調査に関する最終報告書の公表予定。

電力網への接続や今後の規制方針を考えるうえで、重要な判断材料となりそうです。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
■ ⑦ 今後の展望・考察
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

AI株の急落によって、AI産業そのものの成長が終わったかのような悲観論も広がっています。

しかし、今回のニュースからは、大規模なAIインフラ開発構想が依然として存在していることが分かります。

重要なのは、投資計画がどれだけ実行され、企業の利益につながるのかという点です。

AI株の調整が、産業の衰退によるものなのか、それとも過剰な期待や資金調達環境の悪化によるものなのか。

この違いを見極めたいところです。

AIの頭脳は半導体。
AIの神経は光通信。
AIの生命線は電力。

次のAI相場で大きく成長するのは、AIを開発する企業だけでなく、AIを動かすためのインフラを供給する企業かもしれません。

皆さんは、AI半導体株と電力インフラ株、今後どちらに投資妙味があると考えますか？

Market Pulse 28/11

---

**Black Friday half-day: tech-led bounce.**

S&P 500 +1.60% to 7,297.49  
Nasdaq +2.31% to 24,129.50  
Dow +1.18% (+592) to 50,774.94  

**Week**: S&P +5.6% (best since April 2025), Nasdaq +6.7%, Dow +5.5% (best since October 2022). November still on track for worst since 2008.

**Chips led**: SOX +4.7%. $MU +7.6%, $MRVL +7.3%, $SNDK ~+16%, $AVGO ~+4%. $NVDA lagged, +0.8% to $150.49.  
Hyperscalers up: $AMZN ~+4%, $META >+3%, $MSFT and $ORCL higher.  
Anthropic ~+11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price.

**Rates went the other way.** 10Y 4.94% (+9 bp), 2Y 4.69% (+8 bp) (Treasury par curve). Reason: Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%, October PCE 3.8% y/y. December Fed hike almost fully priced.  
Brent −1.2% to $95.44 (week +3.1%). WTI −0.7% to $83.08.

**Week ahead**  
• Sunday: OPEC+ sets 2027 policy.  
• Tuesday: ISM manufacturing, $MRVL earnings.  
• Wednesday: $CRM earnings.  
• Thursday: Huang testifies to Senate Banking.  
• Friday: November payrolls (FactSet est. 90k, 4.1% unemployment).  
• FOMC December 8–9.

**Takeaway**  
A positioning bounce in a thin half-day session, not a re-rating. Chips rallied even as the 10Y rose to 4.94%. Rates are still the ceiling on AI multiples. Payrolls plus $MRVL/$CRM decide whether the bounce holds.
