A token fell by half in a few hours, and the stablecoin next to it slipped off its dollar peg. Here is what is confirmed, what is still a question, and what nobody has answered yet.

On Saturday, Nov 28, World Liberty Financial's WLFI token crashed, and its dollar stablecoin USD1 traded below $1 on several exchanges. A wallet that the analytics firm Arkham labels as World Liberty's strategic reserve had sold about $20M of Ether earlier in the day. World Liberty had not commented as of 14:58 SGT. This is a fast-moving story, so every price below carries a time, and I separate what the data shows from what people are asking.

Thread one: the WLFI crash
- On Binance, WLFI traded around $0.0346 at about 12:25 SGT and around $0.0188 at about 13:55 SGT. That is about -46% in 90 minutes (Binance 5-minute candles, my arithmetic). The low was $0.0158 in the 13:45 SGT candle (Binance).
- At 14:57 SGT, WLFI was about $0.01887, down 54.8% over 24 hours (CoinGecko). Binance showed $0.0191, down 54.2%, with a 24-hour range of $0.0158 to $0.0418, at the same time.
- WLFI's market cap was about $607.7M at 14:36 SGT, with 31.66B of 100B tokens circulating (CoinGlass).
- Derivatives: $15.85M of WLFI futures positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $14.70M of it longs (93%). Open interest fell 60.6% to $114.18M, and the funding rate was -1.07% (CoinGlass, 14:36 SGT). Individual reports of "more than $10M in an hour" refer to narrower windows (Cryptobriefing).
- An early social media report (Watcher Guru) said WLFI fell more than 35% in 15 minutes. I could not confirm it at that granularity. The Binance candles show the steepest part of the move was concentrated between roughly 12:30 and 14:00 SGT.

The ETH sale: what is reported and what is not
- Lookonchain reported that a wallet it tagged as WLFI sold 10,600 ETH (about $17.58M) and 1,378 mETH (about $2.48M), roughly four hours before it posted (Lookonchain via BeInCrypto).
- On-chain analyst Yu Jin (EmberCN) put the total at about 12,121 ETH-equivalent, worth about $20.06M, at an average of about $1,655 per ETH (RootData, TokenPost). The report was timed about 09:05 SGT and said the sale was "about four hours ago," so the sale was around 05:00 SGT, roughly seven hours before the steepest part of the price drop. That timing is my inference from those timestamps.
- The proceeds were about $17.58M in USDC and $2.48M in USD1. The trades ran through CoW Protocol, according to Arkham data cited by BeInCrypto.
- The analysts estimate the ETH was bought at an average of about $3,244. That implies a realized loss of about $19.26M, close to 50% of cost (Yu Jin via RootData, TokenPost). The math checks out: 12,121 ETH times the $1,589 gap per ETH is about $19.26M.
- BeInCrypto, citing Arkham, also reported that the wallet sent 2.5M USD1 to the lending platform Dolomite, and that about 2,000 ETH (about $3.31M) later moved back from Dolomite to the reserve.
- Attribution matters here. The wallet is labeled by Arkham as World Liberty's strategic reserve. I have not seen World Liberty confirm that the wallet is its own or explain the sale. Treat the label as an analyst attribution, not a confirmed fact.
- Selling ETH is not the same as selling WLFI tokens. The ETH sale was about $20M, small against a roughly $600M market cap, so the timing alone does not show it caused the crash. Thin liquidity, leveraged positions and sentiment may all matter. That is my read, not a finding.
- Context from World Liberty's own X posts: on Nov 6 it announced a WLFI buyback program that it said may be funded by an initial allocation that "may include fees earned from USD1 reserves and other sources." On Nov 20 it said it had burned the first 100M WLFI.

Thread two: USD1 slips below $1
- USD1 is the dollar stablecoin tied to World Liberty. According to BitGo's September reserve report, it is issued and redeemed by BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A., while World Liberty and an affiliate own the brand.
- Market cap was about $2.78B at 14:57 SGT (CoinGecko).
- On Binance's USD1/USDT pair, the hourly price was about $1.0007 through the 11:00 SGT hour. It dipped to a low of $0.9987 in the 12:00 hour and $0.9973 in the 13:00 hour. In the 14:00 hour it hit a low of $0.9633 (Binance). At 14:57 SGT it traded around $0.9666, down about 3.4% over 24 hours (Binance). A caveat: that pair is priced in USDT, not in dollars.
- At about 13:48 SGT USD1 was $0.9981 on Binance, and at about 14:31 SGT it was $0.9967 on Coinbase (TokenPost). At 14:57 SGT, CoinGecko showed about $0.9739.
- So the price was a small dip first, then a wider gap in the last hour. Different venues showed different numbers at different minutes, so treat this as a range of roughly 96.3 to 99.7 cents depending on venue and time.
- Redemption is a structural point. BitGo's terms say direct minting and redemption are available to registered customers in good standing. Holders without a BitGo account can transfer USD1 but do not have direct redemption rights (BitGo reserve report). That is one reason the secondary-market price can drift from $1 when sellers outnumber buyers.

The reserve questions, kept separate from the price move
- A community member posted on World Liberty's governance forum on Nov 18, asking where reserve money had gone, citing $4.6B in June and $3.2B "today." I could not verify those figures. I did not see an official reply in the forum list.
- What is on the record: BitGo's September report, examined by an independent accounting firm and dated Oct 29, shows 4,416,180,490 USD1 outstanding against $4,416,592,901 of redemption assets on Sep 30 (BitGo reserve report). That is a ratio of about 1.0001. Eligible reserve assets are limited to cash, short-term U.S. Treasuries, fully collateralized reverse repos and government money market funds.
- USD1's market cap is about $2.78B now, versus about 4.42B tokens on Sep 30. Fewer tokens in circulation means redemptions have happened, which also shrinks reserves. My arithmetic, not a statement about reserve quality.
- I do not have a reserve report newer than September. A smaller supply, by itself, is not evidence that reserves are impaired. The questions are legitimate; the data to answer them would be the next monthly report and the live proof-of-reserves dashboard.
- A third-party risk report says about $888M was redeemed over five weeks to Nov 6 without a depeg and with an hourly low of $0.99667 on Nov 3 (Vitrine, third-party analysis, not an official source).
- Neither BitGo nor World Liberty had commented on today's price move in anything I found as of 14:58 SGT, including their X accounts.

Other stress cracks this week
- The OCC closed United Fidelity Bank of Evansville, Indiana on Nov 27. The FDIC became receiver and First-Citizens Bank & Trust agreed to assume substantially all deposits and purchase substantially all assets. The OCC said the bank was in an unsafe or unsound condition and likely unable to pay its obligations (OCC, FDIC).
- The bank had about $5.9B in total assets and $5.4B in deposits at Sep 30. The FDIC estimates a $1.83B cost to its Deposit Insurance Fund. Depositors keep their funds and insurance coverage (FDIC). Reuters called it the largest U.S. bank failure since Republic Bank in April 2024.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $5.39B of November outflows through Nov 25 (SoSoValue via The Block). Farside showed another -$389.0M on Nov 27, with IBIT at -$327.2M.
- None of these is linked to World Liberty in anything I found. They are separate pressure points arriving in the same week.

Market backdrop
- U.S. stocks closed higher on Friday: Dow 50,774.94 (+1.18%), S&P 500 7,297.49 (+1.60%) and Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50 (+2.31%). The S&P 500 gained 5.6% for the week, its best since April 2025 (Reuters).
- Crypto did not join. At 14:57 SGT Bitcoin was $59,730, down 3.24% in 24 hours, and Ether $1,657.19, down 4.49% (Binance). CoinGecko showed $59,677 and $1,655.91 at the same time.
- The Crypto Fear and Greed Index read 10 today and 12 yesterday, both Extreme Fear (https://t.co/Xg3rc0bwjU).
- The Fed's blackout began today. A 25bp hike at the December meeting was priced at about 99% on Friday (Reuters).

The bull case
- The WLFI move looks like a thin, leveraged market flushing out: open interest is down more than 60% and most liquidations were longs. That clears positioning, even if it does not show demand.
- USD1's last published examination shows reserves matching the token supply, with a narrow list of eligible assets. If the next report looks similar, the peg gap is more likely a liquidity story than a solvency story.
- A weekend price on a USDT pair in a panic can overshoot. A quick return toward $1 would support the liquidity reading.
- Equities had their best week in over a year, and the banking system handled the United Fidelity failure through a same-day sale with depositors protected.

The bear case
- The project has not explained the ETH sale, and the wallet label is still unconfirmed. Silence leaves room for worse readings than the facts may justify.
- A reserve wallet that sold at roughly half its reported cost basis, and received part of the proceeds in the project's own stablecoin, will draw scrutiny whatever the reason.
- USD1's price is moving at the same time as its supply is lower than in September. Confidence in a stablecoin can move faster than its reserve reports.
- The macro setup is hard: a priced-in hike, Fed speakers silent, ETF outflows continuing on a green day for stocks, and Extreme Fear in crypto.

Key dates
- Nov 30 (Mon): Month end. The last November ETF flows land after the session.
- Dec 1 (Tue): ISM manufacturing report, 10:00 a.m. ET.
- Dec 4 (Fri): U.S. jobs report from the BLS, 8:30 a.m. ET.
- Dec 8 to 9: FOMC meeting. The decision is on Dec 9 at 2:00 p.m. ET.
- No date set: BitGo's next monthly USD1 reserve report, and any statement from World Liberty. I found no scheduled WLFI event in this window. World Liberty's docs say the early-supporter unlock schedule starts with a two-year cliff after the vote on or about May 6, 2026.

What I am watching
- Whether World Liberty or BitGo comments, and whether it addresses the wallet and USD1 separately.
- Whether USD1 returns to about $1 across Binance, Coinbase and CoinGecko, or the gap persists into Monday.
- Whether the Arkham-labeled wallet moves more funds, and whether the 2.5M USD1 and the ETH flows with Dolomite change.
- The size of USD1's supply on the next reserve report and on the live proof-of-reserves dashboard.
- Whether Bitcoin holds above Friday's levels over the weekend with no Fed speakers.

Facts above come from the sources named, with times in SGT or ET as marked. Prices move fast, so check live quotes. Everything written as "my read," "my arithmetic" or "watching" is opinion, not a forecast, and nothing here alleges wrongdoing by anyone.

A crash and a depeg of a few cents in the same afternoon are not proof of anything on their own. The facts are still coming in, and the project's own answer is the missing piece.

Not financial advice. Investing involves risk. Do your own research.

So much rumor about AI breaking encryption. This is the top-20 list of cascading failures, ranked roughly by speed and severity:

1. **Global banking systems freeze or implode.** Encrypted ledgers, wire transfers, and account authentication become forgeable or fully readable. Mass account drains and bank runs begin within hours.

2. **Every cryptocurrency dies overnight.** Private keys are extracted at scale. Bitcoin, Ethereum, and every blockchain-based asset lose all value and integrity.

3. **Stock markets, derivatives, and high-frequency trading halt.** Ownership, order authenticity, and settlement can no longer be trusted. Exchanges shut.

4. **HTTPS/TLS and the secure web collapse.** Every site becomes a potential man-in-the-middle or phishing vector. Online banking, shopping, and logins become unsafe.

5. **Digital payments and e-commerce stop.** Credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and similar systems fail. Commerce reverts to cash, checks, or face-to-face barter.

6. **Cloud platforms and authentication systems are wide open.** AWS, Azure, Google Cloud credentials and data stores are exposed or controllable by attackers. Petabytes of corporate and personal data leak.

7. **Power grids, water systems, and industrial controls lose secure command channels.** SCADA/ICS systems become accessible. Regional blackouts, water contamination risks, and factory disruptions follow.

8. **Military and nuclear command-and-control degrade.** Battlefield communications, drone links, and strategic systems become spoofable or readable. Forces fall back to analog radios and physical couriers.

9. **Supply chains seize.** Shipping manifests, bills of lading, inventory records, and trade finance can be forged. Ports and warehouses freeze while goods sit.

10. **Aviation and transportation systems ground.** Air-traffic data links, avionics updates, and rail signaling lose trustworthiness. Massive cancellations and ground stops.

11. **Identity systems fail completely.** Digital IDs, passports, driver’s licenses, and logins can be impersonated at will. Borders, banks, and services face chaos.

12. **Healthcare records and medical devices are exposed or hijackable.** Patient histories, genetic data, prescriptions, and connected implants become readable or alterable. Blackmail, wrong treatments, and device attacks spike.

13. **Government classified networks and diplomatic communications dump into the open.** Secrets, internal memos, and surveillance files become public. Espionage and political crises accelerate.

14. **Code-signing and software update pipelines are forged.** Trusted OS and application updates can deliver mass malware. Devices of every kind are compromised at scale.

15. **IoT, cars, smart homes, and connected infrastructure become remotely controllable.** Locks, cameras, vehicles, and appliances lose authentication.

16. **Legal contracts, deeds, and evidence chains lose authenticity.** Digital agreements and court records become unverifiable. Property disputes and stalled trials explode.

17. **Elections and digital voting systems lose credibility.** Voter rolls, machines, and result transmission cannot be trusted. Political legitimacy crises follow.

18. **Corporate IP, source code, and R&D are instantly exposed.** Trade secrets evaporate. Industrial espionage becomes trivial; many competitive advantages disappear.

19. **Emergency services and 911 systems overload or fail.** Dispatch encryption and coordination break while simultaneous crises hit. Response times collapse.

20. **Everyday private communication ends.** Texts, emails, calls, and cloud storage are readable by anyone with the tools. Personal secrets, family matters, and political opinions become public knowledge, accelerating social fragmentation and a rush toward offline/analog methods.

**Longer-term fallout** (beyond the initial 20): forced retreat to one-time pads, physical couriers, air-gapped systems, and trusted human networks; possible economic depression from lost digital trust; boom in physical security and analog tech; and a partial societal regression away from digital dependence. Some actors would gain short-term power through total transparency or control of the remaining “secure” channels, while others would simply go offline.

This is a high-drama thought experiment. Real progress is more likely to be gradual (or quantum-driven), giving time for migration to post-quantum cryptography, better implementation hygiene, and hybrid physical/digital controls. But the scenario illustrates how deeply modern life depends on the assumption that certain math problems stay hard.

💡 DeFi Liquidity Is About More Than Access to Capital

One important question in DeFi is how users can access liquidity without constantly selling the assets they already hold.

Collateralized borrowing provides one answer.

USDD’s latest Ethereum updates bring two developments into focus: a 1% stability fee promotion for ETH and WBTC Vaults, and the introduction of wstETH as an additional collateral option.

These updates highlight two important aspects of on-chain liquidity.

1. Lower borrowing costs

The temporary 1% stability fee promotion reduces the stated cost of minting USDD against ETH and WBTC collateral during the campaign period.

2. Broader collateral utility

Adding wstETH gives holders of liquid-staked ETH another way to use their assets within a collateralized borrowing system while staking rewards continue to accrue through the token’s value.

This is relevant to the wider DeFi market because liquidity needs differ across users. Some want stablecoin access, while others want to retain exposure to their collateral and preserve its additional utility.

Still, flexibility does not remove risk. Collateral prices, liquidation thresholds, smart contract exposure and the cost of maintaining a Vault all matter.

The next phase of DeFi innovation will depend not only on creating more borrowing options, but also on making their risks and mechanics transparent.

🌐 USDD Adds wstETH as Collateral on Ethereum

Liquid staking assets are becoming increasingly useful across DeFi because they allow users to maintain exposure to staked ETH while interacting with other financial applications.

USDD has expanded its Ethereum Vault collateral options with the addition of wstETH.

The interesting part is how wstETH handles staking rewards.

Unlike stETH, whose token balance changes as rewards accrue, wstETH maintains a fixed balance while its value relative to stETH increases over time.

Now, with wstETH supported as Vault collateral, holders have another way to access USDD liquidity without first unstaking their ETH.

This creates an additional layer of capital flexibility:

• Maintain exposure to ETH through wstETH.
• Retain the staking rewards reflected in wstETH’s increasing value.
• Use the asset as collateral to mint USDD.

However, collateral value can fluctuate, and staking-related risks remain. Using wstETH as collateral also introduces liquidation exposure if the Vault’s required collateral ratio is breached.

The development expands the range of ways staking-linked assets can participate in DeFi.

The broader significance is the expansion of collateral-backed liquidity options beyond simply selling ETH or WBTC.

An asset does not necessarily have to be sold or left idle to become useful in DeFi. It can serve as collateral while maintaining its underlying economic exposure.

Where does your leverage actually leak money? 👇

Most people only look at entry price and leverage. But two quieter questions decide a big part of what a trade really costs you:

1. How do you pay to keep the position open?
2. What happens when price hits your liquidation line?

I mapped 11 protocols on those two questions. Here's how to read it.

← Left side: you pay as long as you're open
Perps like Hyperliquid, dYdX, Binance Futures and GMX charge funding (and on GMX, borrow fees too) while your trade is open. Lenders like Aave, Compound and Morpho charge a variable borrow rate. Liquity V2 lets you set your own rate.

The longer you hold, the more you pay. On a quick scalp it barely matters. On a trade you hold for weeks, it can eat a real chunk of your profit.

→ Right side: you pay once
You pay a fee to open and a fee to close, and nothing in between under normal conditions.

↓ Bottom: hard liquidation
Hit your line and a liquidator closes your position or takes part of your collateral, usually at a discount. On lenders like Aave, the liquidator earns a bonus from your collateral.

↑ Top: soft landing
Instead of one sudden hit, your position shrinks or converts gradually. crvUSD and LlamaLend use "soft liquidation", which converts collateral bit by bit inside a price band.

So where does @protocol_fx sit? 🟢 Top right.

Pay once:
On f(x), you pay a one-time fee to open and another to close. Funding is normally switched off. It only switches on temporarily if fxUSD, f(x)'s $1 stablecoin, needs help holding its peg.

fxMINT, which lets you borrow fxUSD against your ETH or BTC, has a 0% annual interest rate per the f(x) docs. You pay one-time fees instead.

Soft landing:
f(x) uses the Liquidation Brake. When your position reaches 88% LTV, part of your debt is repaid with your collateral, bringing you back to a safer level instead of wiping the position. Hard liquidation only happens at 95% LTV.

You can go up to 7x long or 6x short on ETH and BTC.

The only other protocol on the right side is Liquity V1: a one-time borrow fee and 0% interest, but hard liquidation below a 110% collateral ratio.

The honest part:
• This chart is simplified. It shows cost model and liquidation design, not safety or total cost
• Bottom left isn't "bad". Those platforms have deep liquidity, more markets and are great for short trades
• On f(x), funding can switch on during peg stress, and hard liquidation still exists at 95% LTV
• The brake shrinks your position, so you catch less of any rebound, and you can still lose money
• Fees and LTV levels are set by governance and can change
• Leverage is risky, and DeFi carries smart contract risk

The takeaway: if you hold leveraged positions for days or weeks, how you pay to stay open matters as much as your entry.

Pick the corner that fits how you trade.

Leopold Aschenbrenner's Q3 investor letter is circulating — 167 pages, dated November 24.

His core claim: the gap between the AI labs and the markets is the widest since ChatGPT. The market is pricing 2027 as a 0.3x–0.6x AI progress year. His model says 3x.

Takeaways:

MEMORY — AI agents and reinforcement learning are limited by memory, not raw compute. He calls SK Hynix ($SKHY) the Nvidia of the RL era, and says NAND is next: agents park their work-in-progress in cheap flash memory, and NAND prices have more than tripled since late 2025. After the crash, he says Kioxia trades below 1x his 2027 earnings estimate and could buy back ~three-quarters of its shares by the end of 2027. He also admits he trimmed Hynix from 41.9% of his public book to 3.9%.

NVIDIA — The market charges Nvidia ($NVDA) a premium multiple for a moat he says rapidly improving AI will destroy. His example: Claude got itself running on AMD ($AMD) chips in 3 days, work that used to take dozens of engineers months. He thinks Nvidia's cash flows get cut off far sooner than the market assumes.

NEOCLOUDS — CoreWeave ($CRWV), Nebius ($NBIS) and IREN ($IREN) are valued at ~1.0–1.2x their signed contracts. The market pays almost nothing for the power and chip allocations they have secured but not yet sold, and assumes the chips are worthless after six years, while older chips are recontracting at premiums. Spot compute prices are rising: SpaceX leases Anthropic ~325,000 GPUs for $1.25B a month, and raised the price ~60% in October.

ANTHROPIC ($ANT) — His largest position. Revenue run rate went from $1B at the start of 2025 to $81B in October 2026, at an 86% gross margin on inference. He says Anthropic could be the most profitable company in the world by the end of 2027, and the labs together exit 2027 above $1T in run rate.

Leopold's Situational Awareness Q3 Letter is excellent but long (167 pages) so I made a recap video! Overall I very much agree with most predictions made. (link to the letter at the end)

Most important predictions I read:
• 3 years of AI progress in 2027. The median estimate is 3.0x, with a range of 1.8–6.2x. That is a jump as big as GPT-4 (high schooler) to Opus 5.5 (summer associate or L5 engineer), on top of today's models by the end of 2027.
• Progress keeps speeding up. AI already runs about 1.9x a normal year's pace and reaches roughly 5.2x by the end of 2027 (16.6x in the bull case), because models are starting to automate AI research.
• "Virtual departments" replace "virtual interns." Hundreds of agents work persistently for weeks under their own managers. He expects these multi-agent systems "will be to 2027 as agents were to 2026."
• $1T+ in combined lab revenue run rate by the end of 2027, with anything from $500B to multiple trillions plausible. Wall Street's $150–200B for Anthropic would require AI to stagnate.
• Anthropic could be the most profitable company in the world by the end of 2027, passing Aramco, Nvidia and Samsung.
• AI compute gets far more valuable. An H100 earned $1–2/hour, earns $5–10/hour today, and goes to "$100s/hour+" as AI nears superintelligence.
• The market is the one making the radical forecast. It prices a 0.3–0.6x progress year: memory makers at one times next year's earnings and datacenters at only the contracts already signed.
• The real risk is political, not technical. A terrible accident could trigger a crackdown, but most paths still mean progress "far faster than the market expects."
• A ChatGPT moment for robotics is starting, with a buildout to billions of robots.
• Over $500T of wealth created and about $500T destroyed. Most companies lose most of their value as superintelligence makes their employees, IP and management obsolete. That includes many of today's AI winners and perhaps 400+ of the S&P 500.

2126566480578044005.text:
Retail keeps framing Jensen Huang's low-key return to $NVDA as a 1997 Steve Jobs victory lap, while credit desks are pricing a forced governance overhaul.

Look at the credit tape. On Nov 26, S&P placed NVDA's AA rating on 90-day CreditWatch Negative, explicitly flagging governance concentration, board independence, and the lack of a CEO succession plan. NVDA 5Y CDS just hit YTD wides at 147.3 bps (repricing cost of debt across $32.5B in public notes), a day after key neocloud partner CoreWeave saw its 5Y CDS blow out 1,314 bps to ~70% implied 5Y default odds.

Jensen's famous flat org chart with ~60 direct reports and no deputy layer was a speed advantage in an upcycle. In a regulatory downcycle, it offers zero compliance firewall. Between the BIS remote-compute crackdown in Southeast Asia, scrutiny on neocloud financing structures, and closed-door Congressional testimony on Dec 1, every subpoena and key-man discount lands on one desk. Breaking up that flat structure and naming lieutenants is the price of stabilizing ratings and credit spreads.

Still, the conspiracy theory that he was brought back to take the fall and exit completely within a year ignores board dynamics. NVDA's board is built around decades-long insiders, and with the stock compressed to 10-11x forward P/E ahead of the Vera Rubin ramp and hyperscaler ASIC competition, a hostile exit or executive liability hit would trigger institutional liquidation.

The cleaner historical analog is Microsoft in Jan 2000 at the peak of DOJ antitrust pressure: Bill Gates handed the CEO role and regulatory sign-off to Steve Ballmer while moving to Chairman and Chief Software Architect. Watch two catalysts from here: the tone coming out of Dec 1 Hill testimony, and whether NVDA appoints a COO or President before S&P's 90-day CreditWatch window closes in late February, alongside 5Y CDS compressing back below 100 bps.

Nov 28 | The AI trade has a new dividing line: who captures the returns?

Today’s X Intel tracks 373 posts, with zero new additions. It’s a snapshot of existing sentiment, not fresh market news.

Four debates still matter.

1. $NVDA: Strong earnings don’t eliminate execution risk.

The crowd remains divided between exceptional reported revenue growth and governance concerns.

The real questions are whether Nvidia can sustain its product roadmap, retain key engineers and protect margins as supply costs rise.

2. $NBIS, $CRWV and $IREN: Growth versus financing.

Nebius bulls emphasize a $38.7B backlog. CoreWeave points to potential demand for 300,000 GPUs coming off contract in 2027–28. IREN supporters highlight customer prepayments and asset-backed financing.

But backlog isn’t cash. Potential renewals aren’t signed revenue. And debt financing isn’t free capital.

3. Optical infrastructure shows a capital-allocation divide.

$COHR’s $2B buyback authorization contrasts with shareholder dilution concerns around $AAOI.

Yet AAOI’s newer $2.2B minimum-purchase agreement is missing from this stale sentiment snapshot.

The investment case must incorporate both demand commitments and the cost of fulfilling them.

4. AI capex expectations remain contradictory.

One reported survey finds 52% of investors expecting a major hyperscaler spending cut. Another forecast still projects 44% capex growth.

A slowdown in growth is not the same as a collapse in demand.

My view: The next AI winners won’t be determined by the biggest backlog or the loudest social-media narrative.

Watch actual deliveries, financing terms, dilution and free cash flow per share.

AI is creating enormous economic value. That doesn’t mean every shareholder gets to keep it.

今天X Intel追踪373条帖子，但没有新增内容。这是已有市场情绪，不是当天新增新闻。

① Nvidia：强劲业绩不等于风险全部消失。

$NVDA的多空争议，已经不应该停留在反复传播的管理层新闻。

更值得关注的是产品路线图、核心工程师留任，以及供应成本上升之后能否保持利润率。

真正决定回报的是现金流能否覆盖融资成本、折旧和后续扩张。

AI可以创造巨大的经济价值，但并不意味着所有参与其中的股东都能获得相应回报。

2027: APC Pledges 7,500MW Power Supply, $15bn Annual Non-Oil Exports by 2031

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has pledged to increase Nigeria’s average electricity generation to at least 7,500 megawatts and raise annual non-oil export earnings to $15 billion by 2031 if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu secures a second term in office.

The commitments are contained in Pillar Three of the party’s 2027–2031 manifesto, titled From Reforms to Prosperity, which focuses on energy, infrastructure and economic growth.

Under the proposed plan, the party also targets peak electricity generation of 10,000 megawatts by 2031, alongside reducing electricity distribution losses to no more than 16 per cent and installing an additional seven million electricity meters.

The APC further pledged to strengthen electricity transmission and distribution networks, improve gas supply, expand embedded power generation and provide dedicated, metered electricity to industrial clusters and free trade zones.

On economic diversification, the party aims to increase annual non-oil merchandise exports from $6.1 billion recorded in 2025 to at least $15 billion by 2031.

It said the strategy would prioritise processed agricultural products, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare products and other value-added exports to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on crude oil revenue.

The manifesto also proposes establishing at least one major industrial cluster in each of the six geopolitical zones to support manufacturing, create employment and attract private investment.

In addition, the APC targets increasing manufacturing’s contribution to Gross Domestic Product from 7.72 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 to at least 12 per cent by 2031.

The party also pledged to attract at least $5 billion in annual foreign direct investment and expand port cargo-handling capacity from 129.3 million metric tonnes to at least 180 million tonnes annually.

Other commitments include expanding the national fibre-optic network to 125,000 kilometres, completing strategic road and railway corridors and creating 100,000 jobs in the solid minerals and steel sectors by 2031.

The party said the proposed economic programme would focus on translating ongoing reforms into improved productivity, lower production costs, stronger businesses, increased investment and better household incomes.

The manifesto outlines measurable targets for the proposed 2027–2031 administration, with electricity supply, manufacturing output, export earnings, infrastructure development and job creation identified as key indicators for assessing performance.

India, week ended 27 November. The most consequential thing that happened was not a price. It was an order.

On Monday evening, after the close, IRDAI set up a six member expert committee to review its September consultation paper on the economics of insurance distribution. Dr Indu Bhushan chairs it, with members from NCAER, Oriental Insurance, Howden and SBI Life. The report is due 31 December, and the brief is wide: the effect on agents' incomes, transition glide paths for smaller insurers and distributors, and a rethink of commission limits on smaller premium policies.

Two readings matter. First, the proposals have not been withdrawn, they have been referred. The September paper drew roughly 2.18 lakh responses from more than 13,000 respondents, which is itself why a committee now exists. Second, and this is what the market cared about, final rules cannot reasonably land before the committee created to review the consultation has reported. January is the earliest plausible window for a revised draft, which quietly retires the "revised draft in mid December" line that has circulated for a fortnight without a single source stating it.

Insurance distribution names rose in all four sessions, and PB Fintech closed at its highest level since the September paper. One honest caveat: Monday's 6.5 percent move came hours before the committee was public, so something else drove that session and I have not found what.

The index lost about three quarters of a percent on the week, closing at 25,607.20, with Bank Nifty down about 2.5 percent from its record close. The interesting part is breadth, because it contradicted the index both ways. Wednesday's 1.85 percent gain came on negative breadth with smallcaps down. Friday's 989 point Sensex fall came on positive breadth with smallcaps up. A market that rises when most stocks fall, and falls when most stocks rise, is being pushed around by index weight rather than re-rated. Foreign buying explains it, at about 1.28 lakh crore of net purchases in November on the exchange provisional basis against domestic institutions selling nearly 55,000 crore.

Two macro reversals landed in three days. Brent gave back about six dollars of November's fall after a strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery, and the rupee went from an eight month high on Wednesday to a provisional record low of 92.98 on Friday. That combination is why India fell alone on Friday while every other large Asian market rose.

The week ahead has no large earnings. Monday brings the MSCI rejig after the close and the Coforge lock-in expiry. The RBI decision runs 2 to 4 December, with October CPI at 6.09 percent. The Fed follows on 8 and 9 December, close to fully priced, so January is the live question. SEBI's return to a 30 minute closing VWAP for expiry settlement starts 7 December.

After the $6.3B Breach: The Withdrawal Panic and the Recovery Data

The $6.3B security incident was not a minor event. On October 29, roughly 22,500 BTC exited Binance one of the largest outflow days recorded after the breach.

That initial withdrawal wave deserves attention. Erasing it from the record would leave out a key part of what happened.

But the following two weeks add important context.

CryptoQuant data covering October 29 to November 12 shows a clear shift:

· October 29: About 22.5K BTC left the exchange.
· November 3: Binance netflows turned positive at roughly 5.2K BTC.
· November 9: Another positive reading of about 4K BTC.
· November 11: Net inflows reached around 2.7K BTC.
· Latest reading: Flows were nearly flat at about +118 BTC.

So this was not a case of “nothing happened.” It was a sharp withdrawal reaction followed by a measurable change in exchange flows.

Trading activity tells a similar story. Binance spot trading volume stayed elevated, peaking around $70B–$80B, compared with the $30B–$50B range seen more often earlier in 2026.

Perpetual futures activity also remained strong, with trading volume repeatedly reaching roughly $240B–$320B and open interest holding up. Binance continued to rank as the largest venue by spot and perpetual trading volume.

What the data supports and what it does not

A security incident can trigger an immediate exit. But for the crypto market, the next move should be judged separately.

The return of BTC inflows, sustained trading activity, and continued exchange participation are evidence of operational recovery.

They do not prove that every user came back or that all trust concerns are gone. That distinction matters.

In crypto trading, recovery is better measured by observable behavior than by repeated reassurance.

Sources: CryptoQuant dashboard and Binance Research.

The underlying dashboards are public for independent verification.

Bullshit but lets go through for the sake of the argument:

What even superintelligent AI is likely able to find (and what it is not)
Superintelligence improves search, pattern recognition, proof discovery, and the speed of exploring mathematical spaces. It does not rewrite the underlying structure of hard problems or remove exponential work factors that are inherent to the problem size.
What AI is likely to improve
•  Constant-factor and low-order improvements Better heuristics, smarter search orderings, improved lattice techniques, or optimized implementations of existing algorithms (e.g., better Pollard rho constants, slightly better sieving, faster matrix arithmetic). These can shave bits off the effective security level but rarely collapse an exponential problem into a practical one.
•  Discovery of new algorithms with still-high polynomial degree An AI could in principle find a polynomial-time algorithm for factoring or discrete log whose degree is large (e.g., O(n^{20}) or higher). Such an algorithm is theoretically interesting and would be a major result, yet remains useless for 2048-bit RSA or 256-bit elliptic-curve groups. The crossover point where it beats brute force or the best classical algorithms lies far beyond practical key sizes.
•  Better attacks on reduced-round or weakened constructions We already see this (reduced-round AES, certain hash variants, small elliptic curves). These results calibrate security margins but do not automatically extend to the full standardized parameters.
•  Faster proof verification and formalization AI can help check or complete proofs (as seen with recent Riemann-related work). This increases confidence in hardness assumptions or reveals subtle weaknesses, but it does not itself produce a practical break.
What remains unlikely even for superintelligence
•  A practical (low-degree polynomial or sub-exponential with small constants) algorithm for SHA-256 preimage resistance. The output is a fixed 256-bit string. There is no known algebraic structure that would allow an efficient reverse function. An AI would still have to search a space whose size is exponential in the bit length. No amount of intelligence removes that combinatorial explosion.
•  A practical classical algorithm for the elliptic-curve discrete-logarithm problem on secp256k1. The best classical algorithms remain \Theta(\sqrt{n}). No sub-exponential classical algorithm is known, and the mathematical structure of elliptic curves over prime fields does not currently offer the kind of trapdoor or algebraic shortcut that would let even a superintelligent searcher collapse the work factor to something practical.
•  Transfer of progress from one hard problem to another. An improvement in integer factoring does not yield an improvement in SHA-256 preimage resistance or in the ECDLP. The problems are distinct. Superintelligence does not create a universal reduction that turns every hard problem into an easy one.
Practical consequence for Bitcoin and other systems
Even under optimistic assumptions about superintelligent AI, the most likely outcomes are:
•  Incremental reductions in effective security margins (a few bits to low tens of bits).
•  Discovery of high-degree polynomial algorithms that are still impractical.
•  Pressure to migrate to post-quantum schemes once any concrete attack (classical or quantum) becomes realistic.
All systems that rely on the same primitives—banks, TLS, messaging, software updates, and Bitcoin—would face the same pressure and would migrate. Btc UTXOs being independent and mostly having unrevealed public keys does not make it immune; it changes the attacker’s cost structure relative to a centralized system that concentrates value behind fewer long-lived keys.
The Puzzle addresses remain the simplest empirical check: if a practical classical break of the relevant problems existed, those addresses would already be empty. 
Bottom line: Superintelligence also uses no magic.

THE WEEK THE MARKET BOUNCED BACK

Nov 23-27, 2026. Thanksgiving week. Short, messy, and full of noise.

After last week’s AI-driven smash (S&P down ~8.6%, Nasdaq ~10%), everything bounced. Not cleanly, Not convincingly. But hard enough that most people who panicked last week already missed it. It was a black Friday sale and most of the people missed it.

Equities

S&P 500: +5.6% to 7,297
Dow (DJI): +5.5% to 50,775
Nasdaq: +6.7% to 24,130
Russell 2000: +6.5%

Monday was the whole story. Nvidia brings Jensen Huang back → stock rips ~31% → everything tech follows. Rest of the week was choppy. Friday’s half-day closed strong as people bought the dip in the same AI names they dumped the week before.

Still a bounce. Indexes are still well below the October highs. November is still ugly.

Gold & Silver
Gold: +~3–4% to ~$3,650–3,665
Silver: +~6–7% to ~$43.70–44

Metals got liquidated last week with everything else. Traders rushed to liquidate their PM holdings to save their positions in stock market. This week they bounced once the forced selling eased. Same pattern as stocks: oversold relief.

Oil
Brent mixed-to-higher on the week. Middle East attacks added a bid. OPEC+ meets Sunday. Not a clean story either way.

Bitcoin

Recovered into the high $59ks–$61k zone. Still down hard for the month. Same as equities - relief bounce after a brutal stretch, not a trend change.

Dollar & Yields

DXY stuck near 104. 10-year yield around 4.93–4.94%. Hot data (GDP revised to 4.3%, core PCE 3.3%) keeps a December hike almost fully priced. No one is pricing a pivot.

Bottom line This was an oversold bounce after a violent liquidation. The people who sold last week in a panic bought back higher. The people who sat on their hands or bought the weakness did fine. People who missed, are in FOMO.

Nothing is resolved. AI capex questions are still there. The Fed is still hiking. Next week brings jobs data and Jensen’s congressional appearances.

Same rules as always: don’t chase the bounce, don’t panic on the next dip, and own things you actually understand.

Key levels to watch next week:

Nasdaq – 27100
Gold – 3750
Silver – 47

A 97% share looks like a win. It mostly tells you what the counter is counting.

What changed:

Coinbase says more than 97% of onchain agent transactions in Q2 2026 used x402 (Decrypt). That is close to a default rail, and defaults are hard to displace once SDKs and merchant integrations assume them.

The rail moved too. In May 2026, x402 added batch settlement: agents hand sellers signed vouchers that settle in bulk instead of one onchain settlement per request (Decrypt).

Why it matters:

Batch settlement breaks the link between the metric and the economy it claims to describe. When many agent purchases collapse into a single settlement, transaction counts stop tracking agent activity and start tracking how operators choose to batch. A dominance figure measured that way describes the settlement layer, not how much work agents are doing.

The scarce input is not payment throughput. An agent can read the web but cannot see where people actually stop, how long they stay, what they pay for or how they move. That data sits with operators, devices and apps in no shared format, and usually cannot be proven to come from a real place at a real time. Payments were standardised first because they were the easy part: a signed instruction with a clear owner.

What to watch next:

Operator exits. Chiliz urged holders to bridge USDC off its chain to Arbitrum, BNB Chain or Avalanche ahead of the ChainPort shutdown, and said it cannot guarantee withdrawals after Dec. 1 (The Defiant, 2026-11-28). That is a data supply chain breaking in public: a deadline, a list of destinations, no guarantee.

Disclosures agents are expected to digest. Binance is moving 500 million USDC into its SAFU fund and says 7,500 bitcoin will return to treasury rather than be sold, after tapping the fund following its October breach (The Defiant, 2026-11-28). The transfer is verifiable. The reasoning is not.

Context that disappears while the number survives. A Thanksgiving buyer paid 106.24 USDC per Coinbase share while Nasdaq was closed (Cointelegraph, 2026-11-27). A real trade with no live market behind it.

Takeaway: x402 has effectively won the payment argument, and the harder fight is whether the data agents act on can be proven at all, by anyone, before they spend against it.

INJECTIVE (INJ) – STAKED INJ ETF STARTET AN DER NASDAQ

Ein weiterer Schritt für die institutionelle Integration von Kryptowährungen in die traditionellen Finanzmärkte.

Seit dem 5. November 2026 ist der Canary Staked INJ ETF unter dem Börsenkürzel INJC an der Nasdaq handelbar.

Damit erhält Injective einen zusätzlichen Zugang zum regulierten US-Kapitalmarkt.

Die wichtigsten Fakten:

• NASDAQ-LISTING: Der ETF ermöglicht Anlegern, über ein börsengehandeltes Wertpapier an der Kursentwicklung von INJ teilzuhaben.

• STAKING: Neben der Kursentwicklung strebt der Fonds zusätzliche Erträge durch das Staking von INJ an. Diese sind nicht garantiert.

• INSTITUTIONELLER ZUGANG: Investoren können ein Engagement in INJ über klassische Wertpapierdepots aufbauen, ohne die Kryptowährung selbst verwahren zu müssen.

• MARKTINTEGRATION: Das Produkt verbindet die Blockchain-Infrastruktur von Injective mit dem traditionellen Kapitalmarkt.

WARUM IST DAS SO INTERESSANT?

Während Bitcoin und Ethereum bereits über etablierte börsengehandelte Anlageprodukte verfügen, erweitert sich das Angebot zunehmend auf weitere Blockchain-Ökosysteme.

Für Injective ist diese Entwicklung besonders relevant.

Das Netzwerk positioniert sich mit seiner Infrastruktur für dezentrale Finanzanwendungen, Derivate und tokenisierte Vermögenswerte im Bereich der On-Chain-Finanzmärkte.

Ein börsengehandeltes Produkt könnte die Sichtbarkeit von INJ erhöhen und zusätzlichen Anlegergruppen den Zugang erleichtern.

Allerdings bedeutet ein ETF-Listing nicht automatisch steigende Kurse oder nachhaltige Kapitalzuflüsse.

Entscheidend werden die tatsächliche Nachfrage nach INJC, die Entwicklung des verwalteten Fondsvermögens und die langfristige Nutzung des Injective-Netzwerks sein.

Für uns ist deshalb nicht allein das Listing interessant, sondern die Frage, ob sich daraus eine nachhaltige institutionelle Nachfrage entwickeln kann.

Könnte INJ langfristig zu den Profiteuren der zunehmenden Tokenisierung und Institutionalisierung der Finanzmärkte gehören?

Wie bewerten Sie diese Entwicklung?

🐋 WHALE WATCH : $AAVE V4 crossed $1B in deposits and $310M in active loans. Heres whats building on top of it.

The architecture

V4 runs a Hub and Spoke model. Specialized protocols launch their own markets Spokes while drawing from shared liquidity infrastructure Hubs. Traditional lending requires each market to attract its own deposits. Aave V4 lets markets share liquidity while keeping separate collateral and risk configurations.

Whats live

Ethereum focused Spokes include Lido LSTs https://t.co/aV5c54Kbut plus a separate OP Mainnet Cash instance KelpDAO LRTs Ethena two Spokes on the Plus Hub, both with active incentives Lombard Finance $BTC and Paxos Global Dollar Hub for USDG covering PAXG gold Pendle PT USDG and Maple syrupUSDG.

Maple Finance runs syrupUSDG on the Global Dollar Hub and syrupUSDC as collateral on Arcs Core Hub. Pendle PT tokens serve as collateral across relevant Spokes with automated risk agents managing them.

Base Equities Hub supports seven tokenized equities as collateral via Coinbase. Arc runs a stablecoin native environment with Circle supporting USDC EURC cirBTC and WETH. PAXG is live as collateral for USDG borrowing.

In progress

A proposal introduced lending against assets held with qualified custodians off chain, using non transferable Custodied Collateral Tokens synced via Chainlink CustodySync. Sentora is building an externally curated Hub and Spoke framework with a 50/50 revenue share on an isolated Ethereum Hub. Babylon Labs integration and a Monad deployment are both planned.

Risk stewards can adjust parameters within governance approved limits across deployments.

The takeaway

V4 is early relative to V3, but the Hub and Spoke architecture is proving out as a practical framework for specialized credit markets. Protocols launching on V4 access shared liquidity on day one instead of competing for deposits from scratch.

High conviction on $AAVE after going deep on the research.

ビットコインの感謝祭ラリー、あっさり終了。
6万2000ドルを超えて盛り上がったのも束の間。
Deribitのオプション満期と重なって、たった30分で5万8000ドル台まで急落！
11月の現物ETFからの資金流出も、すでに50億ドルを突破。

24時間365日、いつでも自由に取引できるのが仮想通貨の強み。
そう信じているのは、もう個人だけだよね。

伝統的な金融機関がお休みの日は、市場の流動性がスッカスカ。
少しの売りで価格が急降下して、ロングポジションが次々と狩られていく。
結局、ウォール街の都合で振り回されるだけのATMになってる。

その横で、企業は美味しいところだけを綺麗に持っていく。
保険ブローカー大手のAonが、Solana上でステーブルコインを使った保険料の支払いを完了。
3月のテストでも、CoinbaseやPaxosと組んでUSDCやPYUSDをしっかり使ってた。
GENIUS法やOCCのルールといった法的な枠組みにガッツリ守られながらね。
Visaだって、すでにSolanaでUSDCの決済網を走らせてる。

価格変動のリスクを一切被らずに、安全なインフラだけをちゃっかり構築。

じゃあ、分散化の理想を信じてる個人はどうなってるの？
Bitcoin Coreのローカルテストで、恐ろしい結果が報告されてる。
資金を動かすための鍵を持たない、ただの「監視用ウォレット」。
これでも、トランザクションをブロードキャストする時の通信の癖で、アドレスとノードの結びつきが特定されちゃうんだって。
30回試して、見事に30回とも特定。
Torを使ってIPアドレスを隠しても、ノードの身元が紐づく可能性が残るって言うから驚き。

ただ眺めているだけなのに、行動は丸見え。

企業は価格が動かないステーブルコインで、安全にビジネスを回す。
個人は監視されて身元がバレるリスクを抱えながら、休日のボラティリティに巻き込まれて清算される。

大口の決済手段、個人の絶対不安。

同じブロックチェーンを使っているのに、立っているステージが全然違う。
法定通貨の代わりになるとか、金融の自由だとか。
そんな夢を見ている間に、システムは完全に大企業の都合のいいように整備されていく。

それでもまだ、仮想通貨が個人を解放するって信じて自分の身を削り続けるの？
本当に守るべきなのは、ウォレットの残高より自分のプライバシーだと思うけどな。

One thing I've learned about trading is that being right about the market direction doesn't always mean you'll survive the move.

Take perpetuals vs options, for example.

When the market suddenly moves against you, the difference becomes obvious.

With a leveraged long perp, losses increase as price falls, and if the move is aggressive enough, liquidation becomes a real risk.

With a bought option, your maximum loss is generally the premium you paid. There's no liquidation simply because the market moves against your position.

But options aren't risk-free either.

You pay an upfront premium, time decay works against you, and implied volatility can significantly affect the option's value.

Perps offer straightforward directional exposure, while options provide a different way to structure risk and potential returns.

This is why I'm interested in what @DeriveXYZ is building.

On November 23, Derive opened options markets covering real-world assets, including:
• NVIDIA
• Anthropic
• Gold
• WTI Crude Oil
• S&P 500
• Nasdaq-100

What makes this interesting is that traders can access exposure to these markets onchain, using USDC settlement and crypto collateral.

We're moving beyond the usual crypto-only trading experience.

Personally, I'd be interested in exploring gold options because I like the idea of having another market to trade when crypto gets unpredictable.

The bigger question isn't just whether you can predict the next move.

It's whether you understand the instrument you're using to trade it.

That's what makes learning options worth the effort.

📊 BRIEF DE MARCHÉ — 28 NOVEMBRE 2026

Rebond spectaculaire des indices : véritable point bas ou simple rebond technique ?
Après une semaine particulièrement volatile, les marchés américains rebondissent fortement malgré un environnement macroéconomique toujours fragile.

🌍 Macroéconomie & Fed
Nouveaux droits de douane américains envisagés de 20 à 35 %.
Core PCE à 3,3 %, contre 3,2 % attendu.
Probabilité rapportée de 99 % d'une hausse de taux de 25 pb le 9 décembre.
Nasdaq brièvement en bear market et VIX ayant atteint 40 en novembre.

🤖 Intelligence artificielle & semi-conducteurs
Nvidia accumule les risques réglementaires et concurrentiels, notamment avec le dossier Megaspeed et la montée en puissance des TPU de Google et du Trainium d'Amazon.
La demande en infrastructures IA reste néanmoins solide. Kioxia aurait déjà réservé toute sa capacité de production pour 2027, tandis que JPMorgan anticipe 1400 Md$ d'investissements dans l'IA l'année prochaine.

⚠️ Les signaux de vigilance
Détérioration du marché du crédit : CDS de SoftBank au-dessus de 500 pb et rendement obligataire de CoreWeave proche de 18 %.
Ralentissement de la croissance des usages de l'IA.
Risque de retournement du cycle de la mémoire.
Contraintes énergétiques et financières sur les data centers.

📈 Ma lecture du marché
Le rebond actuel semble principalement alimenté par des rachats de positions vendeuses et une faible liquidité liée à Thanksgiving.
La purge du positionnement institutionnel et la compression des valorisations commencent néanmoins à créer des opportunités intéressantes à moyen et long terme.
Je reste convaincu par la thèse structurelle de l'intelligence artificielle, mais davantage sélectif dans le choix des entreprises.

🎯 Stratégie : rester patient, conserver des liquidités, privilégier les entreprises aux fondamentaux solides et déployer progressivement son capital.
Ne confondons pas rebond technique et retournement de tendance. La priorité reste la gestion du risque, pas la recherche du point bas parfait.

Bon week-end à tous !

Nếu ngành bán dẫn giảm liên tục, SOXS có thể tăng trưởng rất mạnh. Anh em nào view ngành bán dẫn đang bị định giá quá cao hay bong bóng AI đang bị thổi phồng,... thì $SOXS là sự lựa chọn đáng cân nhắc khi stock đi vào suy thoái

急落の後に、急反発。

半導体やAI関連株を中心に買い戻しが進み、
アドバンテストと東京エレクトロンの2銘柄だけで、
日経平均を約555円押し上げた。
つまり、指数の大幅上昇には、
値がさハイテク株の影響も大きかった。
一方で、東証プライムでは582銘柄が下落している。
ここが重要だ。
日経平均が上がったからといって、
市場全体が強くなったとは限らない。
今後は半導体株だけでなく、
光通信、電力設備、銀行株などに
資金が広がるかどうかを確認したい。
■ 来週の日本株を左右する3つの重要材料
① キオクシア×NVIDIA
AI相場は、GPUだけでは終わらない。
11月26日、キオクシアはNVIDIAとの共同実証を発表した。
今回使用されたのは、
・KIOXIA XD8シリーズ 7.68TB SSD
・合計144台のSSD
・NVIDIA GB200 NVL72システム
・18台のサーバーノード
・約1.1PBのSSD容量
さらに、約2兆個のベクトルデータを処理できる可能性を検証している。
なぜ、これが重要なのか。
AIの進化によって、
GPUの計算能力だけでなく、
膨大なデータを効率よく保存し、取り出し、処理する技術も必要になっているからだ。
これまで市場では、
GPUやHBMといった分野に注目が集まってきた。
しかし、AIデータが増え続けるなら、
SSDやストレージ技術にも新たな成長機会が生まれる可能性がある。
今回の実証は、AIインフラの競争が
メモリーやストレージにまで広がっていることを示す材料だ。
ただし、ここは冷静に見ておきたい。
今回の発表はPoC（概念実証）であり、
正式受注や将来の売上を保証するものではない。
今後は技術検証の進展だけでなく、
量産採用や受注、業績への反映を確認する必要がある。
② AIの次に必要になるのは、電力と光通信
AIデータセンターが増えれば、
GPUやメモリーだけでなく、
大量の電力と高速通信も必要になる。
ここで注目したいのが電力インフラだ。
報道によると、東京電力HDは2035年度までの9年間で、
送電網や原子力関連設備などに約10.2兆円を投じる計画とされる。
AIの成長を支えるためには、
データセンターを建設するだけでは足りない。
電力を安定して供給する設備、
送電網の増強、
データを高速で運ぶ光通信網が必要になる。
つまり、AI相場の次の焦点は、
半導体の外側にも広がっていく可能性がある。
私が注目しているのは、
・フジクラ（5803）
・古河電工（5801）
・関電工（1942）
・東京電力HD（9501）
ただし、投資計画の報道と実際の受注・売上は別物だ。
期待だけで株価を判断せず、
具体的な設備投資や受注の進展を追いかけたい。
③ JTの巨額損失と買収をめぐる動き
今週、個別株で大きな注目を集めたのがJT（2914）だ。
JTはロシア事業をめぐり、
現地子会社7社を連結対象から除外することに伴って、
約1兆3,770億円の損失を計上する見通しを発表した。
2026年12月期の年間配当予想も、
従来の272円から204円へ修正された。
高配当株だから安心。
大型株だから大丈夫。
そう考えていた投資家にとって、
今回の発表は決して小さくない。
ただし、今回の損失は、
ロシア側の暫定管理措置によって実質的な経営権を失ったことに伴う会計処理が中心だ。
ロシア事業の工場や販売活動が、
直ちにすべて停止するという意味ではない。
さらに、英国たばこ大手Imperial Brandsをめぐって、
JTが他社と連携した買収を検討しているとの報道も出ている。
米Altriaも買収提案を検討していると明らかにした。
ただし、現時点でJTによる買収成立が決まったわけではない。
今後確認したいのは、
・ロシア事業を除いた利益成長
・204円配当の持続可能性
・買収を実行する場合の資金調達
・財務負担と株主還元への影響
高配当という数字だけでは、
企業の本当の強さは判断できない。
今回のJTの件は、
配当利回りだけで銘柄を選ぶリスクを改めて考える材料だと思う。
■ 月曜日に向けて、注目したい7銘柄
今回の材料を踏まえ、
私が継続して監視したい銘柄は次の7つ。
【AI・半導体】
・キオクシア（285A）
・アドバンテスト（6857）
・東京エレクトロン（8035）
【AIインフラ・電力】
・フジクラ（5803）
・古河電工（5801）
・東京電力HD（9501）
【金融・金利】
・三菱UFJ（8306）
注目している理由は、
単純に今週上昇したからではない。
AI投資の拡大、
データセンターの電力需要、
光通信インフラの増強、
そして日本の金利環境。
それぞれ異なる成長材料や相場材料を持っているからだ。
特に重要なのは、
半導体株だけが上昇する相場なのか、
関連する周辺産業にも資金が広がる相場なのかという点だ。
■ 月曜日、寄り付き後に確認したい5つのポイント
① 日経平均が58,700円近辺を維持できるか
金曜日の終値は一つの参考水準。
ただし、ここを必ず守るという意味ではない。
寄り付き後の売りを吸収できるかを確認したい。
② 半導体株の上昇が続くか
キオクシア、アドバンテストだけでなく、
東京エレクトロンなどにも買いが広がるか。
③ 光通信・電力設備に資金が向かうか
フジクラ、古河電工、関電工など、
AIインフラ関連の値動きを確認する。
④ 銀行株が底堅さを保てるか
物価と日銀の金融政策をめぐる思惑が強まるなか、
三菱UFJなど金融株の反応にも注目したい。
⑤ 出来高とVWAPを確認する
寄り付き直後の上昇だけで飛びつかない。
出来高を伴った上昇なのか、
VWAPを維持できるのか、
前場を通じて買いが続くのか。
このあたりを冷静に確認したい。
■ 来週の相場は3つのシナリオで考える
【シナリオ①：反発が続く】
半導体株への買いが続き、
光通信や電力設備にも資金が広がる展開。
この場合は、AI関連の中でも
実際の業績成長や受注が確認できる企業に注目したい。
【シナリオ②：指数は堅調でも個別株は分化】
日経平均は底堅いものの、
上昇する銘柄と売られる銘柄が分かれる展開。
この場合は、指数だけで判断せず、
個別企業の業績や資金流入を重視したい。
【シナリオ③：再びリスク回避】
米国のAI関連株が失速したり、
金利上昇への警戒が強まったりすれば、
日本の半導体株にも売りが波及する可能性がある。
その場合は、無理に買い向かわず、
下値と需給の落ち着きを確認することが重要だ。
■ 最後に、もう一つ忘れてはいけないこと
11月27日に発表された東京都区部の11月CPIは、
生鮮食品を除く総合指数で前年同月比2.9％上昇した。
物価が依然として高い水準にあることは、
日銀の金融政策を考えるうえでも重要な材料だ。
今後は12月の金融政策決定会合を前に、
金利見通しがどう変化するかにも注意したい。
金利の変化は銀行株だけでなく、
グロース株や不動産株などにも影響する。
だからこそ、来週は半導体だけを見ていればいい相場ではない。
今週の反発を見て、
すぐに強気へ傾く必要はない。
大切なのは、上がった銘柄を追いかけることではなく、
次に資金が向かう分野を見つけること。
そして、その企業が本当に利益を伸ばせるのか、
決算、受注、設備投資、キャッシュフローまで確認することだ。
私はこれからも、
日本株の資金の流れ、
AI・半導体の最新動向、
電力・光通信インフラの成長、
そして企業業績の変化を追いながら、
次に注目される可能性のある銘柄を整理していきたい。
月曜日、あなたが最も注目しているのはどの分野ですか？
① AI・半導体
② 光通信・電力インフラ
③ 銀行・金利関連
④ JTなどの個別材料株
ぜひコメントで教えてください。

Its all being done to destroy DJT and the tech bros build out. I checked for circular financing in the past. Its nothing new.  Various wealthy western powers have been doing it for at least past 6 to 7 decades.  That's how you create perpetual vassal states.

What do you think all the funding to various countries to buy American defense hardware is?  Is it charity?

 Bloomberg and FT were hoping that the dems in power would bring down the AI economy.  Musk said it as much that it will be much cheaper to build data centers in space.  With that will come permenant manned space habitats that can use generated heat if any for habitable environment.

We know very well. Both those publications are heavily biased.  And EU is falling far behind in AI infrastructure.

I digress.  Circular financing is not new.  

Cisco in the 1990s and around 2000: Cisco lent money or offered leases to telecom startups that used the financing to buy networking equipment, often Cisco’s. Cisco described its financing business as helping customers acquire technology; some borrowers later failed, leaving Cisco with unpaid debts.
Lucent around 2000: Lucent disclosed billions of dollars in customer credit commitments and guarantees. Separately, the SEC charged Lucent with improperly recognizing revenue and income. That case shows why customer financing and sales accounting drew scrutiny, but it does not mean every vendor-financing deal is fraudulent.

 Government-funded loop of spending: public funds support a foreign buyer, and the purchase becomes revenue for the donor country’s arms industry. The more precise terms are tied military aid or Foreign Military Financing. It resembles circular financing in the way money cycles back, but it is a disclosed policy mechanism involving a real purchase—not, by itself, a scheme to fabricate revenue.

NVIDIA may be selling real chips to real customers, just as a defense contractor may sell real equipment bought with military aid. In both cases, the funding arrangement can help create or sustain the demand that produces the seller’s revenue.

Hasnt GE financing arm done the same at a very large scale?

GE financing helped support demand for products, including GE’s. That did not by itself mean the resulting sales were fabricated. GE Capital was a large, diversified finance business.

Here are more examoles.

GE Capital did finance large purchases tied to GE’s industrial businesses. GE’s 2018 SEC filing says GE Capital enabled GE orders by directly financing GE transactions or arranging financing, including for GE-made aircraft engines and power equipment; GE also described long-term financing for Power and Aviation customers buying equipment and services.

For a concrete example, GE announced that GE Energy Financial Services helped arrange construction and term loans for a power plant built around GE gas and steam turbines.
So this is a strong historical parallel: GE financing helped customers acquire expensive equipment that generated real GE orders and revenue. The financing was disclosed and treated as a commercial arrangement; that alone doesn’t make the sales fictitious or fraudulent.

This memory supercycle is separating the real heavyweights from everyone else.

Samsung owns its DRAM and NAND fabs, so supply isn't a bottleneck. Apple sits on a $1,000+ ASP, giving it massive margin cushion to eat the BOM hike without flinching.   

Huawei takes a minor hit on its $150–$550 models meant to push HarmonyOS adoption, yet its $700+ overall ASP and strong $1,000+ flagship pull still let it ride out the storm.

The real bloodbath is in the $150 budget tier, where memory alone now eats over half the BOM. You don't have to use in-house silicon for everything, but without vertical supply chain control and real premium pricing power, every component cycle will squeeze you dry.

Opvallend: $NVDA bleef met +0,8% achter en staat nog altijd een flink stuk onder zijn record van oktober. Bij de andere megacaps bleef het rustig, met $GOOGL +0,7% en $MSFT +0,6%.

🚨 Outflows made the headlines. The recovery tells the rest of the story.

After the 29 October 2026 security incident, I tracked two weeks of Binance data to see how the crypto market actually responded.

🔻 THE OUTFLOWS WERE REAL
CryptoQuant data showed peak outflows of:
▪️ 22.5K BTC on 29 October
▪️ 180K ETH on 29 October
▪️ About $2.55B USDT and $1.05B USDC on peak days

⚖️ THEN FLOWS STARTED TO BALANCE
Once withdrawals resumed on 1 November, Binance netflows turned positive for Bitcoin:
✅ +5.2K BTC on 3 November
✅ +4K BTC on 9 November
✅ +2.7K BTC on 11 November

By 12 November, BTC netflow was nearly flat at +118 BTC. ETH settled into a narrower range, though it was still slightly negative at -20.8K ETH.

⚡ TRADING VOLUME STAYED STRONG
According to CryptoQuant:
▫️ Spot trading volume peaked around $70–80B
▫️ Perpetual futures volume peaked around $240–320B+
▫️ Binance stayed the largest venue for both

Binance Research also noted futures volume running 7% above its pre-incident average.

🧭 OPEN INTEREST TELLS ANOTHER STORY
Open interest climbed to one-month highs of 350K BTC and 5.28M ETH, while funding rates stayed mostly positive. Even after a rough stretch, crypto trading participants kept adding positions.

🎯 MY TAKEAWAY
The market showed resilience. Flows normalized, trading volume stayed elevated, and open interest recovered. That doesn't erase the impact of the incident, but it gives a fuller picture than any headline.

Moving from "Funds Are SAFU" to checking real market activity is the right shift.

💬 When judging an exchange after a major incident, what matters most to you: netflows, trading volume or open interest?

Most people stopped reading after the 29 October 2026 security incident.

I didn't.

Instead, I pulled the CryptoQuant data and looked at what happened over the following two weeks. The outflows made headlines. But the recovery data tells a completely different story.

🔴 22.5K BTC withdrawn — 29 October

🟢 +2.7K BTC — 11 November

By 12 November, BTC netflow was essentially flat at +118 BTC.

ETH settled into a tighter range too — latest reading was -20.8K ETH, a fraction of the initial spike.

Aave liquidation risk is a ratio, not a universal Bitcoin price.

Aave defines health factor as collateral value multiplied by the weighted liquidation threshold, divided by the value borrowed. A value below 1 makes a position eligible for liquidation.

In my view, that is why a headline about collateral “at risk” needs a timestamp and position assumptions. Repayments, additional collateral, asset prices and protocol parameters can change eligibility before any liquidation occurs.

An estimate of exposed collateral is not evidence that all of it has already been sold. For a market-wide claim, I would want separately verified executed transactions.

Europe’s debt clock is ticking — and the global rate market just turned hawkish right as the weekend opens.

France’s INSEE revised its Q3 figure on Friday, November 27, 2026: the economy contracted by 0.2% between July and September, twice the initial estimate. Two consecutive quarters of contraction have put France into a technical recession. The revision adds weight to Europe’s sovereign-debt and fiscal story, where markets have spent the year pricing higher borrowing costs and thinner buffers.

Now stack on the second leg: financial markets expect three additional quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increases by June 2027, including the expected December hike. That would put the federal funds target range at a 4.50% floor — a materially different Fed path from the cuts priced earlier in the year, and one arriving while the euro area is absorbing a recessionary shock in its second-largest economy.

Crypto has already felt the repricing. Bitcoin ($BTC) is down nearly 30% since October and slipped below $60,000 into Friday’s expiry of roughly $6.8 billion in Bitcoin options on Deribit — about one quarter of the exchange’s outstanding Bitcoin options positions. The macro transmission is straightforward: a steeper US rate path keeps real yields high, liquidity tight, and the case for risk assets — crypto included — harder to underwrite.

What European traders should watch into the weekend:

• France’s debt-spread reaction to the revised GDP print.

• The December Fed meeting, now priced for a hike.

• Where BTC holds after Friday’s options expiry, with weekend liquidity thin. Because nothing says “risk-on” quite like a thinner book and a hawkish repricing.

One warning on positioning: Galaxy Research has flagged Bitcoin downside levels of $48,500 and even $28,200 based on historical data, while CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju estimates roughly $16 billion in shorts could be squeezed if the market rips higher. Both extremes sit in the same tape — which tells you how unsettled positioning remains.

Two macro inputs, one weekend, thin books. Not financial advice.

📌機関のオンチェーン参入と欧州・政策進展

🇪🇺 米国でビットコインETFの資金流出が続く中、ヨーロ
　ッパや政策の分野では「静かな前進」が起きていま
　す。

📖 今回のテーマは「機関のオンチェーン参入」。
　銀行、資産運用会社、上場企業、そして政府が、ビッ
　トコインを取り入れていく動きのことです。
　1つのプロジェクトではなく、複数の動きが同時に進ん
　でいます。

🇨🇭 まず、スイスの新しいETFです。
　11月26日、スイス取引所(SIX)に「BBIT」が上場しまし
　た。
✅ 初期の保有量は約350BTC。
✅ 年間の手数料は0.19%
✅ 保管はスイスのAMINA Bankのコールドストレージ(ネ
　ットから切り離した保管方法)で、分けて管理。
✅ 証券口座から買える。

💡 特徴は「投資信託の形」であること。
　欧州の多くのビットコイン商品は債券型(ETP)ですが、
　BBITは、直接ビットコインを保有する形をとっていま
　す。

💪 次に、Strategy社(旧MicroStrategy)です。
　11月22日頃に457BTCを買い増し、総保有量は
　851,305BTCに。
　平均取得単価は約75,446ドル、総投資額は約642億ド
　ルで、上場企業としては最大規模のビットコイン保有
　です。
　
🇺🇸 さらに、米国では「Strategic Bitcoin Reserve(戦略的ビ
　ットコイン備蓄)」の法案が動いています。
✅ 政府が持つビットコインを備蓄に移す。
✅ 最低20年間は売却・譲渡を禁止する内容。
✅ 下院の委員会を通過し、11月24日に本会議へ送付。

⚠️ ただし、今の国会の会期が残りわずかなため、成立の
　可能性は低いという見方が強いです。

📱 X上では、11/21〜23頃にStrategyの買い増しで話題が
　急増。
　11/24〜25は法案、11/26〜27はスイスのBBIT上場が最
　大のピークとなりました。
　ただし、米国ETFの大量流出ニュースの陰に隠れ、爆発
　的なバズではなく、ニュースが出るたびにまとまって
　反応するパターンでした。

👀 投資家の見方を整理すると、こうなります。

🌱 前向き(中長期)：米国で記録的な流出が続くなかで
　も、スイスで本格的な現物ETFが生まれ、Strategyが買
　い続けている点を評価。
　BBITの構造(直接保有・分別管理・低コスト)は、機関
　や富裕層が参入しやすいと好感されている。

🤔 慎重(短期)：米国の11月の流出(約54億ドル規模)に比
　べて、BBITの約350BTCは小さく、すぐの需給インパク
　トは限定的。
　Strategyの平均取得単価は現在の価格を大きく上回って
　いて、法案の成立可能性も低いため、「象徴的ではある
　が、短期の買い圧力にはなりにくい」という声も。

💡 つまり、「短期は米国のETF流出が支配的だが、下落相
　場でも採用は止まっていない」というのが、トレーダ
　ーの間の中立〜ややポジティブな見方です。

🔭 派手さはなくても、リスクオフの中で進む「静かな制
　度の進展」として注目されています。

💬 みなさんは、派手なニュースと静かな進展、どちらを
　大切に見ていますか？

🟠 BRIEF ÉCO & MARCHÉS

📅 Semaine du 21 au 27 novembre 2026

Wall Street retrouve des couleurs, @nvidia rebondit, la croissance américaine surprend et les capitaux continuent de quitter les ETF Bitcoin.

Le rallye de Thanksgiving marque-t-il la fin de la correction ou simplement une respiration des marchés ? 👇

1️⃣ LES 5 INFOS CLÉS

① 📈 WALL STREET — Le @Nasdaq rebondit de 6,68 % et le S&P 500 de 5,60 %. Les investisseurs reviennent sur les valeurs technologiques après plusieurs semaines de correction.

② 🇺🇸 CROISSANCE — Le PIB américain du troisième trimestre est révisé de 3,4 % à 4,3 % en rythme annualisé. Une économie nettement plus résistante qu’anticipé.

③ 🏦 INFLATION — Le PCE américain atteint 3,8 % sur un an en octobre, contre 3,3 % hors alimentation et énergie. Une hausse des taux de la Fed en décembre devient un scénario crédible.

④ 🤖 NVIDIA — Le retour de Jensen Huang à la direction du groupe redonne confiance aux investisseurs. Le titre rebondit d’environ 20 % sur la semaine.

⑤ ₿ CRYPTO — Malgré la stabilisation du @Bitcoin , les ETF spot américains bitcoin:native et ethereum:native enregistrent encore près de 1,93 Md$ de sorties cumulées.

2️⃣ ÉCONOMIE MONDIALE 🌍

🇺🇸 USA — La consommation et les investissements des entreprises soutiennent la croissance. Les dépenses en équipements progressent de 21,8 % en rythme annualisé au troisième trimestre. Cette vigueur économique complique toutefois les perspectives monétaires.

🇪🇺 EUROPE — Les marchés européens profitent du retour de l’appétit pour le risque. Les valeurs minières, technologiques et de défense participent au rebond. Les élections espagnoles et les tensions commerciales avec Washington restent des facteurs d’incertitude.

🇨🇭 SUISSE — Le SMI accompagne la reprise européenne tandis que le franc suisse s’apprécie face au dollar. Une évolution favorable au pouvoir d’achat des importateurs, mais moins favorable aux entreprises exportatrices.

🌏 ASIE — Les marchés japonais et chinois rebondissent. Pékin appelle les investisseurs soutenus par l’État à renforcer leur soutien aux marchés financiers. Taïwan bénéficie également du regain d’intérêt pour les semi-conducteurs.

🛢️ GÉOPOLITIQUE — Les tensions dans le golfe d’Oman entretiennent les inquiétudes concernant l’approvisionnement énergétique mondial. Le pétrole reste particulièrement sensible aux risques géopolitiques.

3️⃣ MARCHÉS — BILAN HEBDO 📊

🎯 LES 3 CONSTATS

▪️ Le rebond des marchés actions est mondial, avec une nette surperformance des valeurs technologiques américaines.

▪️ La reprise simultanée des actions et des métaux précieux traduit un repositionnement des investisseurs après la correction.

▪️ La crypto se stabilise, mais les sorties persistantes des ETF montrent que la demande institutionnelle reste fragile.

4️⃣ CRYPTO ₿

📉 ETF SPOT US — 23 AU 27 NOVEMBRE

🔴 Bitcoin : −1 643,4 M$
🔴 Ethereum : −286,8 M$

Total BTC + ETH : −1 930,2 M$

La semaine ne comptait que quatre séances en raison de Thanksgiving.

Bitcoin enregistre huit séances consécutives de sorties nettes sur ses ETF spot, contre neuf pour Ethereum.

Malgré cette pression, Bitcoin, Ethereum et @solana  terminent la semaine en progression, avec une surperformance de SOL.

La divergence avec Wall Street reste néanmoins importante : les actions technologiques rebondissent fortement, tandis que les cryptomonnaies peinent encore à retrouver une dynamique comparable.

Le retour d’entrées nettes sur les ETF constituerait un signal supplémentaire d’amélioration de la demande institutionnelle.

5️⃣ IA & INNOVATION 🤖

🔸 NVIDIA — Le retour de Jensen Huang réduit une partie de l’incertitude liée à la gouvernance du groupe. Les questions concernant les restrictions d’exportation vers la Chine restent toutefois ouvertes.

🔸 SEMI-CONDUCTEURS — @MicronTech , @MarvellTech , @Qualcomm  et @Broadcom  participent au rebond technologique. Les investisseurs reviennent sur un secteur fortement pénalisé par la correction de novembre.

🔸 STOCKAGE DE DONNÉES — @SanDisk gagne près de 16 % vendredi. Les infrastructures de stockage bénéficient également du développement des capacités informatiques nécessaires à l’intelligence artificielle.

🔸 RENTABILITÉ — Les dépenses massives dans les infrastructures IA restent au cœur du débat. La prochaine phase du secteur pourrait davantage récompenser les entreprises capables de transformer leurs investissements en revenus et en marges durables.

6️⃣ OPPORTUNITÉS & TENDANCES 🔎

💾 MÉMOIRE & STOCKAGE

L’expansion des infrastructures IA soutient les besoins en mémoire et en stockage de données.
Catalyseur : croissance des capacités informatiques.
Horizon : moyen terme.
Risque : retournement du cycle des investissements technologiques.

⚡ ÉNERGIE & INFRASTRUCTURES

La croissance des centres de données renforce les besoins en production électrique, réseaux et systèmes de refroidissement.
Catalyseur : nouveaux investissements industriels.
Horizon : moyen et long terme.
Risque : coûts de financement et retards réglementaires.

🏦 FINANCE NUMÉRIQUE

La convergence entre finance traditionnelle et infrastructures blockchain ouvre de nouvelles perspectives autour des paiements, de la tokenisation et des services financiers numériques.
Catalyseur : adoption institutionnelle et développement de nouveaux produits.
Horizon : moyen et long terme.
Risque : réglementation, concurrence et fragmentation des liquidités.

7️⃣ LES 3 IDÉES À RETENIR 🎯

① Le rebond de Thanksgiving améliore le sentiment des investisseurs, mais ne suffit pas encore à confirmer la fin de la correction.

② La vigueur de l’économie américaine constitue un soutien aux entreprises, mais également un obstacle à l’assouplissement monétaire.

③ La divergence entre le rebond boursier et les sorties des ETF crypto rappelle que la reprise de l’appétit pour le risque reste inégale.

I sat with the public charts covering the two weeks after 29 October, and I wanted to walk through what they actually show, not just the headline.

The timeline is straightforward. The first outflow was around 20:05 UTC on 29 October. Withdrawals reopened on 1 November. The figures here run to 12 November. 

CryptoQuant tracks Binance netflows, trading volume and open interest. Binance Research covers the futures and TradFi-perps numbers. You can pull up the same charts yourself.

Here is the part that belongs in the middle of this story, not at the end. The outflows were real. CryptoQuant shows one of the largest outflow days on 29 October, at 22.5K BTC. That is a serious move, and it is honest to say so.

What followed is the part a lot of people have been asking me about. After withdrawals reopened on 1 November, Binance netflows started to normalise within days. 

CryptoQuant then shows green netflow days of about +5.2K BTC on 3 November, +4K BTC on 9 November and +2.7K BTC on 11 November. The latest reading in this window is back near flat, at +118 BTC.

Trading volume held up as well. CryptoQuant shows Binance spot volume has stayed elevated since September, with peaks of about $70 to $80B, compared with the $30 to $50B that was typical earlier in 2026. 

Perpetual volume has repeatedly peaked at around $240B to more than $320B since September, clearly above the January to August range. Binance remained the largest venue by both spot and perpetual volume throughout.

Binance Research adds the futures picture. Futures volume ran 7% above its pre-incident average and is on track to cross US$1T this month. TradFi-perps volume across exchanges hit a record week of US$312B.

The number that stood out to me most is open interest. CryptoQuant shows open interest hit one-month highs on 12 November: 350K BTC with BTC at $72K, and 5.28M ETH with ETH near $2.0K. Funding rates stayed mostly positive. 

Traders were adding exposure while price was still falling. That is not the positioning of a crowd heading for the exit. It is also not proof that every concern has disappeared. It is simply what the charts show about crypto trading and the wider crypto market over those two weeks.

Don't take my word for it. Pull up the charts yourself and form your own view of the two weeks after 29 October: netflows, volume against the pre-incident baseline, and open interest.

On Nov 27 USDD announced two updates to its Ethereum vaults: ETH and WBTC vaults at a 1% stability fee for a limited time, and a new wstETH vault that lets you mint USDD while continuing to earn staking rewards from Lido. The first is a price change. The second is a different kind of collateral, and it behaves differently.

How a wstETH vault works, in plain terms. wstETH is the wrapped form of staked ETH. Your balance doesn't change as staking rewards accrue; the token's value against stETH rises instead. Put it in the vault and you can borrow USDD against it while the rewards keep building inside the collateral. In effect, part of your borrowing cost is paid by the collateral itself.

That's the attraction, and here is the catch. The vault now depends on two prices: ETH against the dollar, and wstETH against ETH. In a calm market the second barely moves. In a stress event, staked-ETH tokens can trade below ETH, and a vault values collateral at the oracle or market price, so the discount can push you toward liquidation while ETH itself holds steady. There's also a layer of contract risk from Lido on top of USDD's own.

Which would I choose? If I planned to hold staked ETH anyway, the wstETH vault removes the trade-off between earning and borrowing. If I wanted clean ETH exposure and expected to repay within the promotion, the ETH vault at 1% is simpler, with fewer layers to monitor. The post doesn't say what stability fee the wstETH vault carries, so before minting I'd read it off the vault screen in the app and not assume it matches the 1%.

USDD announced two vault changes on Ethereum on Nov 27: the ETH and WBTC vaults drop to a 1% stability fee for a limited time, and a new wstETH vault lets you mint USDD while the collateral keeps earning Lido staking rewards.

First, why Ethereum. DefiLlama's stablecoin API today shows USDD at $1.485B in total, of which $1.162B is on TRON and $0.305B on Ethereum. On its USDD page on Nov 26, DefiLlama showed the Ethereum supply down 30.12% over 30 days against 10.26% for TRON. A fee cut that applies only to Ethereum vaults is a response to the leg that is bleeding.

Second, what 1% means in dollars. Mint 10,000 USDD against ETH and you owe $100 a year, $8.33 a month. The fee is charged on debt, not collateral. At a 50% loan-to-value that is 0.5% of the collateral's value a year. That is the useful comparison for the wstETH vault: if the collateral's staking yield exceeds 0.5% of its value at that LTV, the position pays its own fee. Check the live Lido rate before relying on it, because I did not verify it today.

Third, the spread the campaign invites. JustLend's USDD supply mining (phase 24, through Dec 5) targets about 4.00% APY paid in USDD. Mint at 1%, supply at roughly 4%, and a gross spread of about 3 points appears before bridging costs, the collateral's price risk and the fact that the mining rate is dynamic. I am describing arithmetic, not recommending the trade.

What I think is happening: this is a demand-side subsidy where the protocol pays borrowers in forgone fees to rebuild the Ethereum supply, paid for in forgone fee income. It is a sensible tool, and I would judge it by one number: Ethereum-side USDD supply 30 days after the fee returns to normal.

The other side: stability fees are only one cost. Liquidation risk on ETH and WBTC in a drawdown is the larger one, and a 1% fee does nothing about it.
