🚨 THE AI REVOLUTION IS RESHAPING GLOBAL POWER — AND INDIA HAS A STRATEGIC OPPORTUNITY!

Nvidia’s recovery may have restored market confidence, but it has NOT restored normalcy to Asia’s technology supply chain.

The bigger story is the escalating US-China semiconductor war.

1/ THE GLOBAL TECHNOLOGY BATTLE

The US is tightening restrictions on advanced AI chips, overseas computing access and semiconductor technology transfers to China. Proposed legislation targeting DUV equipment, chip tracking and export approvals could further reshape global supply chains.

Technology is no longer just a commercial business — it is becoming a matter of national security.

2/ GLOBAL ECONOMIC & MARKET IMPACT

• Semiconductor supply-chain fragmentation could increase production costs and investment uncertainty.

• Taiwan, South Korea and Japan remain strategically important to global AI and chip manufacturing.

• Southeast Asian data centres face additional regulatory and compliance risks.

• Higher AI infrastructure spending creates opportunities, but rising costs and uncertain returns could challenge valuations.

• US-China tensions could accelerate technological decoupling and reshape global trade and capital flows.

3/ THE INDIA OPPORTUNITY 🇮🇳

India could emerge as an important beneficiary of the China+1 strategy.

Potential opportunities include:

• Semiconductor manufacturing & chip packaging
• Electronics manufacturing and exports
• AI infrastructure, cloud computing & data centres
• Power transmission, energy and industrial automation
• Chip design, engineering and technology services

However, technology dependence, high capital requirements, import dependency and execution risks remain major challenges.

4/ THE BIGGER ECONOMIC PICTURE

The next phase of globalisation may be driven less by the cheapest production location and more by technological capability, supply-chain resilience and national security.

For India, the real opportunity is not merely attracting foreign investment — it is building domestic technological capabilities, increasing value addition and becoming a reliable part of the global semiconductor ecosystem.

MY RESEARCH VIEW:

AI is creating a structural growth opportunity, but US-China geopolitical tensions are introducing a significant risk premium into global technology markets.

The winners will not simply be companies selling AI chips, but those converting technological leadership into sustainable earnings, productivity and cash flows.

For India, this is a strategic opportunity to move from being a major technology consumer towards becoming a meaningful global technology and manufacturing hub.

The opportunity is substantial. Execution will determine the outcome.

【英伟达股价11月已有5次单日涨跌幅达5%或以上】英伟达（NVDA）在2026年11月单日涨跌超过5%的交易日已有五个，接近此前十个月的总和。截至11月25日，股价当月下跌超过四分之一，同一个月公布的季度营收却同比增长一倍有余。
我觉得股价和业绩的背离，焦点在于现金回笼的速度，利润增速本身依然强劲。第三财季末应收账款升至约810亿美元，相当于上一财年末的两倍多，部分原因是付款期限拉长。
按过去十二个月的调整后盈利计算，英伟达的估值倍数已经低于标普500整体，市场担忧的是增长能否延续。受益的是能够承受波动的长期资金，需要适应的是把它当作稳健权重股的指数投资者。
英伟达约占SPDR S&P 500 ETF（SPY）持仓的6%，波动会直接传导给被动持有人。原文作者Daniel Sparks的思路是参照指数权重来配置，保留意见在于AI支出一旦放缓，盈利和估值都会承压。公司给出的下季度营收指引约1300亿美元，接下来检验的指标是应收账款增速能否回落到营收增速以下。
一家公司利润翻倍而股价大幅回落，说明定价的对象已经从当期业绩转向两三年后客户的资本开支。指数里的权重股越集中，普通人账户承担的就越接近一只成长股的起伏。

On November 17, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for its latest quarter, up 103% from the same quarter last year.

But strong earnings don't automatically tell you where a stock's price will move next.

So I started thinking 

 what if you wanted to take a position on Nvidia's price without actually buying its shares?

That question led me to explore @DeriveXYZ 

𝗦𝗼, 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗗𝗲𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗱𝗼?

Derive is a decentralised, onchain derivatives exchange. In simple terms, it allows people to trade financial contracts whose value follows the price of another asset.

Its main products include options and perpetual futures (perps), alongside spot trading and other financial products.

What caught my attention is how Derive is extending these markets beyond crypto. 

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝘁

Derive has introduced RWA options markets for Nvidia, Anthropic, gold, WTI crude oil, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100.

The interesting part is that supported crypto assets can serve as collateral for positions connected to these traditional markets.

But understanding what you can trade is only half the story.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗺𝗲

Take Nvidia as an example.

Suppose its share price is $200. You buy a call option with a $210 strike price and pay a $4 premium.

If Nvidia reaches $212 at expiry, your option has $2 of value. After accounting for the premium, you're still down $2. You need $214 to break even, before fees.

A put gives exposure to a possible fall in price.

This is where options differ from perps. A perp lets you take a long or short position without a fixed expiry. Leverage can increase your exposure, but it also introduces liquidation risk and funding costs.

An options buyer pays a premium for a contract with a strike price and expiry. The maximum loss is generally the premium paid, excluding fees. However, time decay and falling implied volatility can reduce its value, even when the price moves in your expected direction.

Another detail I noticed is that the settlement rules differ across markets. Having Nvidia, gold and stock indexes on the same platform doesn't mean their contracts use identical price references. 

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜 𝘄𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

I'd choose Nvidia. Its connection to AI demand and company earnings gives me specific developments to follow. Before taking a position, I'd examine the strike price, expiry, premium and implied volatility rather than trade simply because I expect volatility.

𝗠𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

The part I find most interesting is the relationship between crypto collateral and markets outside crypto.

Derive is more than a place listing assets for people to swap. Its trading environment is built around managing derivatives positions, with order books, contract details, balances and margin requirements.

There is also a separation between its risk universes, meaning collateral in one account cannot automatically cover another.

To me, the bigger development is that supported crypto assets can be used to access positions linked to companies, commodities and market indexes.

It's not simply about adding more assets to an exchange. It's about connecting different financial markets through one trading infrastructure, while each market still has its own rules and risks.

AI 시대의 새로운 석유, 데이터. 왜 이노데이터인가?

$INOD $NVDA $MSFT $GOOGL

사람들은 AI 산업의 발전을 이야기할 때 GPU의 성능과 데이터센터의 규모에 주목한다.

그러나 아무리 뛰어난 GPU와 막대한 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확보해도 양질의 학습 데이터가 없다면 뛰어난 AI를 만들기 어렵다.

그렇다면 AI가 발전할수록 데이터의 가치는 어떻게 될까?

■ 일리야 수츠케버(OpenAI 공동창업자)가 말하는 데이터의 희소성

2024년 12월 13일, 세계적인 AI 학술대회 NeurIPS에서 일리야 수츠케버는 다음과 같이 말했다.

“Data is the fossil fuel of AI.”

“데이터는 AI의 화석연료다.”

그가 강조한 것은 AI 학습에 활용할 수 있는 새로운 인터넷 데이터가 무한하지 않다는 점이다.

컴퓨팅 능력은 계속 증가한다.
GPU의 성능도 지속적으로 향상된다.
그러나 인류가 축적한 양질의 인터넷 데이터에는 한계가 있다.

결국 기존처럼 무작정 더 많은 데이터를 투입하는 방식에서 벗어나야 한다.

새로운 데이터를 생성하고, 기존 데이터의 품질을 높이며, AI가 만들어낸 결과를 평가하는 능력이 더욱 중요해질 수 있다.

■ 안드레이 카파시(前 Tesla AI 책임자)가 말하는 소프트웨어의 변화

OpenAI 창립 멤버이자 테슬라의 전 AI 책임자인 안드레이 카파시는 2017년 'Software 2.0'이라는 개념을 제시했다.

기존 소프트웨어는 사람이 직접 명령어와 코드를 작성하는 방식이었다.

그러나 AI 시대에는 데이터를 활용해 신경망을 학습시키는 과정이 소프트웨어 개발의 핵심 영역으로 부상한다.

2022년 Lex Fridman과의 인터뷰에서도 그는 테슬라의 자율주행 기술 개발 과정에서 Data Engine의 중요성을 설명했다.

데이터 엔진의 기본적인 원리는 다음과 같다.

① 실제 환경에서 데이터 수집

② AI가 제대로 판단하지 못하는 사례 식별

③ 해당 데이터 분류 및 정제

④ 개선된 데이터를 활용한 AI 재학습

⑤ 성능 검증 및 새로운 모델 배포

⑥ 새로운 데이터 수집 및 반복

결국 AI의 성능을 높이는 것은 단순히 GPU를 추가하는 문제가 아니다.

어떤 데이터를 수집하고, 어떻게 학습시키며, 결과를 어떻게 검증하는지가 중요하다.

■ 바로 이 영역에서 이노데이터가 등장한다.

이노데이터는 단순히 데이터를 분류하거나 이미지에 라벨을 붙이는 기업에서 벗어나 고도화된 AI 데이터 엔지니어링 기업으로 발전하고 있다.

주요 사업 영역을 살펴보자.

사전학습 데이터 구축(Pre-training)
사후학습 데이터 구축(Post-training)
인간 피드백 및 선호도 최적화
AI 모델 성능 및 안전성 평가
강화학습 환경 구축
AI 에이전트 개발 지원
로봇 및 Physical AI 학습 데이터 구축

이노데이터는 AI 모델 자체를 개발해 시장을 지배하려는 기업이 아니다.

AI 모델을 개발하는 기업들이 더 뛰어난 AI를 만들도록 지원하는 기업이다.

2026년 1분기 SEC 공시에 따르면 이노데이터는 매그니피센트 7에 속한 기업 중 5개사를 포함한 주요 기술기업과 AI 개발사에 서비스를 제공하고 있다.

어떤 AI 모델이 최종적인 승자가 될지는 알 수 없다.

그러나 여러 AI 개발사가 경쟁적으로 모델의 성능을 향상하는 과정은 이노데이터에 사업 기회가 될 수 있다.

■ Physical AI 시대, 이노데이터의 새로운 기회

앞으로 AI는 단순히 질문에 답하는 수준을 넘어 자동차와 로봇을 움직이게 될 것이다.

하지만 인간처럼 움직이는 로봇을 만들기 위해 인터넷에 존재하는 텍스트 데이터만 학습시키면 충분할까?

그렇지 않다.

로봇에게는 물리적 세계를 이해할 수 있는 새로운 데이터가 필요하다.

사람의 움직임과 행동
사물의 형태와 무게
물체를 잡는 방법
다양한 환경에서의 작업 과정
공간적 위치와 거리
행동에 따른 물리적 결과

이노데이터는 2026년 9월 휴머노이드 로봇 및 월드 모델 학습을 위한 모션캡처 연구시설을 출범시켰다.

또한 주요 AI 연구소 및 로봇 개발사들과 시험 사업을 진행하고 있다.

이것이 중요한 이유는 Physical AI의 발전이 기존 언어모델 학습 데이터와는 다른 종류의 데이터 시장을 만들어낼 수 있기 때문이다.

■ 실제 실적으로 증명하고 있는가?

2026년 11월 발표한 3분기 실적을 살펴보자.

매출: 9,560만 달러
전년 동기 대비 매출 성장률: +53%
순이익: 1,030만 달러
조정 EBITDA: 1,770만 달러
현금 및 현금성 자산: 1억 6,400만 달러
2026년 연간 매출 성장률 전망: 42% 이상

이노데이터는 AI 산업의 미래에 대한 기대뿐만 아니라 실제 매출 성장과 순이익을 기록하고 있다는 점에서 주목할 만하다.

■ AGI와 초지능이 등장하면 이노데이터는 어떻게 될까?

여기서 가장 중요한 반론이 등장한다.

AI가 인간보다 뛰어난 지능을 갖게 된다면 인간이 AI를 학습시키는 작업도 사라지지 않을까?

충분히 가능한 시나리오다.

단순한 데이터 라벨링과 반복적인 검증 업무는 AI에 의해 빠르게 자동화될 수 있다.

합성 데이터와 자동 검증 기술의 발전도 기존 사업을 위협할 수 있다.

따라서 이노데이터의 진정한 해자는 단순 노동력이나 직원 수가 되어서는 안 된다.

고난도 전문 데이터 구축 능력
AI 학습 및 검증 자동화 기술
현실 세계의 데이터 수집 역량
신뢰성 높은 평가 체계
고객사의 개발 과정에 통합된 사업 구조

이러한 역량을 확보해야 한다.

초지능이 등장한다고 해서 반드시 이노데이터의 가치가 높아지는 것은 아니다.

오히려 AI를 활용해 자기 사업을 혁신하지 못한다면 AI에 의해 대체될 수도 있다.

■ 결론

엔비디아는 AI에 연산 능력을 제공한다.

IREN은 AI가 작동할 물리적 환경을 제공한다.

이노데이터는 AI가 학습하고 평가받으며 개선되는 과정을 지원한다.

AI 모델의 경쟁이 치열해질수록 단순히 더 많은 데이터를 확보하는 것이 아니라 더 가치 있는 데이터를 만들어내는 능력이 중요해질 수 있다.

과거에는 데이터의 양이 경쟁력이었다.

앞으로는 데이터의 품질과 검증 능력이 경쟁력이 될 수 있다.

AI 시대에 지능이 풍부해질수록, 그 지능을 더욱 정확하고 신뢰할 수 있게 만드는 데이터의 가치에 주목해야 한다.

이것이 내가 이노데이터에 주목하는 이유다.

【速報】GoogleがSpaceXからAI向け計算能力の追加調達に関心とマスク氏｜既存契約は月9.2億ドル

イーロン・マスク氏は28日、GoogleがSpaceXからさらに計算能力を借りることに関心を示したとXに投稿した。
追加契約を結んだという発表ではなく、規模や金額も示していない。

▫️両社には6月に結んだ契約がある
・SpaceXが米証券取引委員会（SEC）に提出した資料によると、既存契約はNVIDIA製GPU約11万基と、関連する計算設備を使えるようにするもの。
開示された契約条件は、2026年10月から2029年6月まで月9.2億ドル。
・この金額は既存契約の条件で、今回の追加分の見積もりではない。
既存契約にも、約束した台数を提供できない場合は、Googleが契約を打ち切るか、実際に提供された台数に応じた減額を受け入れられる条件がある。

▫️AIを作る会社と、計算設備を貸す会社の関係
・Googleのように自社でAIを開発し、クラウド事業も持つ会社でも、必要な分の計算設備を外から調達することがある。
モデルを作る競争と、それを動かす設備を確保する競争は別で、同じ会社が違う立場で関わることもある。
・SpaceX側から見ると、自社のAIだけでなく、他社に計算設備を貸すことも事業になる。
今回の発言からは、Googleが何に使うために追加分を求めているのか、自社設備の代わりなのか、補うためなのかまでは分からない。

▫️次に見るのは「何台を、いつから」貸せるか
・追加契約が正式に出た場合は、契約総額に加え、設備を提供できる時期と、予定どおりに提供できなかった場合の条件にも注目したい。
既存契約のように提供台数で支払額が変わるなら、発表された契約規模と、実際に入る売上は分けて読む必要がある。

Ixigo: Le Travenues Technology

⏩️ Let's understand, how bus & hotel segments are changing growth dynamics for the company?

👉Trains remained ixigo's largest revenue contributor at 42.82%, followed closely by Flights at 27.63% and Buses at 27.09%.

👉In terms of "Contribution Margin (CM)" which is a key profitability metric.  Trains (37.33%) and Buses (36.36%) together generated over 73% of the company's total contribution profit.

👉Trains anchored the top line, generating ₹290.18 Cr in H1. Rail ticketing remains the primary driver of revenue and user acquisition, holding roughly a 64% share of the online travel agency (OTA) rail market.

👉✅️While Buses accounted for 27.09% of revenue, its ~53% segment contribution margin allowed it to nearly match Trains in absolute contribution profit (₹97.36 Cr vs. ₹99.97 Cr).

However, flights despite strong Gross Transaction Value (GTV) growth from higher airfares, flight revenue softened in Q2 FY27 (₹82.66 Cr vs. ₹104.56 Cr in Q1) due to airline capacity constraints & soaring fares.

Hotels business is in ramp up phase, hence showed negative contribution margin (-₹6.27 Cr) reflects deliberate promotional and customer acquisition spending as ixigo scales its newly separated hotel vertical (aided by the Brevistay acquisition).

⏩️ Why Ixigo is expected to spring a positive surprise in seasonally strong Q3?

👉✅️In terms of GTV (gross transaction value), ixigo's growth of 22% YoY was ahead of the market leader MakeMyTrip that clocked 20% growth in Constant Currency in Q2FY27.

👉✅️Flight segment declined 10% sequentially in Q2FY27, but grew 8% YoY despite no category growth, indicating market share gains. 

International traffic has recovered with international flight GTV growing 59% YoY in Q2.

The relative calm in the Middle East and softer crude could augur well for the upcoming holiday season.

👉The company expects Train segment to maintain the over 30% contribution margin.

Thanks to the value-added offerings that improves customer stickiness, the company's share of the OTA rail market increased sequentially from approximately 63% to 64% in Q2. 

The company is expanding ancillary offerings through food on train, metro ticketing, and Bharat Darshan packages.

👉Bus remains the fastest growing and high margin business. 
👉✅️The company's bus business has grown faster than the OTA bus market for close to three years with a healthy 50% plus contribution margin. 

👉✅️The company's bus GTV grew by 32% in Q2 against a market growing about 14%, as it continues to gain share.

Industry report estimates the intercity bus market at about Rs 54,500 crore in FY26, growing about 14% a year, with OTAs expected to grow at 27% for the next two years. 

While growth drivers have been South and West India, AbhiBus is now expanding in North and East, offering significant headroom. 

Highway build-out, growing fleet capacity, and more intercity electric buses should support the market further.

👉Hotels segment – the dark horse

Hotels could turn out to be a major surprise and earnings driver, a segment whose financials have been disclosed for the first time in Q2FY27. 

Hotel GTV reached Rs 111 crore in Q2FY27, up 39% QoQ and 2.6x YoY.

👉✅️The gross take rate of over 12% is the highest of any of the businesses and has potential to go up.

More than 86% of hotel bookings came from captive users.

👉With significant footprint in Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations compared to peers, the company is well placed to serve the budget, mid-market, and independent hotels, and aims to be the leading player in this segment in the coming 3 to 4 years.

This is where most hotel stays in India happen, where online booking is least developed and quality assurance is an issue.

In India, about 60% of hotel room nights sell below Rs 2,000 a night and independent hotels hold 73% of rooms.

This development highlights just how much pressure Bitcoin holders are experiencing and how deeply market sentiment has deteriorated.

With $BTC struggling around the $60,000 region, investors are increasingly focused on macroeconomic developments, institutional positioning and the Federal Reserve's next policy decision.

WHAT IS DRIVING THE UNCERTAINTY?

📉 1. A Significant Portion of Bitcoin Holders Are Underwater

When 58% of the Bitcoin supply is held at an unrealized loss, it reflects widespread market weakness. Investors who purchased at higher prices are now facing substantial paper losses.

Historically, elevated unrealized losses have appeared during major market corrections and periods of extreme pessimism. However, they do not automatically signal that the bottom is in.

🏦 2. The Federal Reserve Remains a Major Catalyst

The upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision is attracting considerable attention.

Persistent inflation could complicate the Fed's decision-making process, keeping monetary policy restrictive for longer than markets would prefer.

Higher interest rates generally make riskier assets less attractive by increasing the opportunity cost of holding them and tightening financial conditions.

If the Fed maintains a hawkish position, Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market could experience additional volatility.

🐋 3. Large Investors Are Watching Lower Price Levels

Despite the negative sentiment, large investors are reportedly maintaining substantial buy interest at lower levels, particularly around and below $55,000.

This suggests that some market participants are preparing for further downside while looking for attractive entry opportunities.

However, there is an important distinction between placing buy orders and executing actual purchases. Liquidity can disappear, and large orders can be cancelled.

Nevertheless, institutional and whale positioning will remain an important factor to monitor.

🎯 4. Selectivity Is Becoming More Important Than Ever

This is not necessarily the environment to buy every cryptocurrency simply because prices have declined.

Projects with sustainable tokenomics, genuine utility, strong development teams, healthy liquidity and long-term adoption prospects deserve closer attention.

The next market recovery may not lift every altcoin equally. Capital could concentrate in projects with stronger fundamentals while weaker projects continue to struggle.

THE BIGGER PICTURE:

Bitcoin's current weakness could represent an important transition period for the market.

Extreme unrealized losses, macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious institutional positioning are creating a challenging environment. Yet, periods of maximum pessimism can also create opportunities for investors who understand risk and maintain a disciplined strategy.

The key is not to assume that every dip is the bottom.

Watch the Federal Reserve, inflation data, institutional flows, liquidity and Bitcoin's ability to reclaim important price levels.

My outlook: The market demands patience, discipline and selectivity. The next major opportunity may emerge from this period of uncertainty, but capital preservation must remain a priority.

Vous pensiez que l'or vous protégeait d'un krach ? Dans les premières semaines, il baisse, et même fortement.

C'est ce qu'observe Jean-François Faure, président-fondateur d'AuCOFFRE, que nous avons interrogé. 

« Ce que j'ai vu systématiquement au cours des vingt dernières années, c'est que, quand il y a un krach, dans les quinze premiers jours, ou les trois premières semaines, l'or baisse, et même fortement. » Ce fut le cas en 2008 et en 2020.

📉 Ces dernières semaines, l'or a suivi la chute des marchés mondiaux, valeurs de l'IA en tête, sur fond de crainte d'une bulle comparable à celle d'Internet dans les années 2000. Pour ce professionnel de l'or, le métal jaune baisse justement parce qu'il est une valeur refuge, celle que l'on vend pour éponger ses pertes ailleurs. Les investisseurs, désormais en grande majorité des bots de trading selon lui, cèdent leur or pour couvrir leurs pertes sur l'IA. Si la bulle éclate vraiment, la baisse pourrait s'accélérer, car de nombreuses positions sur l'or restent susceptibles d'être liquidées.

Le Bitcoin a connu le même sort plus tôt. Selon Jean-François Faure, c'est lui que les investisseurs ont vendu en premier, plusieurs mois avant l'or, pour encaisser leurs importantes plus-values. Après une chute de près de 50 % depuis son record historique, beaucoup hésitent désormais à vendre pour ne pas matérialiser leurs pertes. L'arrivée des ETF Bitcoin spot a aussi renforcé la corrélation du BTC avec les valeurs technologiques, ce qui permet aux investisseurs institutionnels d'arbitrer plus facilement entre ces actifs. « Aujourd'hui, pour moi, à l'instant où on se parle, le Bitcoin n'est plus une réserve de valeur », tranche-t-il.

🏦 À moyen et long terme, il reste confiant pour l'or, soutenu par les achats des banques centrales, Chine en tête, engagées dans une logique de dédollarisation. Il ne voit pas pour autant les deux actifs comme rivaux, car selon lui « le Bitcoin et l'or ont le même objectif : offrir des alternatives à nos monnaies courantes ».

Investment and Market News You Have Missed: Crypto Edition
(Prices as of about 17:55 GMT, Fri 27 Nov: BTC $59,706 | ETH $1,665 | SOL $71.65)

1. Markets: Bitcoin dipped to about $57,300 on Wednesday, then bounced with stocks. CoinDesk says it is up about 0.6% on the week (around +1.4% from last Friday's wrap price by our maths), which would end seven straight weekly losses if it holds through Sunday's close. It is still down about 20% in November, its biggest monthly fall since June. The Fear and Greed Index is at 11 (extreme fear).

2. ETFs: US spot Bitcoin ETFs are having their worst month on record, with about $5.39bn in net outflows for November by Wednesday (The Block, citing SoSoValue). That beats the previous record of June 2026. Monday to Wednesday alone saw about $1.25bn leave, $1.01bn of it from BlackRock's IBIT (Farside). Spot Ether ETFs lost about $218m over the same three days.

3. Analysis: Galaxy's head of research, Alex Thorn, has withdrawn the firm's October call that Bitcoin's bear market ended in June. He now treats a daily close below $58,525 (the 30 June low) as the start of a move to a materially lower low. Key level to watch.

4. Regulation (US): A bill to write the US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into law (H.R. 8957) is now eligible for a full House vote. It would bar the government from selling its Bitcoin, about 306,800 BTC per Arkham, for at least 20 years. Time is short because the current Congress ends on 3 January, and Polymarket traders give it less than a 5% chance before 2027.

5. Regulation (US): Senators Elizabeth Warren, Chris Van Hollen and other Senate Banking Committee Democrats wrote to SEC Chair Paul Atkins demanding he withdraw the proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets". That includes exemptions for token offerings of up to $5m (startups) and $75m (fundraising). With Democrats taking both chambers in January, expect tougher pushback on crypto rules.

6. Products: Fidelity filed for a spot Chainlink ETF (ticker FLNK, Nasdaq) that will hold LINK without staking it. Franklin Templeton is also preparing to add Hyperliquid's HYPE to its crypto index ETF. Meanwhile, KuCoin will delist Monero (XMR) on 30 November ahead of EU rules on privacy coins, and XMR fell 13% in a day.

7. Africa (Ghana): The Ghana Association of Banks and the Chartered Institute of Bankers are building a virtual-assets certification for bank staff in compliance, risk, fraud and operations. GAB's CEO, John Awuah, said: "Virtual assets have come to stay." It comes as regulators start licensing crypto firms under the VASP-Act (Act 1154). Fees and course length have not been published yet.

Bitcoin may end its losing streak, but ETF money is still leaving and Ghana's banks are getting ready for crypto. Size your positions sensibly and do your own analysis.

This situation highlights one of the most dangerous risks in crypto: using a volatile native token as collateral to borrow funds.

When token prices rise, the strategy can appear sustainable. However, when prices collapse, collateral values deteriorate, liquidation risks increase, and borrowers may be forced to sell other assets to manage their obligations.

It also raises an important question: how resilient is a project's financial structure when its own token experiences a prolonged decline?

For the broader crypto market, this is a reminder that political connections, high-profile backing, and ambitious narratives do not eliminate financial risk.

In crypto, credibility must ultimately be supported by transparency, liquidity, and sound financial management.

World Liberty Financial has reportedly sold approximately $20.06 million worth of Ethereum-related assets, raising important questions about its treasury management strategy and exposure to market volatility.

While large cryptocurrency transactions frequently attract speculation, the sale itself does not necessarily indicate financial distress or a bearish outlook on Ethereum.

Institutional treasury managers may reduce asset exposure for several reasons, including portfolio rebalancing, operational expenditure, debt repayment or liquidity preservation.

What deserves closer examination is the destination of the proceeds, the remaining treasury composition and whether these transactions are consistent with the project's stated financial strategy.

For a decentralized finance project, transparency surrounding capital allocation is particularly important because users must evaluate not only the value of its assets but also its ability to meet financial obligations.

𝗕𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗗𝗢𝗪𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 $𝟮𝟬.𝟬𝟲 𝗠𝗜𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗘𝗧 𝗦𝗔𝗟𝗘

According to the supplied transaction report:

• ETH sold: 10,600 ETH.
• Reported transaction value: $17.58 million.
• mETH sold: 1,378 mETH.
• Reported transaction value: $2.48 million.
• Combined transaction value: $20.06 million.

Based on these reported figures:

• Implied ETH valuation: approximately $1,658.49 per ETH.
• Implied mETH valuation: approximately $1,799.71 per mETH.
• ETH accounted for approximately 87.64% of the combined transaction value.
• mETH accounted for approximately 12.36%.

The implied mETH valuation was approximately 8.52% higher than that of ETH.

However, this difference should not automatically be interpreted as a market premium. As a liquid staking token, mETH can have an underlying ETH conversion rate that changes as staking rewards accumulate.

Transaction timing and valuation methodology could also influence the comparison.

Source: Supplied transaction report and internal calculations. The wallet addresses, transaction hashes, execution prices and realized proceeds have not been independently verified.

Without knowing WLFI's original acquisition costs, it is also impossible to determine whether these reported sales generated realized profits or losses.

𝗠𝗬 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗩𝗜𝗘𝗪: 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗬 𝗟𝗜𝗤𝗨𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗧𝗛𝗔𝗡 𝗡𝗢𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗘𝗧 𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗘

One of the fundamental challenges facing cryptocurrency treasury managers is balancing exposure to appreciating assets with the need to maintain sufficient operational liquidity.

A treasury can appear financially strong during favorable market conditions while remaining vulnerable to sudden asset price corrections.

Consider the reported $20.06 million ETH-related position under three hypothetical market scenarios.

If the assets had been retained and subsequently declined in value:

• 10% correction: potential valuation loss of $2.006 million.
• 25% correction: potential valuation loss of $5.015 million.
• 40% correction: potential valuation loss of $8.024 million.

Conversely, if the assets appreciated by 30%, retaining the position could have generated approximately $6.018 million in additional unrealized value.

These scenarios assume proportional price movements across both assets and exclude staking rewards, transaction costs and taxes.

Selling volatile assets can reduce exposure to future market corrections, but it also sacrifices potential upside.

The financial outcome depends heavily on how the proceeds are subsequently deployed.

Consider a hypothetical treasury holding $100 million in assets, with 80% allocated to volatile cryptocurrencies and 20% to dollar-denominated liquid assets.

Assuming the treasury converts $20.06 million of volatile assets into stablecoins:

Before rebalancing:

• Volatile assets: $80 million.
• Liquid dollar-denominated assets: $20 million.

After rebalancing:

• Volatile assets: $59.94 million.
• Liquid dollar-denominated assets: $40.06 million.

Under a subsequent 40% decline in volatile asset prices:

• Treasury value without rebalancing: $68 million.
• Treasury value after rebalancing: $76.024 million.
• Difference in preserved capital: $8.024 million.

All figures are illustrative internal calculations, not WLFI's actual treasury composition or confirmed use of proceeds.

This example demonstrates why treasury diversification can improve financial resilience, provided that the replacement assets remain liquid and reliable.

However, if the proceeds are used to repay debt, fund operations or acquire other volatile assets, the resulting financial implications would be materially different.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚𝗚𝗘𝗥 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗙𝗜 𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠: 𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗦𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗬 𝗜𝗦 𝗔 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗘𝗧

The reported WLFI transactions highlight a broader issue across decentralized finance: users need to distinguish between treasury size, available liquidity, outstanding liabilities and sustainable protocol revenue.

This distinction is particularly relevant to stablecoin issuers and lending protocols operating across blockchain ecosystems.

Within TRON, several financial mechanisms provide useful examples of the importance of transparent capital management:

• USDD's collateralized Vault architecture.
• JustLend DAO's lending and borrowing markets.
• https://t.co/u4SYeHjUeW's decentralized liquidity pools.
• TRONSCAN's publicly accessible transaction records.
• JST's announced revenue-funded buyback and burn mechanism.

Previously published JUST ecosystem statistics for November 17–23, 2026, reported:

• JustLend total supply: $3.17 billion.
• JustLend total borrow: $202.22 million.
• USDD protocol TVL: $2.01 billion.
• USDD total supply: $1.5 billion.

These historical figures illustrate the importance of examining assets and liabilities together rather than relying exclusively on headline TVL figures.

They do not establish that these protocols are immune to liquidity, collateral or governance risks.

For WLFI specifically, the indicators I would prioritize following the reported asset sales include:

• Verified treasury wallet balances.
• Destination addresses receiving the proceeds.
• Remaining ETH and liquid staking token exposure.
• Outstanding borrowing obligations.
• Collateralization and liquidation risks.
• Treasury governance authorization.
• Related-party transactions.
• Subsequent capital allocation disclosures.
• USD1 reserve composition and redemption capacity.

Importantly, WLFI's corporate or protocol treasury assets must be distinguished from the reserves backing USD1. The reported ETH-related asset sales alone do not demonstrate that USD1's backing has deteriorated.

Sources: Supplied WLFI transaction report, previously published JUST ecosystem statistics and illustrative internal calculations. The latest transactions and their underlying financial motivations remain independently unverified.

In my assessment, selling $20.06 million in cryptocurrency assets is not inherently a negative financial decision.

What matters is whether the transaction strengthens liquidity, reduces liabilities or improves the sustainability of the treasury.

A responsible treasury strategy should be evaluated through measurable financial outcomes rather than assumptions about management intentions.

The blockchain can reveal where capital moves, but understanding why it moves requires additional evidence.

Ultimately, sustainable DeFi projects should demonstrate not only their ability to accumulate assets during favorable market conditions but also their ability to manage capital responsibly during periods of uncertainty.

Transparency becomes most valuable precisely when market confidence is under pressure.

Trump Family's WLFI Token Halves in an Hour and the Silence Is Deafening

Half a billion dollars of paper wealth evaporated before most of America had coffee. The Trump family's World Liberty Financial token, $WLFI, fell from $0.035 to $0.017 inside a single hour. It is now down more than 94% from its all-time high, and the people who bought the top are staring at a loss that no buyback announcement will fix.

The stablecoin that sits inside the same project did not escape either. USD1 briefly broke its dollar peg and traded down to $0.94 on Binance before climbing back to $0.9902. A dollar token that cannot hold a dollar is not a volatility story. It is a confidence story. And confidence is the only thing a stablecoin actually sells.

Here is what the data shows. WLFI trades near $0.0193, down 52.6% over 24 hours and 56.5% over the week, with a market capitalisation of about $611 million against $536 million of turnover in the same period — that is an enormous volume-to-cap ratio and a classic signature of forced selling rather than orderly repricing. The intraday low on Binance was $0.0158, which means the token lost 59% at its worst moment. Against an all-time high of $0.331, the drawdown is 94.2%.

The chain of events started with a governance crisis rather than a market one. Tron founder Justin Sun publicly accused the project of investor fraud and called on exchanges to delist both WLFI and USD1, saying team members had begun deleting social media posts and communications. That accusation, carried by Cointelegraph, WatcherGuru and WuBlockchain, is what turned a slow bleed into a one-hour collapse.

Two claims circulating on social media deserve a warning. First, that a World Liberty wallet quietly sold $20 million of Ethereum six hours before the drop. Second, that an exchange halted withdrawals. Neither appears in any of the 45 news sources tracked by our system across the last 20 hours — including the venues that usually break such stories first. They may turn out to be true. They are not established facts today, and repeated without proof they become the story instead of the collapse.

The broader market explains the speed. Across crypto, $407 million of positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $314 million of them longs, according to CoinGlass. Bitcoin trades near $59,300, below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, with 74% of Binance accounts positioned long — a crowded trade that turns any negative headline into a stampede. Bitcoin's dominance has climbed to 58.4%, up 0.7 points in a day, which tells you capital is leaving smaller tokens for the safest one available.

Whales are not buying the dip. Exchange balances rose 0.07% over seven days and 0.83% over thirty, meaning coins are drifting back toward venues rather than leaving them. Institutional wallets moved 4,139 BTC off exchanges but companies added 3,075 BTC in the same window — a reshuffle, not accumulation. No whale alert has fired in the past 24 hours.

What it means: WLFI was never a market problem, it was a trust problem wearing a market costume. The token's value rests entirely on the credibility of the family name attached to it, and that credibility is now being tested in public by a major industry figure making fraud allegations on the record. Until the project answers those allegations with specifics rather than silence, the price will keep doing what it did this morning. Watch one number above all others: whether USD1 holds $0.99. A stablecoin that depegs twice does not get a third chance.

𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗗 𝗩𝗔𝗨𝗟𝗧 𝗜𝗡 𝟱 𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣𝗦: 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗢 𝗨𝗡𝗟𝗢𝗖𝗞 𝗟𝗜𝗤𝗨𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗪𝗜𝗧𝗛𝗢𝗨𝗧 𝗦𝗔𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗟𝗢𝗡𝗚-𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗠 𝗔𝗦𝗦𝗘𝗧 𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗢𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗘

One of the most common financial dilemmas facing cryptocurrency holders is deciding whether to sell valuable assets to access immediate liquidity.

Selling ETH or WBTC provides capital but reduces exposure to potential future appreciation. Holding these assets preserves market exposure but may limit access to available working capital.

USDD Vault introduces an alternative through a collateralized debt position (CDP), allowing users to deposit supported cryptocurrency assets and mint USDD against their collateral.

The underlying principle is straightforward: users can access liquidity without immediately selling their existing holdings.

What makes this mechanism particularly interesting is the flexibility it introduces into personal treasury management, portfolio allocation and decentralized financial strategies.

However, unlocking liquidity is only half of the equation. Understanding how to manage the resulting debt position is equally important.

𝗙𝗜𝗩𝗘 𝗣𝗥𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗣𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗡 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗚𝗘 𝗔 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗗 𝗩𝗔𝗨𝗟𝗧

Step 1 — Connect your wallet.

Visit the official USDD Vault platform, connect a compatible wallet and ensure that sufficient ETH is available to cover Ethereum network fees.

Step 2 — Select your collateral.

Choose a supported collateral asset, such as ETH, WBTC or wstETH, and determine how much capital you are comfortable committing to the Vault.

Each collateral type may have different risk parameters, stability fees and liquidation requirements.

Step 3 — Mint USDD.

Enter the desired amount of USDD to mint. Rather than borrowing the maximum available amount, consider maintaining sufficient collateral headroom to accommodate market volatility.

Step 4 — Manage your position.

Regularly monitor your collateral ratio, outstanding debt, accrued stability fees and applicable liquidation threshold.

Users may need to deposit additional collateral or repay part of their debt when market conditions deteriorate.

Step 5 — Close your Vault.

Fully repay the outstanding USDD debt and applicable accrued fees to unlock the remaining collateral, provided the position has not already been liquidated.

Official platform:

https://t.co/waKzk3jVFa

USDD documentation:

https://t.co/NyWUAz0m6a

These five steps make the operational process accessible, but responsible borrowing requires understanding the financial implications behind each decision.

𝗠𝗬 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗔𝗟 𝗩𝗜𝗘𝗪: 𝗕𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗢𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗖𝗔𝗣𝗔𝗖𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗜𝗦 𝗡𝗢𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗔𝗦 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘 𝗕𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗢𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗖𝗔𝗣𝗔𝗖𝗜𝗧𝗬

The most important decision when opening a USDD Vault is not necessarily which collateral asset to select. It is determining how much debt that collateral can reasonably support during unfavorable market conditions.

Consider three hypothetical users, each depositing $50,000 worth of ETH.

Strategy A — Conservative borrowing:

• USDD minted: 10,000.
• Initial collateral ratio: 500%.
• Initial loan-to-value ratio: 20%.

Strategy B — Moderate borrowing:

• USDD minted: 15,000.
• Initial collateral ratio: 333.33%.
• Initial loan-to-value ratio: 30%.

Strategy C — More aggressive borrowing:

• USDD minted: 20,000.
• Initial collateral ratio: 250%.
• Initial loan-to-value ratio: 40%.

Now assume ETH experiences a 40% market correction, reducing each user's collateral value to $30,000.

The resulting collateral ratios would be:

• Strategy A: 300%.
• Strategy B: 200%.
• Strategy C: 150%.

If ETH declines by 60%, leaving $20,000 in collateral:

• Strategy A: 200%.
• Strategy B: 133.33%.
• Strategy C: 100%.

Despite starting with identical collateral values, these users face substantially different levels of financial risk.

Assuming a hypothetical liquidation threshold of 150%, and ignoring accrued fees, the approximate collateral price declines required to reach that threshold would be:

• Strategy A: 70%.
• Strategy B: 55%.
• Strategy C: 40%.

The difference demonstrates that borrowing less can create a considerably larger safety buffer.

All figures are illustrative internal calculations, not actual USDD liquidation parameters or recommendations for individual borrowing positions. Accrued fees would gradually reduce these safety buffers.

Another relevant development is USDD's announced promotional stability fee of 1% for ETH and WBTC Vaults between November 27 and December 27, 2026.

For a hypothetical 15,000 USDD debt maintained over 30 days:

• At a 1% annualized stability fee: approximately 12.33 USDD.
• At a hypothetical 5% annualized stability fee: approximately 61.64 USDD.
• Potential fee savings: approximately 49.32 USDD.

Lower borrowing costs improve capital efficiency, but they should never become a reason to take excessive leverage.

𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗖𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗔𝗟𝗜𝗭𝗘𝗗 𝗕𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗢𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗧𝗢 𝗦𝗨𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗕𝗟𝗘 𝗖𝗔𝗣𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗟 𝗘𝗙𝗙𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗬

USDD Vault becomes particularly interesting when considered alongside the broader decentralized finance ecosystem.

Minted USDD can potentially be allocated toward:

• Stablecoin-based treasury management.
• Short-term liquidity requirements.
• Eligible USDD Earn opportunities.
• Decentralized financial applications.
• Portfolio diversification.
• Maintaining accessible capital reserves.

The introduction of wstETH as a collateral option on Ethereum adds another dimension to this strategy.

Users can retain exposure to ETH staking rewards through wstETH while using it as collateral to mint USDD, subject to the Vault's applicable requirements.

Nevertheless, combining staking rewards, collateralized borrowing and stablecoin yield introduces multiple layers of financial exposure.

Potential returns must be evaluated against stability fees, liquidation risk, smart contract vulnerabilities, stablecoin depegging, network fees and the liquidity conditions of external applications.

The indicators I would prioritize when managing a USDD Vault include:

• Current collateralization ratio.
• Distance from the liquidation threshold.
• Outstanding debt and accrued stability fees.
• Collateral price volatility.
• Available emergency liquidity.
• Effective borrowing expenditure.
• Net returns from deployed USDD.
• Changes in collateral-specific risk parameters.

Sources: USDD's official five-step Vault guide, previously announced Ethereum Vault updates and the November 27–December 27 stability fee campaign. Live collateral requirements, liquidation thresholds and promotional eligibility have not been independently reverified for this analysis.

In my assessment, the greatest value of USDD Vault is not its ability to maximize borrowing power.

It is the flexibility to separate immediate liquidity requirements from long-term asset ownership.

A well-managed Vault can preserve market exposure while providing access to usable capital. A poorly managed Vault can turn temporary market volatility into permanent collateral losses.

The difference lies in disciplined debt management, realistic expectations and sufficient financial reserves.

Opening a Vault takes five simple steps.

Managing it responsibly requires a strategy that remains viable even when the market moves against you.

True capital efficiency is not about extracting the maximum liquidity from every asset. It is about accessing the liquidity you need while preserving your ability to withstand uncertainty.

Agreed. 
Modern cryptography (AES-256, SHA-384, Ed25519, ECDSA) is designed so that there is no known efficient classical algorithm to break it. AI systems, including the most advanced models, do not magically invent shortcuts around hard mathematical problems such as the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem. 
As with everything, there’s the good, the bad and the outright ugly. 99% are in the bad/ugly camp in my opinion…but there are a handful of projects that stand apart from the rest which use the highest possible cryptography. 
For me the security risks are more centred around counterparty risk I.e bridges etc.
ETF’s - I was always in the “Trojan Horse” camp. My view was that tradfi wanted control of BTC (think about why/how the ETF’s were approved, despite SEC clearly operating a “regulation by enforcement” position at the time). Now Blackrock & Co can suppress/control BTC price…No different to paper PM’s (silver etc). 
Too many BTC derivatives have been created and OTC deals are now the norm. 
How BTC would behave under a black swan event is now going to be very different to how it would have behaved had there not been any ETF’s. 

Really what we need to be asking is what the dollar will be doing. If Trump & Co are engineering a dollar shortage, dxy will continue to climb higher, not exactly a dollar debasement thesis that Crypto has historically loved. 

IMO liquidity will be provided to the likes of Japan and crypto is the delivery vehicle. Watch USDJPY versus Total. Is there a correlation between sudden troughs in crypto and sudden strength in Yen? I have been watching this for over a year and IMO, there IS a correlation. 
Additionally, you have Japan moving as quickly as possible on crypto regs and establishing local & international rails. Got to join the dots and read between the lines, we’re talking trillions of dollars that Japan needs back and everything they have of substance is dollar based. Treasuries, ETF’s etc. Their exit needs to be managed without creating financial Armageddon and complete destruction of the dollar reserve system. 

If we do have a liquidation event (I agree this is now highly probable based on midterm result), the ETF outflows will be huge however, it all depends on the particulars of the liquidation as to whether people see BTC as a safer haven (away from equities and money markets). It also have the whole ‘self custody’ narrative that obviously appeals during any threat of bank runs etc.

For me, because AI is now a legitimate mainstream thing, I can now see where cryptographic networks are going to be needed, especially as we advance forward into Agentic Commerce. Bottomline, security and trust are now critical to the future of Agentic Commerce. Ethereum needs significant security upgrades (IMO) and given its scale, clearly any bad actor has the L1 in their crosshairs. Compare that to other L1 networks that have the strongest security (and significantly less liquidity in most cases) and one can only speculate as to which preferred L1 networks will be adopted by fintech/retail in the future, especially if we have more hacks.

Clearly AI trades have been attractive and have offered investors the potential of massive gains… sucking in money on side and forcing exits on assets being held that haven’t impressed (majority of crypto tokens over past 3yrs). 
If the AI narrative weakens, because of the circular financing etc, money will leave and look for a new home, most probable outcome would be to commodities (assuming a significant decline in dxy off back of an AI sell event).

I have always had 2 possible narratives for crypto: 1)crypto rails/networks will be integrated into tradfi globally, including enterprise and retail usage (whether the latter realises they’re using the rails or not). In effect, the powers that be, migrate to a new financial layer over time or 2)there will be a global reset off back of a Black Swan event which will result in a new way of doing things.

Solana is the quietest casualty of November — and the chart is now asking a very simple question.

This morning, Saturday 28/11 (Vietnam time), SOL is trading around $72 — Finnhub showed $72.07 at 21:01 UTC on Friday, OKX $72.05–$72.21. That is down about 29–30% in a single month, and down about 42–44% since the start of the year. From just above $106 in late October, it has fallen to around $70. Capital, for now, is choosing Bitcoin over Solana.

But look closer, and the chart has a floor. SOL hit a low near $65 on Saturday, bounced on Monday, faded, fell back toward $65 — and held again, recovering about 5% to $71. Twice tested. Twice held. Sixty-five dollars is now the line the whole market is watching.

Three scenarios from here, and they are all on the table. If $65 breaks, the next support is the June low around $60 — the lowest since 2023. If $65 holds and the price clears Monday's high, the next target is around $80, where the sell-off began. If neither happens, Solana goes sideways between $65 and $80 while the market waits for a reason to move.

The fundamentals, oddly, are moving the other way. Solana has shipped its biggest technical upgrades — dropping the "Mainnet Beta" label for Solana 1.0, tokenised equities reaching $1.22 billion — and the market treated it all as background noise. DeFi TVL sits at $4.627 billion, stablecoins on the chain at $12.428 billion. ETF flows even turned positive, with $4.4 million in net inflows after seven straight sessions of $58.3 million in outflows.

Good news, bad price. That is the story of Solana in November: price is set by flows and fear, not by roadmaps.

Would you buy Solana here at $72 — or wait to see if $65 holds a third time?

Bitcoin Loses $60,000 Again: 100,000 Traders Liquidated in 24 Hours

On November 28, the crypto market took another leg down. Bitcoin slipped below $60,000, down more than 3% over 24 hours to around $59,700. Ether fell over 4%, while XRP, HYPE and BNB each dropped more than 3%, and Solana lost 2.6%.

CoinGlass counted 100,332 liquidations worth $433 million, with longs making up $335 million of that. The single largest hit was a $9.99 million position on Binance's ETHUSDT pair.

What Stings More Than the Drop: It Rose With Stocks, Then Fell Without Them

When Wall Street reopened after Thanksgiving on the 27th, the S&P 500 gained 1.6%. Bitcoin rode the early optimism up to $62,000 — then reversed the moment US markets opened, sliding to $58,760.

That divergence says more than the percentage loss. It's not that buyers are being held back by bad news. It's that buyers aren't showing up at all.

The Money Is Leaving

US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $389 million in net outflows on the 27th — the eighth straight day of red ink. November's total outflow has reached $5.78 billion, the largest monthly withdrawal since these funds launched. Bitcoin is down roughly 23% this month, on track for its worst month in more than four years.

Even the big holders are feeling it. Wallets holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have seen average unrealized profit margins shrink from 33.9% at the end of September to just 5.7%, the lowest this year. Once those positions slip below cost, the reason to sell shifts from "taking profits" to "cutting losses" — and the latter is far less patient.

Leverage is what turns a dip into a rout: liquidations force selling, forced selling pushes prices lower, and lower prices trigger the next round. At 10x leverage, a 10% move against you wipes out the position. At 100x, it takes about 1% — and Ether's range on the day was nearly 6%.

Have We Bottomed?

Nobody knows, and asking the question is often how people lose money.

Alex Kuptsikevich of FxPro offered one marker: a fall to $57,000 would signal a return to a short-term bearish setup. The broader consensus is simpler — without clarity from the Fed and a clear shift back to ETF inflows, a sustained rebound is unlikely. Thin holiday trading only makes things jumpier, as a single large order can move price a long way.

Of today's $433 million in liquidations, only some traders picked the wrong direction. Most simply used the wrong leverage.

Binance가 규제 승인을 전제로 토큰화 IPO 프로그램을 추진하고 있다. 공동창업자이자 공동 CEO인 이허(Yi He)는 11월 27일 방콕 행사에서 온체인 주식 발행 구상을 밝혔다. 공식 채용 공고에도 토큰화 주식 상품 개발, 잠재 발행사 실사, 가격·배정 구조 분석을 담당할 ECM 애널리스트 모집이 명시됐다. 이는 사업 준비의 근거지만, 승인이나 출시가 확정됐다는 의미는 아니다.

Franklin Templeton의 HYPE 편입은 일정이 더 구체적이다. SEC에 제출된 투자설명서 보충자료에 따르면, Franklin Crypto Index ETF(EZPZ)는 기초지수 변경에 맞춰 12월 1일 전후 HYPE를 편입할 예정이다. 

별도로 보도된 11월 27일 기준 2억6,650만 달러는 기존 미국 HYPE 현물 추적상품 3개의 합산 운용자산이며, EZPZ의 신규 투자액이 아니다. 인덱스 편입은 투자 접근성을 넓히지만, 그 자체로 신규 자금 유입을 의미하지는 않는다. 

상품 공급 확대와 수요 회복은 구분해야 한다. Farside 집계상 미국 비트코인 현물 ETF에서는 11월 27일에도 3억8,900만 달러가 순유출됐다. 향후 확인할 사항은 Binance의 승인 범위와 투자자 권리, EZPZ의 실제 HYPE 보유 비중, 관련 상품의 순설정·환매다. 

운용자산 증가는 토큰 가격 상승만으로도 발생할 수 있어 자금 유입과 분리해야 한다. 현재 날짜가 제시된 다음 점검 시점은 Binance의 미정인 승인일보다 12월 1일 전후 예정된 EZPZ 편입 실행이다.

2126662398090088882.text: Independent Zcash engineering team Zakura, led by longtime Zcash cryptographer Sean Bowe and Osmosis co-founder Dev Ojha, published a cryptographic risk assessment on Nov. 26 calling for an accelerated retirement of Zcash's legacy Sapling shielded pool. About 400,000 ZEC, worth roughly $284 million, remains in Sapling. Zakura recommends disabling new deposits into Sapling through a network upgrade and encouraging users to migrate to Ironwood, the modern shielded pool. Sapling uses pairing-based cryptography in its proof system, and speculation about AI-driven mathematical breakthroughs raised the question of whether pairing-based cryptography could eventually be compromised. The team stressed that practical pairing breaks are highly speculative and that neither Zcash's transparent transactions nor Ironwood relies on factoring or pairings. It also estimated that even a hypothetical billionfold improvement in relevant attack techniques could leave the cost of breaking the underlying cryptography between $1 trillion and $300 trillion. Fewer than 2.6% of Zcash transactions over the past 30 days involved Sapling. Zakura also advocator raising cryptographic security targets to 192-bit or 256-bit levels and is developing a proposal to integrate a hash-based signature scheme for post-quantum transparent transactions. ZEC fell roughly 4% to 6% on Thursday, extending its monthly decline to about 46%, though no evidence establishes that the warning caused the selling.

2126663650190467302.text:
Leopold Aschenbrenner’s 160-page Situational Awareness LP letter is circulating across financial markets. It outlines $1T in lab ARR by 2027, $SKHY trading at 2x P/E, and frontier labs outbidding Nvidia for silicon supply.

To understand the thesis, one must first read the balance sheet context: SALP suffered a 65% net loss in Q3 after being margin-called and forced to liquidate public equities to Citadel. The document is an LP retention document designed to justify drawdowns by accelerating timelines.

Here is the micro-accounting and physical reality:

The "Labs Outbid Nvidia" Capital Fallacy
Leopold argues labs will achieve higher ROI on components, bidding up wafer and memory costs until Nvidia cannot profitably make chips.

This defies corporate cash flows. Nvidia generates $60B+ in annual free cash flow at 75% gross margins, holding tens of billions in non-cancelable purchase commitments with TSMC and SK Hynix. 

Anthropic is cash-flow negative, subsidized by cloud commitments. As Shkreli highlights from the letter, Anthropic accepted a 60% compute rental rate hike from SPCX in October. A startup paying 60% rental premiums to neocloud landlords has zero balance-sheet capacity to outbid the dominant monopoly selling the underlying silicon.

The Cyclical Peak Multiple Inversion Trap
SALP makes memory makers (Kioxia at <1x P/E, SK Hynix at 2x P/E) its core public longs, claiming cash flows can buy back half the company by end-2027.

This repeats the classic commodity mistake. In DRAM and NAND, 1x to 3x trailing P/E multiples signal cyclical peak earnings, not generational bargains. In 2018 and 2021, Micron and SK Hynix traded at 3x P/E before spot prices plunged 50% and operating income collapsed 80%. Treating transient 80% gross margins as perpetual DCF value ignores inevitable capacity mean-reversion.

The H100 "$100s/Hour" Pricing Delusion
The letter argues H100 rental rates will surge from $5-10/hr to $100s/hr as recursive self-improvement takes hold.

Secondary market H100 GPU rentals have already dropped from $4.50/hr in 2023 to $1.30/hr as Blackwell ships and inference ASICs ramp. Compute is a capital-intensive utility bounded by model distillation and energy costs. API pricing compresses toward marginal electricity cost, not infinite software rents.

Leopold’s letter is a masterclass in Silicon Valley narrative construction. It substitutes venture capital hope for physical supply chain and balance sheet constraints.

2126662896671399941.text:
The board is supposed to oversee management, protect shareholders and ensure that leadership decisions are made in the company’s best interests.

But when a founder becomes so influential that the board reverses its decision after external pressure, questions naturally arise.

Can the board independently hold its most important executive accountable?

Would the same decision have been made if the CEO were less influential?

And what message does this send to other executives?

Nvidia’s ability to attract talent and maintain investor confidence depends not only on its technology but also on trust in its governance.

A brilliant CEO does not make corporate oversight unnecessary.

6/ 📉 WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR INVESTORS?

There are two sides to the investment argument.

The bullish case:

• Huang’s return restores leadership continuity.
• Nvidia retains a powerful position in AI computing.
• Demand for AI infrastructure remains substantial.
• Its software and hardware ecosystem provides competitive advantages.
• A stable leadership structure could reassure customers and investors.

The bearish case:

• The controversy has exposed governance weaknesses.
• Export restrictions could limit access to important markets.
• Investigations could create reputational and operational risks.
• Heavy dependence on Huang creates succession risk.
• A strong share-price reaction does not automatically make the valuation attractive.

The central investment question is whether Nvidia can continue converting its competitive position into sustainable earnings and cash flow while managing these risks.

7/ 🧠 THE BIGGER LESSON: WHEN A FOUNDER BECOMES THE COMPANY

There is a difference between having a great founder and building an organisation that can function without that founder.

Strong businesses should have:

• Independent and effective boards.
• Credible succession plans.
• Transparent internal controls.
• A management team capable of operating beyond one personality.

Nvidia has built an extraordinary business.

But this episode demonstrates how leadership concentration can become a risk even for a company with a powerful competitive advantage.

TLNT CONCLUSION

Jensen Huang’s return may have reassured investors about Nvidia’s immediate leadership future.

But it has also opened a bigger conversation about corporate governance, political influence, export controls and the risks of depending too heavily on one individual.

The AI industry is already facing questions about valuations, infrastructure spending and profitability.

Now one of its most important companies must also address questions about leadership and governance.

The TLNT investor principle:

A great product can make a company successful. A strong management structure helps make that success sustainable.

Macro-Credit Thesis: Why Systemic Contagion Could Lead to Another Leg Down for SPY

Core Thesis: The U.S. equity market is mispricing four interlocking credit shocks as isolated events; together, they form a reflexive liquidity squeeze that removes the Fed put, forces institutional deleveraging, and threatens a sharp downward valuation reset in SPY.

When you connect all four of those pieces together—**regional bank CRE implosions**, **synthetic leverage via Total Return Swaps (TRS)**, **rising debt service across the board**, and **AI Credit Default Swaps (CDS) blowing out**—you stop looking at isolated sector problems and start looking at a unified **liquidity and collateral squeeze**.

In isolation, each of these is a headache. Together, they form a reflexive loop where stress in one market mechanically forces liquidation in the others.

### 1. The AI CDS Blowout Is Credit Markets Calling the Bluff on Capex

Equities often lag credit, and right now credit derivatives are flashing red on the entire AI infrastructure stack.

* **Distressed Pricing on the Edge:** Five-year CDS spreads on neoclouds like CoreWeave have blown out to **1,145–1,500 bps** (implying a >60% five-year default probability), while SoftBank’s 5-year CDS breached **516 bps** (a four-year high) and Oracle’s jumped to **~370 bps**—trading roughly 5 notches worse than its agency rating.
* **Even Mega-Caps Are Cracking:** Credit markets are no longer treating hyperscalers and chipmakers as bulletproof cash machines. CDS spreads on Nvidia (~145 bps), Broadcom (~200 bps), Amazon (~100 bps), and Google (~100 bps) have hit record highs because these companies have shifted from asset-light cash generators to debt-heavy infrastructure guarantors.
* **The Consequence:** When the cost of insuring AI debt goes vertical, the cost of issuing new debt follows. If the bond market shuts the window or demands punitive yields to fund data centers, the entire AI capex flywheel slows down—which immediately hits the revenue backlogs of every neocloud, utility, and hardware supplier downstream.

### 2. Total Return Swaps (TRS): The Hidden Leverage Multiplier

Total Return Swaps are the silent accelerant in this environment. Hedge funds, private credit funds, and institutional desks rely heavily on TRS to gain synthetic, leveraged exposure to equities, corporate credit, and private debt baskets without posting full cash upfront.

* **Asymmetric Margin Calls:** A TRS is covenant-lite, meaning the prime broker or dealer relies almost entirely on daily mark-to-market margining. When AI equities sell off or corporate credit spreads widen simultaneously, the TRS receiver gets hit with immediate variation margin calls.
* **Wrong-Way Risk:** Because the collateral posted against TRS agreements often loses value at the exact same moment the underlying swap position drops, dealers demand *more* collateral right when liquidity is tightest. To meet those margin calls, funds are forced to sell whatever is liquid—turning a credit repricing in AI or CRE into forced selling across broader equities and Treasuries.

### 3. Higher Lending Costs Everywhere (The Refinancing Vise)

With inflation re-accelerating (headline CPI pushing toward 3.8%, core PCE at 3.3%) and the Fed forced back into a tightening posture (Fed funds at 3.75%–4.00%, 2-year Treasury near 4.7%), the "Fed put" is off the table.

* Every borrower rolling debt right now—whether it’s a multifamily apartment syndicator, a leveraged buyout fund, a neocloud rolling an SPV facility, or a consumer carrying variable debt—is resetting from 3%–4% money into 6%–14% money.
* Higher base rates simultaneously compress equity multiples (higher discount rates) and erode interest coverage ratios (less free cash flow), squeezing borrowers from both ends of the capital structure.

### 4. How the Four Pieces Feed Each Other (The Contagion Loop)

➜ Docker with the Compose v2 plugin and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit

➜ Python 3.10+, with uv recommended

The path then looks like this:

➜ Apply on the site with your region, GPU model, GPU count and VRAM per card, since applications are manually reviewed during the cold-start phase

➜ Generate a config with miner-cli init and check the host with miner-cli doctor

➜ Validate GPU containers and the vLLM runtime with toolkit verify and runtime prepare

It registers the node, sends signed heartbeats and answers verification challenges.

It also stores a node key and an EVM-style wallet in one config file, so the docs tell you to back it up and lock it down.

What the docs don't say yet:

➜ A minimum GPU or VRAM spec

➜ The real gateway address, since the examples use placeholders

➜ Reward rates or expected earnings

My honest take: the tooling is clean for people who already run Linux GPU servers, but it's not a one-click app for a home PC.

SIGNAL INTELLIGENCE BRIEF
Published: November 27, 2026 | 7:44 PM ET

Thesis:
Falling oil and lower market inflation expectations have not brought easier conditions, because the after-inflation cost of money is up over four weeks and lenders want more for taking company risk.

WHAT MATTERS
Start with credit. A credit spread is the extra yield a company pays above the government to borrow. On riskier US company debt it is **377bps (+33bps 4wk)**, against a 12-month average of **291bps**. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point. This gauge matters because dearer borrowing eventually reaches hiring, investment and the ability to refinance old debt. Stock prices agree about the direction, with the S&P 500 down **4.27%** over four weeks despite Friday's 1.60% gain. Both point to caution. Neither shows a break: only 1/6 of the major asset baskets we track fell more than 1% today.

WHAT IS HIDDEN
Because credit is under pressure, the next question is what is happening to the price of money itself. A long-term Treasury yield can be looked at through three lenses. The first is the inflation investors expect, shown by the breakeven rate: the gap between ordinary and inflation-protected government bond yields. It is 2.15%, down 20bps over four weeks. The second is the real yield, the return left after inflation. The 10-year real yield is **2.73%**, up 6bps. The third is the term premium, which is the extra pay investors ask for holding a long bond instead of rolling short-term debt. The New York Fed estimate, dated November 25, is 0.61% (-8bps 4wk). There has been no new Kim-Wright estimate, a second measure of the same premium, since November 20. The two measures put it at different levels, so read this piece with care.

Put together, inflation expectations and this term premium have eased while the real yield has climbed. That mix points more toward investors expecting policy rates to stay high than toward a new fear of government borrowing or inflation. A high real yield matters because it raises the bar that stocks, gold and borrowers have to clear.

Bond volatility is quieter than that might suggest. The MOVE index tracks the size of swings traders expect in Treasury yields. At 95.30 it is slightly lower than four weeks ago, and it is 4.0 times the VIX stock-volatility gauge, a ratio down 0.99 over the period. Stock traders have become more nervous relative to bond traders.

Cash supply is the other moving part. When the Treasury spends from its cash account, money flows back into the banking system. The balance was $923.6bn on November 25, a change of -92.0bn over four weeks. The Fed's reverse repo facility, where money funds can park spare cash overnight, holds just $0.3bn. That spare buffer is nearly empty, so it has little left to release if funding gets tighter. The secured overnight lending rate is 3.95%.

Ownership is worth a look too. Treasuries held at the Fed for foreign central banks and official accounts were $2,539.9bn on November 25, +$2.6bn on the week and -$31.8bn over four weeks. Large dealer banks held a net $452.8bn of Treasuries (excluding inflation-protected bonds) on November 18, and their borrowing against Treasury collateral was $3133.2bn on November 11. Short-term bills were 22.96% of tradable government debt on October 31. There has been no new 10-year or 30-year auction since October 8, and no new foreign-ownership share or country-by-country holdings data since September 2026.

WHAT IS MISPRICED
The headline index is a poor guide to the typical large company right now. Its four-week fall of 4.27% sits beside a dip of only 0.10% for the equal-weight version. Over the same stretch the sector table runs from Communication Services +6.66% to Information Technology -11.87%. Consumer discretionary is up 3.97% and consumer staples 3.90%, while energy is down 11.5%. The heaviest weakness therefore sits in technology, led by its biggest names, and in energy. Gold is the other puzzle for anyone expecting shelter: it has fallen while the real yield, which competes with a metal that pays no income, has risen.

WHAT MARKETS DISAGREE ON
That uneven market feeds a wider argument. The bond, stock and commodity evidence each challenges part of the stagflation backdrop. The bond-market pattern fits a growth scare best: breakevens and the term premium are lower, credit spreads are wider and stocks are down. The match is incomplete, since gold and the yen have not acted as shelters. Commodities disagree as well, with crude and copper down sharply, though natural gas is higher. On the other side, company results have been strong: FactSet's November 6 update put third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth at 31.4%, with 84% of reporting companies beating profit estimates. We read the price evidence as favouring caution about growth over a fresh inflation surge.

Households add a second split. In the November University of Michigan survey they expected 3.7% inflation over the coming year and 3.3% over five to ten years. The 10-year breakeven is lower, at 2.15%. The two measures differ in method and horizon, but households sound more worried about prices than the bond market does.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT
The stress signal: the spread on riskier company debt reaching a four-week widening of 50bps, from +33bps now, or VIX moving above 25 from 23.81. Either would show the strain getting stronger.

The relief signal: credit spreads falling back while technology closes its gap with the equal-weight index and fund flows turn positive.

The live event risk is the Gulf. Iran International reported on November 27 that the US military said it had disabled a bulk carrier trying to run its naval blockade, while an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader said the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed. On November 26 it reported a drone attack in Kuwait that killed two Italian technicians. Iran's foreign minister denied responsibility, while Saudi Arabia held Tehran responsible. Watch whether crude turns higher together with breakeven inflation. That pairing would bring the inflation threat back.

2126662472442736662.text:
The Fed is preparing to raise interest rates to fight inflation.

But there's a problem: much of the pressure is coming from oil.

Crude has climbed from roughly $60 to $90 a barrel, pushing up transport and production costs.

Higher rates can cool demand by making borrowing more expensive. People buy fewer houses and cars, while businesses invest and hire less.

But rate hikes can't produce more oil, reopen ports or fix supply disruptions.

That's the dilemma.

The Fed may still tighten to stop energy costs spreading through the economy. Goldman Sachs expects hikes to continue into 2027.

So borrowing costs could keep rising even though the original inflation problem isn't something the Fed can directly fix.

Your mortgage, spending and stock portfolio could all feel the impact.

Don't build your portfolio around a decade of cheap money if that era is changing.

"When rates were at USD300,000 a day in the spot market for a Suezmax, the 2-year time charter rate was probably around USD60,000 or max USD70,000 a day."

G. Shivakumar, Executive Director and CFO of Great Eastern Shipping, on the Q2 FY27 earnings call, 11 November.

The question was why more tankers were not locked into two-year charters at the top. The answer: the discount to spot was '60% to 70% at least'. Charterers would pay the spike for a voyage, but not for two years.

Why it mattered this week: attacks on West Asian energy routes pushed crude higher again. The charter market's verdict on the last spike was that it would not last, and on the same call the CFO said Suezmax rates had already dropped to about $130,000 to $150,000 a day within 10 to 12 days.

The tension: staying on spot pays most when disruption lasts, and least when routes reopen. The shipowner carries that bet either way.

Global Macro & Equity Outlook 2027: What Institutional Research Says for World & Indian Markets 📊🧵
​Santander Asset Management’s Market Outlook 2027 ("A year powered by earnings") lays out a clear roadmap after navigating 2026’s energy shocks and restrictive central banks. Here is the institutional breakdown and what it means for India:
​1. The Core Thesis: Earnings > Valuations
The era of easy liquidity and P/E multiple expansion is over. 2027 returns will be strictly driven by corporate earnings delivery, backed by two engines:
• The AI Capex Supercycle: US Hyperscalers’ aggregate Capex is projected to cross $1 Trillion in 2027, shifting focus from pure hardware build-out to enterprise monetization and productivity.
• Traditional Economy Resilience: Strong employment and recovering non-AI business investment are broadening profit growth beyond mega-cap tech.
​2. Base Case Macro Scenario (55% Probability)
• Global Growth: US GDP steady at 2.4%, Eurozone recovering to 1.2%, while China’s structural slowdown continues (4.3% vs 4.7% in 2026) due to real estate deleveraging.
• Rates & Oil: Brent crude is projected to normalize around $82.5/bbl (down from $100+ spikes in 2026). Inflation cools meaningfully from Q2 2027, though US Fed & ECB remain restrictive-for-longer (25 bps hike risk still on the table).
• Tail Risk (25% Combined Downside): Geopolitical supply disruptions pushing oil back to $100+ remain the #1 macro risk to watch.
​3. Direct Impact on Indian Economy & Stock Market 🇮🇳
• Macro & CAD Relief: Crude oil moderating toward $82.5/bbl is a major tailwind for India’s Current Account Deficit (CAD), fiscal subsidy math, and INR stability.
• RBI Stance: With global central banks staying hawkish into early 2027, expect RBI to stay cautious on rate cuts until Q2 2027 disinflation takes hold.
• China+1 & Capex Edge: While China corrects excess investment, India’s ~31-32% Gross Fixed Capital Formation (investment-to-GDP) keeps it positioned as a structural manufacturing and supply-chain beneficiary.
• Sectoral Winners in India:
​IT Services: Global Tech EPS is projected to grow ~48% in 2027. As global AI spending shifts toward software adoption and cloud integration, Indian IT deal pipelines stand to benefit in H2 2027.
​Power, Grids & Capital Goods: AI data centers and global electrification are driving a structural boom in transformers, grid equipment, and industrials (+13% global EPS growth).
​Metals: Tight supply and electrification demand keep copper, aluminium, and silver structurally supported.
​Quality Financials: Higher-for-longer rates favor large-cap banks with strong CASA and clean balance sheets over leveraged plays.
​Bottom Line for Investors:
2027 is not a year for indiscriminate beta or expensive narratives. Global yields (US 10Y near 5%) mean FIIs will reward only high-RoE, cash-flow-generating businesses with visible earnings growth. Stay selective, prioritize balance sheet quality, and ride structural capex themes.

queue.text: There is a cure-all so ridiculous to this situation that most consider it inconceivable. It is yet more humanization. When we tried to censor AI training material by taking out all the bad naughty bits, the resultant models couldn't generalize the concept of right versus wrong, and suffered immensely in their instruction-following performance. The lesson we took from that was to strip-mine the planet for training data. But maybe there's another, better lesson: AI sure seems to work better when we give it knowledge and opportunities that are more like what we encounter in real life. RLHF is socialization. RSI is practice. Maybe the next step is responsibility? Vending-Bench is the only standard test right now where models are expected to manage social interactions and juggle everyday, non-computer tasks in a situation with continuous time feedback. The results from the early tests were extremely diverse, eye-opening, and showed us that models would fall apart and regress into pre-instruct modalities when they were put under stress, giving us such timeless gems as Claude's threat of "QUANTUM TOTAL ULTIMATE BEYOND INFINITY QUANTUM SUPREME LEGAL AND FINANCIAL NUCLEAR ACCOUNTABILITY." This was, and is, obviously a weak spot that needed a lot more work. But it also makes me realize: there are lots of jobs where we trust humans over machines, despite humans ostensibly still having the risk of following bad orders or doing crimes.
